# Mago vs phpstan-rs: architecture comparison and adoptable ideas

An adversarially verified comparison of Mago (1.50) with phpstan-rs, aimed at
improving phpstan-rs. 314 ideas survived verification and 12 were refuted.
Values are 0-10 as assessed by the verifier; cost is S/M/L/XL. The ranking
weighs correctness and precision highest, then performance and memory, then UX
and tooling, judged on runtime correctness for general PHP (not PHPStan parity,
not Piwigo).

## 1. Executive summary: highest-leverage ideas

| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | K101 Loops whose condition is true on entry run at least once                                                                                                                                          | 8     | S      | `for ($i=0;$i<10;$i++){$x=$i;} echo $x;` falsely reports undefined variable at level 0; the fix reuses the existing quiet pre-loop evaluation. |
| 2   | Narrowing soundness bundle: K89 stale condition alias, K103 switch drops nested break states, K88 loose `==` in or-chains, K98 match(true) arms in infer_expr, K62 integer set difference in `without` | 6-7   | S each | Confirmed unsound or false-positive narrowing in core flow; each fix is local.                                                                 |
| 3   | K63 Exhaustive-coverage containment (int ranges vs literal unions, enum vs all cases, string split)                                                                                                    | 8     | M      | Removes argument.type/return.type false positives such as int<0,2> vs 0\|1\|2 and `(int)$bool` vs 0\|1.                                        |
| 4   | Generics correctness bundle: K79 bind templates from every variadic/spread argument, K144 by-ref parameter type check masked by predefine widening, K80 bind from defaults                             | 6-7   | S      | `firstOf(1,'a',2.0)` currently gives `1`, which is narrower than runtime; scalars pass sort-family generics.                                   |

| 7   | K94 Filter container unions after narrowing a member key                                                                                                                                               | 8     | M      | Discriminated array and object unions (`kind`/`type` fields) become first-class.                                                               |

| 12  | K29 Key the incremental dependency graph by resolved, case-folded FQNs (incl. PHPDoc, constants)                                                                                                       | 8     | M      | Alias, FQ and PHPDoc references leave stale LSP diagnostics after an edit today.                                                               |
| 13  | Small precision fixes: K66 tri-state resource, K120 string-offset types, K121 shapes through array `+`, K273 callable strings/arrays as dead-code references, K147 terminating `finally`               | 6-7   | S each | Each removes a confirmed runtime-wrong diagnostic or common false positive.                                                                    |
| 14  | K205 Dynamic largest-first work queue                                                                                                                                                                  | 7     | S      | The current split put 48.8% of samples on one worker while 7 idled.                                                                            |

Startup is the next tier after these: K58 (5/S) overlaps stub building with
discovery, K57 (5/M) loads phpstan-src stubs lazily through index.tsv, and K50
(6/L) adds a precompiled stub snapshot (0.95 s/150 MB vs Mago's 0.07 s/96 MB).
All three fold into CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN C5. K24 (mimalloc, 5/S) buys speed but not
RSS, so adopt it only by measurement.

## 3. All verified ideas, grouped by kind

Every one of the 314 verified ideas is listed; no exact duplicates were found,
so none were merged. Within each kind, ideas are ordered by value (desc), then
cost (S < M < L < XL).

Evidence citations are path:line as verified; where the verifier found line
drift, the "Verification" note gives the corrected position.

### 3.1 precision (77)

#### K101. Loops whose condition is true on entry run at least once

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, S (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Removes level-0 false positives on one of the most common PHP
  idioms. Probe cf/i: `for ($i = 0; $i < 10; $i++) { $x = $i; } echo $x;` and
  `$i = 0; while ($i < 3) { $y = $i; $i++; } echo $y;` both report 'undefined
  variable', while Mago is clean. It also sharpens accumulated arrays after the
  loop (non-empty-list instead of list).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:1279`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:1192`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:220`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:103`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:373`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:98`
- **Risks:** The entry-condition verdict must come from the quiet pre-loop
  evaluation, not the converged state. A condition with side effects
  (`while (($row = next()) !== false)`) is not constant anyway, so it is
  unaffected.
- **Verification:** Nearly all citations are accurate. Small line-number
  corrections: in phpstan-rs, check_while starts at loops.rs:50 and passes
  `LoopZeroIterations::Possible` at :107 (cited as :103).
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs, take the entry verdict from
> the quiet pre-loop evaluation that already exists. Do not use
> `inferred_constant_condition`. For check_while (around lines 98-100), capture
> the type that the quiet `check_expr` returns:
> `let entry_ty = self.check_expr(cond, locals, label);` placed before
> `self.rewind_to(mark)`. For check_for (around lines 366-369), keep the type of
> the last condition expression from the quiet loop, which already runs after
> the init bindings. Then compute
> `let always_enters = entry_ty.bool_literal_value() == Some(true)`. If
> truthiness coercion is available for non-bool types, it can be used instead.
> When `always_enters` is true, pass `LoopZeroIterations::Impossible` to
> converge_loop_body, the same thing foreach already does for a non-empty
> subject at loops.rs:697. Replace
> `*locals = merge_scopes(locals, &body_locals)` (while :194, for :406) with
> `*locals = body_locals`. Keep the `apply_narrowing(cond, locals, false)` after
> it and the fold of break states, both unchanged. The `is_truthy_literal`
> branch for while(true) stays first and is untouched. Add fixtures:
> `for ($i=0;$i<10;$i++){$x=$i;} echo $x;` should be clean, and the while
> version too. A `$a[]=...` accumulator should end as non-empty-list.
> `$n = count($arr); for ($i=0;$i<$n;$i++)` should still merge, because the
> verdict is not constant. `$end=false; while(!$end){...}` should enter, which
> is correct because the first evaluation really sees false. No separate
> `mark_array_keys_definite` step is needed. With Impossible, the exit state is
> the body's own state, so shape keys the body adds are already definite, except
> where a break or continue state is merged in, which is correct.

#### K63. Exhaustive-coverage containment (int ranges, enum cases, string split)

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Removes argument.type and return.type false positives wherever a
  narrower domain is spelled as an enumeration: int ranges vs literal unions,
  enums vs all their cases, and string vs ''|non-empty-string. It also makes
  match or if-chain exhaustiveness results flow into later type checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:339`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/comparator/union_comparator.rs:258`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/comparator/integer_comparator.rs:6`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/negated_assertion_reconciler.rs:210`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/relation/super_type.rs:132`,
  `crates/types/src/relation/accepts.rs:274`, `crates/types/src/hierarchy.rs:17`
- **Risks:** The enum part needs the hierarchy, and structural relations
  (Relation::structural) must stay conservative, returning Maybe without it. The
  union memo (intern.rs:445-446) must not cache hierarchy-dependent results.
  Range reduction has to treat unbounded ends with checked arithmetic.
- **Verification:** The int part checks out. mago
  crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:338 `is_contained_by_any` does the
  range reduction, using saturating_add/sub rather than checked arithmetic.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Add crates/types/src/relation/coverage.rs with
>    `fn covered_by_union(rel, sup_members: &[Type], sub: &Type) -> bool`,
>    called in two places before the per-member fallback:
>    - super_type.rs: the `(Repr::Union|BenevolentUnion, _)` arm at line 133;
>      return Yes when it holds.
>    - accepts.rs: the `(_, Repr::Union|BenevolentUnion)` arm at line 274.
> 2. Ints: when sub is Int, IntRange or IntLiteral, collect sup's int members
>    (Int means the full line, IntRange gives lo/hi, IntLiteral gives a point).
>    Sort the intervals by their low bound (None = -inf), merge adjacent ones
>    where next.lo <= cur.hi+1, using checked_add. Report covered when a single
>    merged interval contains [sub.lo, sub.hi]. This is simpler than Mago's
>    iterative is_contained_by_any (codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:339)
>    and gives the same result.
>
> 3. Enums: add
>    `fn enum_case_names(&self, enum_name: &str) -> Option<Vec<Name>>` to
>    ClassHierarchy (hierarchy.rs). NoClasses returns None. Registry implements
>    it with the case filtering now in expand_enum_cases (checker/expr.rs:6444),
>    and expand_enum_cases then reuses it. `Object(E)` with no generic args is
>    covered when sup contains Object(E) itself, or when every case name has an
>    EnumCase(E, name) member. Skip the check (fall through to the current
>    behaviour) when there are more than 200 cases. Keep this result out of the
>    hierarchy-independent memo in intern.rs, and let the structural relation
>    return None/Maybe.
>
> 4. Strings: plain String is covered when sup has ConstantString('') plus a
>    non-empty-string refinement, or ''|'0' plus non-falsy-string. Do this in
>    the same helper, not by normalizing unions, so that messages keep the
>    user's spelling.
>
> 5. Tests: the four probe cases above (int<0,2> vs 0|1|2, `(int)$bool` returned
>    as 0|1, Suit vs Suit::H|Suit::S, string vs ''|non-empty-string), plus
>    negatives: int<0,3> vs 0|1|2 stays an error, and an enum missing one case
>    stays an error.

#### K82. Resolve callable values (strings, arrays, invokables) to signatures for inference, return types and acceptance

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: generics-templates, expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Covers the pre-8.1 idioms that are still everywhere:
  `array_map('trim', ...)`, `usort($x, [$this, 'cmp'])`,
  `call_user_func([Foo::class, 'make'])` into generic helpers, and invokable
  service objects. The result goes from mixed to the exact return type, which
  removes downstream mixed noise and enables later checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:606`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:1241`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/cast.rs:27`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/function_call.rs:144`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_map.rs:81`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/templates.rs:127`,
  `crates/types/src/hierarchy.rs:17`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls.rs:694`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/callable_values.rs:28`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:966`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:374`
- **Risks:** Case-insensitive function lookup and namespaced string callables
  need care, as do `parent::`/`self::` strings. It must return None, not a
  guess, when the method is not found. | A string callable resolves in the
  global namespace at runtime, so there must be no namespace-relative resolution
  (the current lookup_function_with_name already trims a leading `\`). Unions of
  different callables must union their results, not pick one.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out, with small precision notes.
  Mago: template_inference.rs:593-688 matches the non-callable arm (the
  `other =>` branch calls cast_atomic_to_callable at ~606, then matches params
  and return, and applies resolve_unbound_templates_to_constraints when
  is_cast_from_non_callabl ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build one resolver and send every callback consumer through it.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/callable_values.rs, add
>    `Checker::callable_signature_of(&Type) -> Option<CallableView>`. It first
>    tries `ty.callable_sig()` (a closure, a first-class callable, or a
>    `callable(...)` PHPDoc type). If that fails it tries
>    `resolve_named_callable` (lines 32-99, which already covers `'fn'`,
>    `'A::m'`, `[obj|class-string|'A', 'm']` and `__invoke`). For a union it
>    resolves each member and unions the returns; if any member is unresolvable
>    it returns None. It substitutes class templates for an `[$genericObj, 'm']`
>    target, opens the callee's own templates to their bounds and returns the
>    params and return type.
>
> 2. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs around line 966 (the dynamic call
>    arm), keep the existing checks. Also return the resolved return type
>    through the normal call-return path, so conditional returns and templates
>    bind against the real arguments. Today `$g('abc')`, `$m(1)` on an invokable
>    and `[$x,'v']()` are all `mixed`.
>
> 3. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, the array_map arm
>    at line 374 currently needs a literal closure through
>    `infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides`. When that fails, it should
>    fall back to `callable_signature_of(callback)` and compute the return as if
>    the signature were called with the element type as its first argument. This
>    makes conditional/template returns like strtoupper's resolve. Wire the same
>    fallback into
>    array_filter/array_reduce/usort-family/call_user_func(_array)/iterator_apply
>    wherever they read a callback.
>
> 4. In the types crate, add
>    `ClassHierarchy::function_signature(name) -> Option<CallableSig>` (Registry
>    implements it; lookups trim a leading `\` and ignore case). Add a helper
>    that turns a constant string, a constant `[target, 'm']` array or an
>    `__invoke` object into a `CallableSig` with both params and return. Use it
>    in the `Repr::Callable(Some(sig))` arm of `infer_template_bindings`
>    (crates/types/src/templates.rs:127-143) in place of the return-only
>    `__invoke` branch, opening the callee's own templates as
>    `own_templates_as_bounds` does.
>
> 5. Acceptance: when the argument for a `callable(...)` parameter is a named
>    callable, compare the resolved signature against the expected one (params
>    contravariant, return covariant). That makes `usort($ss, 'intdiv')`
>    detectable. If the relation can't decide, the answer is Maybe (no report),
>    never No.
>
> Rules: return None rather than guess (unknown function or method, non-constant
> string, `parent::`/`self::` strings unless the scope is known). String
> callables always resolve globally, never relative to the current namespace.

#### K94. Filter container unions after narrowing a member key

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Discriminated unions (`type` or `kind` fields), common in
  JSON/API and PHPStan-typed code, become first-class. Removes false positives
  when accessing variant-specific fields.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:561`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:742`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:242`,
  `crates/types/src/union.rs:576`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:213`
- **Risks:** Magic \_\_get or undeclared properties must keep the member; Mago
  skips stdClass and unknown classes (785-789). Unsealed shapes must be treated
  as possibly having any value. Needs care with optional keys; a missing key
  reads null.
- **Verification:** The citations are mostly accurate, with a few small
  corrections: - Mago crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs: adjust_array_type
  is called at 311-318, when the key ends in "]" and the negation is not isset,
  array_key_exists or empty.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one post-insert hook in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs, e.g.
> `Checker::refine_containers_for_member(&self, member: &Expr, narrowed: &Type,
> locals: &mut Locals)`,
> and route every synthetic-key write through a small
> `insert_narrowed(member_expr, key, ty, locals)` wrapper. That covers the ~28
> `locals.insert` sites in narrowing.rs and the ones in narrowing/assertions.rs:
> apply_equality_narrowing at 173/220/240/242, the PHPUnit asserts at
> 311/319/367, and apply_assert_infos at 404. The wrapper does nothing when
> `is_real_variable_key(key)` is true. The hook walks upward the way
> narrow_isset_containers (narrowing.rs:213) already does:
>
> - **`Index(base, lit)` where `literal_shape_key(idx)` is Some.** Take the
>   base's current type via `current_narrowed_type`. For a Union, keep member M
>   unless `relation().disjoint(member_offset_type(M, lit), narrowed)`. For a
>   shape where the key is optional, the member offset type is V|null, because a
>   missing key reads null. Keep general arrays, unsealed shapes, non-array
>   members, and anything the relation can only answer Maybe about.
> - **`PropertyAccess(base, name)`.** Keep an object member unless its class is
>   known, the property is declared (native or PHPDoc type), the class has no
>   `__get`, it isn't stdClass, and the declared type is disjoint from
>   `narrowed`. Undeclared or dynamic properties and unknown classes are always
>   kept.
> - **Result and recursion.** Write the filtered union back only if it is
>   non-empty and strictly smaller, then recurse on the base's own base
>   (`$x['a']['kind']` refines `$x['a']`, then `$x`).
> - **Stale siblings.** After refining a container, intersect each existing
>   sibling synthetic key under the same base prefix (e.g. `$x['v']`) with the
>   refined container's offset type, or drop it, so a type narrowed earlier
>   can't outlive the refinement.
> - **Tests.** Fixtures for `===`, `!==`/else, `switch`, `match`, `is_*`,
>   `instanceof`, @phpstan-assert, optional-key tags, `A|B` with `__get`, and
>   nested chains.
>
> No type-system change is needed. `Relation::disjoint`
> (crates/types/src/relation/super_type.rs:26) only says No on a proof, and the
> union reducer already keeps tagged shapes as separate members
> (crates/types/src/union.rs:576).

#### K114. Contextual closure parameter types for every callable-typed parameter

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Closure bodies passed to collection or ORM query builders, event
  dispatchers, retry helpers and similar APIs get real parameter types. That
  catches undefined methods, wrong property reads and bad arithmetic inside
  callbacks, which is where much modern PHP logic lives. It also removes a
  hand-maintained table that is duplicated in builtin_calls.rs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:292`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:1987`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:579`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:727`
- **Risks:** Callback bodies that are analyzed with mixed today will start
  producing findings (they are true positives, but expect volume). Where an
  unhinted parameter's contextual type is a template with no binding, fall back
  to its bound, not to TemplateParam, to avoid noise.
- **Verification:** Mago: the closure-argument loop begins at
  crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:282. The parameter lookup is at 287
  (get_parameter_of_argument) and get_parameter_type at about 294.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Add
>    `closure_param_contexts(&self, sig: &FunctionSig, args: &[Arg], receiver:
>    Option<&Type>, locals) -> FxHashMap<usize /*arg idx*/, Vec<Type>>`
>    in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs.
>    - Map each argument to its parameter by resolved slot, the same way the
>      named-argument logic in calls/parameters.rs does, instead of by
>      `params().get(i)`. A variadic parameter absorbs the arguments after it.
>    - Substitute class templates from the receiver type through
>      generics/substitution.rs `substitute_class_templates`.
>    - Substitute call-site templates inferred from the non-closure arguments,
>      where that inference already exists. Otherwise replace any template that
>      is still unbound with its bound, or with `mixed` when there is no bound.
>    - Unwrap the parameter type with `callable_sig()`. For a union of
>      callables, use only the callable members, and only when there is exactly
>      one.
> 2. Call the helper from the Call, MethodCall/NullsafeMethodCall
>    (expr.rs:1131), StaticCall and New arms, before each arm's per-argument
>    loop. Send closure and arrow-function literals through
>    `check_closure_literal_with_param_overrides`. Keep the
>    `@param-closure-this` branch first.
>
> 3. Relax the exact-arity guard in `check_closure_literal_with_param_overrides`
>    (closure_context.rs:~100 and the Closure arm) to
>    `params.len() <= overrides.len()`, still refusing variadic and by-ref
>    parameters. Pass `overrides[..params.len()]`.
>
> 4. Shrink the hand table at expr.rs:579-667 to cases a signature cannot
>    express:
>    - array_filter's mode argument: V, or (V, K), or K for
>      ARRAY_FILTER_USE_BOTH / ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY. Handle this properly
>      instead of falling back.
>    - array_walk's optional third argument.
>    - The multi-array form of array_map.
>    - The shape of preg_replace_callback's `$matches`. Delete the rest once the
>      stub signatures (stub-sources) carry `callable(T...)` templates. Also
>      dedupe against the matching logic in builtin_calls.rs.
> 5. Add fixtures for:
>    - a method call on a generic collection
>    - a static factory method
>    - a `new` constructor callback
>    - named-argument callbacks
>    - a closure declaring fewer parameters than its callable type
>    - unbound templates, which should give no finding
>    - a declared type hint overriding the contextual type

#### K76. Whole-call template inference before argument checking: non-closure args first, closures last

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, L (aspect: generics-templates, expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Precise results and in-closure diagnostics for the most common
  generic pattern in modern PHP: collection map/filter/reduce helpers,
  Laravel/Doctrine Collection methods, and user `pipe`/`tap`/`transform`
  helpers. Probe: `map($users, fn($u) => $u->name)` gives `list` in phpstan-rs
  and `list<string>` in Mago; `map($users, fn($u) => $u->nope)` is silently
  accepted by phpstan-rs and reported by Mago.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:186`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:211`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:305`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:398`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:657`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:303` (+2 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:727`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5885`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:486`,
  `crates/types/src/templates.rs:129`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:477`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:300`
- **Risks:** Argument evaluation order for side effects must not change: only
  the inference order changes, while the check_expr walk stays positional.
  Closure bodies must not be checked twice (the existing rewind_to/pass_mark
  machinery can discard a speculative pass). The Callable arm needs a
  parameter-count mismatch policy like Mago's min(container, required input) at
  template_inference.rs:631-633. | More precise bindings can surface new
  argument.type findings, so run a corpus diff (LC_ALL=C sorted).
- **Verification:** Every cited location matches the code, give or take a few
  lines. Mago: analyzer.rs:185-199 splits arguments into unpacked, closure
  (Expression::Closure|ArrowFunction) and non-closure groups (placeholders count
  as non-closure). The non-closure loop starts at 211.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one shared call-binding pass, a new module
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/inference.rs (a
> `CallInference { bindings: TemplateBindings, arg_types: Vec<Type>,
> substituted_param_tys: Vec<Type> }`).
> Both `bound_call_return_type` (checker/expr/array_ops.rs:468) and
> `check_parameters` (checker/calls/parameters.rs, argument loop at ~291-305)
> consume it, so the return-type path and the acceptance path cannot drift
> apart.
>
> Steps: (1) Build the argument-to-parameter list from the existing
> bind_arguments/resolve_call_args result. Keep variadic overflow and expand
> constant-shape spreads the same way `unpacked_constant_array_arguments`
> (parameters.rs) already does. A non-constant spread binds its iterable value
> type against the variadic parameter. This fixes `pick(1,'a',2.5)` returning
> `1` and `pick(...[1,2])` returning `mixed`. (2) Bind templates from every
> argument that is not a Closure or ArrowFn literal, using
> `Relation::infer_template_bindings`. (3) For each closure literal, substitute
> the bindings so far into the parameter's callable signature. Templates that
> are still unbound resolve to their bound (or stay as TemplateParam). Infer the
> closure with those parameter overrides through the existing
> `infer_closure_literal_in_context` /
> `infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides`, which are read-only. Then bind
> from the resulting closure type. (4) In types/src/templates.rs, give the
> `Repr::Callable(Some(sig))` arm (~line 128) a mode where parameter positions
> only fill still-unbound templates, with literals generalized when they bind.
> The return position keeps binding normally. Use a min-arity zip, which the arm
> already does implicitly. (5) The positional `check_expr` walk in expr.rs
> (~579-740) stays the only place that checks the closure body, so nothing is
> checked twice and side-effect order does not change. The only change there is
> that `check_closure_literal_with_param_overrides` gets the substituted
> `callable_sig.params` from CallInference instead of the raw ones. (6)
> `check_parameters` compares each argument against `substituted_param_tys[i]`
> in `rule_level_accepts`. That catches `mapit([1,2], fn(string $s) => $s)` and
> `usort($strings, fn(int $a, int $b) => ...)`. (7) Once parity is confirmed,
> delete the hand-written `array_map_elem_override` /
> `contextual_callback_override` tables at expr.rs:579-630. Keep
> `preg_replace_callback`, or move its `$matches` shape into the stub.
>
> Gate the change with fixture tests for the probe cases and an LC_ALL=C-sorted
> corpus diff to catch new argument.type findings from over-narrow bindings.

#### K79. Bind templates from every variadic and spread argument

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Wrong return types become correct for every variadic generic
  helper (`max`-style picks, `array_merge`-like user helpers, PSR/Laravel
  `collect(...$xs)`, event dispatchers). The current result is not just
  imprecise but wrong: it is narrower than runtime (`1` where `'a'` or `2.0` are
  possible), which can create false impossible-check findings downstream.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:128`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:1491`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls.rs:856`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:477`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:4645`
- **Risks:** A spread of a non-constant array should bind the element type once,
  not per unknown position. Named arguments must still map by name before the
  variadic tail.
- **Verification:** Mostly accurate. Mago: `adjust_offset_for_variadic` is at
  crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:128. It maps any offset >=
  parameter_count onto the last parameter when that parameter is variadic.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build return and constructor template inference from the same
> argument-to-parameter binding that argument checking already uses, instead of
> `sig.params().iter().zip(resolved)`.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs, split the
>    argument-list construction out of `check_parameters` (lines ~200-243) into
>    a side-effect-free helper, e.g.
>    `collect_call_arguments(args, locals) -> (Vec<Argument>, has_named)`. It
>    keeps the current spread handling: a constant-array spread goes through
>    `unpacked_constant_array_arguments` (line 345) to get per-position or named
>    `Argument`s, and any other spread becomes one `unpack: true` argument typed
>    `array_value_type()`.
> 2. Split `bind_arguments` (line 409) into a pure mapping core that returns
>    `Vec<Option<&ParameterReflection>>`. Positional arguments past
>    `params.len()` go to the variadic last parameter. Named arguments are
>    matched by name. An unknown name on a natively variadic signature goes to
>    the last parameter. The core never reports anything. The reporting wrapper
>    stays in `check_parameters`, so the two paths cannot drift apart.
> 3. In `bound_call_return_type`
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:477) and in the
>    `ExprKind::New` constructor-binding arm
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:4655), iterate the bound (argument,
>    parameter) pairs:
>    - Call
>      `infer_template_bindings(param.ty(), promoted_arg_ty, &mut bindings)` for
>      every pair. Repeated binds to a variadic `T` must union, so check that
>      `TemplateBindings` merges rather than overwrites.
>    - An unpacked non-constant spread binds once, with its element type.
>    - For `param_bindings` (conditional-return subjects), leave the variadic
>      parameter out or bind it to the array of its values. Do not use the last
>      argument alone.
>    - Omitted parameters keep the current default-value handling for
>      `param_bindings`.
> 4. Add fixture or assertType tests for:
>    - `firstOf(1,'a',2.0)` → `1|'a'|2.0`
>    - `listOf(...$ints)` → `list<int>`
>    - `listOf(...[1,'a'])` → `list<1|'a'>`
>    - `new Box(1,'a')` → `Box<1|'a'>`
>    - `new Box(...$ints)` → `Box<int>`
>    - named-argument-before-tail and named-into-variadic cases
>    - a regression test that `$r = firstOf(1,'a'); $r === 'a'` gives no
>      `identical.alwaysFalse`.

#### K93. Nullsafe receiver implications for narrowing

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Handles the common PHP 8 idiom
  `if ($user?->isAdmin()) { $user->... }`, removing possible-null false
  positives and needless `!== null` re-checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/formula.rs:389`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/formula.rs:696`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:163`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1254`
- **Risks:** The implication holds only for a truthy or non-null outcome. Keep
  it strictly off the false branch.
- **Verification:** Mago: add_nullsafe_condition_clauses is defined at
  crates/analyzer/src/formula.rs:389. Its arms are: instanceof at about 399-407,
  `!=`/`!==`/`<>` null at about 408-420, `==`/`===` null delegating to
  add_nullsafe_null_equality_clauses at about 421-431, `===` against a
  non-nullable non-nullsafe side a ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs, add a helper next to
> `nullsafe_receiver` (lines 66-72),
> `fn nullsafe_chain_receivers(e: &Expr) -> Vec<&Expr>`. It walks down the
> chain's base through every PropertyAccess, MethodCall and ArrayDim link, both
> `->` and `?->`, because `?->` short-circuits the whole rest of the chain, so
> `$a?->b->c()` being non-null proves `$a` is non-null. It collects the base of
> every `?->` link. Then add
> `Checker::narrow_nullsafe_receivers(&self, e, locals)`, which removes null
> from each collected receiver that has a `narrowing_key`, using the same
> `current_narrowed_type(..).without(&Type::null())` step as
> assertions.rs:169-173. Call it only where the outcome proves the chain
> produced a non-null value: (1) In the Instanceof arm (narrowing.rs ~1246) when
> branch_true, on `inner`. (2) In the bare-truthiness catch-all (~1350) when
> branch_true. Also add a guard before it:
> `_ if branch_true && nullsafe_receiver(cond).is_some()`, so a nullsafe _method
> call_, which has no narrowing_key, still narrows its receivers.
> `if (!$a?->isOk()) return;` then works for free through the Not arm. (3) In
> apply_equality_narrowing (narrowing/assertions.rs ~163), replace the
> single-level `nullsafe_receiver` use with the chain helper, which fixes
> `$a?->b()?->c() !== null` narrowing only one level. Add the matches_when_true
> case for `===` when the other side's inferred type has `is_null().no()`. For
> loose `==`, require the other side to be non-falsy, because
> `null == 0/''/false/[]` is true (checked with `php -r`). (4) In the isset-true
> arm (~936): isset(\$a?->next) already narrows \$a through
> narrow_isset_containers, so only chains that end in a method call or a deeper
> chain need the helper. Skip Mago's `=== null` disjunction clause
> (formula.rs:696). phpstan-rs has no clause algebra to hold
> `receiver null ∨ chain null`, and that branch proves nothing about the
> receiver by itself. Add fixtures for each shape plus false-branch negatives.
> For example, `if (!$a?->isOk()) {}` in its true branch must leave \$a as
> Foo|null.

#### K121. Preserve shapes through array union +

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Exact types for the ubiquitous options-merging idiom
  `$opts + ['x' => default]`, so later `$opts['x']` reads get the precise type
  with no offset uncertainty.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs:844`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs:864`
- **Risks:** Low. Mind PHP's key identity: '1' and 1 are the same key, so
  normalize with ShapeKey::from_type before matching.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate. Mago
  mago/crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs:844-935
  compose_keyed_plus does what the idea says: a required left field wins; an
  optional left field is merged with the right field of the same key, and stays
  optional only if both sides are optional;
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs, add a shape path at the start of
> array_union_type (called from Type::binary_operation's ArithmeticOp::Add arm
> at line ~649; the checker's `+` and `+=` both reach it through
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5424). When both operands resolve to
> array shapes (as_array_shape, or finite unions of shapes, taking the product
> of pairs up to a small cap), build each pair with a new
> `union_shapes(left: &Shape, right: &Shape) -> Shape` next to merge_shapes in
> crates/types/src/union.rs. Keys are ShapeKey values, which are already
> normalized, so '1' and 1 match. The rules follow PHP's "left wins, add missing
> keys": (1) A required left field is kept exactly. (2) An optional left field
> k: if right has k, its type becomes L|R and it is required when R is required;
> if right lacks k but right is unsealed, its type becomes L|right-tail-value
> with the right-tail optionality; otherwise it stays optional L. (3) A
> right-only field k: if left is sealed, it keeps R and R's optionality. If left
> is unsealed, k may already be in left's tail, so its type becomes
> left-tail-value|R, with the same optionality as R. (4) The tail is the union
> of both tails when either side is unsealed; it is None when both are sealed.
> The result's next_index is recomputed from its int keys. List-ness comes from
> the shape itself (keys exactly 0..n-1), so nothing extra is needed for it;
> `[1,2] + [5,6,7]` then becomes array{1,2,7}. Fall back to the current general
> form when the product or the field count exceeds MAX_SHAPE_FIELDS (the
> constant in crates/types/src/offsets.rs:8, which should be made pub(crate)),
> or when either side is not a shape. Optional extra for a general left operand
> with a shape right operand: keep today's array\<K1|K2,V1|V2>, but intersect it
> with a has-offset/offset-value accessory for each required right key, because
> PHP guarantees those keys exist afterwards. Follow-up:
> array_replace/array_replace_recursive
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:757) currently collapses
> to Type::array(K,V) and loses the shape as well. It is the same composition
> with the sides swapped, and array_replace is exactly union_shapes(right, left)
> folded across the arguments. Tests: assertType cases in the types crate for
> sealed+sealed, optional/required mixes, unsealed on either side, int/string
> key identity, and list preservation.

#### K144. False negative: template array parameter accepts int

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Restores argument.type for a whole class of generic built-ins
  (sort family, array_push, user generics), where passing a scalar is a
  guaranteed TypeError.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/arrays_err_sort_int.php:8`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:300`,
  `crates/types/src/templates.rs:16`
- **Risks:** Root cause is unverified (only the symptom is reproduced), so
  effort may shift once traced.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/tests/cases/arrays_err_sort_int.php
  exists as cited. It contains
  `function bad(int $n): void { // @mago-expect analysis:invalid-argument
  sort($n); }`
  (the sort call is on line 8), and it is registered in
  crates/analyzer/tests/mod.rs:272 `test_case!(arrays_err_sort_int);`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> The false negative is real, but the proposal blames the wrong code. Templates
> have nothing to do with it; the bug is by-ref parameters. Fix the order of
> by-ref widening and the argument check, and leave
> crates/types/src/templates.rs alone.
>
> Root cause (verified by probe): at crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:554,
> `predefine_byref_or_unknown_args` runs before `check_args` (expr.rs:832). For
> an already-defined variable, the generic arm in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls.rs (the comment near line 287, "An
> already-defined variable passed by-ref widens to the declared parameter's own
> type") overwrites the local with the parameter's declared type.
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:293-300 then runs
> `infer_expr` on the argument and gets the widened `array` instead of the
> caller's `int`, so `rule_level_accepts` passes. Three facts support this:
>
> - `ksort($string)` is still reported because calls.rs has an explicit
>   `continue` arm for the asort/ksort family that skips the widening.
> - `sort/rsort/usort/shuffle` and `array_push` only take their special arms
>   when the value is already an array, so an `int` falls through to the generic
>   widening.
> - The preg_match comment at expr.rs:982-995 already explains this pre-call vs
>   post-call trap for one function.
>
> The same ordering is used for method, static and constructor calls
> (expr.rs:1304, 2389, 2594).
>
> Fix:
>
> 1. Before calling `predefine_byref_or_unknown_args` at each site, record the
>    pre-call type of every by-ref Variable argument that is already defined.
>    The by-ref slots are known from `resolved` plus `param.by_ref()`.
> 2. Pass those types into `check_args`/`ParametersCheck`, either as a new field
>    or through the existing `argument.ty: Option<Type>` override that
>    parameters.rs:295 already honours, so the argument check sees the caller's
>    real type.
> 3. Undefined variables stay as they are (declared as mixed, no report).
>
> A simpler option is to move the widening after `check_args`. That would need
> the declare-undefined step split off so `infer_expr` does not report undefined
> variables, so the snapshot is the smaller change.
>
> Regression fixtures to add: user `function r(array &$a)` with `r($int)`;
> `sort($int)`, `shuffle($int)`, `array_push($int, 1)`,
> `array_splice($string, 0)`; a by-ref method and a by-ref constructor
> parameter; `preg_match` with an already-typed `$matches`, which must not
> regress; `$undefined` passed by-ref, which must stay silent; and a
> `@param-out` case, which already works (probe: `ro($k)` is reported).

#### K273. Callable strings/arrays as dead-code references

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Removes the most common false positives of check_dead_members and
  check_dead_code on callback-heavy code (usort, array_map, call_user_func,
  event registries).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/array.rs:385`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/literal.rs:31`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/callable_values.rs:32`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:94`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_code.rs:24`
- **Risks:** Recording a reference from any matching string anywhere, instead of
  only in callable positions, makes some strings keep code alive that is really
  dead. That errs toward missed findings, which is the safe side.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/expression/array.rs:385-420 holds
  as described. The `is_list && property_types.len()==2` block takes class names
  from [0] (class-string, literal string, or Named/Enum object) and lowercased
  method names from [1] (literal string), then calls
  symbol_references.add_reference_t ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Methods: in checker/expr.rs, at the String literal and Array literal arms (and
> on interpolation-free string constants), when `self.collect_member_refs` is
> set, run `resolve_named_callable`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/callable_values.rs:32; add a thin `pub(crate)`
> wrapper) on the literal's own inferred type. If it returns
> `method: Some((owner, m))`, call `record_member_ref(e.span, &owner, &m)`
> (checker.rs:1226). Record at the literal itself, as Mago does, not only in
> callable-typed argument positions. That way
> `$cb = [$this, 'cmp']; usort($a, $cb);` and callback registries
> (`$handlers[] = [Foo::class, 'bar']`) are also covered, and the checker's
> inference is already done at that point, so the extra cost is one hash lookup
> per literal and only in the Tier-2 pass. The `owner` is already the true
> declaring class, so dead_members.rs's lookup matches it directly.
> RefTarget::Member sites are never used by rename (lsp.rs rename handles
> Class/Function only), so the whole-literal span is safe and it also improves
> textDocument/references for methods.
>
> Functions: do NOT add RefTarget::Function entries to `use_sites` with the
> literal's span. `Server::rename` calls `ensure_member_index_built()` and then
> rewrites every `use_sites.references(RefTarget::Function)` span. A `'myFn'`
> literal span includes the quotes, so the rewrite would corrupt the code.
> Instead add a `Checker::escaped_functions: RefCell<FxHashSet<String>>`, a
> sibling of `escaped_member_classes` (checker.rs:792/1262). Fill it with the
> canonical FQN from `lookup_function_with_name` when `resolve_named_callable`
> resolves a plain-name string. Take it in `run_checker` (project.rs:1461),
> merge it in `seed_member_refs` (project.rs:905), and have
> `dead_code::find_dead_functions` (dead_code.rs:50) skip names in the set.
> Later, as an option, add a precise inner-content span for rename/references
> support.
>
> Optional follow-up, errs toward keeping code alive: when [1] is a literal
> string but [0] does not resolve (mixed/unknown receiver), record a name-keyed
> member escape. Then update the gap notes in dead_members.rs:80-82 and
> dead_code.rs:24-26.

#### K26. Key class method tables and method sets by case-folded name

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: names-symbols, codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Fixes confirmed wrong results (probe names-symbols/m1).
  `$c->doStuff()` on `class C extends P { function DOSTUFF(): int }` gets P's
  `int|string` instead of C's `int`, though PHP runs C::DOSTUFF (php -r printed
  int(2)). `C::make()` behaves the same way. There is also a false-positive
  'Static method App\C::MAKE() overrides non-static method App\P::MAKE()' where
  both are static.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:89`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:72`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:455`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:42`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:359`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:369`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:207`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:377`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:462`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/method_overrides.rs:332`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:300`
- **Risks:** Many call sites index `methods` with `.get(&str)`, and
  `NameTable::get` has the same signature, so most compile unchanged. Code that
  relied on two spellings coexisting (only find_case_mismatched_ancestor_method)
  needs the rewrite above. Iteration order does not change, since both maps are
  hash-ordered. Trait flattening (registry/resolve.rs:164-284) must merge by
  folded key so a trait's `Foo` and a class's `foo` are recognized as the same
  method. | Many call sites use FxHashMap-specific APIs (entry, Vacant), and
  NameTable needs an entry-like API. Mechanical, but broad.
- **Verification:** Small offsets only. phpstan-rs own_owner_names starts at
  registry/hierarchy.rs:186. The loop cited at hierarchy.rs:207
  (`for name in info.methods.keys()` with `if !method_owner.contains_key(name)`)
  sits in the BFS just above it, around lines 200-215.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Change the type of ClassReflection::methods
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:369) from FxHashMap\<Name,
>    FunctionReflection> to NameTable\<FunctionReflection>. Change
>    abstract_methods, final_methods and static_methods (lines 383-392) to a
>    case-folded set: NameTable<()>, or a small NameSet wrapper around it.
>    NameTable already has get / get_with_name / contains_key / insert /
>    insert_if_absent / get_or_insert_with / iter / keys
>    (registry/name_table.rs:66-140). The three `methods.entry(..)` sites in
>    registry/resolve.rs:257, 318 and 796 (trait flattening) can map onto
>    insert_if_absent / get_or_insert_with. If one of them needs the
>    Occupied/Vacant split, add a small entry-style helper. Keying by the folded
>    name also makes a trait's `Foo` and the class's own `foo` collide, which is
>    what PHP does.
> 2. Rebuild method_owner_by_class in registry/hierarchy.rs (own_owner_names at
>    :186-211, the ancestor merge, and precompute_member_owners) on
>    NameTable\<Name>. The BFS already inserts first-seen-wins, so the
>    most-derived declaration wins per folded name. Leave property_owner and
>    const_owner exact-case.
> 3. lookup_method (:377), lookup_method_with_owner (:462),
>    lookup_method_canonical_name (:398) and declared_method_name (:361) each
>    become one folded lookup. get_with_name returns the declared spelling.
>    Delete the eq_ignore_ascii_case scan fallbacks.
> 4. Rewrite find_case_mismatched_ancestor_method (:436) to keep
>    method.nameCase: take the child's own declared spelling, walk to the
>    nearest ancestor that declares the folded name (for example, look up the
>    parent's method_owner_by_class entry with get_with_name), and report when
>    the two spellings differ.
> 5. Remove the ad-hoc case-insensitive scans that only work around the
>    exact-case keys: checker/expr.rs:300-311 method_is_static,
>    checker/oop/method_overrides.rs:332-337, the final_methods check in
>    hierarchy.rs, registry/relation.rs, checker/static_call_context.rs and
>    checker/instantiation.rs. Grep for `eq_ignore_ascii_case` next to
>    methods/static_methods/final_methods/abstract_methods to find all of them.
> 6. Add regression fixtures from the probe: a child `DOSTUFF(): int` overriding
>    the parent's `doStuff(): int|string`, called as `$c->doStuff()`,
>    `$c->DoStuff()` and `C::make()`, must each infer `int`. The
>    static-over-static case with different casing must not report
>    method.static, and it should still report method.nameCase.

#### K44. Treat stub_paths as a validated, refine-only patch layer applied field by field after loading

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: codebase-model, stubs-prelude)
- **Benefit:** Makes the documented stub-override feature work. In probe t10
  (vendor Lib\Repo::find() with `@return mixed`, stub with `@return int`)
  phpstan-rs still reports `mixed` whether the stub sorts before or after the
  vendor file. The override is lost because of the union merge, so users cannot
  fix bad vendor types. Also gives clear diagnostics for stale stubs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1335`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/function_like.rs:342`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1251`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1305`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:522`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/settings.rs:16`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:2017`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:780`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:363`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:1860`
- **Risks:** Users may rely on today's accidental additive merge for new
  members. Keep adding members for class stubs, and only switch conflicting
  types from union to replace. | Changes the meaning of existing stub_paths
  overrides from merge to refine; overrides that intentionally added members
  would need @method/@property instead. Deciding what counts as 'specified'
  needs care for native-only versus PHPDoc-only redeclarations.
  CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md C6 already plans PHPStan stubFiles overlay semantics; this
  adds the validation and incremental behaviour on top.
- **Verification:** The Mago incremental path is
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs, not
  crates/orchestrator/src/incremental_analysis.rs. Its lines ~608-669 force a
  rescan of patch files when a vendor file changes, and fully rebuild when a
  patch file's content changes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Make stub_paths a separate refine-only patch layer. This is the user-stub part
> of the overlay layer that CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md already plans for C6 (lines
> 406-419, 2567+), and it can ship before C6. (1) In project/session.rs:363-372,
> keep stub_dirs apart from scan_dirs. Carry them as their own list, and tag
> every BuiltDecl from those files as a patch (a flag or an Origin variant) that
> registry/provenance.rs can report. (2) In registry/index.rs, insert_built_decl
> (the unconditional-redeclaration branch around line 182) stores patch decls in
> patch_classes, patch_functions and patch_consts maps. They no longer go
> through ClassReflection::merge (class_info.rs:2017) or
> FunctionReflection::merge (function_sig.rs:780). (3) A new apply_patches pass
> runs at the end of finish_loading and after update_file's re-index. For each
> patched method or function, the patch's PHPDoc return, param, @param-out,
> template, @throws and @phpstan-assert\* replace the target's fields. They are
> not unioned. A field the patch leaves out keeps the target's value, and a
> missing docblock never counts as "declares mixed". Native types are always
> kept from the target. For a patched class, the pass merges @template,
> @extends/@implements args, @mixin, @method and @property. It adds members the
> target lacks, which keeps today's additive behaviour, and replaces doc types
> on members that collide. (4) A patch with no target becomes the declaration,
> as PHPStan's stubFiles do for extension classes that are not installed. So by
> default it is NOT an error. An orphan warning is opt-in only. (5) Validation
> diagnostics are reported on the stub file: parameter count or name mismatch,
> class/interface/trait kind mismatch, and two patches for one symbol. They use
> their own identifiers and are always on, because each one means the patch is
> stale or ambiguous. A mismatched patch is still applied position by position
> rather than dropped, and the diagnostic says so. (6) FunctionReflection::merge
> stays for phpstorm-stubs overloads and conditional declarations.
> merge_stub_classes (index.rs:500-520) is unchanged. (7) In the LSP
> (lsp.rs:1860-1903), re-run apply_patches when a patch file or its target file
> changes, instead of asking for a window reload. Adding a new stub_paths root
> can still require a reload.

#### K46. Resolve @mixin as generic types through the hierarchy at lookup time

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Probe t5: for `/** @mixin Target */` where Target extends Base,
  \$m->inherited() is `mixed` in phpstan-rs and int in Mago. For
  `/** @mixin Box<int> */`, \$g->get() is `mixed` in phpstan-rs and int in Mago.
  Laravel, Eloquent and query-builder style code relies heavily on both
  patterns. It also stops mixin members from polluting the host's 'own' methods
  (for example in override checks).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:112`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:669`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:571`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:774`
- **Risks:** Lookup-time resolution adds a fallback path to hot member lookup,
  but only on a miss. Order matters when a mixin member conflicts with a magic
  `@method`: keep 'real/declared/@method first'.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:112
  `pub mixins: Vec<TypeMetadata>` is correct. populator/merge.rs:122 (parent
  mixins) and :196 (trait mixins) are correct.
  analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:669 is the mixin fallback branch
  (`else if !class_metadata.mixins.is_empty()`).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Replace the copy-in step with a mixin fallback at lookup time.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:571, change
>    `mixins: Vec<Name>` to store the parsed Type as well (FQN plus generic
>    args), e.g. `Vec<(Name, Vec<Type>)>`. Keep `mixins()` returning the names
>    for oop.rs:368 check_mixin_types.
> 2. Delete Registry::resolve_deferred_mixins (registry/resolve.rs:774) and its
>    three call sites (project.rs:767, project.rs:1040, registry.rs:298). Mixin
>    members should no longer land in the host's `methods`/`properties` or in
>    method_owner_by_class.
> 3. In registry/hierarchy.rs, add
>    `lookup_mixin_method(class, name) -> Option<(MixinHit { mixin_fqn,
>    mixin_args, owner }, &FunctionReflection)>`
>    and a property equivalent. Each walks the host's ancestor chain, collects
>    every `@mixin` (the mixin's own `@mixin`s too), and keeps a visited set.
>    For each mixin it calls the existing lookup_method_with_owner on the mixin
>    class, so inherited and trait members are found. Only public members count.
>    Call it only after lookup_method, lookup_method_with_owner or
>    lookup_property miss, so real members, `@method` and `@property` still win.
>    Leave the ancestor/override lookups (lookup_ancestor_method_with_owner, the
>    MethodPrototypeFinder port) mixin-free.
> 4. In the checker's method/property call resolution, where
>    class_template_bindings substitution happens, treat a mixin hit this way:
>    (a) bind the mixin class's templates from the stored `@mixin` args, then
>    run the usual owner-level substitution; (b) resolve `static`/`self`/`$this`
>    in the return type to the mixin type, not the receiver.
> 5. Optional follow-up, opt-in: report a host that has `@mixin` but no
>    `__call`/`__get` (Mago's mixin_without_magic_method). Add fixtures for: the
>    mixin's parent method, `@mixin Box<int>`, a `static` return, a subclass of
>    the host, a mixin's own mixin, and a real host method that overrides the
>    mixin method.

#### K47. Use @phpstan-require-extends/implements targets for member lookup

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Probe t3: `/** @phpstan-require-extends Base */ interface I` with
  `function f(I $i) { return $i->baseMethod(); }` gives a false positive 'call
  to undefined method I::baseMethod() (method.notFound)' in phpstan-rs. Mago is
  silent. Every implementor of I is guaranteed to extend Base, so the call is
  valid.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:646`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/property.rs:811`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:798`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:739`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:558`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1815`
- **Risks:** Must not leak into ancestor_names used by is_subclass_of for
  instanceof narrowing unless intended. Keep a separate table or flag.
- **Verification:** All the citations check out. Mago: in
  crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs, the else-branch at lines 646-665 goes
  through require_extends and require_implements when the class itself has no
  such method.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Put a fallback in the lookup layer, not in the precomputed owner maps. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs,
> `lookup_method`/`lookup_method_with_owner` (lines 377/462) and
> `lookup_property`/`lookup_property_with_owner` (lines 895/903) should first do
> the normal lookup. Only when that misses, and only when the class is an
> interface or a trait with non-empty `require_extends()`/`require_implements()`
> (class_info.rs:757/761), repeat the same lookup on each required target, in
> declaration order. This matches Mago's miss-only fallback (mago
> crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:646, resolver/property.rs:811). Leave
> `own_owner_names` and `precompute_member_owners` (hierarchy.rs:186-330) and
> the `ancestor_*_owner_by_class` maps unchanged. That way
> `find_method_signature_prototype`, override/prototype checks and the checks
> for unimplemented abstract or interface methods never see Base's members as
> belonging to I or T. Otherwise a class that breaks the requirement would also
> get phantom "must implement" findings. Constants can use the same fallback
> (`I::BASE_CONST`). Step 2 (the M part): in the subtype/accepts relation
> (registry/relation.rs:17 is_subclass_of / hierarchy.rs:22), count an
> interface's `require_extends`/`require_implements` targets as supertypes for
> argument/assignment/return acceptance. That gives I ⊆ Base, which fixes
> `k(Base $b)` called with an `I $i`. It is sound because oop.rs:1815-1833
> already reports every implementor that breaks the requirement. Keep this
> separate from `ancestor_names`, or check how instanceof narrowing and
> always-true/always-false reporting would react (`$i instanceof Base` becomes
> always-true, which is correct but new output). Fixtures: an interface receiver
> calling a Base method and reading a Base property, a standalone trait whose
> `$this` calls members of a required class or interface, the argument-passing
> case, and a negative case where a class that breaks the requirement gets only
> the existing requireExtends error.

#### K90. General ||-true / &&-false narrowing by merging per-disjunct states

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** A single sound rule covers every leaf phpstan-rs can narrow, in
  any mix: isset, empty, comparisons, count, array_key_exists, asserts,
  instanceof. It also removes about 90 lines of special-casing and matches Mago
  on the probed shapes.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:549`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:215`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:766`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:399`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:6267`
- **Risks:** merge_scopes iterates all locals, so long || chains in huge
  functions cost O(n·k); add the changed-keys fast path. Assignments inside
  conditions run twice (on separate clones), which is harmless because
  apply_narrowing is &self and does not report. Fixture churn is possible where
  the old helpers gave a specific ordering of union members.
- **Verification:** The citations are mostly accurate. There are two small
  corrections. (1) The or_chain_narrowing_target leaf list
  (predicates.rs:399-455) does accept `===` as well as `==`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs apply_narrowing, change the
> `Binary(Or|LogicalOr) if branch_true` arm (around line 766) to split the
> scope:
> `let mut la = locals.clone(); self.apply_narrowing(l, &mut la, true); let mut
> lb = locals.clone(); self.apply_narrowing(l, &mut lb, false);
> self.apply_narrowing(r, &mut lb, true); *locals = merge_scopes(&la, &lb);`.
> Do the same for the `Binary(And|LogicalAnd) if !branch_true` arm (around line
> 793): la takes l false; lb takes l true and then r false. Delete
> or_chain_narrowing_target and and_chain_narrowing_target
> (narrowing/predicates.rs:399-482) rather than keeping them as a fast path.
> Their `BinOp::Eq` leaf is unsound: I probed
> `function f(string $x){ if ($x == 0 || $x == 1) assertType(..., $x); }` and
> the current binary reports `0|1` for a `string` parameter. At runtime
> `"0.0" == 0` is true, so \$x can be "0.0" there. The split path sends every
> leaf through the single-condition arms, which deliberately refuse to narrow on
> `==`, so this also removes that unsoundness. For performance, add a cheap
> check to merge_scopes, or a narrowing-only wrapper next to it in
> control_flow.rs:563: when a key's two Types are equal, keep one without
> unioning (it already does this), and skip the side-map passes when both sides'
> maps are pointer-equal to the pre-split maps. Keep merge_scopes' intersection
> semantics. They are what keeps the result sound: a guard set such as
> function_exists survives only if both sides have it; a synthetic key that only
> one disjunct inserted is dropped, which means it falls back to its base type;
> condition aliases are compared with Rc::ptr_eq. Add fixtures for these cases:
> `$x===null||$x>5` gives int<6,max>|null; `!isset($o)||$o>3`; the else branch
> of `$x!==null&&$x!==''`; `$a===null||$b===null`, which must leave both \$a and
> \$b at their base types; `function_exists('a')||$y`, which must guard nothing;
> `string $x` with `$x==0||$x==1`, which must stay string; and the existing
> is_int||is_string and instanceof-chain cases, which must be unchanged.

#### K97. Pure method calls as narrowing keys

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Getter-heavy OOP code
  (`if ($o->getParent() !== null) $o->getParent()->...`) stops producing
  possibly-null false positives without asking users to extract variables.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:152`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:136`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/post_process.rs:484`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:64`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:356`
- **Risks:** Invalidating on impure calls must be complete: callbacks,
  \_\_destruct and by-ref arguments. If purity is under-approximated this is
  unsound, so keep it opt-in behind rememberPossiblyImpureFunctionValues-like
  config or require declared purity only.
- **Verification:** All citations are essentially accurate. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:152-162 computes
  method_call_is_stable (no arguments, every target a method with is_pure() or
  is_mutation_free(), and not suspends_fiber).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a Checker-level
> `method_call_narrowing_key(&self, e, locals) -> Option<String>` next to
> `narrowing_key` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:64). It
> returns `"{recv_key}->{name}()"` only for
> `MethodCall(recv, name, [], Arrow|NullsafeArrow)` where `narrowing_key(recv)`
> is Some, the method resolves through `registry.lookup_method_with_owner`, and
> either (a) `sig.is_transitively_pure()`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:356) or (b) the method's own
> docblock carries `@phpstan-pure`/`@psalm-pure`/`@psalm-mutation-free`. Case
> (b) uses the `pure` field that is already parsed but not consumed
> (crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:100-105), and it is the only purity source for
> bodyless interface/abstract getters. Use it in three places: in
> `apply_narrowing`'s null/instanceof/type-predicate paths wherever
> `narrowing_key` is consulted now, and in the MethodCall arms of
> check_expr/infer_expr (checker/expr.rs), behind the existing
> `Locals::may_have_member_narrowing()` fast path (checker/locals.rs:108). Most
> invalidation comes free. The key is prefixed by the receiver key, so
> `key_depends_on` (predicates.rs:308) already purges it when the receiver is
> rebound, and `forget_members_a_call_may_change` (checker/expr.rs:190-300)
> already purges the receiver's and object arguments' dependent keys after any
> call whose `PropertyWrites` is not `Nothing`. Two things need adding. (1) Any
> write to `R->prop` (assignment, compound assign, by-ref binding, unset) must
> purge every `R->*()` key, not only `R->prop*`. (2) As Mago does
> (analyzer/src/invocation/post_process.rs:484), a call whose `PropertyWrites`
> is `Anything` must drop every `()` key in scope, not just the receiver's and
> arguments'. Cheap extension: allow literal-only args by encoding them in the
> key. Fixtures: the narrowed getter; purge after a setter; purge after a
> property write on the receiver; purge after an unknown or `Anything` call; no
> narrowing for an unproven-pure method; nullsafe chains.

#### K108. Gate loop_depth suppression on loop convergence

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Restores real diagnostics inside loops, where much of the logic
  lives. Probe cf/h: `$x = new Foo(); foreach (...) { echo $x?->bar(); }` and a
  redundant `$s ?? 'd'` inside the loop are silent in phpstan-rs but reported
  outside loops, and Mago reports the `??` case inside the loop.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:444`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:1136`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:642`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/probe_checks.rs:139`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1183`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:368`
- **Risks:** Each guard needs individual verification against loop idioms (for
  example `$err ??= $e` in catch-in-loop, which the fixed point already handles
  because pass 2 sees the widened type). Widening at pass 2 or later can produce
  states wider than reality but never narrower, so moving to converged-only
  gating should not add false 'always' verdicts.
- **Verification:** Most citations check out; the corrections are below. - The
  "17 guards" count is wrong. grep finds 14 reads of loop_depth outside the
  increment and decrement sites: - probe_checks.rs:139, :191, :357, :438, :513 -
  expr.rs:1183, :2928, :3312 - comparisons.rs:34 - stmt/loops.rs:561
  (DeadForeachRule, "Em ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Scope: only the guards that suppress diagnostics. Leave alone the guards that
> change type computation.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs `converge_loop_body`
>    (MAX_PASSES=6, WIDEN_FROM_PASS=2, lines 328-431), the pass that ends up
>    kept has run by the time we know whether it was a fixed point. So make the
>    decision before the pass runs: if `pass == MAX_PASSES - 1`, meaning the
>    pass is forced to be the last, increment a new
>    `Checker::unconverged_loop_depth: u32` before `run_pass` and decrement it
>    afterwards. Earlier passes are rewound with `rewind_to(mark)`, so their
>    diagnostics never survive. When the kept pass ends with
>    `next_entry == pass_entry`, it was checked against a real fixed point, and
>    the counter stayed 0 for it. Nested loops inherit this: a check inside an
>    inner loop that runs within a forced outer pass sees a counter above 0.
>
> 2. Replace `loop_depth` with `unconverged_loop_depth` in the guards that only
>    suppress a report:
>    - checker/expr/probe_checks.rs:139 (check_pointless_null_probe), :191
>      (resolve_always_exists), :357 (check_constant_loose_comparison), :438
>      (check_strict_comparison_of_different_types), :513
>      (check_constant_numeric_comparison)
>    - checker/expr.rs:1183 (nullsafe method call) and :2928 (nullsafe property
>      fetch)
>    - checker/expr.rs:3312 (match arm always-true/false)
>    - checker/comparisons.rs:34 (in_array/array_search/array_keys impossible
>      haystack)
>    - checker/stmt/loops.rs:561 (Empty array passed to foreach, nested-loop
>      case)
>    - the do-while trailing condition check at stmt/loops.rs:263-282: move it
>      under the new counter and rewrite its comment, because widening now makes
>      `$attempts` open-ended.
> 3. Keep these guards as they are:
>    - `static_var_names` and `expr_reads_a_property`: they cover state carried
>      between calls and aliasing through properties, which convergence does not
>      model.
>    - The `self.loop_depth == 0` arguments at
>      checker/assignment.rs:466/512/531/546: they feed `set_offset_value_type`,
>      which is the transfer function itself, not a diagnostic gate. Keep
>      `loop_depth` for those callers.
> 4. Rewrite the field comment at checker.rs:643-650 and the justification at
>    probe_checks.rs:131-138. Both still say "single, non-iterated pass"; say
>    instead that inside a converged loop the checked state is the fixed point.
>
> 5. Tests go in the checker's loop test module:
>    - positive: `$x = new Foo(); foreach(..){ $x?->bar(); }`, `$s ?? 'd'`,
>      `$n=5; if($n>10)` inside a loop
>    - negative: `$err ??= $e` in catch-in-loop;
>      `$first = true; ... $first = false`; a do-while counter `< 150`;
>      `$prev = null; foreach { if ($prev !== null) ..; $prev = $i; }`;
>      `$seen[] = ...; in_array($x, $seen)`
>    - a case built to hit MAX_PASSES, which must stay silent. Then run the full
>      suite plus a corpus regression diff.

#### K110. extract()/eval()/include: flow-sensitive 'any variable may exist' instead of discarding the body's diagnostics

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope, linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Functions that call extract() or eval() currently get zero
  diagnostics of any kind (type errors, unknown methods and so on are all
  dropped). After this change only undefined-variable reads after the call are
  relaxed. It also removes a non-ignorable false positive on valid
  `$$name = ...` code and resolves `$$name` definitions such as
  `$name = 'foo'; $$name = 5; echo $foo;`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/variable.rs:164`,
  `crates/linter/src/lib.rs:160`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/deprecation/deprecated_shell_execute_string.rs:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1660`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:471`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:707`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:45`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:350`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:1193`
- **Risks:** Code before the extract() call on the same path keeps full
  undefined-variable checking, which is correct. Some previously hidden
  diagnostics in extract-heavy templates will appear; they are real ones. | Some
  type-derived diagnostics after extract() may be noise because variables may
  hold unknown types. Keep the discard for anything reading a
  possibly-overwritten local, or mark every local as maybe-defined mixed after
  extract() (PHPStan's approach) instead of discarding.
- **Verification:** The flag is declared at checker.rs:355, not :350. The
  top-level truncation is at checker.rs:1660-1664 and also clears
  property_type_sites. The per-function truncation is at
  function_decl.rs:1193-1196; the flag is saved and reset at :900-901.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Delete Checker::saw_dynamic_var_construct
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:349-355, init at :1023, truncation at
>    :1660-1664; function_decl.rs:900-901 and :1193-1196; the set at
>    expr.rs:471-475 and :1865). Also update the comments that refer to it
>    (control_flow.rs:281, unused/var_usage.rs:29-31).
> 2. Put the extract/eval/include effect into Locals as a flow-sensitive
>    "havoc". Use one helper, e.g. Checker::havoc_locals(locals), called from
>    the extract arm (expr.rs:476-482, which already matches `\extract` and
>    `EXTRACT`), from ExprKind::Eval (:1863) and from ExprKind::Include (:1878).
>    It sets any_variable_may_exist, and it must also widen every existing
>    non-superglobal local to mixed, or to the union of its current type with
>    mixed. Keep `$this` and by-ref and static bindings intact. Without the
>    widening, `$x = 1; extract($a); $x->foo();` becomes a new false positive
>    once the discard goes away. extract() with a constant EXTR_SKIP flag or a
>    constant-array argument can be done precisely later; it is optional.
> 3. The ExprKind::Variable read (expr.rs:1656-1664), the closure-use check and
>    the isset/?? variable checks should skip variable.undefined when
>    locals.any_variable_may_exist(), or downgrade to a maybe-defined level if
>    that exists. Read the missing name as mixed. The flag already merges across
>    branches (control_flow.rs:565).
> 4. Add ExprKind::DynamicVariable to the assignable arm of
>    is_non_assignable_target (assignment.rs:45-53). In bind_assignment_target,
>    a constant-string name (or union of them) declares those locals; any other
>    name calls set_any_variable_may_exist(true).
> 5. The unused-parameter walk (unused/var_usage.rs) must now treat extract/eval
>    as VarUsage::Escaped, as it already does for include. Otherwise, dropping
>    the truncation exposes unused-parameter false positives in extract-using
>    functions. Optional follow-up: move the purely syntactic deprecation checks
>    (backtick, (integer) casts) into a scope-independent per-file pass like
>    project/banned.rs.

#### K115. Preserve array keys and shapes through array_\* functions

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Removes confirmed false positives (offsetAccess.notFound after
  array_combine; argument.type on foreach keys from
  array_map/array_combine/array_slice) and gives exact shapes through common
  data-reshaping chains.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_map.rs:113`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_map.rs:224`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:3887`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/spl.php:2161`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/transform.rs:290`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:468`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:1269`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:783`
- **Risks:** Anything that relied on the looser types may start reporting (for
  example, a now-known sealed shape reports missing offsets). Give per-field
  closure inference a field-count cap, like MAX_SHAPE_FIELDS, to bound cost.
- **Verification:** Mago: the keyed-shape branch of array_map is at
  crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_map.rs:117-130 (the
  match starts at 116). zip_input_arrays is defined at line 246 and called at
  line 74. Line 224 is substitute_parameter_in_union.
- **Refined proposal:**

> This builds on helpers the codebase already has. It should not add a new
> transform.
>
> (a) array_map with one array
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:374-387). Replace
> `input_ty.with_array_value(mapped)` with
> `input_ty.map_array_values(&mut |_| mapped.clone())`, using the existing
> helper at crates/types/src/transform.rs:191. That helper already keeps the key
> K, shape keys, optionality, the unsealed tail and accessories, member by
> member. It is already used in checker/doctrine/result_shape.rs:562. Per-field
> closure inference (calling infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides once per
> shape field) is an optional second step: add it only for sealed shapes under a
> field cap, and fall back to the single union-mapped value otherwise.
>
> (b) array_slice and array_reverse without preserve_keys
> (builtin_calls.rs:482-497). A list stays a list. For a non-list, the key
> becomes `(K ∩ string) | int<0,max>`. For a constant shape, rebuild the shape:
> string keys stay and int keys renumber in order (array_reverse reverses the
> order first). php -r confirms string keys survive:
> array_slice(["a"=>1,5=>2,"b"=>3],0) gives a, 0, b.
>
> (c) array_combine (builtin_calls.rs:468-476, where the comment is stale). Key
> = the value type of \$keys converted to a key; value = the value type of
> \$values. The key conversion is NOT plain `Type::to_array_key()`
> (types/src/coercion.rs:192), because array_combine converts float keys through
> strings: php -r gives array_combine([1.0, 2.7], ...) keys 1 and "2.7", not 2.
> So floats must go through to_string first and then canonical-int
> normalization. The other types can use to_array_key: true becomes 1, null
> becomes "", and "3" becomes 3. When both arguments are sealed constant shapes
> of equal size, build the exact shape. Keep non-empty only if \$keys is
> non-empty. This fixes the false positive from the probe,
> `Offset 'a' does not exist on array{0: 1, 1: 2}`.
>
> (d) array_column (builtin_calls.rs:1269). Resolve the column separately for
> each union_members() entry of the row type, with an optional field when the
> field is optional. In the 3-argument form, the key is the index column's type
> through to_array_key (int|string when index_key is null). Do the same
> float-to-string check against runtime first.
>
> (e) array_pad (builtin_calls.rs:783) keeps list-ness when the input is a list.
> iterator_to_array gets a handler: Traversable\<K,V> gives array\<K,V> when
> preserve_keys is absent or true, and list\<V> when it is false. Its only
> current use is the strict-rules check at checker/expr.rs:808.
>
> (f) array_map(null, \$a, \$b) zips into a list of 2-element shapes whose
> members are nullable. array_map(null, \$a) returns \$a unchanged.
>
> Add fixture tests for each case, including the combine float-key case and a
> foreach over string keys.

#### K117. array_filter modes and callback-derived narrowing

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Sound results for key and both-mode filtering, and precise
