  results for any predicate the narrowing engine understands (`$x !== ''`,
  `$x instanceof A && $x->ok()`, `is_numeric`, `!empty(...)`) without adding a
  new matcher per shape.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_filter.rs:74`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:1987`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:403`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:600`
- **Risks:** Running apply_narrowing on a callback body needs a clean scratch
  scope (closure_scope() plus the bound parameters) so outer narrowing doesn't
  leak. Multi-statement closures should still fall back.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate, with some nuances. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_filter.rs:73-86 reads
  the callback's `if_true_assertions` (line 74 is the is_empty check that
  returns None), takes the FIRST parameter's assertions (78-80) and narrows each
  value, returning ` ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, in the "array_filter"
> arm (around line 396):
>
> 1. Work out the mode from args[2]: absent means USE_VALUE;
>    contains_flag_name(…, "ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY") or "ARRAY_FILTER_USE_BOTH"
>    (builtin_calls.rs:2475) set the other two. If the mode is non-literal or
>    unknown, return `stripped` with no narrowing. This alone removes the
>    current unsound value narrowing: my probe of array_filter(\$a, fn(\$k) =>
>    is_string(\$k), ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY) returns array\<string> for
>    array\<string|int, int|string|null>.
> 2. Replace is_null_filter_callback, is_instanceof_filter_callback and
>    is_type_check_filter_callback (2236-2360) with one helper,
>    `derive_filter_narrowing(callback, mode, K, V, locals) -> Option<(Type
>    /*true-branch*/, Type /*false-branch*/)>`
>    per bound parameter. For an ArrowFn, or a Closure whose body is a single
>    `return e`, build the scope the same way
>    infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides already does (expr.rs:4983: arrow
>    = locals.clone(), closure = closure_scope() + uses + \$this). Bind the
>    parameters by mode: [V], [K] or [V, K]. Then run
>    Checker::apply_narrowing(e, &mut scratch, true) (narrowing.rs:620) and read
>    the parameters back. Keep the string-callable or first-class-callable
>    `is_*` form as a thin adapter that makes a synthetic predicate, or keep
>    that one matcher. Fall back (no narrowing) when any of these holds: a
>    parameter is by-ref or variadic; the parameter count does not match the
>    mode; a parameter has a native type hint that is not a supertype of the
>    bound type (coercion under non-strict_types changes what gets narrowed); or
>    the body assigns to or unsets a bound parameter (e.g. fn(\$v) => (\$v =
>    trim(\$v)) !== '', where the narrowed \$v is no longer the element).
> 3. Result: the value's true-branch type replaces V (USE_VALUE and USE_BOTH).
>    The key's true-branch type intersects K (USE_KEY and USE_BOTH). For
>    constant shapes, go per field through filter_array_values
>    (types/src/transform.rs:220). Drop a field whose true-branch type is never.
>    Also narrow with branch_true=false, and make a field optional only when
>    that false branch is not never. That keeps `b: string` required under
>    `$v !== null`, which the current code already gets right (probe: array{a?:
>    int, b: string}). Making every field optional, as first proposed, would
>    regress this. For USE_KEY on shapes, test each literal key against the key
>    narrowing.
> 4. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:600, extend
>    contextual_callback_override for "array_filter" to 3 arguments with a
>    literal mode: slot 1 gets [V], [K] or [V, K]. The closure's \$k/\$v then
>    stop being mixed in key and both modes.

#### K118. Type the pipe operator as a call of its right-hand callable

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** PHP 8.5 pipe chains are typed end to end and checked. Without
  this, all code written in pipe style loses its types (an early-adopter cliff).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/pipe.rs:33`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:1104`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5434`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/pipe_operator.rs:19`
- **Risks:** Low. The fallback stays mixed when the callable can't be resolved.
- **Verification:** Mago: the analyze_invocation_targets call with
  InvocationArgumentsSource::PipeInput(self) spans
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/pipe.rs:34-46; the PipeInput argument is
  on line 39, and resolve_targets is on line 31.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the pipe-as-call logic to crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/pipe_operator.rs
> and share one resolver between the existing pipe.byRef check and the new code.
>
> (1) Write `pipe_target(&self, rhs, locals) -> Option<PipeTarget>`. It does
> what `pipe_target_first_param_is_by_ref` (pipe_operator.rs:39) already does:
> `infer_expr(rhs)`, then either `ty.callable_sig()` or
> `named_callable_signature` (callable_values.rs:28). It returns either the
> named `&FunctionReflection` or the structural callable sig. `pipe.byRef` is
> then rebuilt on top of it.
>
> (2) Inference, at the `BinOp::Pipe => Type::mixed()` arm in expr.rs:5434:
>
> - If rhs is a parenthesized ArrowFn or Closure, call
>   `infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides(rhs, &[infer_expr(lhs)], locals)`
>   (expr.rs:4983). Mago misses this case: its probe gives mixed-operand for
>   `$s |> (fn($v) => $v . 'a')`.
> - Else, for a named FunctionReflection, call
>   `infer_call_return_type(sig, &[Some(lhs)], locals)` (expr/array_ops.rs:455).
>   It takes `&[Option<&Expr>]`, so the real lhs expression is passed directly
>   and no synthetic Arg is needed. Template binding and conditional returns
>   come for free.
> - Else, for a structural callable sig (Closure<...>/callable(...)), use its
>   declared return type.
> - Otherwise fall back to mixed.
>
> (3) Checks, in the check_expr Binary arm at expr.rs:1646 next to
> `check_pipe_byref`:
>
> - Check the lhs type against param #1 using the same acceptance and coercion
>   logic as a normal call (strict_types aware; Mago flags `5 |> strlen(...)`
>   even in coercive mode, and that should not be copied).
> - Add a pipe arity check: the target has more than one required parameter, or
>   it has zero parameters and is not variadic. Use pipe-specific wording.
>
> (4) Leave the throw-type entry at expr.rs:384
> (`BinOp::Pipe => Some(anything())`) alone, or refine it later from the
> target's @throws.
>
> Add fixtures for chained first-class callables, a templated function such as
> `[1,2] |> array_first(...)` or a user @template function, a parenthesized
> arrow fn, a string callable 'strtoupper', an invokable object, and an
> unresolvable rhs that stays mixed.

#### K225. Never analyze vendor as first-party or load a file twice

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** `check-project .` at a project root, the most natural invocation,
  currently reports every vendor bug as the user's own (probe:
  vendor/foo/bar/src/B.php return.type reported). It also doubles parse time and
  memory for vendor, and duplicate same-file declarations can trip
  duplicate-class logic and make results depend on order.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/lib.rs:243`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:172`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:594`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:623`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:599`
- **Risks:** Some users do want to analyze a vendored package in place. Resolve
  that with Mago's specificity rule: an explicit path deeper than the vendor
  root wins.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small line
  offsets. Mago: crates/orchestrator/src/lib.rs:242-245 shows
  `if !include_externals {
  excludes.extend(create_excludes_from_patterns(&include_strs, workspace)) }`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> I could not refute this. It is a real CLI defect, and the fix fits inside
> Session::load in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs.
>
> (1) Collect analysed files with a vendor-aware walk.
> Session::collect_php_files (session.rs:553) calls super::collect_php_files,
> which is collect_php_files_excluding with no excluded names (project.rs:2084).
> Instead, prune any directory that equals a discovered composer root's vendor
> dir, taken from the manifest's config.vendor-dir, not a bare "vendor" name
> match. Skip the pruning when the user gave a path at or below that vendor dir.
> That is Mago's specificity rule, so `check-project vendor/foo/bar` still
> analyses in place. A cheap fallback is to reuse
> DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES (project.rs:2093) for `.git` and
> `node_modules`, which the LSP and Project::update_file (project.rs:1000)
> already apply. The CLI would then classify files the same way the editor does.
>
> (2) Before `analyze_files.sort()` at session.rs:599 and before
> `combined_files` at session.rs:623, key every path by fs::canonicalize,
> falling back to lexical normalisation, the way lsp.rs:496/527 do. Keep the
> first spelling seen. A file in both lists becomes analysed only when an
> explicit path reached it under the specificity rule, and otherwise stays
> context only. Never parse or insert it twice.
>
> (3) Add "N vendor file(s) skipped (pass the vendor path explicitly to
> analyse)" to the summary line.
>
> (4) Optionally add a general excludePaths/`paths` config field alongside this,
> since the config crate has none today. The composer-vendor rule should still
> be the default either way.
>
> Tests: a fixture/session test where `check-project .` with vendor/ reports
> nothing from vendor, one where `check-project vendor/foo/bar` does report, and
> one where `check-project src src/A.php ./src` reports 1 file checked.

#### K243. Inherit asserts/throws/param-out/self-out docblocks

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Probe p1: `if ($impl->isValid($v))` narrows nothing because the
  interface's @phpstan-assert-if-true is lost. Probe p2: a redeclared
  `protected $items = []` loses `list<int>`, `public string $name` loses
  non-empty-string, and @param-out leaves \$z mixed. Fixing these removes false
  positives and restores narrowing in any interface/abstract-base codebase.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:412`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:569`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:340`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:980`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:336`
- **Risks:** An assert inherited by position must remap parameter names when the
  child renames params. Throws inheritance interacts with throws.notCovariant
  (method_overrides.rs:92). Keep the existing private/constructor carve-outs.
- **Verification:** The citations check out. Mago
  crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:412 has should_inherit_thrown (set when
  the child's thrown_types is empty). Lines 422-427 have
  should_inherit_assertions, should_inherit_if_true_assertions and
  should_inherit_if_false_assertions;
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Methods, in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs
>    flatten_phpdoc_inheritance_one_pass (Backfill tuple at :968, slot gates at
>    :980-981). Add these slots, each filled only when the child has none of its
>    own, and each run through the same ancestor_bindings /
>    template_param_scopes_all_safe_to_backfill substitution already used for
>    params and return:
>    - assert, assert_if_true and assert_if_false (FunctionReflection fields at
>      function_sig.rs:207-209). AssertTarget::Param(name)
>      (function_sig/asserts.rs:24-26) is remapped to the child's parameter at
>      the same position, or by name for \_\_construct, as the existing param
>      fill does. An assert whose ancestor parameter has no counterpart is
>      dropped, never turned into a NotFound target. ThisSelf and ThisProp are
>      copied as-is.
>    - throws (function_sig.rs:202).
>    - per-param out_ty (:79). Only when the child parameter is by_ref.
>    - self_out (:166). Keep the existing private-ancestor and
>      built-in-constructor carve-outs (:990-1016).
> 2. Provenance: add an inherited bit, e.g. throws_inherited /
>    asserts_inherited, next to has_own_doc and return_has_own_doc.
>    Declaration-site rules skip inherited tags: too_wide / throws.unusedType
>    (checker/throws/too_wide.rs:35-38 already notes this bit is missing),
>    assert validity and parameter.notFound checks, and param-out checks.
>    Call-site consumers (checker/throws.rs:117, narrowing, by-ref out handling)
>    read the merged values. method_overrides.rs:112 then naturally sees the
>    parent's throws instead of the implicit Throwable fallback. That is correct
>    and removes a spurious covariance comparison.
> 3. Properties: add a pass beside inherit_property_hooks (resolve.rs:372). When
>    a redeclared property has no own @var, it copies the doc type from
>    lookup_ancestor_property_with_owner (hierarchy.rs:687), substituted by the
>    class's ancestor bindings and reconciled against the child's native type
>    (drop it if incompatible, like safe_to_backfill_mixed). A private ancestor
>    property is never used. Update the 'methods only, no properties' doc
>    comment at resolve.rs:341-344. Its current premise ignores parent-class
>    property redeclaration, which is the real path.
> 4. Fixtures: an interface assert with a renamed child parameter, an
>    abstract-base property redeclared untyped and native-typed, @param-out, and
>    a @throws implementation that throws nothing (it must not produce
>    throws.unusedType on the child).

#### K268. Type-resolved member references for private-member check

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Removes a real class of false positives: private members reached
  through factory results, phpdoc-typed parameters, typed properties, nullable
  self parameters and return values, which the syntactic walk misses. Also stops
  one unrelated dynamic access from disabling the check for a whole class.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:482`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:59`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused/member_usage.rs:79`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused/member_usage.rs:215`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1226`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1641`
- **Risks:** The accumulator must stay scoped per class, with nested anonymous
  classes and closures bound elsewhere kept out. Typed references depend on
  inference quality: a mixed receiver adds no reference, so the syntactic set
  must remain as a fallback so no existing true use is lost.
- **Verification:** No material errors. Mago's add_reference_for_method_call is
  at crates/codex/src/reference.rs:482, with property read and write at about
  491-515.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs, add a per-class
> `private_member_uses: RefCell<FxHashSet<(MemberKind, Name /*lowercased for
> methods*/, Access{Read,Write})>>`
> plus `private_member_escape: Cell<bool>` and
> `current_private_scan_class: Option<String>`. Set the class name before the
> `for m in &c.def.methods { self.check_function(..) }` loop at checker.rs ~1628
> and clear it after `check_unused_private_members`. Inside `record_member_ref`
> (checker.rs:1226), before the `collect_member_refs` gate, also insert into the
> per-class set when `owner` equals the current class (canonical,
> case-insensitive) and the current function's class context is that class, so
> anonymous classes and nested class-likes are kept out. Add a read/write flag
> at the property-assign call sites in checker/expr.rs. In the
> DynamicPropertyAccess and DynamicMethodCall arms (expr.rs ~3088-3150, plus
> DynamicStaticCall), stop gating the escape on `collect_member_refs`. Compute a
> cheap local test instead: the receiver is mixed, or `object_class_names()`
> contains the current class or one of its ancestors or descendants. If so, set
> `private_member_escape`. This avoids the full registry scan in
> `escape_targets_for_receiver_type`, which the private check does not need
> because privates are only reachable from the class's own bodies. In
> checker/unused.rs `check_unused_private_members` (line 138), union the typed
> set into the syntactic `MemberUsage`. Keep the syntactic walk as a fallback:
> it covers property, const and param defaults and hooks, which check_function
> does not type-check, and array callables on non-\$this receivers. Drop the
> blanket `usage.escaped` from Dynamic\* in member_usage.rs:215 in favour of the
> typed escape flag. Keep the syntactic escaped flag only for dynamic accesses
> that appear in the walked-but-not-type-checked regions (defaults and hooks).
> Add fixtures: factory-returned self, phpdoc-typed param, `?self` nullsafe, a
> typed property holding self, stdClass dynamic access not hiding a dead
> private, and a mixed-receiver dynamic access still escaping.

#### K124. Precise builtin signatures from generated functionMap overlay

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Hundreds of builtin return types improve at once (list\<string>,
  non-empty-string, int<0,max>, etc.) without per-function Rust code. The
  overlay can also be precomputed at build time, which aligns with the known
  startup cost of parsing stubs at runtime.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:1337`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:3887`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/spl.php:2161`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:75`,
  `vendor/phpstan-src/resources/functionMap_php82delta.php:26`
- **Risks:** The functionMap syntax has quirks (the `=` optional marker,
  `&rw_`/`&w_` by-ref prefixes, multiple variants such as 'fn\'1'). Only take
  entries that parse and are strictly narrower, so the overlay can never widen
  or break a parameter; corpus-diff the change.
- **Verification:** All Mago citations check out. At standard.php:1337-1344,
  str_split has `@param int<1, max> $length` and `@return list<string>`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> The gap is real and not already covered somewhere else.
> crates/stub-sources/build.rs:69,98 embeds only vendor/phpstan-src/src and
> vendor/phpstan-src/stubs, never resources/functionMap\*.php.
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs uses the map only through hand-copied
> patches (patch_usleep, patch_printf_values, and patch_functionmap_array_shapes
> at ~254 with about 15 shapes). I ran a probe in scratchpad/probes/fmap using
> check-project. It gives str_split(\$s) = `array` (the functionMap says
> `non-empty-list<string>|false`, and the 8.2 delta says `list<string>`),
> mb_str_split = `array`, array_combine = `array`, and iterator_to_array(\$it) =
> `array` even though the phpstorm-stubs docblock already has a conditional
> return (SPL_f.php:152).
>
> About 647 entries in functionMap.php have a refined return (`<`, non-empty,
> positive, list and so on). So this change lifts a large part of the builtin
> surface at once, where today each function needs its own Rust code in
> checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs.
>
> Refined plan: (1) In stub-sources, embed functionMap.php and each
> functionMap_php8\*delta.php as text. Do not parse them in build.rs. Parse them
> lazily in registry/stubs.rs with the existing syntax crate, inside the same
> LazyLock that already builds the stubs. This avoids a build-dependency cycle
> on the parser, and parsing one array literal costs little next to the ~2351
> stub files already parsed. (2) Apply the deltas in order up to the newest PHP
> version: each delta's 'new' section replaces the base entry, and names in
> 'old' are removed. This matches how the file comments say
> patch_functionmap_array_shapes already takes the newest revision. (3) First
> pass, return types only. Replace the stub's return type only when
> is_super_type_of(stub, overlay).yes() and the overlay is not a supertype of
> the stub. Skip any entry the type-string parser rejects, including
> `__benevolent<...>` for now (scandir, date_sun_info), so that nothing can get
> wider. (4) Parameter types go in a separate, later pass. Match parameters by
> position. Always keep phpstorm-stubs' parameter names, by-ref flags and
> optional/variadic flags, because functionMap uses older names ('str' where PHP
> 8 uses 'string'), and taking them would break named-argument checking. Only
> take a narrower type when the arity and variadic shape match exactly and the
> entry has no `'fn\'1'` variant. Corpus-diff the new argument.type findings for
> types like positive-int or int-mask<...> before turning them on. (5) Keep
> phpstan-src/stubs/\*.stub and the existing dynamic handlers in
> builtin_calls.rs as the higher priority. Remove the transcribed shapes in
> patch_functionmap_array_shapes that the overlay now produces identically. (6)
> Add a small checked-in overlay .stub file in stub-sources for generic
> signatures that neither source has: array_combine as template K of array-key,
> V, and iterator_to_array keys/values. Separately, find out why phpstorm-stubs'
> own TKey/TValue conditional on iterator_to_array does not resolve. That fix
> may help other functions too.

#### K28. Resolve and fold use-site targets; record function references under both fallback candidates

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Probe names-symbols/d1 with --set rules.check_dead_code=true
  gives three confirmed false positives. The used `global_helper()` is called
  unqualified from `namespace App`, `\OTHER_HELPER()` is called in a different
  case, and `new \widget()` references `Widget`. All three are reported as never
  referenced. LSP references and rename miss the same sites, so a rename
  silently leaves stale call sites.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/names/src/lib.rs:112`,
  `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:493`, `crates/analyzer/src/context/mod.rs:163`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:44`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:177`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:107`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_code.rs:50`
- **Risks:** Recording both fallback candidates could keep a same-named
  namespaced function alive when only the global one is used. Choosing via the
  registry avoids that. Rename must still rewrite the original written span,
  which is unaffected because only the key changes.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small
  corrections. (1) Mago crates/codex/src/reference.rs:493 is inside
  add_reference_for_property_read (ascii_lowercase_word on the class name,
  around lines 491-495).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Fold only the class and function halves of RefTarget, and resolve the function
> fallback at query time rather than while indexing.
>
> (1) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs, change `RefTarget::Class`
> and `RefTarget::Function` to carry `registry::name_table::Folded`, or a String
> built with `folded_key`/`function_key` from registry/name_table.rs:12-22. Then
> every index key and every query compares case-insensitively. The key changes
> but the recorded span does not, so rename still rewrites the text exactly as
> written.
>
> (2) Leave `RefTarget::Member` as it is. The checker already records the
> canonical owner and method name: probed `public function Run()` called as
> `->run()` is not reported. Property, constant and enum-case names are
> case-sensitive in PHP, so folding them would be wrong.
>
> (3) In `ClassFnRefWalker::function_at` (use_sites.rs:177), keep the fallback.
> When `name.candidates()` returns `(primary, Some(global))`, record the site
> under the primary key and also add it to a secondary
> `fallback_sites: FxHashMap<FoldedGlobal, Vec<(PathBuf, Span, FoldedPrimary)>>`
> in `UseSiteIndex`. `remove_file` must undo that map as well.
>
> (4) Add `UseSiteIndex::function_references(&self, registry, fqn)`. It returns
> the sites keyed exactly on `fqn`, plus the fallback sites for `fqn` whose
> recorded primary the current registry does not declare
> (`registry.functions.get(primary).is_none()`). This mirrors Mago's
> resolve_function_name (analyzer/src/context/mod.rs:163), but it stays correct
> under incremental `Project::update_file`: adding or removing `App\foo` later
> changes the answer without re-indexing, and a namespaced function that shadows
> a global one never keeps the global one alive by mistake.
>
> (5) Switch the function queries to it: dead_code.rs:50-60, lsp.rs:1262/1360
> (references/rename) and composer_hygiene.rs:308. The class queries at
> dead_code.rs:75, lsp.rs:1260/1353, composer_hygiene.rs:296 and
> architecture.rs:354 only need the folded key.
>
> Add regression tests to project/tests/use_site_index.rs:
>
> - an unqualified call from a namespace to a global function
> - a differently-cased `\FOO()` call
> - `new \widget` for class `Widget`
> - a namespaced function that shadows the global one, where only the namespaced
>   one should count

#### K62. Integer set difference in Type::without

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Fixes verified false positives (argument.type after `!== N`
  guards on ranges and ints) and makes non-zero, boundary-trimmed and
  hole-punched ranges available to later checks: division by zero, array
  offsets, comparisons. The operation is cheap and already memoized through
  Operation::Without.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:472`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/negated_assertion_reconciler.rs:371`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/simple_negated_assertion_reconciler.rs:779`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:299`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:6412`
- **Risks:** Interior splits can grow unions inside loops, which the existing
  widening and MAX_UNION_MEMBERS cap should absorb; check loop fixpoint
  convergence on the fixture suite. Only apply the rule for strict `!==` (the
  caller already restricts this), never for loose `!=` against non-int operands.
- **Verification:** Mago: TInteger::difference is at
  crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:472 as cited. It handles a Literal
  subtracted from Unspecified, Literal, Range, From and To, splitting ranges in
  the interior, and a Range subtracted when conservative_subtraction is false.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/types/src/narrowing.rs, before the final `_ => self.clone()` arm of
> without_uncached (line ~299), add arms for `Repr::Int` and
> `Repr::IntRange(min, max)`: (a) when `excluded` is `IntLiteral(n)`, return the
> set difference as at most two intervals; (b) when `excluded` is
> `IntRange(bmin, bmax)`, likewise; (c) when `excluded` is a Union whose members
> are all int literals or ranges, fold `without` over those members. An excluded
> union means "none of these values", so the fold is sound. It covers the false
> branch of strict in_array.
>
> Generalize the existing `without_zero(min, max)` helper (narrowing.rs:595)
> into
> `int_interval_difference(min: Option<i64>, max: Option<i64>, emin:
> Option<i64>, emax: Option<i64>) -> Type`.
> Use None for unbounded, and checked_sub/checked_add at the i64 edges, as
> Mago's TInteger::difference does at
> crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:472-600. Rebuild the result with
> Type::int_range and Type::union, and turn an int\<n,n> into an int literal.
> Reimplement without_zero, which without_falsy calls at narrowing.rs:643-644,
> as `int_interval_difference(min, max, Some(0), Some(0))` so the two paths
> cannot drift apart.
>
> No change is needed in the caller. apply_equality_narrowing
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:199-205) already calls
> exclude only when `target_ty.is_single_value()`, so `$a !== $b` with a ranged
> `$b` stays unsound-free. An excluded range can only arrive from type-guard
> paths (is_int false branch, negated @phpstan-assert), where "every value of
> the excluded type is absent" is exactly the contract of `without`.
>
> Tests:
>
> - Unit tests in the types crate for the edge cases: int<0,10> minus 0, 10 and
>   5; int minus i64::MIN; a literal outside the range.
> - A fixture with the probe below.
> - A loop fixture such as `for ($k = 0; $k !== 10; $k++)` and
>   `while ($i !== N) { $i++; }` to confirm the fixpoint still converges with an
>   interior-split union.

#### K65. Arithmetic over int-literal unions: pairwise folding with a cap and a bounds-hull fallback

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: type-representation, control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Counters, offsets and flag arithmetic keep literal or ranged
  precision through `+ 1`, `* 2` and `% n`, which feeds offset-existence,
  comparison-always-true/false and division-by-zero checks. The existing
  overflow-to-float correctness is kept, which is better than Mago's saturating
  ops. | `$i = 0; while ($c) { $i = $i + 1; }` currently ends as `int` (probe
  cf/d), while `$i++` ends as `int<0, max>`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs:242`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:950`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:545`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs:646`,
  `crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs:812`, `crates/types/src/queries.rs:707`,
  `crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs:654`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:344`
- **Risks:** Union blow-up is bounded by the 64-pair cap plus MAX_UNION_MEMBERS.
  Loops need widening so literal sets don't grow each pass; the existing loop
  widening (widen_towards, queries.rs:328) should cover it, but verify on loop
  fixtures. | Low. For Sub, Mul and other operators, check overflow and sign
  handling per operator, reusing the existing checked_bound_op.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are materially wrong. Mago:
  analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs has the
  `for mut left_atomic in left_atomic_types` /
  `for right_atomic in &right_atomic_types` pair loop at about lines 242-258. It
  also maps false to 0 and true to 1, and skips null with `continue`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> All changes go in crates/types/src/arithmetic.rs, with an optional helper in
> crates/types/src/queries.rs. (1) Add
> `Type::int_hull(&self) -> Option<(Option<i64>, Option<i64>)>` to queries.rs.
> It returns int_bounds for a single member and, for a Repr::Union whose members
> all have int_bounds, the min of the mins and the max of the maxes (None on
> either side means unbounded). Then make widen_towards's local `hull` fn
> (queries.rs:367-379) call it, so there is one implementation. Leave
> `int_bounds` alone, because other callers depend on it meaning "exactly one
> int atomic". (2) In fold_float_constants (arithmetic.rs:~795), let int-only
> operands take part for Add/Sub/Mul/Mod/Pow/Spaceship when both sides are
> finite int-literal unions and |L|\*|R| <= LIMIT (64). In practice that means
> removing the `takes_part` restriction for int literals while keeping the
> single-literal x single-literal case, which the range code already handles
> exactly. The existing `apply` keeps the checked-overflow-to-float behaviour
> and drops pairs that divide or take a modulo by zero. Rename the function to
> something like fold_numeric_literals. (3) In binary_operation's
> Add/Sub/Mul/Pow/Mod/Div/Shl/Shr arms (arithmetic.rs:646-745), replace
> `lt.int_bounds()`/`rt.int_bounds()` with `int_hull()`. Mixed unions such as
> `int<0,5>|10`, and literal unions too big to fold, then go through the
> existing range code: checked_bound_op, sub_int_range_full, mul_int_range,
> mod_int_range, div_int_range and shift_int_range. For Shl/Shr with a
> non-constant amount union, fold pairwise when it is small. (4) Optional and
> separate: distribute over null (as 0) and bool (as 0|1) members of int unions,
> e.g. `?int + 1`. Keep float/array/string rules unchanged. Tests: the
> types-crate unit tests in arithmetic.rs, plus a loop fixture checking that
> `$i = 0; while ($c) { $i = $i + 1; }` and `$k = $k * 2 + 1` both converge to
> int<0, max> or int<1, max>|0 (or similar) within MAX_PASSES.

#### K80. Bind templates from parameter default values

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Generic functions and constructors with defaulted templated
  parameters (`@param T $default = null`, `@param TKey $key = 0`, Collection
  constructors with `= []`) get concrete types instead of mixed. That removes
  silent mixed propagation and matches runtime, where the default really is the
  value.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:750`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:1212`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:478`
- **Risks:** The default's literal type should probably be generalized the same
  way `generalize_inferred_class_template` does for invariant class templates,
  to avoid over-literal types such as `Box<5>`.
- **Verification:** Mago: the call sits at
  crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:753 (inside the loop over unused
  parameters, lines ~733-765; it skips parameters where `!has_default()`, and a
  missing default type falls back to mixed).
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs, `bound_call_return_type`
> (lines 468-509): keep the main loop as it is, and record the omitted slots
> whose `param.default_ty()` is Some (line 481). After the loop, and before the
> substitution at line 502, run a second pass. For each recorded (param.ty(),
> default_ty), infer into a scratch `TemplateBindings` with
> `self.relation().infer_template_bindings(param.ty(), default_ty, &mut scratch)`.
> Then copy into `bindings` only the template names that are not already there
> (`bindings.entry(k).or_insert(v)`). This is the only-if-unbound rule, so a
> real argument always wins. It has to be a post-pass rather than inline,
> because a defaulted parameter can come before the argument that binds the same
> template. Apply the same post-pass in the constructor arm of
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs (the loop at about 4650-4672 that
> currently does `let Some(arg) = slot else { continue };`). Its bindings
> already go through `generalize_inferred_class_template` (expr.rs:78, used at
> 4703), so `new Box()` with `@param T $v = 5` gives `Box<int>`, not `Box<5>`,
> and nothing extra is needed. Function and method templates keep the literal
> (`wrap()` gives `list<5>`), which is exact at runtime. No change is needed in
> crates/types/src/templates.rs. Existing guards already stop bad bindings:
> `Never` returns early (line 23), a `mixed` argument binds nothing (line 41),
> and `infer_const_type` returns mixed for defaults it cannot evaluate, so an
> `= []` default and an unresolved `self::X` default bind nothing. Tests:
> `wrap()` should give list<5>. `C<int>::get('a')` with
> `@param TD|(\Closure(): TD) $default = null` / `@return TValue|TD` should give
> int|null. `orDefault()` should give null. `pick(true)` with both params `T`
> should give true, because the real argument wins. `new Box()` should give
> Box\<int>. A Collection-style `@param array<TKey,TValue> $items = []` must
> stay unbound, not `<never,never>`.

#### K88. Fix unsound loose-== leaf in or_chain_narrowing_target

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Removes an unsound narrowing that makes false positives
  (argument.type, never-typed code) whenever a loose comparison sits inside an
  || or a negated && chain.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/assertion.rs:31`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:189`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:441`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:801`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/narrowing/an_or_chain_of_equality_comparisons_narrows_directly_to_the_union.php:4`
- **Risks:** Small precision loss for loose chains that were accidentally right,
  such as `?int $x == null || $x == 0`. The helper can recover those cases.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate. Mago:
  crates/codex/src/assertion.rs:29-32 has
  IsIdentical/IsNotIdentical/IsEqual/IsNotEqual as separate variants.
  crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:189-196 sends Equal|Identical to
  scrape_equality_assertions with binary.operator.is_identity().
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs, change the equality
> leaf of `or_chain_narrowing_target` (line 441,
> `ExprKind::Binary(BinOp::Identical | BinOp::Eq, l, r)`) to match only
> `BinOp::Identical`, and update the comment at lines 433-440, which currently
> says this leaf has "the same shape `apply_equality_narrowing` already
> recognizes". That brings it in line with the single-condition rule at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:801-809, which already accepts only
> `Identical`. The fix also covers the De Morgan path, because
> `and_chain_narrowing_target` (predicates.rs:480) reuses this leaf when it
> un-negates a term.
>
> Optionally, in the same commit or a follow-up, keep `Eq` through a small
> helper `loose_eq_is_identity(current, value) -> bool` in
> crates/types/src/narrowing.rs (or next to the leaf). It returns true only
> where `==` and `===` give the same result for every member of `current`. Two
> cases qualify: (a) the value is `null` and `current` has only object and null
> members; (b) the value is an int literal and `current` is int, or int|null
> with a non-zero literal. Note that `?int == null` is not an identity, because
> `0 == null` is true. The helper must treat that case as unsafe and must not
> recover it, which corrects the risk note in the proposal. Anything else
> returns `None` from the leaf.
>
> Add fixtures under tests/fixtures/checker/narrowing/ for:
>
> - `string $x == 0 || $x == 1`: must stay string, with no strlen error.
> - `int|string $x == '1' || $x == '2'`: must not narrow to `'1'|'2'`.
> - `?int $x == null || $x == 5`: must not narrow to `null|5`, because 0 passes.
> - `?Foo $x == null || $x instanceof Bar`, only if the helper is added. Also
>   add the negated-and form `!(!($x == 0) && !($x == 1))`.

#### K96. array_key_exists/isset with a variable key narrows the key variable

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Lookup-table idioms
  (`if (isset(self::MAP[$k])) return self::MAP[$k];` or
  `array_key_exists($status, $labels)`) give literal-union keys, which removes
  offset-might-not-exist noise downstream.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:310`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1087`
- **Risks:** PHP key coercion: '1' becomes 1, true becomes 1, null becomes ''.
  It must be modelled or restricted to string/int keys whose types already match
  the key type.
- **Verification:** Mago: the non-literal-key branch is in
  crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs around lines 290-320. The key-argument
  InArray assertion is inserted at about line 317 (not 310).
  get_possible_array_key_argument_type starts at about line 587 and
  add_possible_key_argument_type follows it.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs, add a second `array_key_exists`
> arm directly after the literal-key arm (1076-1118). It fires when
> `literal_string_key(key_arg)` is None and `narrowing_key(key_arg)` is Some.
> Add a matching step to the `ExprKind::Isset` true branch
> (narrowing.rs:923-945): for each operand `Index(base, Some(idx))` whose idx
> has a narrowing_key and is not a literal, run the same step. Put the shared
> logic in a helper next to `in_array_narrowing` in
> checker/narrowing/assertions.rs, for example
> `fn array_key_narrowing(&self, arr: &Expr, locals) -> Option<(Type /*true*/,
> Option<Type> /*false-excluded*/)>`.
>
> 1. Get K = `infer_expr(arr).array_key_type()` (types/src/queries.rs:794). Stop
>    if K is None, mixed, or the plain `int|string` key type, because nothing
>    can be learned then.
> 2. Model key coercion by widening K to K'. Every int literal n in K adds the
>    string literal "n", since PHP stores canonical numeric strings as int keys
>    and a string \$k equal to "1" still matches key 1. If K holds a non-literal
>    int (or a range), add no string forms and leave a string-typed key alone
>    (only its int part is narrowed). A string key never matches an int \$k,
>    because PHP canonicalizes numeric string keys to int when it stores them.
> 3. Narrow only the array-key part of the current type. Split current into
>    (current ∩ int|string) and the rest. Narrow the first part with
>    `relation().narrow(part, K')` and union the rest back in unchanged. This
>    keeps null→'', true→1 and 1.7→1 sound: `php -r` confirmed
>    `isset($m[true])`, `isset($m[1.7])` and `array_key_exists(null, [''=>1])`
>    all return true. If the narrowed part comes out never while the input was
>    not never, skip the narrowing so it cannot produce a false 'unreachable'
>    result.
> 4. The false branch of array_key_exists (not isset, where the value may be
>    null) applies only when the array is a single constant array whose fields
>    are all required. Then exclude those literal keys and their string forms
>    from \$k, like `in_array_narrowing`'s excluded half. Fixtures:
>    `array_key_exists($k, self::MAP)` returning \$k as `'a'|'b'`,
>    `isset(self::MAP[$k])` passing \$k to a `'a'|'b'` parameter, an int-keyed
>    map checked with a string \$k (stays numeric forms plus string), and a
>    mixed \$k (the non-array-key part is kept).

#### K145. Constant-condition checks via toBoolean

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Finds typo bugs (`=` written for `==`, `if ($s = null)` is always
  false), dead branches, and conditions that are always true because of a
  literal non-bool value. This is a real precision gap in a check that is on by
  default.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/constant_condition.rs:100`,
  `crates/syntax/src/utils/condition.rs:14`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_assign_in_condition.rs:99`
- **phpstan-rs:**
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow/boolean_conditions.rs:14`,
  `crates/types/src/queries.rs:873`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow/boolean_conditions.rs:201`
- **Risks:** Imprecise non-bool literal types, for example after loops, could
  cause new false positives. The existing loop_depth and property guards should
  apply, and a corpus diff (LC_ALL=C sorted) is needed.
- **Verification:** Mostly accurate, with these corrections: (a) The Mago linter
  rule constant_condition.rs is purely syntactic. At line 108 it calls
  mago_syntax is_truthy and at line 150 is_falsy, and it targets only
  NodeKind::If.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Change a single line in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow/boolean_conditions.rs:18 from
> `self.infer_expr(e, locals).bool_literal_value()` to
> `self.infer_expr(e, locals).to_boolean().bool_literal_value()`. No work is
> needed in crates/types/src/queries.rs, because to_boolean (:883) already
> covers everything the proposal asks for. An empty ArrayShape gives false. A
> shape with a required field, or a NonEmptyArray accessory, gives true.
> Objects, closures (Callable), resources and enum cases give true.
> SimpleXMLElement stays `bool`, and unions are folded per member.
>
> Also correct the doc comment at :5-13. It says trusting "exactly true/false"
> is PHPStan's design, but vendor/phpstan-src
> ConstantConditionRuleHelper::getBooleanType (lines 53-63) actually returns
> `$scope->getType($expr)->toBoolean()`.
>
> For conditions that are assignments, add one message variant in the callers:
> check_if (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:1119), while and do-while
> (stmt/loops.rs:137/144 and :292/300) and the ternary (expr.rs:2194). When
> `cond.kind` is `ExprKind::Assign` (and compound assignments), keep the same
> identifier but append a hint such as "(assignment used as condition; did you
> mean ==/===?)".
>
> The change reaches every caller of the helper with no further work: the
> `&&`/`||` operand checks (boolean_conditions.rs:89/105/145/159), the `!` rule
> (expr.rs:1742), and match(true) exhaustiveness (expr.rs:6326
> condition_is_provably_true). The last one gets more precise, not noisier.
>
> Fixtures to add:
>
> - `$a=[]; if ($a)` gives alwaysFalse.
> - `$s='abc'; if ($s)` gives alwaysTrue.
> - `$n=null; while ($n)` gives alwaysFalse.
> - `if ($x = 1)` and `if ($s = null)` give the assignment hint.
> - `while (1) {...break;}` and `do {...break;} while (0)` stay silent, because
>   the existing stmt_contains_break guards cover them.
> - The loop-flag patterns `$first=1; foreach { if ($first) { $first=0; } }`,
>   the `$acc=[]` / `$acc[]=` pattern and the `$str=''` / `.=` pattern stay
>   silent.
>
> Then run a sorted (LC_ALL=C) corpus diff at the next checkpoint.

#### K148. Rebind parameter on global/static/catch and report shadowing

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Removes wrong types, and the false positives they cause, after
  `global`. It also reports code where the parameter's value is silently lost.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/no_parameter_shadowing.rs:103`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:819`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:831`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:261`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/strict_rules.rs:628`
- **Risks:** Legacy code that runs `global $x` for a name already defined as a
  local would now get a mixed type. That is correct at runtime but may surface
  mixed-related findings.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with small line offsets. Mago's
  crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/no_parameter_shadowing.rs has `fn check`
  at about line 101 (the match over Function/Method/Closure starts at about
  106).
- **Refined proposal:**

> (1) Correctness fix in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs, in the
> StmtKind::Global arm (around lines 811-828). Drop the
> `if !locals.contains_key(name)` guard when checking a function, method or
> closure body, so that `global $x` always declares `$x` with
> `registry.global_variables.get(name)`, or `Type::mixed()` when there is none.
> Also clear any stale narrowing on that name, as try_catch.rs:260 does with
> purge_stale_narrowing_for. Keep the guard only for file-level (pseudo-main)
> code: there `global $x` binds the global to itself and changes nothing at
> runtime, so the existing precise local type is still right. (2) Add opt-in
> checks to the family in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/strict_rules.rs, gated
> by check_loop_variable_overwrite at about lines 628-660, or by a sibling flag.
> `global.parameterOverwrite` and `static.parameterOverwrite` fire when the name
> is a parameter of the enclosing function. PHP 8 already rejects
> `global $param` as a compile-time fatal error ("Cannot re-assign... "? verify
> with php -l first; if it is fatal, report it as a normal error, not a strict
> rule). `catch.variableOverwrite` fires when the catch variable is a parameter
> or an already-defined local. The catch check should be limited to parameters
> by default, because reusing `$e` across sequential catch blocks is idiomatic
> and flagging every defined local would be noisy. Fixtures: the sh1, sh2 and
> sh3 probes, the file-level `global $x` no-op, and a `global $x` after a local
> `$x = 1` inside a function, which should now have the global's type.

#### K176. Static closures/arrow functions must not see \$this

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** This is a runtime Error that is currently invisible inside
  methods. It also stops `$this`-typed inference from leaking into static
  callbacks, which feeds wrong types into callers.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/function_like/mod.rs:278`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/function_like/mod.rs:338`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3973`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5843`
- **Risks:** Very low. `static fn` inside a static method already has no \$this.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are correct.
  crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/function_like/mod.rs:277-291 is
  check_arrow_function's static+\$this error, with a secondary annotation on
  `static` and help text. Lines 337-351 are check_closure's equivalent.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Fix the arrow-function sites in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs so that
> none of them leaks `$this` into a `static fn`, the same way the Closure paths
> already avoid it (expr.rs:3611, 5026, 5784
> `if !is_static && let Some(this_ty) = locals.get("this")`): (1) check_expr's
> ArrowFn arm (expr.rs:3959-3973): destructure `is_static`, and when it is set
> call `arrow_locals.remove("this")` right after
> `let mut arrow_locals = locals.clone();`. (2) The override-inference helper's
> ArrowFn arm (expr.rs:4990-5008): same removal on its `arrow_locals`. (3)
> arrow_fn_inferred_return (called at expr.rs:4527 and 5895): give it an
> `is_static` parameter, or drop `this` from the cloned scope inside it, so the
> syntactic and expected-callable return inference both see no `$this`. The
> simplest single point is a small helper, e.g.
> `fn arrow_scope(locals, is_static) -> Locals`, that all three sites use.
> Diagnostics: static closures already get the generic
> `undefined variable $this (variable.undefined)` (probe: a.php:5:37). Once
> `this` is removed, static arrow fns will get the same. Better: in the
> Variable-read path, when the name is `this` and the innermost function-like is
> a static closure or arrow fn inside a non-static method, report a dedicated,
> non-ignorable-by-default `closure.staticThis` / `arrowFunction.staticThis`
> error, "Cannot use \$this in a static closure/arrow function.", with the tip
> "Remove the `static` modifier". That needs a small `in_static_closure` flag on
> the checker's function-like context. Fixtures: a static fn, a static closure
> and a nested static fn inside a non-static method (error); a static fn inside
> a static method (no duplicate error beyond the existing one); a non-static fn
> (clean).

#### K245. Truthy/falsy/equality assertion patterns

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Fixes an actively wrong narrowing: a nullable string becomes an
  object of a nonexistent class, which then drives downstream false positives.
  It also supports Psalm-annotated helper libraries (webmozart/assert-style
  `@psalm-assert non-empty-string`, `@psalm-assert =int`).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/cst/tag/assert.rs:33`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:802`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:256`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:265`
- **Risks:** `empty` is also a Psalm type keyword, so treat it as a pattern only
  in assert position. Make sure a genuine class named `Truthy` written as
  `\Truthy` still resolves as a class.
- **Verification:** Mago: the AssertPattern enum is at
  crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/cst/tag/assert.rs:33-38 with variants Type, Truthy,
  Falsy and NonEmpty. There is no Empty pattern variant.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs: change `AssertTag.ty: TypeNode` to
>    `kind: AssertKind { Type(TypeNode), Truthy, Falsy, Identical(TypeNode) }`.
>    In parse_assert_tag (line ~256), after stripping `!`, check for a bare
>    keyword followed by whitespace: `truthy`/`non-empty` become Truthy,
>    `falsy`/`empty` become Falsy. Only an unqualified lowercase bare word
>    counts; `\Truthy` or `Foo\truthy` still go through parse_type_prefix.
>    `non-empty` is followed by whitespace, so it does not collide with
>    `non-empty-string` or `non-empty-array`. Collapse the pairs: `!truthy` is
>    Falsy, and `non-empty` is the same as `truthy` for scalars, strings and
>    arrays. `=T` becomes Identical(T). `!=T` is kept only when T is a
>    single-value type (null, true, false or a literal); otherwise return None
>    as today, because "not identical to some int" does not exclude int. Update
>    the tests in crates/phpdoc/src/docblock/tests/assert_tags.rs.
> 2. crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig/asserts.rs: AssertInfo carries
>    the same kind, resolved: `Type(Type) | Truthy | Falsy`. Identical(T)
>    resolves to Type(T) for the positive direction, since narrowing to T by
>    `===` with an unknown value of T is no stronger than narrowing to T.
> 3. crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:385
>    apply_assert_infos, and the assert_if_true/false application in
>    checker/narrowing.rs around line 1209: Truthy uses
>    `current.without_falsy()` and Falsy uses `current.only_falsy(&relation)`
>    (crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:566/621). The negated form swaps the two.
>    These are the same primitives `if ($x)` uses.
> 4. crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1533-1620, the declaration-site
>    assert checks: skip the unresolvable, class-exists, trait and
>    alreadyNarrowed/impossible checks for the keyword kinds. The one exception
>    is a cheap "always truthy/falsy" alreadyNarrowed check, which is optional.
> 5. Update the substitution in function_sig.rs:246-250 (the template map over
>    info.ty) to map only the Type variant.

#### K278. Record is_generator on FunctionReflection and type calls to generator functions as Generator

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: hir-lowering-ir)
- **Benefit:** Callers of untyped or iterable-typed generators get a sound,
  precise object type. They get method checks on ->send()/->current(), no mixed
  noise, and correct instanceof narrowing. This matches a runtime fact that
  holds for every generator.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:129`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:110`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/item/member/method.rs:59`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:692`,
  `crates/syntax/src/visit.rs:759`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:903`
- **Risks:** The walk must not count a yield inside nested closures or classes
  (body_contains_yield already honours scope). Abstract and interface methods
  have no body, so they stay unchanged.
- **Verification:** Minor corrections only. In Mago,
  crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:129-137 is the method path. The
  function path is line 189 and the closure path is line 257, and all three call
  utils::block_has_yield.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an `is_generator: bool` field to FunctionReflection, set in
> `FunctionReflection::from_decl`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:592) from
> `syntax::visit::body_contains_yield(f.body_stmts())`. That one constructor
> covers functions (registry/index.rs:574) and methods
> (registry/class_info.rs:1036). Stubs have empty bodies, so they stay false.
> Keep `return_type` and `return_type_native` as they are, so the body checker's
> `declared_return` (checker/function_decl.rs:632) and the TReturn and
> missing-return logic at function_decl.rs:1001-1063 and stmt.rs:528-560 behave
> the same. Add an accessor, e.g. `caller_return_type()`, and use it wherever
> call and method-call results are resolved, including hover and completion. It
> works like this:
>
> - No doc and no native hint, or plain `mixed`: return
>   `Generator<mixed, mixed, mixed, mixed>`.
> - The declared type (doc or native) is iterable, Traversable, Iterator or
>   Generator: narrow it to Generator and keep the key and value generics. So
>   `@return iterable<int,string>` becomes
>   `Generator<int, string, mixed, mixed>`.
> - The declared type is incompatible with Generator (a wrong phpdoc such as
>   `@return array`): keep the declared type and do not intersect it to `never`.
>   A native `array` hint on a generator is already a PHP compile error. Do the
>   same for generator closures and arrow functions. At checker/expr.rs:3950,
>   `inferred_return` is currently skipped for generators, so pass
>   `Generator<mixed,mixed,mixed,mixed>` there. Otherwise
>   `$f = function(){ yield 1; }; $f()` stays mixed (probe confirmed). As an
>   optional second step, collect yield key/value types and return points during
>   the body walk to fill in K, V and TReturn for untyped generators. That needs
>   a per-function summary cache, because callers are resolved from the registry
>   and not from a checked body, so it is M cost and should be a separate step.
>   The missingType.return tip for a generator can suggest `Generator`.

#### K292. Clamp memoized property values to the magic \_\_get / @property-read read type

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a soundness bug. The probe
  `class N { function __get(string $k): int { return 1; } function __set(string
  $k, mixed $v): void {} } $n->zz = 'hello'; assertType('int', $n->zz);`
  fails in phpstan-rs, which infers 'hello', while PHP returns int(1). Every
  later check on that property (comparisons, arguments, offsets) then works from
  a value that never exists at runtime.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/assignment/property_assignment.rs:208`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/assignment/property_assignment.rs:240`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/property.rs:328`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:264`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:309`
- **Risks:** Code that relies on \_\_set/\_\_get round-tripping a value (a
  typical bag object) loses literal precision and falls back to \_\_get's
  declared type. That is the honest answer; a mixed \_\_get return still yields
  mixed as before.
- **Verification:** Mago: the read_type is recorded at
  property_assignment.rs:208-210 (the readable_type accumulation). The clamp
  decision is `has_read_clamp`, set at lines 71/75. The memoize
  intersect-or-fallback is at lines 240-259, with the intersection computed at
  252-257.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs::property_value_after_write
> (line ~264), work out whether a later read of `$obj->prop` will go through
> \_\_get. That happens in three cases: (a) find_property_owner returns None and
> the class has `__get` (registry.lookup_method(c, "\_\_get")); (b) the only
> match is a magic @property/@property-read/@property-write tag; (c) a declared
> property is not accessible from the current scope and the class has \_\_get.
> In those cases, store `value ∩ read_type`, where read_type is the tag's type
> for (b), otherwise \_\_get's declared return type. When the intersection is
> never, store read_type itself.
>
> Two corrections to the original proposal:
>
> 1. When there is no \_\_get, keep today's behaviour and return `value`. A
>    plain dynamic property (class R {}; \$r->d = 'x') really stores 'x'. "Store
>    nothing" is only right when \_\_set exists and \_\_get does not.
> 2. Case (b) needs a way to tell a tag-derived PropertyReflection apart from an
>    untyped native `public $x;`. The existing `!sig.has_native_type()` branch
>    already covers both and must keep returning `value` for the native one.
>    PropertyReflection (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:49) has
>    tag_read_only/tag_write_only but no general "from @property tag" flag, so
>    add an `is_magic_tag` bool that is set where the tag sigs are built.
>
> For case (c), reuse the visibility logic that expr.rs already runs after
> find_property_owner (~line 3030).
>
> Related bug seen in the same probe, worth fixing alongside: `$q->p` on a
> private property of a class that has \_\_get/\_\_set reports "access to
> private property Q::\$p" on both the write and the read. At runtime PHP routes
> those accesses to the magic methods, so both reports are false positives.

#### K30. Build static-property narrowing keys from the resolved, folded class

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Fixes an unsoundness confirmed by probe names-symbols/sp1. Inside
  `class Foo`, after `if (self::$x !== null) { Foo::$x = null; ... }`,
  `self::$x` is still typed `int` because the write purged a different key. It
  also restores missed narrowing: after `if (Foo::$x !== null)`, reads through
  `\App\Foo::$x` and `foo::$x` still see `int|null`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/mod.rs:390`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/mod.rs:338`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:84`
- **Risks:** Low. Keys only merge for expressions that PHP guarantees address
  the same static slot; `static` stays separate.
- **Verification:** All citations check out. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/mod.rs:390-401 is
  get_static_property_access_expression_id, which calls
  get_extended_expression_id(..., true).
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Resolve the class half of the key through the Checker.
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:84-88 builds the key
>    from the written `QualifiedName` text. There are about 50 free-function
>    call sites (checker/expr.rs, narrowing.rs, narrowing/assertions.rs), so
>    threading a context parameter through all of them is too much churn. Two
>    better options:
>    - (a) Have the name-resolution pass in the syntax crate record the FQN, so
>      `QualifiedName::resolved_class()` (syntax/src/ast.rs:879) is set for
>      class names. Then `narrowing_key` can use it, and only `self` and
>      `parent` still need resolving.
>    - (b) Add a `Checker::static_prop_key(&QualifiedName, name)` built on the
>      existing `Checker::resolve_static_class_name` (checker/resolve.rs:267).
>      Have `narrowing_key` emit a placeholder for `StaticTarget::Name` that
>      each Checker entry point canonicalizes.
>    The canonical key should be the lowercased FQN of the class that declares
>    the property, looked up in the registry. `Child::$x` and `Parent::$x`
>    address the same slot when Child does not redeclare `$x`, so they should
>    share one key. Keep `static::` as a separate key.
> 2. Close the matching soundness hole on the write side. In
>    `bind_assignment_target` and the purge helpers, a write to any
>    static-property key should also purge every other static-property key with
>    the same property name. Otherwise `static::$x = null` leaves a
>    `self::$x !== null` narrowing in place, and so does `Foo::$x = null` when
>    Foo cannot be resolved. This is cheap and removes the "separate keys" risk
>    entirely.
> 3. Add fixture tests for these shapes: `self`, a short name, `\FQN`, a
>    lowercased name, `parent`, an inherited property accessed through a child
>    class, and a write through `static::`.

#### K45. Model trait adaptations fully (insteadof, as visibility, final)

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Correct types and visibility errors at runtime-relevant sites.
  Probe t1: with `use A, B { B::hello insteadof A; }`, phpstan-rs types
  \$x->hello() as int while PHP returns 'x' (a string). With
  `use C { secret as private; }`, calling \$x->secret() from outside is a PHP
  fatal error ('Call to private method X::secret() from global scope') that
  phpstan-rs misses and Mago catches.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs:1240`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:891`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/methods.rs:101`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:876`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:339`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:413`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:704`
- **Risks:** Visibility of an aliased copy differs from the original name's
  visibility (both names stay callable), so the host view needs per-name
  visibility rather than mutating the shared signature. That fits the
  own/derived split well.
- **Verification:** Every citation checks out, give or take a line or two. Mago:
  crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs has the TraitUseAdaptation::Alias
  handling at about lines 1242-1275. It records add_trait_alias and
  trait_final_map for Modifier::Final, and then maps visibility.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:337: extend registry
>    TraitAlias to {trait_name: Option\<Name>, method, alias: Option\<Name>,
>    visibility: Option\<Visibility>, is_final: bool}. Stop the
>    `a.alias.as_deref()?` filter at ~line 1511, which silently drops
>    `m as protected;` even though the AST keeps it
>    (crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:625-631). Add a trait_precedences: Vec<{trait,
>    method, instead_of: Vec\<Name>}> built from the AST's insteadof node.
>    resolved_trait_conflicts stays in place for the conflict rule in
>    checker/oop.rs:622-660. 2) In registry/resolve.rs flatten_traits
>    (~150-185), before the plain first-wins push over `uses`, work out the
>    source trait for each method name. Skip a (trait, method) pair when that
>    trait appears in some precedence's instead_of for that method. Then add
>    alias copies from the named trait, or from the unique trait that has the
>    method. Apply the visibility override per name, meaning the alias name or
>    the original name when there is no alias, by cloning the FunctionReflection
>    for that name, so the original and the aliased copy each keep their own
>    visibility. 3) Propagate trait final_methods and final_methods_by_phpdoc
>    into the host's final set, the same way abstract_from_traits and
>    static_from_traits already are, plus the `as final` flag. Update the
>    comment on find_final_ancestor_method in registry/hierarchy.rs:~700, which
>    then gets trait finals through the host with no other change. 4) Parser:
>    accept `as final [alias]` (PHP 8.3), and also check that the other
>    modifiers are rejected as PHP rejects them. Add fixtures for insteadof
>    return typing, calls to `as private` or `as protected` methods from
>    outside, calling an alias whose visibility was changed while the original
>    name stays public, and overriding a trait-final method in a subclass.

#### K52. Infer assertions from single-expression boolean function bodies

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Precise narrowing through the very common predicate-helper
  pattern (isFoo, isValidId, isNonEmptyString) without the user writing
  @phpstan-assert. Removes follow-on mixed noise and false positives. Probe t9:
  Mago narrows `Foo|int` to Foo through isFoo(), while phpstan-rs keeps mixed.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/assertion_inference.rs:49`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:232`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig/asserts.rs:1`
- **Risks:** Inferring for overridable methods is unsound, so restrict it as
  described. The inferred assertion must be dropped if the body changes, so
  recompute per file on re-index.
- **Verification:** Mago: infer_assertions_from_block_body is at
  crates/codex/src/scanner/assertion_inference.rs:50 (the doc comment starts at
  47), not 49. The expression-body variant is at :28.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Derive the assertions syntactically when the registry is built, and do it more
> strictly than Mago does. Do not reuse checker/narrowing.rs apply_narrowing,
> because it works on a live Checker and Locals, which do not exist at index
> time.
>
> 1. Where it runs. Next to the existing explicit-tag path
>    (function_sig/asserts.rs resolve_assert_tags, called while building a
>    FunctionReflection), add a module such as
>    registry/function_sig/inferred_asserts.rs. It applies only when all of
>    these hold:
>    - sig.assert, assert_if_true and assert_if_false are all empty, after the
>      assertion table has been applied too;
>    - the body is exactly one `return <expr>;` statement (arrow functions: the
>      expression itself);
>    - the native return type is bool, or there is none.
> 2. What it recognizes, all against a by-value, non-variadic parameter `$p`,
>    walking through parentheses:
>    - `$p instanceof Name`, resolved with the declaration's NameContext. `self`
>      resolves to the declaring class. `static` and dynamic class names are
>      skipped.
>    - `is_int`, `is_string`, `is_float`, `is_bool`, `is_array`, `is_object`,
>      `is_null`, `is_numeric`, `is_callable`, `is_iterable` called with exactly
>      one argument, `$p`.
>    - `$p === null` and `$p !== null` (strict comparison only).
>    - `!e` swaps the true and false sets.
>    - `a && b`: the if_true set is the union of both sides' if_true sets.
>      `a || b`: the if_false set is the union of both sides' if_false sets.
>
>    Each result becomes an AssertInfo { target: AssertTarget::Param, ty,
>    negated } in assert_if_true or assert_if_false. apply_assert_infos
>    (checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:385) already turns a negated entry into an
>    exclusion, so for a mixed argument the false branch keeps the information
>    too.
>
> 3. Soundness gates:
>    - **Overridable methods.** Skip them unless purity.rs:504
>      is_non_overridable holds. That means private, a final method, or a final
>      class (the calling-class part does not apply at index time).
>    - **Scalar coercion.** Skip a parameter whose native type includes a
>      scalar. In a coercive-mode caller, `isInt(int|string $x)` called with a
>      float is coerced inside the callee, so the caller's variable is not what
>      the assertion claims.
>    - **By-reference parameters and assignments.** Skip by-reference
>      parameters, and bail out if the expression contains any assignment.
>    - **Loose comparisons.** Never infer from `==` or `!=` against null. Mago
>      does, and it is wrong: `0 == null` is true.
> 4. Mark inferred entries. Add `inferred: bool` to AssertInfo (or keep separate
>    `inferred_if_true` and `inferred_if_false` lists).
>    checker/narrowing.rs:1488 check_assert_tag_types must skip them, or it
>    would report assert.alreadyNarrowedType or assert.impossibleType about tags
>    the user never wrote. Any LSP hover or signature display should skip or
>    label them in the same way.
>
> 5. Leave names_with_assert_tags alone. It only gates bare-statement
>    @phpstan-assert (checker/stmt.rs:1028); conditional asserts are applied
>    through apply_function_conditional_asserts and the method arms regardless.
>
> 6. Incremental updates need nothing new: the signature is rebuilt when its
>    file is re-indexed. Dependents of a changed predicate body are already
>    re-checked through Project::update_file's transitive dependents, as long as
>    the change changes the signature. Make sure the signature's equality or
>    hash covers the inferred lists.
>
> 7. Optional follow-up: also infer ThisProp targets for
>    `return $this->p !== null;` and `return $this->p instanceof X;` on
>    non-overridable methods. The AssertTarget::ThisProp path already exists.
>
> Files touched: registry/function_sig.rs, the new
> registry/function_sig/inferred_asserts.rs, registry/function_sig/asserts.rs
> (the flag), checker/narrowing.rs (skip inferred entries in
> check_assert_tag_types), plus fixtures.

#### K54. First-party declarations fully replace extension stub symbols instead of merging

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: stubs-prelude)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a verified soundness and precision bug. In probe
  shadow/a.php, a first-party `class Redis { __construct(string $dsn) }` gets
  `array|null|string` for \$dsn, which causes a bogus missingType.iterableValue
  report, lets `new Redis(['host'=>'x'])` pass unreported, and resolves the
  stub-only `$r->get()`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1664`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1074`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:204`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:331`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:780`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:2017`
- **Risks:** Code that relied on stub members leaking into a user class (for
  example an incomplete vendored copy of a core class analysed in an unscoped
  run) would start reporting method.notFound. The tier classification of such
  files needs fixtures. Registry tests in
  registry/tests/stubs_and_conditional_declarations.rs that pin today's union
  behaviour must be rewritten per case.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with small refinements. Mago:
  should_replace_metadata is at crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1664. Its order
  is user-defined > patch > external > built-in > polyfill, then span, as its
  doc comment at 1654-1661 says.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a declaration tier to registry/index.rs insert_built_decl in place of
> today's single `analyzed: bool`. The tiers are Embedded
> (merge_stubs/merge_stub_classes), StubFile (configured stub_dirs, already
> known at parse time: project/session.rs:621-628 passes
> `stub_files.contains(p)` into read_and_parse_file), Context (scan
> paths/vendor) and Analysed. The collision rules for unconditional
> declarations: (1) If an Analysed or Context declaration, from a file that is
> not a stub file, hits a name that is still in built_in_stub_classes or
> stub_provided_functions, it replaces the entry outright: the class with all
> its members, or the function signature. The replacement drops the name from
> built_in_stub_classes/stub_provided_functions and records the decl site.
> Today's merge at index.rs:204-252 and index.rs:331-357 is removed for this
> case. (2) A StubFile declaration keeps the merge at index.rs:180/257
> (ClassReflection::merge, class_info.rs:2017), which is the stubFiles
> patch-one-method case the Imagick test pins. (3) FunctionReflection::merge
> (function_sig.rs:780) stays only for two declarations of the same name that
> are both Embedded or both StubFile, which is phpstorm-stubs' version-split
> strtr pair. (4) A vendored phpstorm-stubs copy analysed in a --no-composer run
> is classified as StubFile when its path matches
> vendor/jetbrains/phpstorm-stubs/ or \*.stub/\*.stub.php. That keeps
> index.rs:204's generics-preserving behaviour and the tests
> an_analyzed_files_redeclaration_of_a_built_in_stub_class_still_keeps_its_generics
> and a_stub_slot_survives_an_unconditional_duplicate_of_the_stub_itself. (5)
> Conditional declarations keep today's better_conditional_function_declaration
> and polyfill-merge logic (index.rs:112-180, 262-315), which is already
> tier-aware. (6) Incremental: Registry::remove_declarations (index.rs:423)
> currently deletes the name outright. That already loses the builtin today when
> a file that shadows or patches it is removed or edited. It must re-seed the
> Embedded entry (the stub class/signature from registry::stubs) and restore the
> stub markers when the removed name is a builtin. Also add an opt-in rule,
> using registry::stubs::builtin_class_extension/builtin_function_extension
> (stubs.rs:836-844): an unconditional first-party declaration named after an
> optional extension's symbol is reported, because PHP fatals when that
> extension is loaded. The same check should report a declaration named after a
> core or standard symbol, which fatals every time. Nothing reports this today;
> the only "already in use" check is checker/imports.rs:259, which covers
> imports. Fixtures:
>
> - user `class Redis { __construct(string $dsn) }`: no
>   missingType.iterableValue, `new Redis([...])` reported, `->get()` reported
>   as method.notFound;
> - user `function apcu_fetch(string $k): ?string`: its return type is ?string
>   and an array argument is reported;
> - the Imagick stub-file patch still merges;
> - the no-composer vendored phpstorm-stubs keeps its templates;
> - removing the shadowing file restores the stub.

#### K64. Relational/int-comparison narrowing per union member, including nullable/bool operands and non-literal bounds

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: type-representation, narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Brings range precision to the most common real shapes: nullable
  ints from parameters, literal unions from match or constants, and int|string
  ids. It also avoids replacing a precise literal union with a coarser range. |
  Loop and bounds code (`$i < $n`, `$offset >= $len`), nullable numeric guards,
  and array-index range checks become precise. Tighter int ranges feed
  offset-exists and arithmetic checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/int.rs:697`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/simple_assertion_reconciler.rs:1763`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:1401`, `crates/codex/src/assertion.rs:500`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:869`,
  `crates/types/src/queries.rs:707`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:871`,
  `crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:340`
- **Risks:** The PHP 8 loose-comparison table for string members is subtle
  (numeric vs non-numeric strings), so leave non-int members untouched rather
  than guess. Literal floats could be handled later. | Float and numeric-string
  operands follow different PHP comparison rules; restrict the change to int
  members plus single-value null/bool members. Take care with i64 overflow at
  the edges; the checked_add/checked_sub pattern already exists.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate: int.rs:697-750 to_less_than\* /
  to_greater_than\* return None when the range becomes empty.
  simple_assertion_reconciler.rs:~1763-1820 goes through the atomics one by one.
  Detail: it removes null and false only when `is_less_than && value == 0`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add
> `Type::narrow_by_int_comparison(op: OrderingOp, keyed_on_left: bool,
> branch_true: bool, bound: (Option<i64>, Option<i64>)) -> Type`
> in crates/types/src/narrowing.rs, next to `comparison_narrowed_bounds` (line
> 350). It maps over `union_members()` and rebuilds the type with `with_members`
> (constructors.rs:262), dropping never members:
>
> - IntLiteral: keep it or drop it by evaluating the comparison.
> - IntRange and Int: clamp with `comparison_narrowed_bounds`. Change that
>   function to take the bound pair. For a range bound, use the side that stays
>   sound for the outcome after polarity. `Smaller`/`SmallerOrEqual` clamp
>   against bound.max. `Greater`/`GreaterOrEqual` clamp against bound.min. If
>   that side is unbounded, leave the member unchanged.
> - Null, true, false and bool: keep or drop only when the bound is a single
>   literal. Evaluate it with PHP 8 semantics, where the other side is cast to
>   bool and false < true. Checked with php -r: null>0 false, null<1 true,
>   null>=0 true. Otherwise keep it.
> - Everything else (float, string, numeric-string, mixed, objects): leave
>   unchanged.
>
> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:847-885:
>
> - Remove the `current.int_bounds()` gate and the `bound == bound_max` gate.
> - Gate instead on the bound's inferred type having `int_bounds()`. Keep a bare
>   `int` bound as a no-op.
> - Store the result only when it differs from the current type.
> - Also narrow the bound operand when it has a `narrowing_key`, using the
>   mirrored op and the keyed side's pre-narrowing bounds. This makes `$i < $n`
>   narrow `$n` to > min(\$i).
>
> Rewrite the arm's comment so it no longer says loose comparison is unmodelled.
