> Add fixtures for: ?int > 0 (both branches), a literal union, int|string (only
> the int part changes), `$n<10 && $i<$n`, the else branch of a range bound, and
> the i64::MIN/MAX edges.

#### K78. Polarity-aware substitution of use-site variance

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Fixes wrong types and false positives today. Probe:
  `Box<covariant Animal>::get()` returns the pseudo-type `covariant Animal`, and
  `Box<contravariant Cat>::set(new Cat)` is falsely reported with
  `expects contravariant Cat, Cat given`. `Box<*>::set()` reports `expects *`.
  After the fix, writes through a covariant view are reported correctly (never)
  and reads get the real type.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/template/variance.rs:66`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/template/inferred_type_replacer.rs:42`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_result.rs:161`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:1461`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/generics.rs:97`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/generics/substitution.rs:78`,
  `crates/types/src/queries.rs:115`
- **Risks:** Every consumer of `substitute_class_templates` must pass the right
  polarity; property writes versus reads need separate call sites. A wrong
  default polarity would turn reads into never. The default must stay covariant
  so behaviour is unchanged for plain arguments.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate. Mago:
  `Variance::project` is at variance.rs about lines 69-86. It returns Some(true)
  to keep the type, Some(false) for mixed on a read, and None for never on a
  write.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Go with option (b), a polarity-aware `substitute`, but make it slightly more
> precise than the proposal's rules.
>
> 1. Add `enum Polarity { Read, Write }`, with a `flip()`, to
>    crates/types/src/templates.rs. Thread it through the private `substitute()`
>    function (currently around line 413). Add public entry points
>    `substitute_templates_of_with_polarity` and
>    `substitute_templates_with_polarity`. The existing `substitute_templates*`
>    entry points keep the default: Read (covariant).
>
> 2. In the `Repr::TemplateParam` arm, if the binding is a `Repr::VarianceArg`,
>    project it:
>    - Read: covariant X gives X; contravariant X gives the template's bound
>      (`tp.bound`, substituted); `*` gives the bound.
>    - Write: contravariant X gives X; covariant X and `*` give `never`.
>    - A plain binding is unchanged.
> 3. In the fallback `map_children` arm:
>    - Flip the polarity for `Repr::Callable` / Closure parameter types.
>    - Keep it for the callable's return type, arrays, shapes and iterables.
>    - For a generic object argument (`@return Collection<T>`), do not project.
>      Carry the use-site variance through by composition:
>      `Box<covariant Animal>::all()`, typed `Collection<T>`, gives
>      `Collection<covariant Animal>`. An invariant generic slot receiving a
>      variance-annotated binding keeps the wrapper. Projecting at that point to
>      a bare Animal would be unsound.
> 4. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/generics/substitution.rs:
>    - `substitute_class_templates` (line 51): parameter types (`ty`,
>      `ty_native`) use Write, and `out_ty` and the return type use Read.
>    - `substitute_class_template_property_type` (line 171) takes a polarity
>      argument.
>    - The call in checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:851 passes Read for
>      fetches. The property-assignment check (`assign.propertyType`) uses a
>      separate Write call, so `$b->v = new Cat` on `Box<covariant Animal>`
>      reports that it expects `never`. The message should say the property is
>      read-only through a covariant view.
> 5. Leave crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/generics.rs
>    (`class_template_bindings_rec`, line 97) alone, so the wrapper still
>    reaches `substitute`. Its `extends_args` substitution (line 107) already
>    goes through the default Read path, which keeps the wrapper at
>    generic-argument positions under rule 3.
>
> 6. Add fixture tests for:
>    - get/set/property read/property write under covariant, contravariant and
>      `*`
>    - a Closure(T) parameter under covariant
>    - a `Collection<T>` return keeping its variance
>    - `$b->get()->method()` resolving on Animal
>
> For the write-side messages, printing `never` alone is unfriendly, so consider
> a dedicated message along the lines of "cannot pass a value through a
> covariant view of Box".

#### K81. Pin templates bound through invariant generic slots

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Probe: `put(Box<int> $b, 'str')` with
  `@param Box<T> $b @param T $v` returns `int|'str'` with no error in
  phpstan-rs, while Mago reports invalid-argument `expected int`. Invariant
  containers (collections, repositories, typed maps) are exactly where this
  mixing corrupts data at runtime.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:757`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/template/bounds.rs:100`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/template/definition_type_replacer.rs:194`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/templates.rs:181`,
  `crates/types/src/templates.rs:118`
- **Risks:** This needs the resolved-parameter argument check to surface
  anything. Two pinned bindings that disagree (two invariant containers with
  different T) must produce a violation rather than one silently winning.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:756 sets
  `appearance_depth = usize::from(!top_level)` for a direct generic parameter in
  a Named-object container slot.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this in two steps, in this order. Doing step 2 without step 1 is net
> harmful.
>
> Step 1 (prerequisite, and the bigger win): add a template-resolved argument
> check. Today `check_parameters`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:280-305) checks each
> argument against the declared `param.ty()`, with templates still unresolved.
> `T` accepts `'str'` through its bound, and nothing after inference re-checks
> the arguments. Add a second pass inside `check_parameters`, after
> `bind_arguments`:
>
> - Infer `TemplateBindings` from all the bound arguments with
>   `Relation::infer_template_bindings`, using the same
>   `promote_class_string_literals` step as
>   crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5089-5099.
> - For every parameter whose type references a template, run
>   `substitute_templates` and then `rule_level_accepts` against the argument
>   type.
> - Report a failure under `argument.type`, or under a separate identifier such
>   as `argument.templateType`, and only when the first-pass check passed, so
>   the same argument is not reported twice.
>
> This check alone already catches `put(Box<int>, 'str')`. The union binding
> `T = int|'str'` makes the resolved parameter `Box<int|'str'>`, which rejects
> `Box<int>` under invariance. The trouble is that the error lands on argument
> #1 with a confusing type.
>
> Step 2 (this proposal): pin bindings made through invariant slots. Keep a
> parallel `FxHashSet<String>` of pinned names instead of changing
> `TemplateBindings` (checker.rs:229). That type alias has many users, and a set
> avoids touching them. Add an `infer_template_bindings_pinned` variant, or an
> optional `&mut FxHashSet` argument, in crates/types/src/templates.rs.
>
> - In the `Repr::Object` arm (templates.rs:118-126), check each slot. If the
>   parameter slot is a bare `TemplateParam` with no call-site `VarianceArg`,
>   and `self.hierarchy.slot_variance(class, i)` is `Some(Invariant)`, insert
>   the name into the pinned set and bind it exactly.
> - In `bind` (templates.rs:181), leave a pinned entry alone when a later
>   non-pinned binding arrives. When a second pinned binding does not equal the
>   first one, record a conflict instead of forming a union. That conflict
>   becomes a violation reported on the second argument, as in
>   `two(Box<int>, Box<string>)`.
> - Covariant slots, and slots with `@template-covariant` or call-site
>   `covariant`, keep today's union behaviour.
>
> The result is that the step 1 check blames the right argument: "#2 expects
> int, 'str' given".
>
> Tests: fixtures for these cases:
>
> - `put(Box<int>, 'str')` is an error on #2.
> - `put(Box<int>, 5)` is clean and returns `int`.
> - `two(Box<int>, Box<string>)` is an error.
> - A `Box<covariant T>` parameter and a covariant class slot are both clean and
>   still form a union.
> - A subclass argument read through `@implements` (`object_arguments_as`) pins
>   against the ancestor's slot variance.

#### K84. Evaluate new\<T>, template-type and template-keyed offset access T[K]

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Removes a false positive (`new<T>` reported as class.notFound on
  valid PHPStan and Psalm syntax used by DI containers and factories). Gives
  exact types for service-locator and typed-registry signatures (`Services[K]`)
  and for `template-type<>` extraction, a precise return type in place of mixed.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/template/inferred_type_replacer.rs:363`,
  `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/parameter_variable_index_access.php:20`,
  `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/parameter_variable_derived_types.php:45`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/parse.rs:731`,
  `crates/types/src/parse.rs:868`, `crates/types/src/late.rs:120`
- **Risks:** Adding Repr variants touches Display, hashing, traversal and
  relation code. Unresolved nodes must degrade to their upper bound (mixed or
  object), never an error.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are accurate. In
  crates/codex/src/ttype/template/inferred_type_replacer.rs,
  TDerived::IndexAccess replaces both the target and index types at lines
  363-369, TDerived::New is handled at 379-382 and TDerived::TemplateType at
  383-392.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Fix the offset-access key in crates/types/src/parse.rs:726-746. Parse
>    `key_part` with `parse_written_type` whenever it is not a quoted string or
>    an int literal, so that `A[K]` produces
>    `Type::offset_access(base, Object("K"))`. Then `mark_template_params`
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig/generics.rs:133, which runs
>    `replace_objects`) turns K into a TemplateParam without further work. If K
>    is left over as an unmarked Object, it should become a literal ShapeKey, so
>    the old reading of `Foo[bar]` is kept. Build the node whenever base OR key
>    is an Object or template; today (line 738) only a template base qualifies.
> 2. crates/types/src/late.rs. `settle` (line 120) must require that neither
>    inner nor key `references_template()`; today it only checks inner.
>    `offset_access` (line 92) needs to accept keys that are not literals. A
>    union key becomes the join of `offset_access` over each member. A general
>    key (int, string, array-key) becomes the join of every field value plus the
>    unsealed tail. Today `ShapeKey::from_type` returns None, which silently
>    falls to the tail or mixed. `resolve_late_to_bounds` then gives the right
>    answer inside the body too: K bounded by key-of\<A> maps to the join of all
>    values.
> 3. Add `Repr::New(Type)` in crates/types (repr, Display, hash,
>    `map_children`/`any_child`, `contains_late`). parse.rs gets a `"new"` arm
>    next to key-of/value-of. It resolves in `settle`/`resolve_late_to_bounds`:
>    ClassString(Object(c)) and Object(c) both become Object(c), a union maps
>    over its members, and anything else becomes `object`. This also removes the
>    class.notFound false positive in the return-type validity check.
> 4. `template-type<Obj, Class, 'T'>` goes last and is optional. It needs the
>    registry-backed `ClassHierarchy::ancestor_template_bindings`
>    (crates/types/src/hierarchy.rs:52), so it has to resolve at the call site
>    where the hierarchy is available, not in the registry-free `settle`. Until
>    then, parse it to `mixed` rather than to a pseudo-class, which removes the
>    FP cheaply. Tests go in crates/types (parse/late) and the registry generics
>    tests: `pick(['a'=>1,'b'=>'x'],'b')` should give 'x', a union key should
>    give a union of values, `make(Foo::class)` via new\<T> should give Foo with
>    no class.notFound, and an unbound key should give the bound join or mixed
>    with no error.

#### K92. Cross-variable implications from disjunct deltas

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Solves the most common guard shapes involving two variables
  (p1/p2 in the probes) with the current data structures, about a day of work
  instead of the full CNF. It also reuses existing purge-on-rebind logic.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:175`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/if.rs:1482`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:213`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:522`
- **Risks:** Only discriminants with a single value work, so is_string on one
  variable implying something about another is not covered. Recorded facts must
  be purged when either variable is rebound; that already happens through
  purge_branch_implied_facts_depending_on. Watch that the facts map does not
  grow too large in long functions.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:175-230 is the
  unit-propagation branch of the CNF simplifier. The comment at line 178 reads
  "(A) & (!A | B) => (B)", which is the capability the idea describes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the implication recording inside `record_branch_implied_facts`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:419), for the two compound shapes
> where `apply_narrowing` gives up today: `&&` with branch_true=false (the else
> side and surviving early-return path, recorded from stmt.rs:1219) and `||`
> with branch_true=true (stmt.rs:1191). For `!(L && R)`, build each disjunct
> state on a scratch clone of `before`: D1 = apply_narrowing(L,false) and D2 =
> apply_narrowing(L,true)+apply_narrowing(R,false). Also build the mirrored
> decomposition (D1' = R false, D2' = R true + L false), because otherwise only
> `if ($a === null)` is solved and `if ($b === null)` is not. For `L || R` true,
> do the same with the polarities flipped. In every disjunct pair, a key K whose
> type is a single value v (`is_single_value()`: null, bool literal, scalar
> literal, enum case) in one disjunct and that is absent from the other
> disjunct's K type gets `Discriminant(K, v)`. The implied facts are every other
> real-variable key whose type in that disjunct is a strict subtype of its
> `before` type, excluding keys whose disjunct type is never. Store them through
> `record_implied_facts` (narrowing.rs:522). Two replay-side changes go with
> this. (1) At narrowing/assertions.rs:213, intersect the replayed fact with the
> current type, `locals.insert(k, relation().narrow(&current_k, &implied_ty))`,
> rather than overwriting it. The plain `insert` now widens a variable that was
> narrowed after the fact was recorded, for example
> `if ($b === 5) { if ($a === null) ... }`, which would bring \$b back up to
> `int`. (2) Add the same Discriminant(K, null) lookup to the other ways of
> proving null: the `is_null($a)` predicate (narrowing/predicates.rs) and
> `!isset($a)`/`$a == null` where those already narrow to null. Otherwise the
> feature only fires for the `===` spelling. Invalidation stays as it is:
> `purge_branch_implied_facts_depending_on` (locals.rs:195) already drops a fact
> when either its subject or an implied variable is rebound, and the if-join
> intersection at control_flow.rs:703-733 already applies. Put a small cap on
> how many recordings one condition can make, so long `&&` chains do not blow up
> the facts map. Add fixtures for p1/p3 (early-return `$a===null && $b===null`
> followed by `if ($a===null)` and `if ($b===null)`), p2 (`||`-true), the rebind
> case (p5, already safe), and the narrowed-then-replayed precision case.

#### K95. count()/strlen() comparison assertions

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Array destructuring after length checks
  (`if (count($p) === 2) [$a,$b] = $p;`) and string-emptiness guards through
  strlen become precise. phpstan-rs could exceed Mago, which only reaches
  non-empty-list.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:731`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:1302`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs:1363`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:813`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:975`
- **Risks:** count() on Countable objects gives no shape change, so only refine
  array members. COUNT_RECURSIVE with a second argument must be ignored.
  mb_strlen counts characters, not bytes, so only the emptiness facts transfer.
- **Verification:** Mago: the citations are accurate. assertion.rs:731-757 maps
  `count($x) === N` to HasExactCount(N), or to EmptyCountable when N is 0, for
  both operand orders.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Types crate (crates/types/src/narrowing.rs, next to `to_non_empty_array` at
>    line 306 and the private `refine_arrays`): add
>    `Type::with_count_range(min: u64, max: Option<u64>) -> Type`. It works per
>    union member and changes only array members, so Countable objects and other
>    members pass through unchanged. For each array member:
>    - A constant shape: keep it if its possible field counts (required fields
>      up to required plus optional fields) intersect [min, max], and drop it
>      otherwise. Optional fields could also be trimmed, but that can come
>      later.
>    - `max == Some(0)`: gives `array{}`, the empty constant array.
>    - Otherwise, `min >= 1`: intersect with NonEmptyArray, reusing
>      `refine_arrays`.
>    - A list member with `min == max == N` and N ≤ 8: gives the sealed tuple
>      `array{0: V, …, N-1: V}`.
>    - A non-list keyed array with an exact N gets only the non-empty fact.
>      Never invent keys for it.
>    - When `max` is below the member's known minimum (for example, a
>      non-empty-array against `max = 0`), the result is never.
>    Add `Type::with_string_length_range(min, max)` the same way. It refines
>    only string members; `int`, `null` and other members pass through, because
>    strlen coerces them.
>    - `max == Some(0)` gives `''`.
>    - `min >= 1` gives non-empty-string.
>    - `min >= 2` gives non-falsy-string.
>    - A literal member outside the range is dropped.
>    - `mb_strlen`, `iconv_strlen` and `grapheme_strlen` should pass only the
>      emptiness facts (`min >= 1` and `max == 0`), because they count
>      characters, not bytes.
> 2. Checker (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs):
>    - Generalize `count_call_operand` (lines 26-41) into a
>      `length_call_operand` that returns (arg, kind: Count | ByteLen | CharLen,
>      on_left). It must require exactly one argument, so
>      `count($x, COUNT_RECURSIVE)` is ignored, and it should resolve names
>      through `registry.called_function_name` rather than `trim_start_matches`
>      (which is what line 30 does now). It should also accept `sizeof`.
>    - Replace the special-cased count arm (lines 813-846) with a general one.
>      It takes any ordering op, or `===`/`!==`, with an integer bound, in
>      either operand order and on both branches. Compute the new interval with
>      the existing `comparison_narrowed_bounds` (used at line 874), starting
>      from (0, None). For `===`, use [N, N] on the true branch. On the false
>      branch, use min 1 only when N == 0. Other `!==` cases add nothing.
>    - The `===`/`!==` path currently goes to `apply_equality_narrowing` first
>      (line 811). The length check must run either before it or as well as it.
>    - Wire the false branch of bare `count($x)` at line 975 to
>      `with_count_range(0, Some(0))`. Add bare `strlen($s)` truthy/falsy
>      handling the same way.
> 3. Also, in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:53, make
>    `strlen` return `int<1,max>` for a non-empty-string argument and the exact
>    integer for a literal argument. Then `strlen($s) > 0` and similar
>    round-trip consistently.
>
> 4. Add fixtures for:
>    - `count($l) === 0` giving array{}.
>    - `count($l) === 2` followed by `[$a, $b] = $l`.
>    - `count($l) < 2` in the else branch giving non-empty.
>    - `!count($l)`.
>    - `strlen($s) > 3`.
>    - `strlen($s) === 0` on both branches.
>    - `string|null` with `strlen === 0` keeping null.
>    - A Countable|array union.
>    - `count($x, COUNT_RECURSIVE)` staying unnarrowed.

#### K119. Resolve dynamic member names from constant strings

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Normal method or property existence checks, argument checks and
  return types for the common `$method = 'get' . 'Foo'`-free pattern where the
  name is a literal held in a variable or constant, or comes from a foreach over
  literal names. It also makes the dynamic-method and dynamic-static paths
  consistent.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/selector.rs:77`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3124`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3153`
- **Risks:** Some intentional dynamic dispatch (`$this->$handler()` over a list
  of literal names) may now report method.notFound for names that don't exist.
  That is correct, but could be noisy in magic-heavy code; \_\_call receivers
  should keep suppressing it.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate. Mago:
  /home/torres/projects/mago/crates/analyzer/src/resolver/selector.rs:77
  `resolve_member_selector` analyzes the Expression or Variable selector, reads
  its type (and casts it to string when asked), then calls
  `resolve_selector_from_type`, which returns a Vec\<ResolvedSe ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a helper in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs next to `static_call`
> (line 5960), for example `fn method_call(recv, name, args, op, span)` /
> `fn property_access(base, name, op, span)`, that builds a synthetic
> `ExprKind::MethodCall` / `ExprKind::PropertyAccess` (ast.rs:1438-1439) keeping
> the ObjectOperator, which carries the nullsafe flag. Then: (1) In check_expr,
> DynamicMethodCall (expr.rs:3124) and DynamicPropertyAccess (expr.rs:3090): run
> check_expr on the name first. If `name_ty.constant_strings_text()` is
> non-empty, dispatch each name to the synthetic node with the original e.span,
> the same way DynamicStaticCall does at 3154-3160, and union the result types.
> When there are several names, check the receiver and args only once. Either
> run the per-name member checks under a flag that skips re-checking
> sub-expressions, or evaluate args in the first pass only. Otherwise keep
> today's escape and mixed path. This also covers the plain literal
> `$a->{'v'}()`, which today returns mixed even though its member ref is
> recorded. (2) In infer_expr: add the matching arms. Today there are none, so
> both fall through to mixed. Mirror the DynamicStaticCall arm at expr.rs:4792.
> (3) Write/isset/unset paths: when the name is constant, the property-write
> checks in checker/assignment.rs (lines 41-49 group DynamicPropertyAccess with
> the other targets) and the isset probe walk in expr/probe_checks.rs:95 should
> also resolve to the named property. Otherwise `$a->$p = 'str'` still skips the
> property type/readonly checks. (4) First-class callable `$a->$m(...)` at
> expr.rs:4335 gets the same rewrite, so a missing method is reported there too.
> Keep recording member refs and escapes as today: resolved names go through
> record_member_ref via the MethodCall path, and only a genuinely non-constant
> name escapes.
