  remove_possible_reference at :587-644 re-roots the remaining aliases.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build this in stages, starting with the cheapest sound fixes. (1) Small fix in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs around line 809. The by-ref
> foreach feedback currently runs only when `subject_ty.array_value_type()` is
> Some. Extend it to constant-array shapes. The simplest sound version
> generalizes a literal shape to `array<K, old_value|final_value>`, or keeps the
> shape and unions each value slot with final_value. It should also cover
> non-Variable subjects that have a narrowing_key, such as `$this->items` and
> `$a['x']`. (2) Add an alias side map to Locals in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs, keyed like the existing condition_aliases /
> narrowing_key machinery so declare-time invalidation can be reused. Fill it
> only for `$b = &$a` between plain variables and for `$r = &$a['lit']`,
> recorded in the Assign/AssignRef arm of crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs
> at line 2013. On a write to either end, Locals::declare/insert rebinds the
> other end: exact for variable-to-variable, and a literal offset write for
> offset targets. It also purges branch facts for both keys. merge_scopes keeps
> only links that both sides share. unset or a plain AssignRef of either end
> drops the link. (3) Soundness fallback for anything unmodelled, meaning a
> dynamic offset, a property target, a static or global binding, or an alias
> that did not survive a merge. On a write through such an alias, widen the
> target's declared or native type, or mixed if none, instead of leaving a stale
> precise type. (4) Closures: keep the write-back at definition in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs line 340. Record the
> by-ref use set against the closure variable, and at each later `$f()` /
> call_user_func(\$f) re-apply the closure's final written types, unioned. If
> the callee is unknown or the closure escapes to a call, treat by-ref-captured
> variables as clobbered to their written-type union. Test with the fixtures
> from probes cf/b k, cf/j k3 and k4, plus negative fixtures that check
> narrowing of the root is not lost when the alias is only read.

#### K270. Whole-program dead code via reachability

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, L (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Finds dead subgraphs (helper functions and classes used only by
  other dead code, recursive functions, self-referencing classes). Today these
  are silently treated as live, which weakens all four opt-in whole-program
  rules.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:35`,
  `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:262`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:251`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:58`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_code.rs:313`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:229`
- **Risks:** Framework and reflection entry points become roots that need
  configuring. Memory grows with one origin per site, which can be interned. The
  LSP rename/references consumers of use_sites must be unaffected, so the origin
  should be an extra field, not a change to the key.
- **Verification:** Mago: reference.rs:35-41 ReferenceOrigin {Symbol, File} is
  correct. reference.rs:262-265 add_symbol_reference_to_symbol does return early
  on self-reference.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add liveness by reachability to the opt-in whole-program rules, as one shared
> pass that all of them use. Do not copy Mago's per-class fixpoint.
>
> 1. Record an origin for every site. Add
>    `enum RefOrigin { File(PathBuf), Function(String), Class(String),
>    Member(String, String) }`
>    in `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs`. Store it as an extra field
>    in `by_file`, and add a new `edges: FxHashMap<RefOrigin, Vec<RefTarget>>`
>    map (or an origin column next to `by_target`). The `RefTarget` key and
>    `references()` stay unchanged, so LSP references and rename are not
>    affected. `remove_file` also drops that file's edges.
>    - Tier 1: `ClassFnRefWalker` (use_sites.rs:157) keeps an origin stack. It
>      pushes in `visit_function_def`, `visit_class_def` and the method visit. A
>      closure or arrow function takes its enclosing named symbol as origin.
>      Top-level statements get `File`.
>    - Tier 2: `Checker::record_member_ref` (checker.rs:1226) adds
>      `(current_class, current_method)` from checker.rs:307/312 to the tuple. A
>      free function uses the function's FQN, and top-level code uses `File`.
>      For a trait method checked under its host, the origin is the host's
>      method. That is conservative, which is fine.
> 2. Compute liveness with a least fixpoint, a BFS from the roots, in a new
>    `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/reachability.rs`. Do not use
>    Mago's "all referrers are dead" greatest fixpoint. Mago's version cannot
>    kill mutual recursion A<->B. It gets away with dropping self-edges only
>    because it runs per class.
>    - Roots:
>      - every `File` origin;
>      - everything the existing exclusions already treat as live: `__autoload`,
>        `IMPLICITLY_INVOKED_METHODS` and `is_magic`, `is_phpunit_test_method`,
>        and every escaped class from `escaped_classes`;
>      - enum builtins and enum cases handled by `dead_enum_cases`;
>      - optionally, configured entry-point namespaces or symbols in the config
>        crate, for libraries.
>    - `overrides_an_ancestor_method` becomes a conditional root: live when its
>      class is live. This covers vendor or polymorphic callers that Tier 2
>      never sees.
>    - A live member makes its declaring class live. A live class does not make
>      all of its members live.
> 3. Keep the finding sets apart. `find_dead_functions`, `find_dead_classes`
>    (dead_code.rs:50/68) and `find_dead_members` (dead_members.rs:194) keep
>    reporting the zero-reference set under their current identifiers. Symbols
>    that are referenced but unreachable are reported under separate identifiers
>    (for example `*.unreachable`, "only used by dead code"), behind their own
>    opt-in flag.
>
> Set aside the "replace `dependents` (project.rs:126) with this graph" part.
> Per-file re-checking does not benefit from member-level invalidation the way
> Mago's `get_invalid_symbols` does. It is a separate project.

#### K4. Close PHP-divergent lexer acceptances (unterminated strings/comments/heredocs, stray bytes, cast spelling, comments in {\$...})

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Two directions of benefit: - phpstan-rs stops analysing code that
  PHP refuses to run, where results can be meaningless (a runaway string
  swallowing the rest of the file). - It stops skipping valid files with
  comments inside braced interpolation. Each fix is a local, testable lexer
  change.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:1742`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:478`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:705`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:562`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:1249`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer/strings.rs:150`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:527`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/strings.rs:317`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:878`, `crates/syntax/src/parser/expr.rs:555`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/strings.rs:218`
- **Risks:** Turning silent acceptance into errors can surface new parse
  failures in vendor files that were previously analysed, however imperfectly.
  Without error recovery (see the recovery idea) those files would now be
  dropped, so ideally land this after recovery or report these as recoverable
  errors. The cast token must not break `(int)` used in other positions, such as
  a first-class-callable-like shape or `(INT)` in constant contexts; check
  against php -l.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small
  corrections: - Mago lexer/mod.rs:562: the cast peek loop skips
  `is_ascii_whitespace()`, which includes newlines. So Mago would lex
  `(\nint\n)` as a cast, which diverges from PHP (PHP allows only spaces and
  tabs).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Scope this down to the cheap, local lexer fixes and use the error channel that
> already exists. Leave out the cast-token redesign.
>
> (a) Reuse `LexWarning { is_error: true }` (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:9-15).
> The machinery is already in place: crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:69 turns the
> first `is_error` warning into a `ParseError`. The file is then reported as
> skipped with a parse error, so structured error kinds or error recovery are
> not needed first.
>
> Push `is_error` warnings with PHP-like messages in these places:
>
> - `lex_single_quoted` (lexer/strings.rs:150) and the double-quoted/backtick
>   run (lexer/strings.rs ~200) when EOF comes before the closing delimiter.
> - `lex_heredoc`'s unterminated branch (lexer/strings.rs ~317, the "treat rest
>   of file as body" comment).
> - The `/* */` loop in `skip_whitespace_and_comments` (lexer.rs ~527) and
>   `lex_doc_comment` (lexer.rs ~682): "Unterminated comment starting line N".
> - lexer.rs:878-887, where an unknown byte becomes `is_error: true` with
>   "syntax error, unexpected character 0xNN". Keep the byte-skip only for bytes
>   PHP itself tolerates.
>
> (b) Fix the valid-code rejection in the `{$...}` brace scan
> (lexer/strings.rs:216-235). Also skip `/* */`, `//` and `#` comments there,
> stopping a line comment at the string delimiter as PHP does. This is the one
> real false negative on valid code.
>
> (c) Optionally, and cheaply, tighten `try_parse_cast` (parser/expr.rs:555)
> without a new token. Reject when the spans of `(`, the name and `)` are on
> different lines. For comments inside the parentheses, check whether the
> lexer's comment list has an entry between the spans. A new `Token::Cast` is
> not worth the churn.
>
> Add one unit test per case in the lexer test module. Run a corpus/vendor
> regression pass to confirm no previously parsed file now fails.

#### K179. Default to a concrete PHP version when none configured

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Single-file checks, LSP scratch buffers and non-composer projects
  currently lose every version-sensitive compile error (removed casts, removed
  constants, version-gated syntax). Only PHP 8+ can run such code at all.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/php-version/src/lib.rs:442`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/expression.rs:122`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs:214`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:426`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/coercion.rs:39`
- **Risks:** Legacy PHP 7 code analysed without composer would get removal
  errors. That is correct for any modern runtime, and the tip plus an explicit
  php_version override makes it easy to opt out.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are wrong. Mago:
  crates/php-version/src/lib.rs:98 sets `LATEST = PHP85`, and lines 441-446 have
  `impl Default for PHPVersion` return `Self::LATEST`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do NOT set Registry::php_versions to a default. Leave `php_versions: None`
> meaning "unknown" everywhere type inference reads it. Add a separate, narrow
> fallback used only by the removal gates. Define a new Registry helper (in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs, next to php_supports_everywhere at :214),
> e.g.
> `php_removed_assuming_supported(feature) -> Option<(bool, assumed: bool)>`. It
> returns the configured answer when php_versions is Some. When php_versions is
> None, it evaluates the feature against the oldest _still-supported_ PHP
> release (a const in crates/types/src/php_version.rs, e.g. 8.2 today, rather
> than 8.5) and flags the answer as assumed. Only the removal rules switch to
> it: check_unset_cast_supported and check_real_cast_supported
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/coercion.rs:39 onward) and the
> case-insensitive-constants removal. Their diagnostics get a tip: "No PHP
> version is configured; assuming a supported PHP (>= 8.x). Set php_version to
> change this." Put the fallback behind a config key
> (`assume_supported_php_when_unset`, default on) in crates/config. The key also
> needs to be carried through ProjectSettings
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:305, project/session.rs:426) and
> lsp/workspace_config.rs:164 so the CLI and the LSP agree. Leave these on
> "unknown": PHP_VERSION_ID/PHP_MAJOR_VERSION typing
> (checker/predefined_constants.rs:41), php_version_consensus users
> (expr.rs:5346, comparisons.rs:54, format_string.rs:383/529,
> probe_checks.rs:365), next_array_index, feature-availability gates
> (type_declarations.rs:176) and deprecations. Do not detect the `php` binary on
> PATH.

#### K74. Hierarchy-aware union simplification at join points

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Smaller unions after branches, which means less relation work
  downstream, clearer messages ('Base given' instead of 'Base|Child given'), and
  fewer members hitting the union cap in class-heavy code.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:1062`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:1530`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/union.rs:292`,
  `crates/types/src/relation/super_type.rs:321`
- **Risks:** A merge-time normalization must be idempotent and cheap, so cache
  it per (type ptr, registry generation) for LSP incrementality. Covariant
  merging loses information (Box\<int>|Box\<string> is narrower than
  Box\<int|string>), so use it only as the pre-mixed cap fallback, never by
  default.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs lines ~1062-1135 do
  what is claimed. Named-object members are compared against existing ones using
  codebase.is_instance_of (subclasses are removed, around line 1099),
  class_extends and class_implements (the incoming type is skipped when already
  covered, aroun ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Break it into three pieces and give the first one priority. (1) Display-time
> absorption, cost S. Everywhere a diagnostic prints a value type ("X given",
> return/assign/property mismatch), first pass it through
> Registry::absorb_union_subtypes
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/relation.rs:132, which wraps
> crates/types/src/relation/super_type.rs:341). Also add a collapse in the same
> helper: when a union contains every case of an enum, show the enum instead
> (S::A|S::B shows as S). This only runs on the error path, so it costs nothing
> in the hot loop and needs no cache. (2) Hierarchy-aware reduction before the
> union cap, cost M. Type::union (crates/types/src/union.rs:198-212) currently
> goes generalize_by_key_set, then widen_extension_types, then
> generalize_members, then mixed. Add an optional step before the mixed
> collapse: a hierarchy-aware absorption, plus same-class generic merging over
> covariant template slots only. Supply it through a callback or trait object
> from the registry so the memoized structural path (intern.rs memoized is
> hierarchy-free by contract) stays unchanged. The best place to call it is
> where the checker assigns a local (both the ternary/match/?? results and the
> merge_scopes output), and only when the unioned result would go over
> MAX_UNION_MEMBERS. Losing precision (Box\<int|string> instead of
> Box\<int>|Box\<string>) is still far better than mixed. (3) Do not normalize
> at every merge_scopes call
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563). It takes only Locals, not
> the registry, and has about 24 call sites. It would also miss expression-level
> joins: the probe `$b ? new Base : new Child` is a ternary, not a scope merge.

#### K233. Validate configured PHP version

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** A typo like 8.9 or 9.0 currently changes which version-gated
  rules and stubs apply without any notice. A mismatch with composer is usually
  a stale config that gives wrong portability diagnostics.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/main.rs:252`, `src/config/mod.rs:541`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/php_version.rs:145`,
  `crates/types/src/php_version.rs:111`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:422`
- **Risks:** When a new PHP release is out, users need the allow flag until
  KNOWN_PHP_VERSIONS is bumped. That's acceptable and explicit.
- **Verification:** All citations check out. Mago src/main.rs:251-259 returns
  PHPVersionIsTooOld/TooNew against MINIMUM_PHP_VERSION/MAXIMUM_PHP_VERSION
  unless configuration.allow_unsupported_php_version is set.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep it small and make it warn, not fail. (1) In
> crates/types/src/php_version.rs parse_php_version (line ~145), also accept
> 'X.Y.Z' by dropping the patch, and accept PHPStan's 5-digit int form (80100).
> Update php_version/tests.rs line 17, which currently asserts that '8.1.0' is
> an error. (2) Add a helper next to KNOWN_PHP_VERSIONS (line 111) that returns
> a warning when the parsed version is not one of the known releases. For
> example: 'php_version 8.9 is not a known PHP release (known: 5.3..8.5);
> treating it as newer than 8.5'. For an inner typo like 7.9, name the nearest
> known version. Emit the warning from both callers,
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:313 and
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/workspace_config.rs:94. Do not exit, so there is no
> need for an allow_unsupported_php_version flag. (3) In session.rs near line
> 426, where `php_version.map(PhpVersions::exactly).or(composer_php_versions)`
> is computed, warn when an explicit version lies outside composer's declared
> range. Keep the explicit override winning. (4) Leave the
> `php_version = {min,max}` range config out of this item and treat it as a
> separate feature.

### 3.2 new-check (67)

#### K111. switch/match reachability: duplicate cases/conditions, never-matching and unreachable cases

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope, analyzer-issue-catalog,
  linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Catches copy-paste duplicate cases (probe cf/j: Mago flags
  `case 1:` twice, phpstan-rs is silent) and dead defaults in enum switches, and
  makes exhaustive enum switches terminate correctly (probe cf/f a3). |
  Duplicate case labels are classic copy-paste bugs where the second branch
  never runs. Unreachable arms or defaults after a tautological case hide dead
  logic.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:745`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:393`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:346`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:437`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:415`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_duplicate_match_arm.rs:98`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:90`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3300`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/strict_rules.rs:686`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:88`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3312`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:6` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Switch uses loose `==`, so never-matching must use a PHP-version
  consensus of loose equality, as check_constant_loose_comparison already does.
  Inside loops, apply the same convergence gating as the loop_depth idea. |
  switch uses loose comparison (`==`), so duplicate detection must compare
  loosely-equal literals (1 vs '1' vs true) or stay limited to same-type
  literals. Reporting after next_arm_is_dead is a deliberate break from PHPStan,
  which is fine under the project's goals. | Switch comparison must be loose,
  not strict. Skip non-constant conditions.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are correct, with small line offsets. In
  mago crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs: UnreachableSwitchDefault is at
  :297, UnreachableSwitchCase at :311, and the exhausted-subject pair is at
  about :358-360, not :346.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split this into three pieces, in order of value.
>
> (1) Switch exhaustion. This is a precision fix and removes false positives. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs check_switch, keep
> `remaining_subject_ty = self.expand_enum_cases(&self.infer_expr(subject, locals))`,
> the same seeding match uses in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3301-3305. Subtract every single-value
> case whose loose comparison with the subject is exact. Enum cases and
> same-type literals are safe; for mixed scalar types, gate on the
> php_version_consensus loose equality from probe_checks.rs:346
> check_constant_loose_comparison / types::arithmetic.rs:348 loosely_equals.
> When no default exists and the remaining type is never, do not push the
> pre-switch `locals` into exit_states (currently lines 63-65). Make the
> `Switch` arm of `always_terminates` agree, so an exhaustive enum switch where
> every case returns counts as terminating.
>
> (2) Dead labels. Keep a Vec<(Type, Span)> of single-value case types, as
> Mago's seen_case_condition_types does and as array_ops.rs:30-70 does for keys.
> Report a repeat as `switch.duplicateCase`, with the earlier span as secondary.
> A repeat is either strictly identical (identical_result == Some(true)) or,
> under the switch's `==`, loosely equal by version consensus. Emit
> `switch.unreachableCase` instead when the previous case terminates, so the
> body cannot be reached by fallthrough either. Report
> `switch.unreachableDefault` when the remaining type is never at `default`.
> Report `switch.caseNeverMatches` only when loose equality is false on every
> PHP version. Guard everything with `loop_depth == 0`, as the match checks do.
>
> (3) Match arms. In the expr.rs:3308-3380 loop, keep the same seen-list and
> report `match.duplicateCondition` for a single-value condition identical to an
> earlier one. This covers wide subjects (int, string) where
> `remaining_subject_ty.without(1)` is a no-op. Also report
> `match.unreachableArm` for arms, and the default, after `next_arm_is_dead`
> becomes true, instead of going silent.
>
> Tests go in the checker's switch/match test modules plus fixtures. Cover
> `case 1:` twice, `case 'x'` twice, `1 => ..., 1 => ...` on int,
> `case 1:`/`case '1':`, and exhaustive enum switches with and without default:
> no return.missing and no undefined variable afterwards.

#### K180. Extend PhpFeature for syntax-level features

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** A library declaring `"php": ">=7.4"` that uses
  match/enum/nullsafe/never gets a parse-time fatal on the oldest supported
  runtime, which phpstan-rs currently never flags. Real runtime correctness for
  multi-version packages.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/php-version/src/feature.rs:3`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/hint.rs:140`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:817`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/php_version.rs:170`
- **Risks:** The composer range needs care: `>=7.4` means report when the
  minimum lacks the feature (php_supports_everywhere), not when the maximum
  does. The lexer must already tokenise `#[` the same way on all versions.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are right, give or take a few lines.
  crates/php-version/src/feature.rs:3 is `pub enum Feature` with 104 variants
  (Enums at :39, NewWithoutParentheses at :82, NumericLiteralSeparator at :85,
  MatchExpression at :88, NullSafeOperator at :89, TrailingCommaInParameterList
  at :93, Catch ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the missing syntax-level PhpFeature variants to
> crates/types/src/php_version.rs, with their thresholds in
> PhpFeature::threshold (line 356):
>
> - 7.1: NullableTypes, VoidReturn, IterableType, MultiCatch,
>   ClassConstVisibility, KeyedListShortDestructuring
> - 7.2: ObjectType
> - 7.4: TypedProperties, ArrowFunctions, NullCoalesceAssign,
>   NumericLiteralSeparator, SpreadInArrayLiteral
> - 8.0: MatchExpression, NullsafeOperator, MixedType, StaticReturnType,
>   Attributes, TrailingCommaInParamsAndClosureUse, ClassOnObject
> - 8.1: Enums, NeverType, NewInInitializers
> - 8.4: NewWithoutParentheses
> - 8.5: PipeOperator, CloneWith Add all of them only where the parser keeps
>   enough information to detect them.
>
> Start by wiring up the two variants that already exist but are never read,
> NoncapturingCatch and ThrowExpression. Grep finds no consumers for them
> anywhere in crates/phpstan-rs/src.
>
> Put the checks in one new module,
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/syntax_versions.rs. It walks AST shapes the
> parser already produces: ExprKind::Match and ArrowFn (ast.rs:1525/1537),
> ObjectOperator::NullsafeArrow (ast.rs:1324), the Pipe binary op (ast.rs:767),
> class kind Enum (ast.rs:502), catch without a variable, throw in expression
> position, and ??=. Gate every check on
> `registry.php_supports_everywhere(f) == Some(false)`, the same way
> type_declarations.rs:180 and oop.rs:1341 do, so nothing is reported when no
> version is known. Emit "X is supported only on PHP A.B and later.", matching
> the wording of the existing gated messages.
>
> Put the type-hint features (mixed, never, static, void, iterable, object,
> nullable, typed properties) into the existing check_type_version_support in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/type_declarations.rs:175. Do not add a second
> walker for them.
>
> Two features are not in the AST. The lexer strips `_` from numbers
> (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:564), so check the literal's span in the source
> text for numeric separators. Trailing commas need either a flag on the
> parser's arg/param lists or a look at the source bytes before the closing
> paren.
>
> For attributes before 8.0, report that the attribute is silently ignored as a
> comment, rather than calling it a parse error.
>
> Report once per construct. Add an opt-out for files loaded only under a
> version guard, such as polyfill-style bootstrap80.php loaded through
> `if (PHP_VERSION_ID >= 80000)`. Either reuse the guard-judging logic the F75
> design plans, or suppress a file when every include of it sits under such a
> guard.
>
> Add fixtures under crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/ that pair a
> composer.json declaring `"php": ">=7.2"` with each construct.

#### K286. Report modifications of readonly properties: compound assignment, ++/--, array write/append, unset

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: property-initialization-readonly)
- **Benefit:** These are certain runtime Errors ('Cannot indirectly modify
  readonly property A::\$arr', verified with php -r). phpstan-rs misses all of
  them today: probe `$this->arr[] = 1; $this->n++; $this->s .= 'z';` is silent,
  and Mago flags each one.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:141`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:598`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:2108`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1683`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs:13`
- **Risks:** The object-intermediate exception must be exact:
  `$this->ro->prop = 1` and `$this->ro[0]->x = 1` (ArrayAccess objects) are
  legal. `??=` on an uninitialized readonly property is a legal initialization
  and must not be treated as a mutation.
- **Verification:** The citations check out. Mago
  crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:141 maps `PropertyWriteKind::Mutation` to
  `PendingCertainty::Invalid(InvalidWriteReason::Mutation)` before it looks at
  the init state. Line 140 returns early for `ArrayAccessMutation` (the
  ArrayAccess-object case).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add
> `check_readonly_modification(&mut self, target: &Expr, kind: ModKind, locals)`
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs, reusing
> `find_property_receiver`, `is_member_access_visible`/`write_visibility` and
> the native vs phpdoc split already used by `check_property_assignment`
> (property_assignment.rs:7-55) and `check_property_assign_by_ref` (:268-336).
> Target resolution: (a) For a direct `PropertyAccess` target (CompoundAssign
> other than `??=`, and Pre/Post Inc/Dec), report
> `Cannot modify readonly property X::$p` (property.readOnlyModify) whenever the
> property is native readonly. Do this in every scope, the constructor included:
> runtime errors there too, because compound needs a prior value, and once the
> property is initialized the write is a modification. (b) For an `Index` target
> (Assign lhs `$this->p[...] = v`, `$this->p[] = v`, nested `$this->p[0][] = v`,
> and index targets of CompoundAssign/IncDec), peel Index layers only. Stop at
> the first PropertyAccess; any PropertyAccess or method call in between ends
> the walk, since `$this->b->x = 1` and `$this->a[0]->x = 1` are legal. Then
> report `Cannot indirectly modify readonly property X::$p` only when that
> property's declared/inferred type cannot hold an object (a pure array or
> scalar), because `$this->o[] = 1` on a readonly ArrayObject is legal (verified
> with php -r). (c) `??=`: send it through the existing
> `native_readonly_assignment` path, not the mutation path. It is a legal
> initialization when the property is uninitialized, and an error once it is
> initialized, even to null (verified). (d) `StmtKind::Unset` (stmt.rs:778 ->
> assignment.rs:571 `check_unset_target`): report
> `Cannot unset readonly property` outside the declaring-class scope. Inside the
> constructor it is legal only while uninitialized, so either skip that case or
> gate it on the existing uninitialized_dataflow.rs facts. Follow-ups on the
> same helper: foreach-by-ref over `$this->ro` and passing `$this->ro` to a
> by-ref parameter (for example `sort($this->ro)`) also raise "Cannot indirectly
> modify" at runtime. Mirror everything for @readonly/@immutable with the phpdoc
> identifiers, but outside the constructor only, since those rules are advisory.
> Call sites: expr.rs CompoundAssign arm (~2108), Pre/Post Inc/Dec arm (~1683),
> the Assign arm next to `check_property_assignment` (~2068) for Index lhs, and
> check_unset_target.

#### K129. Method override compatibility: extra required params, explicit mixed

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Two families of guaranteed class-declaration fatal errors that
  currently pass silently. Both are common during refactors (adding a parameter
  to an implementation, or tightening an interface typed `mixed`).
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/inheritance_param_count_more_required.php:13`,
  `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/inheritance_implementing_method_more_specific_param.php:13`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/method_overrides.rs:453`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/method_overrides.rs:567`
- **Risks:** Needs a parser/reflection flag for 'hint was the literal mixed'.
  Stubs with `mixed` must record it correctly.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are accurate.
  crates/analyzer/tests/cases/inheritance_param_count_more_required.php:12-13
  expects analysis:incompatible-parameter-count on `run(int $a, int $b)`
  implementing `run(int $a)`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> All changes go in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/method_overrides.rs, in
> the parameter loop that starts at line 453. No parser or reflection work is
> needed.
>
> (1) Extra required parameters. After the ancestor loop, go through
> own_sig.params()[ancestor_sig.params().len()..]. Report every parameter that
> has no default and is not variadic, with a new identifier such as
> `parameter.extraRequired`. There is no exemption for a variadic ancestor tail.
> PHP rejects `f(int $a, int $b)` implementing `f(int ...$a)`, and
> `f(int $a, $b=1, ...$r)` implementing `f(int $a, ...$r)` is fine, so optional
> and variadic extras are always legal. Checked with php -r.
>
> (2) Replace the symmetric mixed skip at line 567 with a one-sided rule.
>
> - If own_param.ty_native().is_mixed(), whether untyped or written `mixed`,
>   `continue`. The child accepts everything, which is always legal.
> - If the ancestor's native type is mixed and the child's is not, report
>   `method.childParameterType`. PHP treats an untyped parameter as mixed for
>   this check:
>   `class A{function f($a){}} class B extends A{function f(int $a){}}` is a
>   fatal error. So a user-code ancestor needs no explicit-mixed flag at all.
> - The one false-positive risk is stub (internal) ancestors. There, an untyped
>   phpstorm-stubs parameter may hide a real narrower internal type. For those,
>   report only when ancestor_param.explicit_mixed_hint() is true (or the type
>   is_explicit_mixed()), which catches cases like
>   ArrayAccess::offsetExists(mixed \$offset). Otherwise keep the skip.
> - Rewrite the comment at 553-566, which is wrong: it says PHP does not enforce
>   compatibility for an untyped parameter.
>
> (3) Fix a false positive in the same loop at line 454. When the child's
> parameter list ends in a variadic that covers the ancestor's remaining
> positions, compare those positions against the variadic parameter and don't
> report `parameter.missing`. Today
> `class A{function f($a,$b){}} class B extends A{function f(...$args){}}`
> reports "misses parameter #2 (\$b)", but PHP accepts it.
>
> Add fixture cases for C1 through C5 of the probe.

#### K31. Support class_alias() as a symbol alias in the registry

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: names-symbols, codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Probe names-symbols/a1:
  `class_alias(Original::class, 'Legacy_Original')` followed by
  `function f(Legacy_Original $o)` and `new Legacy_Original()` gives two
  false-positive class.notFound, and member calls lose their types. Mago reports
  nothing. class_alias is a common compatibility idiom in long-lived libraries
  (Twig, PHPUnit and Laminas compat layers), so this removes a class of false
  positives and missing types.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_alias.rs:18`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/mod.rs:475`, `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:133`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:232`, `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:135`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:369`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:1022`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:558`
- **Risks:** An alias declared conditionally or dynamically may not exist at
  runtime; mark such aliases like conditional stubs. Types must display a
  consistent spelling, and resolving aliases to the target name at
  type-construction time keeps Repr::Object equality simple. Alias cycles need a
  bound, as Mago uses at metadata/mod.rs:198-210. | Dynamic class_alias
  arguments must be ignored. An alias that collides with a real class needs a
  rank rule (a real declaration wins, as in Mago's populate_class_like_aliases
  line 172).
- **Verification:** The citations check out, with small line offsets. Mago:
  scan_class_like_alias is at crates/codex/src/scanner/class_alias.rs:18.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/syntax/src/declarations.rs: add
>    `Declared::ClassAlias { original, alias }`, detected in `visit_expr` beside
>    `define_call` (line ~124). Match a call to global `class_alias` whose first
>    two arguments, positional or named `class:`/`alias:`, are each a literal
>    string or a `Name::class` const-fetch (resolved through the file's
>    namespace or use-imports; skip self/static/parent outside a class, and skip
>    any dynamic argument). It takes the same `conditionally` flag as `define`,
>    so a guarded `if (!class_exists('Old')) class_alias(...)` polyfill still
>    counts as a declaration, marked conditional.
> 2. Registry: add `class_aliases: NameTable<Name>` (alias to target). After
>    indexing, in registry/resolve.rs next to `canonicalize_class_name_case`
>    (resolve.rs:49), resolve each alias to its terminal target. Bound the chain
>    walk by the table size so a cycle cannot loop. Drop any alias whose name
>    collides with a real declared class, because the real declaration wins.
>    Extend that same canonicalize pass so
>    `extends`/`implements`/`uses`/`mixins`/`type_imports` that name an alias
>    are rewritten to the target. `class B extends Old_Thing` then gets a
>    working hierarchy at no per-lookup cost.
> 3. `lookup_class` (hierarchy.rs:1022): on a miss, try `class_aliases` and
>    return the target's reflection. At the checker's type-resolution sites
>    (type hints, `new`, `instanceof`, static calls, catch, PHPDoc), build
>    `Type::object(target)` rather than the alias spelling. `Repr::Object`
>    equality and subtyping then need no change, and this matches runtime, where
>    `get_class(new Old)` returns the target name. `Old::class` stays the
>    literal string 'Old', because that is PHP's runtime value too.
> 4. project.rs `declared_names` (line 2153) and the incremental `update_file`
>    path (project.rs:746/1018 already re-run the canonicalize pass): include
>    aliases so that editing or removing the class_alias line invalidates
>    dependents. Record the call span in decl_locations so LSP go-to-definition
>    on `Old_Thing` lands on the class_alias call. Completion and hover can show
>    the target.
> 5. Tests: fixtures covering a namespaced target with a global alias, a
>    named-args form, a guarded conditional alias, an alias chain, an alias used
>    in `extends`, an alias colliding with a real class, and a dynamic argument
>    (must be ignored).

#### K77. Check arguments against template-resolved parameter types and report bound violations

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Catches real runtime errors that are currently invisible: passing
  an int where `T of Countable` or `T of object` is declared means the body's
  `$x->count()` or `get_class($x)` fatals. It also catches every mismatch where
  the same template appears twice and the resolved type rejects one argument
  (see the invariant pinning idea).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:622`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:921`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:1177`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:304`,
  `crates/types/src/relation/accepts.rs:840`, `crates/types/src/templates.rs:49`
- **Risks:** Templates of the enclosing generic body (the caller's T, carried as
  TemplateParam in argument types) must keep their current leniency, or real
  code inside generic classes gets false positives. Scope-aware filtering needs
  the qualified template identity from the declared-template-list idea. Some new
  findings will appear on the corpus, which is expected.
- **Verification:** Every citation checks out, with small line offsets. - Mago
  analyzer.rs: `resolve_parameter_type_for_invocation` is at about lines 622-629
  and `verify_argument_type` at about 637-644.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Stage 1, bounds only (low risk). In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs check_parameters (around
> lines 290-316), before `rule_level_accepts(&param_ty, &arg_ty)`, rewrite
> `param_ty` so that each of the callee's OWN function/method templates is
> replaced by its declared bound. Do this only where the template sits in a
> covariant position of the parameter type: a bare `T`, `list<T>`, `array<K,V>`,
> a shape field, a union or intersection member, or a generic object argument
> whose class template is covariant. Inside a callable/Closure parameter list,
> or an invariant generic argument, leave the TemplateParam alone so the
> existing escape still applies. Build this on the existing
> `substitute_templates_resolving_to_bounds`
> (crates/types/src/templates.rs:397), which `check_default_parameter_types` in
> checker/function_decl.rs:1492 already uses in the same way. Pass a
> polarity-aware walker, or a `to_bound` predicate limited to the callee's
> template scope, so class templates of an enclosing generic body stay opaque.
> Leave the `(_, Repr::TemplateParam(_))` arm in
> crates/types/src/relation/accepts.rs:840 as it is: it still has to cover the
> enclosing class's T (for example `$this->set($y)` inside `Box<T>`), and once
> the callee's own templates are resolved they no longer reach it. Report the
> result as the usual argument.type, or as a dedicated `argument.templateType`
> message ("Parameter #1 \$x of function cnt() expects T of Countable, int
> given"), which names the template and its bound. Stage 2 (optional, after this
> is solid): also substitute the inferred bindings from
> `Relation::infer_template_bindings` (the call's bindings are already computed
> for the return type near checker/expr.rs:4670/5095, so compute them once per
> call and share them). This catches mismatches between two arguments that share
> a template in an invariant position. Gate it on the binding for that template
> having been inferred from a non-closure argument, so a closure literal whose
> own inference was imprecise can't create a false positive.

#### K131. Trait property composition compatibility

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Closes a family of load-time fatals. Mago's tests list 14
  incompatible-property-default and 11 incompatible-property-visibility sites
  that phpstan-rs misses.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:182`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:640`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:641`
- **Risks:** Defaults must be compared by evaluated value (`[1,2,3]` vs
  `[1,2,4]`, `'42'` vs `42` differ). Unresolvable constant defaults should be
  treated as unknown, not as different.
- **Verification:** Mago: the enum PropertyConflict is at
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:170-177. Line 182 is inside
  describe(), not the enum. The issue-code mapping at 217-224 is correct.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Rewrite `check_trait_conflicts` in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:625
> into a property-compatibility check that runs whenever `info.uses()` is
> non-empty (not only when there are 2 or more traits). It should cover (a)
> every pair of used traits and (b) the class's own declared property against
> each used trait's property of the same name. PHP's message uses the class name
> as the first party in case (b).
>
> Build the predicate from existing PropertyReflection fields
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:49 onward):
>
> - visibility and write_visibility
> - is_static
> - is_readonly
> - has_native_type
> - has_default
> - has_get_hook / has_set_hook: any hook on either side counts as incompatible
>
> Compare `ty_native` (class_info.rs ~line 147), not `ty()`. The phpdoc-merged
> `ty()` in use now gives a false positive today. My probe was
> `trait T1 { /** @var list<int> */ public array $a = []; } trait T2 { public
> array $a = []; } class C1 { use T1, T2; }`:
> phpstan-rs reports `trait.propertyConflict`, but `php -r` runs it fine.
>
> Remove the `resolved_trait_conflicts().contains(prop_name)` skip at
> oop.rs:641. `insteadof`/`as` apply only to methods, so a same-named method
> adaptation hides a real property fatal. Probe: T5 `public string $r`, T6
> `public int $r`, `use T5, T6 { T5::r insteadof T6; }` gives no report.
>
> For defaults, the registry keeps only `has_default: bool`. You need one of two
> things:
>
> - store the default as a constant-evaluated Type when you build the registry,
>   or
> - look up the PropertyDecl default expression from the AST at check time and
>   evaluate it with the existing constant-expression evaluator.
>
> Compare the evaluated values strictly (1 vs 1.0 and '42' vs 42 differ; [1,2]
> vs [1,2] is the same). A class or global constant that resolves to the same
> value is compatible: PHP accepts
> `const X=1; trait T{public $a=X;} class C{use T; public $a=1;}`. If either
> side cannot be evaluated, treat it as unknown and stay silent.
>
> Handle implicit null:
>
> - `public $a;` with no type and no default equals `public $a = null;` (PHP
>   accepts it).
> - `public ?int $u;` with no default does not equal `public ?int $u = null;`
>   (PHP fatal, verified).
>
> Keep the identifier `trait.propertyConflict`, and name the differing attribute
> in the message (type / visibility / static / readonly / default / hook). Add
> fixtures for:
>
> - the trait-pair variants
> - the class-vs-trait variants
> - the insteadof-alias case
> - the phpdoc-only difference, which must stay silent
> - the constant-equal default, which must stay silent

#### K134. Offset reads on null, string offsets, false auto-vivification, null keys

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Covers the most common source of 'Trying to access array offset
  on null' warnings, plus a TypeError and two deprecations on the path to PHP 9.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:293`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:350`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:511`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:151`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/relation/kinds.rs:44`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:697`
- **Risks:** PHPStan treats null as offset-accessible on purpose. Diverging is
  fine (parity is not a goal) but may be noisy. Keep the possibly-null variant
  at level 8 like the other nullable rules.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are accurate. In
  crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs: NullArrayIndex is at about line
  151 (fires when index_type.is_null()).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split into what's actually missing; one of the four parts already exists.
>
> (a) Null container reads (main value). In
> crates/types/src/relation/kinds.rs:39-45 (`is_offset_accessible`), move
> `leaf.is_null()` out of the Yes arm so null returns No, the same answer false
> already gets through `is_scalar_or_null`. The only caller is
> check_offset_accessibility (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:722).
> Its `failing_level` call
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/rule_level_helper.rs:34-50) then already gives
> base level 3 for a definite null and level 8 for `?array`. Pick a distinct
> identifier/message for null (e.g. `offsetAccess.onNull`, "Trying to access
> array offset on null") instead of reusing nonOffsetAccessible's "Cannot access
> offset on null". isset/??/??= are already covered because
> check_expr_quiet_root
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/probe_checks.rs:41-65) never calls it.
> Nullsafe chains are already covered by chain_link_type (expr.rs:2289-2293).
> What's missing is a write-context guard. CompoundAssign (expr.rs:2108-2143)
> sends its lhs through check_expr, which reaches check_offset_accessibility
> (expr.rs:2298). So `$n = null; $n['z'] .= 'x'` would become a false positive:
> PHP 8.5 auto-vivifies silently and only warns "Undefined array key". The same
> applies to `++`/`--` on an offset, by-reference args, and `=& $n['a']`. Add an
> in-write-target flag (or a separate path) so these skip the null arm. On those
> paths false should become (c) instead of "Cannot access offset on false",
> which already fires today (probe: `$g=false; $g['z'] .= 'x'`).
>
> (b) Non-numeric string offset on a string. Don't route this through
> has_offset_value_type/notFound (crates/types/src/offsets.rs:13, whose
> `_ => Maybe` arm covers strings): "Offset 'foo' does not exist on string" is
> the wrong diagnosis. Add a string-container arm next to
> check_dim_fetch_key_type (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:630,
> which currently returns early unless the base is an array). A constant
> non-numeric string key on a definite-string base is a TypeError ("Cannot
> access offset of type string on string"). A leading-numeric key like '1x' only
> warns ("Illegal string offset"), so treat it as a lower-severity variant. Use
> failing_level for string|array unions. Skip quiet roots, since
> isset(\$s['foo']) is just false.
>
> (c) False to array on write. Add `PhpFeature::DeprecatesFalseAutovivification`
> in crates/types/src/php_version.rs, next to DeprecatesNullArrayOffset (line
> 252). In the assignment-target/compound/append write path, report writing
> through a false-typed container using failing_level (definite false at base,
> array|false at 7), gated on the same "deprecated" helper pattern as
> invalid_array_key_description.
>
> (d) Already implemented. invalid_array_key_description
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5494-5525) reports a null key under
> DeprecatesNullArrayOffset. A probe with `--php-version 8.5` reports
> `$arr[null] = 1` and `$arr[null]` as offsetAccess.invalidOffset. The original
> probe was silent only because no PHP version was set. The only gap is a
> nullable key (`?string $k`), because a legal member makes the whole function
> return None. An optional level-8 "possibly null key" extension is the only
> remaining work here.

#### K140. Dynamic property creation deprecation

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Typos in property writes (`$this->nmae = $x`) are silent today.
  They are deprecated since 8.2 and will be errors in PHP 9.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/tests/cases/classes_unknown_property_write.php:13`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs:20`
- **Risks:** Legacy codebases set many dynamic properties on purpose, so it
  needs its own identifier and a level (or opt-in) so it can be baselined.
- **Verification:** No wrong citations. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/tests/cases/classes_unknown_property_write.php:12-13 has
  `/** @mago-expect analysis:non-existent-property */ $obj->bar = 1;` on a final
  class that only declares `$foo`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a write-side undefined-property check in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs, in the
> `find_property_receiver(...) else { return; }` branch (line 20-25). Reuse the
> read side's machinery: `member_confirmed_missing`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:258), which already has
> union=any / intersection=all semantics and only fires on a single known
> registered class. Its `has_member` closure should be true when any of these
> holds: `lookup_property(c, prop)` finds it (this already covers @property tags
> and inherited props), `lookup_method(c, "__set")` exists, the class or an
> ancestor is `stdClass`, the class or an ancestor has
> `#[AllowDynamicProperties]`, or the Pest `$this` hook-property case applies.
> Also honour the `property_exists()` guard the read arm uses (expr.rs ~2957).
> The #[AllowDynamicProperties] flag needs a new field on the class reflection
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs, filled from class attributes
> through the existing `is_allow_dynamic_properties_attribute_name`
> (registry/function_sig.rs:566) and checked with ancestor inheritance.
> Reporting has three cases. (a) The receiver is a readonly class or an enum:
> report a level-0 error, since PHP throws "Cannot create dynamic property". Use
> `class_info.rs` `is_readonly()`. (b) Otherwise report at level 2 with its own
> identifier `property.dynamicCreation` (not `property.notFound`), so a legacy
> codebase can ignore or baseline it separately. Word the message as "Creation
> of dynamic property C::\$p is deprecated" when the configured php_version is
> 8.2 or later (add a PhpFeature variant in crates/types/src/php_version.rs).
> Below 8.2, word it as an undefined-property write, because a typo is still a
> typo. (c) A mixed or non-object receiver keeps the existing property.nonObject
> path. Add fixtures for: a final class, a non-final class with `$this->typo`,
> `__set`, stdClass and subclasses of it, the attribute inherited from a parent,
> a readonly class, a union with one member missing the property, and a
> property_exists guard.

#### K186. Property semantics provider with Doctrine implementation

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Removes a real false positive on every Doctrine entity with a
  generated id or ORM-hydrated field, which is common in general PHP. It also
  gives DI and serializer frameworks a principled escape hatch that is more
  precise than a baseline or ignore entry.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/provider/property.rs:13`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:1515`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:1554`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/initialization.rs:272`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:360`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info/doctrine_entity.rs:45`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized.rs:42`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:2948`
- **Risks:** An over-broad attribute rule could hide genuinely unused
  properties, so keep the flags separate (read, written and initialized are
  different claims, as Mago's docs stress) and match attributes by
  fully-qualified name only. Doctrine XML/YAML mapping isn't modeled; this stays
  attribute-only, consistent with doctrine_entity.rs.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are accurate, with two caveats. First,
  Mago ships no native implementation of this trait: grep finds no
  `impl PropertyInitializationProvider` anywhere in crates/.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Core fix, which is S to M: add a read/written exemption for ORM-managed
> properties in `report_unused_property`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:346-364). Next to
> `tag_always_read`/`tag_always_written`, OR in `orm_managed(fqn, name)` when
> `[ext.doctrine]` is active (ext/doctrine.rs, `config::Extension`). A property
> is ORM-managed when its own attributes carry an FQN-resolved
> `Doctrine\ORM\Mapping\{Column, Id, ManyToOne, OneToOne, OneToMany, ManyToMany,
> Embedded, Version}`,
> and its class carries `Entity`, `MappedSuperclass` or `Embeddable`. Don't key
> it on `DoctrineEntity::fields`. That map is filled for every property before
> the `Column` check (registry/class_info/doctrine_entity.rs:236-237), so
> unmapped properties would be exempted too. It also doesn't exist for
> `MappedSuperclass`/`Embeddable`, because `compute_doctrine_entity` returns
> None without `#[ORM\Entity]` (:203). Better: record a
> `mapped: FxHashSet<Name>` (column_names keys ∪ associations ∪ ids) in
> doctrine_entity.rs and extend the extraction to MappedSuperclass/Embeddable.
> Or add a small helper that shares `find_orm_attribute`. Treat mapped
> properties as both read (flush/UnitOfWork reads them through reflection) and
> written (hydration writes them).
>
> For `check_uninitialized_properties` (checker/uninitialized.rs:42, opt-in via
> rules_settings.rs:20), exempt only a `GeneratedValue` id, a composite id
> included. Don't exempt every mapped field. `new User()` without setting
> `$name` really does leave it uninitialized at runtime, so that report is
> correct.
>
> Second part, which is M: add a declarative `[[property_semantics]]` config
> table with `attribute` (FQN), optional `class` (with descendants) and optional
> `property`, and separate `read`/`written`/`initialized` flags. It would cover
> Symfony `#[Required]`, JMS/Serializer and similar. Consult it at the same two
> sites. A full trait with native and external providers, as in Mago's
> plugin/provider/property.rs:13 and registry.rs:1515, is only worth building
> once there is a second native implementation. Moving the Pest `beforeEach`
> special case (checker/expr.rs:2940) behind the trait is churn with no
> user-visible gain, so drop it from scope.

#### K224. Source exclude paths and --exclude flag

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Real projects have generated code, fixtures with intentional
  errors, compiled templates and legacy trees. Today the only choices are
  listing every wanted directory in `paths` or checking the files and then
  hiding results with ignore_errors, which still pays parse and check cost and
  can still crash on those files. Pruning also removes walk cost for large
  excluded trees.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/database/src/matcher.rs:173`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:108`, `crates/database/src/loader.rs:497`,
  `src/config/analyzer.rs:30`, `crates/database/src/matcher.rs:134`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:44`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2085`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2093`
- **Risks:** 'Excluded from analysis' has to stay distinct from 'excluded from
  context'. Excluding a file that declares symbols used elsewhere must not
  produce class-not-found errors, which is why the analyse/scan split is
  proposed. The glob dialect also has to be documented.
- **Verification:** Mago: ExclusionMatcher::compile is at
  crates/database/src/matcher.rs:93 and build_glob_set at matcher.rs:54. It
  returns DatabaseError::InvalidGlobSet, as documented at lines 89-91.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `exclude_paths` to SessionSettings
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:44). It takes two forms: a plain
> list, which excludes files from analysis only, or a table
> `{ analyse = [..], analyse_and_scan = [..] }`. Add a repeatable `--exclude`
> flag in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs next to `scan_dirs` (line
> ~102), merged through `Overrides` (session.rs:69).
>
> Resolve relative patterns against the config file's directory with the
> existing `resolve_against_config`. Compile them once in `Session::resolve`
> into a small `PathExclusion { prefixes: Vec<PathBuf>, globs: Vec<String> }`:
>
> - A pattern with no wildcard is a component-wise prefix match, so `gen`
>   matches `gen/x.php` but not `gen-old/`.
> - A pattern with a wildcard reuses `ignore_errors::glob_matches`
>   (crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:96). That keeps one glob dialect for
>   both `ignore_errors.path` and excludes, so no globset dependency is needed.
> - Match against both the root-relative spelling and the canonical absolute
>   path.
> - Report a missing literal (non-glob) path as a config warning, the way
>   `config.warnings()` already does.
>
> Apply it in `Session::collect_php_files` / `Session::load` (session.rs:554 and
> :590):
>
> - `analyse`-excluded files are moved from `analyze_files` into
>   `context_files`, so the symbols they declare still resolve and there is no
>   class-not-found fallout.
> - `analyse_and_scan` excludes are pruned while walking. Give
>   `collect_php_files_excluding` (project.rs:2106) a predicate that takes the
>   full path instead of the name-only `&[&str]`, so excluded trees are never
>   read or parsed.
>
> The LSP workspace load uses the same matcher
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:490-516), and so does `Project::update_file`'s
> default classification, which currently uses `path_under_excluded_dir`.
> `DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` stays as the LSP's default floor.
>
> Add fixture/unit tests for three cases:
>
> - prefix vs `gen-old`
> - a glob
> - an analyse-excluded file whose class is used from an analysed file, which
>   must produce no unknown-class error
>
> Mago's crates/database/src/loader.rs:108 turns `x/**` into a prune pattern.
> That optimization is only needed if the glob dialect is kept. With
> prefix-plus-fnmatch semantics, a literal prefix prunes naturally.

#### K49. Record PHP-version availability (@since/@removed, ElementAvailable) on built-in symbols and report unavailable usage

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: codebase-model, stubs-prelude,
  analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Catches real fatal errors ('Call to undefined function
  array_is_list()' on PHP 8.0) in libraries that declare a PHP range in
  composer.json. Signature choice becomes correct for projects pinned to older
  PHP. | Catches runtime fatals ('Call to undefined function') when code uses
  APIs newer or older than the project's supported PHP range, for example
  composer `php: >=7.4` code calling str_contains or array_is_list.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/version_constraint.rs:14`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/availability.rs:19`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:1`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/availability.rs:68`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:481`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/mago.php:19` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/stub_attributes.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs:138`,
  `vendor/phpstorm-stubs/standard/standard_9.php:866`,
  `types/src/php_version.rs:59`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:652`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:946`
- **Risks:** Polyfills (symfony/polyfill-\*) legitimately define these functions
  for older versions. A project-level conditional declaration of the same name
  must suppress the report, which the registry's conditional tracking can
  already tell. phpstorm-stubs @since tags are sometimes imprecise. |
  phpstorm-stubs @since tags are occasionally wrong or record a PECL version
  rather than a PHP version (for extension functions), so limit the tags to core
  and bundled extensions or cross-check with PhpStormStubsElementAvailable.
- **Verification:** Almost every citation checks out. Corrections and nuances:
  (a) Mago's use-site check_availability
  (crates/analyzer/src/utils/availability.rs:19-35) calls
  version_constraint.allows_version(context.settings.version), which tests a
  single version.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep the version data instead of throwing it away. Right now
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/stub_attributes.rs (header lines 1-13) applies
> PhpStormStubsElementAvailable and LanguageLevelTypeAware for the newest PHP
> version only, then deletes them. Instead, while stripping, record an
> availability range set: a Vec of (Option\<PhpVersion>, Option\<PhpVersion>)
> intervals, merged with the `@since X.Y` / `@removed X.Y` doc tags (for example
> vendor/phpstorm-stubs/standard/standard_9.php:866 `@since 8.1` on
> array_is_list). Store it on built-in function, class, method, class-constant,
> enum-case and global-constant reflections. A closed-range (`to:`) declaration
> should be kept as a "removed" marker rather than dropped, so messages can say
> "removed in PHP 8.0". Trust `@since` only for core and bundled extensions; for
> PECL extensions it can record the extension's own version, so rely on
> ElementAvailable there.
>
> Add one checker rule (function.unavailable, class.unavailable,
> staticMethod/method.unavailable, constant.unavailable) that fires only when
> Registry.php_versions is Some (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs:138; set from
> config or composer). Compare the symbol's ranges with PhpVersions
> (crates/types/src/php_version.rs) and report two cases: missing on every
> configured version, or missing on some. Suppress it when:
>
> - a non-stub declaration of the name exists anywhere in the project or vendor.
>   Polyfills are merged onto stub entries (registry/index.rs:112-150,
>   built_in_stub_classes), so availability has to stay a stub-only attribute
>   that any user or vendor declaration overrides.
> - guarded_functions, guarded_classes or guarded_constants cover the name (used
>   at checker/expr.rs:909 and rule.rs:138).
> - a PHP_VERSION_ID or version_compare(PHP_VERSION, ...) branch narrowed the
>   range. Add a scope-level PhpVersions narrowed with
>   PhpVersions::narrow_at_least (php_version.rs:94).
>
> Treat the second half, choosing version-specific LanguageLevelTypeAware
> signatures for the configured minimum version, as a separate follow-up. It
> changes the types in every checked file and needs its own regression pass.

#### K127. Report throw of non-objects

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Catches a guaranteed runtime fatal (`throw $errorCode`,
  `throw "message"`) that is currently silent at every level.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/throw.rs:66`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:174`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:382`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1897`
- **Risks:** Very low. Mixed must stay unreported, or go only through
  strict_mixed_receiver_level.
- **Verification:** All cited locations are accurate. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/throw.rs:56-81 loops over every atomic of the
  thrown type; any atomic where `extends_or_implements(codebase, b"Throwable")`
  is false is reported as IssueCode::InvalidThrow (report at ~line 66).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Replace the object-only early return in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:157
> thrown_value_not_throwable with a per-member classifier, and have both callers
> (stmt/try_catch.rs:382 and expr.rs:1897) report through Checker::failing_level
> (checker.rs:973, which calls rule_level_helper.rs:34) with base 0 instead of
> the hard-coded level 0.
>
> Classifier `thrown_member_fails(m) -> bool`:
>
> - Scalars, arrays or shapes, null, resources, void and never-returning values
>   fail. Never itself should not fail, because the throw is unreachable.
> - A known class that is not a subclass of Throwable (the current
>   is_subclass_of test) fails.
> - An enum case fails.
> - A closure fails, since Closure does not implement Throwable.
> - These pass: mixed, a generic `object`, a template or its bound, an
>   unresolvable class name (keep the existing guard for scoped or vendored
>   names), any Throwable subtype, and interfaces not known to be unrelated.
> - For an intersection, it fails only if every part fails, as now.
>
> Message: build it from the member's describe(), for example "cannot throw
> string: only objects implementing Throwable can be thrown", with the
> identifier kept as throw.notThrowable.
>
> Levels:
>
> - `throw 'x'` and `throw $int` report at 0.
> - int|Exception reports at 7.
> - ?Exception reports at 8.
> - mixed stays silent, or is routed through strict_mixed_receiver_level
>   (checker.rs:994) only at level 10 if you want that.
>
> This also fixes a current inconsistency: Foo|Exception is reported at level 0
> today because the union branch runs find_map over the members.
>
> Add fixture cases for the same things as the probe:
>
> - the string literal
> - an int parameter
> - ?Exception
> - int|Exception
> - mixed
> - `$x ?? throw 'y'` (the expression form)
> - a template T of Throwable
> - a closure
>
> Tests should cover this module and the fixtures only.

#### K128. Check yield key/value against Generator types

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Generator element types are the most-used generic in PHP code.
  Today the declared Generator\<K,V> is trusted but never enforced at the yield
  sites that produce it.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/yield.rs:77`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/yield.rs:130`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/yield.rs:410`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1949`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow/generators.rs:114`
- **Risks:** The implicit-key type has to follow PHP semantics (auto-increment
  int). Untyped or bare Generator declarations must stay exempt, as the
  yield-from path already does.
- **Verification:** The citations hold, give or take a few lines. In Mago's
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/yield.rs, the value is checked with
  union_comparator::is_contained_by at about line 77 and reported as
  IssueCode::InvalidYieldValueType just before line 102.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs, in the ExprKind::Yield arm (line
>    1949), keep the types that check_expr returns for the key and the value. If
>    current_declared_return_type is set and not mixed, get enclosing_key and
>    enclosing_value from generator_template_param(.., "TKey"/"TYield")
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow/generators.rs:53). Report under
>    generator.valueType or generator.keyType when a param is not mixed and
>    !rule_level_accepts(param, actual).yes(). Use the same gate and messages as
>    check_yield_from_compatibility (generators.rs:136-160), and put the helper
>    in generators.rs next to it (e.g. check_yield_compatibility). A bare
>    `yield;` yields null. A missing key is the auto-increment key, typed as
>    `int`; a narrower type would only matter for exotic TKey declarations. 2)
>    In check_yield_from_compatibility (generators.rs:114), when inner_ty is not
>    Generator-shaped, fall back to the array or iterable key and value types
>    (Type::array_key_type in crates/types/src/queries.rs:794 and the matching
>    value/iterable-element queries). Check those against enclosing TKey/TYield
>    only, since a non-Generator has no TSend. 3) Optional follow-up:
>    generator_template_param only resolves Generator bindings. Also resolving
>    TKey/TValue from a declared `iterable<K,V>`, `Iterator<K,V>` or
>    `Traversable<K,V>` return would cover the many generators declared that
>    way. 4) Report `yield`/`yield from` with no enclosing function-like as a
>    non-ignorable error. PHP rejects it at compile time ("The \"yield\"
>    expression can only be used inside a function"). Check how Checker tracks
>    the current function-like and make sure closures and arrow functions count
>    as enclosing. Test fixtures: a scalar mismatch, an implicit int key into
>    Generator\<string,..>, `yield from [1=>'v']` into Generator\<string,..>,
>    and bare, untyped or mixed-param Generators staying silent.

#### K137. ::class/::CONST/::\$prop on non-class expressions

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Closes an asymmetry: static calls through bad receivers are
  checked, constant and property fetches through the same receivers are not.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/class_constant.rs:178`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/class_name.rs:396`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:2867`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:6048`
- **Risks:** Low. A string is legal for `$s::CONST` and `$s::$p` (class-string),
  so only `::class` on a string is invalid.
- **Verification:** Almost all citations check out. - Mago
  crates/analyzer/src/resolver/class_constant.rs:176-188:
  `handle_class_magic_constant` reports IssueCode::InvalidClassConstantOnString
  when `class_resolution.origin` is ResolutionOrigin::AnyString.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add receiver and scope checks to the three static-member forms that currently
> skip them. Reuse the pattern already in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/static_call_context.rs:55-67 (`failing_level`
> combined with `relation().can_name_a_class(m).no()`, which already handles
> mixed/union receivers per level). (1) crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs
> check_static_member_fetch (~6048-6056): in the StaticTarget::Expr arm, before
> `receiver_class(...)`, report `classConstant.nonObject` (or
> `staticProperty.nonObject` when is_property) if can_name_a_class is No.
> Strings and class-strings stay legal here. (2) expr.rs
> ExprKind::ClassNameFetch (~2867): for StaticTarget::Expr, report
> `classConstant.classOnNonObject` when the receiver's is-object check is No.
> This covers string, int, null and so on, since PHP 8 throws
> `TypeError: Cannot use "::class" on string`. Nullable objects (`?A`) are
> flagged at the level `failing_level` already uses for maybe-null. Keep the
> current class-string/Type::string() result type. (3) For StaticTarget::Name
> with self/static/parent outside a class scope, route ClassNameFetch,
> ClassConstFetch, StaticPropertyFetch and DynamicStaticPropertyFetch through
> the same `outOfClass.{keyword}` report that static_call_context.rs:35 and
> instantiation.rs:41 already use. Factor it into one shared helper so all of
> these paths share it. Tests: add fixtures for `$s::class`, `$i::class`,
> `$i::FOO`, `$i::$st`, `$a::class` with `?A`, and
> `self::class`/`self::FOO`/`static::$st` inside a plain function. Also add
> negative cases: `$s::FOO` with a string or class-string receiver,
> `$obj::class`, and `static::class` inside a closure bound in a class.

#### K150. Report short (\<?) and misspelled open tags that leave code unanalyzed

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness,
  linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Stops whole regions of code from silently going unchecked, and
  warns about code leaking to output, which is a security issue on servers with
  short_open_tag=Off. | Real runtime bug. Probe:
  `<html><? echo undefined_fn($x); ?></html>` gets 0 diagnostics from
  phpstan-rs, and PHP 8.5 (short_open_tag off by default) prints the source
  verbatim to the client. The whole region is currently an analysis blind spot.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/invalid_open_tag.rs:92`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_short_opening_tag.rs:90`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:427`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:417`
- **Risks:** Real templates can contain `<?xml` in inline HTML. Exclude `<?xml`.
  | `<?xml` declarations in templates must be excluded, as must a `<?` inside
  inline HTML text (e.g. JS strings). Limit to `<?` followed by
  whitespace/newline.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are correct. INVALID_TAGS is at
  crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/invalid_open_tag.rs:22 and targets
  NodeKind::Inline, with the check logic about 92-110 trimming leading
  whitespace before matching.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a new check to crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/whitespace.rs (or a sibling
> module such as open_tag.rs). whitespace.rs is the right place because it
> already inspects StmtKind::InlineHtml text for BOM and fileStart/fileEnd.
> Unlike check_file_whitespace, the check must visit every InlineHtml statement,
> including ones nested in if/foreach/function bodies (template code). It can
> hook the existing statement walk, or use a visitor from
> crates/syntax/src/visit.rs, which already reaches InlineHtml at :110 and :856.
> For each InlineHtml text: (a) Find every `<?` followed by ASCII whitespace or
> end of text and report `phpTag.short`, e.g. "Short open tag \<? is not a PHP
> tag when short_open_tag=Off (the default); the code after it is output
> verbatim and is not analyzed." A `<?` followed by a letter, such as `<?xml` or
> `<?xml-stylesheet`, is not flagged, since those are legitimate XML processing
> instructions and flagging them would cause false positives. `<?php` and `<?=`
> never reach InlineHtml anyway, as seen in crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:427-429.
> (b) Case-insensitively find Mago's typo set `<php?`, `<ph?p`, `<p?hp`, when
> followed by whitespace, and report `phpTag.misspelled`. The span is the
> InlineHtml statement's start offset plus the match's byte offset within the
> text, with a length of 2 (or the typo's length). No lexer change is needed;
> this stays purely a checker rule. A fix-it rewriting `<?` to `<?php` can go
> through the LSP code-action path. Leave the optional `short_open_tag = true`
> config, which would make the lexer enter PHP mode at `<?`, as a separate
> follow-up. It needs lexer state plumbed from config, and a warning already
> closes the blind spot. Add fixtures for: `<? echo $x; ?>` (flagged),
> `<?xml version="1.0"?>` inside HTML (not flagged), `<?` inside a PHP string
> (not inline HTML, so never seen), a nested template
> `<?php if ($a): ?> <? foo(); ?> <?php endif; ?>` (flagged), and `<php?\n`
> (flagged).

#### K152. Empty loop body and stray-semicolon loops

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Catches the classic stray-semicolon bug precisely. Purity
  information avoids Mago's false positives on `while (next($a));`-style loops.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_empty_loop.rs:93`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:43`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:1`
- **Risks:** Part (b) needs purity knowledge. Keep it opt-in.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with two small precision notes.
  In mago/crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_empty_loop.rs, line 93 is
  `fn check`. It targets For, Foreach, While and DoWhile, including the
  colon-delimited bodies.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Part (a) is the valuable part. Ship it always on, as a syntactic check in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs, with the `if` handling in the
> stmt.rs dispatch. The check fires when a control statement's body is the empty
> statement. The parser builds that as StmtKind::Block(Vec::new()) whose span is
> the one `;` byte (crates/syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:43-45), so `{}` can be told
> apart by span length or by the first source byte. It applies when the next
> sibling statement is a braced Block, or when the next statement starts on the
> same line as the header. It fires for foreach, for, while and if/elseif/else,
> not just loops. The probe shows `if ($a > 1); { echo 1; }` is also silent
> today. Identifiers: `loop.straySemicolon` and `if.straySemicolon`. Message:
> "Body of \<kind> is an empty statement; the following block runs
> unconditionally/once after it". Offer a quick fix that deletes the `;` and
> attach it to the existing LSP code-action plumbing. Leave `do ; while(...)`
> alone. Part (b) should be narrower than proposed and opt-in only. It flags an
> empty-bodied foreach/for/while only when the whole header (init, cond and
> step) has no side effects visible outside the loop, using registry/purity.rs
> for calls. The step must not assign outer variables. This keeps the idiomatic
> search loops out of scope, such as
> `for ($i = 0; $i < $n && $a[$i] !== $x; $i++);` and `while (next($a));`. Mago
> flags both, which is a false positive, because \$i is live after the loop. An
> empty foreach over an array that isn't a Generator and isn't taken by
> reference is a real no-op. The only thing it can do is leave the key/value
> variables set, so exempt the case where those variables are read after the
> loop. Fixtures: stray `;` + block for each construct, with no diagnostic for
> `while (next($a));`, for-search loops, `for(;;);`, alt-syntax `endwhile` with
> empty body, or `{}` bodies. Part (a) needs no purity at all.

#### K287. Promoted readonly property re-initialized by the parent constructor

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: property-initialization-readonly)
- **Benefit:** Catches a certain runtime Error ('Cannot modify readonly property
  K::\$id', verified) caused by a plausible refactoring (re-declaring a parent's
  promoted property in the child). phpstan-rs is silent and Mago reports it.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:278`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:356`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs:160`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized_dataflow.rs:127`
- **Risks:** The parent's writes must be computed from the actual ancestor body.
  Private parent properties are separate slots and must be excluded (Mago
  :336-341).
- **Verification:** All the citations are accurate, with small clarifications.
  In Mago, check_parent_constructor_reinitializations is at
  crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:274 (the doc comment is at 270-273).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a standalone class-level check, `check_promoted_readonly_parent_reinit`,
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs next to
> `check_parent_constructor_call` (:1653), and call it from the same class pass.
> It should not wait on the separate double-init idea.
>
> 1. Take the class's own constructor (`c.def.constructor()`). Collect its
>    promoted params whose promotion is readonly, or whose class is readonly. Go
>    on only if the body contains `parent::__construct(...)`. Reuse the existing
>    `body_calls_parent_construct` (oop.rs:1910).
> 2. Resolve the parent's effective constructor: walk up the ancestors until one
>    declares `__construct`. For that class, the written set is:
>    - its own promoted params;
