>    - the `$this->x = ...` and `$this->x ??= ...` targets in its body, plus any
>      private/final `$this->helper()` bodies it calls (the absorption
>      uninitialized_dataflow.rs already does);
>    - recursively, the set for its own `parent::__construct()` if it contains
>      one. Guard the recursion with a visited set.
> 3. For each child promoted readonly name in that set, look up the declaring
>    ancestor's property. Skip it when that property is private, because it is a
>    separate slot. Report at the child param with a secondary label at the
>    ancestor declaration. Suggested message: "Readonly property K::\$id is
>    promoted here but also initialized by parent::\_\_construct(); the second
>    write throws Error". The fix hint: drop the promotion and pass the value as
>    a plain param.
> 4. Add fixture tests for:
>    - parent promoted;
>    - parent explicit assign;
>    - grandparent via an inherited ctor;
>    - a private parent property (must not fire; probe verified K3 runs fine);
>    - a parent writing through a helper;
>    - no parent::\_\_construct call (must not fire). Keep it always-on: a hit
>      is a certain or near-certain runtime Error, not a style issue. Writes in
>      the parent that are conditional still count, since they make a reachable
>      Error.

#### K288. Check readonly properties that are never initialized

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: property-initialization-readonly)
- **Benefit:**
  `final class G { public readonly int $r; public function __construct() {} }`
  is silent in phpstan-rs. Every read of `$r` throws at runtime, and since it is
  readonly it can never be assigned from outside the class, so this is one of
  the most certain uninitialized-property bugs there is.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/initialization.rs:235`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized.rs:47`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized_dataflow.rs:224`
- **Risks:** Readonly properties hydrated by reflection or serializers
  (Doctrine, Symfony serializer) would be reported. The property-semantics
  provider / always-written tag (unused.rs:361 already reads always_written)
  should suppress them.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with small clarifications. Mago:
  `fn property_requires_initialization` is at
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/initialization.rs:235-307.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Scope: the opt-in `rules.check_uninitialized_properties` pass, with the same
> `property.uninitialized` identifier. (1)
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized.rs:50: remove `p.is_readonly` from
> the skip condition. The "assigned anywhere in the class or its ancestors" test
> (`property_assigned_anywhere_in_hierarchy`) is enough for readonly properties,
> because an assignment made from the wrong scope is already reported by
> `property.readOnlyAssignNotInConstructor`. Use a readonly-specific message
> such as "G has an uninitialized readonly property \$r. Assign it in the
> constructor." Also rewrite the doc comment at lines 30-40, which says readonly
> properties are a separate check. They aren't: the existing readonly checks
> only police where assignments happen, and nothing reports a readonly property
> that is never assigned. (2)
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized_dataflow.rs:224-225: remove
> `!p.is_readonly && !c.is_readonly` from `trackable()`. Also remove the
> matching readonly exclusions at lines 133-134, so that promoted readonly
> parameters and readonly-class promotions count as initialized up front.
> Without that, a promoted readonly property read in the constructor would be a
> false positive. For unset handling on a readonly property, keep the current
> rule that `unset($this->p)` makes it uninitialized, but only while it is still
> uninitialized. That matches the lazy-init pattern (unset in the constructor,
> initialize in `__get`). An unset of an initialized readonly property throws,
> so it should not mark the property as uninitialized. (3) Suppression: honour
> the always-written PHPDoc tag / property-semantics provider (already read at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:361), so properties hydrated by
> reflection or a serializer can be exempted. Apply it to readonly and
> non-readonly properties alike, since the existing non-readonly check has the
> same hydration risk. Tests: add fixtures for a final class with a readonly
> property that is never assigned (should report), a readonly property read
> before assignment in the constructor (should report), a promoted readonly
> property read in the constructor (clean), the unset plus `__get` lazy-init
> pattern (clean), and a readonly property assigned in the parent's constructor
> (clean).

#### K36. Unused use-import detection with PHPDoc-precise usage tracking via NameContext

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: names-symbols, linter-catalog-other,
  dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** A common, high-signal cleanup check. Because phpstan-rs resolves
  PHPDoc names through the same NameContext, docblock uses can be marked
  exactly. Mago falls back to a whole-word substring scan of docblocks
  (no_redundant_use.rs:389), which over-approximates, for example an alias word
  appearing in prose. | The most common PHP hygiene finding, useful in the LSP.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:105`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:378`,
  `crates/names/src/lib.rs:80`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:389`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:518`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:151`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_context.rs:13`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:127`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/imports.rs:37`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:285`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:193`
- **Risks:** Names used only in contexts phpstan-rs does not resolve through
  NameContext would be reported falsely unused. Candidates are attribute
  arguments that are strings, `@see` tags, and framework annotation strings such
  as Doctrine `@ORM\\...` annotations resolved elsewhere. The mitigation is to
  also mark aliases found by the phpdoc tag parser for unknown tags, and to keep
  the rule opt-in. | Names used only in string class references (`'App\\Foo'`),
  in @method/@property tags, or in attributes of unparsed docblocks must be
  counted to avoid false positives.
- **Verification:** The citations hold, with small line offsets. Mago:
  crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:105 is where `check`
  starts (Program node). The same-namespace block with the delete-range fix is
  at about lines 134-170. is_item_used is at :378.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build this as a standalone per-file pass, for example
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused_imports.rs, reported as `use.unused` and
> `use.sameNamespace`. Do not thread a Cell/RefCell hit-set through
> NameContext::resolve_as (crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:193).
>
> Why a separate pass: resolve_names (name_resolution.rs:285) runs in the syntax
> crate at parse time. PHPDoc resolution happens later, in many consumers:
> registry ClassReflection building, the checker's inline @var handling, and
> resolve_names_in_type / collect_class_name_case_refs in
> registry/name_context.rs:13-30. Some of those are cached per registry and not
> re-run when a file is checked. A mutable "used" flag on a shared context would
> give order-dependent answers that differ between CLI and LSP.
>
> Pass design:
>
> 1. Walk the file with syntax::name_resolution::for_each_in_context. It already
>    handles braced and multiple namespaces and group uses; it is used in
>    checker/anonymous_class.rs:68 and phpstan_api.rs:95. Build the live import
>    set for each namespace block.
> 2. Collect uses from the AST. Take every QualifiedName in code: `written`'s
>    first segment plus its kind, including attribute names, `Foo::class`, and
>    function/const calls under the matching UseKind. Mark the import whose key
>    matches, using the same use_map_key normalization (case-insensitive for
>    class and function, case-sensitive for const).
> 3. Collect uses from PHPDoc. Parse every docblock in the block with
>    phpdoc::docblock::parse (docblock.rs:292). Walk every TypeNode it yields:
>    params, param_out, return_type, var_type, template_bounds and defaults,
>    extends/implements/uses, properties, methods, asserts, and type imports
>    (@phpstan-type / @phpstan-import-type `from` targets). Mark each class
>    name's first segment.
> 4. Fallback for tags the typed DocBlock does not model (@see, @throws if
>    untyped, @mixin, @covers/@uses, and Doctrine/Symfony annotation tags like
>    `@ORM\Column`): treat the tag name's first segment and the whole-word
>    identifiers in those tags' bodies as uses. This keeps prose inside typed
>    tags from counting, which is the one place phpstan-rs beats Mago's
>    contains_word scan (mago
>    crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:389,415). Unknown
>    tags stay conservative, so false positives are avoided.
> 5. Report never-marked imports as `use.unused`. Report `use.sameNamespace` for
>    an unaliased import whose parent namespace equals the current namespace.
> 6. Attach a DiagnosticFix (diagnostics/src/lib.rs:120, a single literal
>    replacement) that deletes one contiguous range: the whole `use` statement
>    plus its trailing newline, or one group item with its adjacent comma. No
>    multi-edit engine is needed.
> 7. In the LSP, map these identifiers to DiagnosticTag::UNNECESSARY. Grep found
>    no existing DiagnosticTag use under src/lsp.
> 8. Ship it opt-in via a `[rules]` flag, or on by default at low severity once
>    fixtures cover grouped, braced, aliased, attribute-only and annotation-only
>    cases.

#### K48. Type-alias imports as lazy references with transitive chains and diagnostics

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Probe t7: a chain A (@phpstan-type Id int) <- B
  (@phpstan-import-type Id from A) <- C (@phpstan-import-type Id from B) gives a
  false positive 'parameter \$x of C::f() has invalid type Id (class.notFound)'
  and type 'Id' in phpstan-rs. Mago resolves it to int and catches the wrong
  argument type.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/hierarchy.rs:163`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/hierarchy.rs:43`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/sorter.rs:86`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:668`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:750`
- **Risks:** A lazy alias node in the types crate touches every type operation.
  A cheaper route is ordered resolution plus transitive lookup at registry-build
  time, while keeping type_imports so re-resolution is possible.
- **Verification:** Mago: hierarchy.rs pending-import loop starts ~line 162
  (std::mem::take of imported_type_aliases), with
  TAtomic::Alias(TAlias::new(..)) at line 169 (not 163). The invalid-import-type
  code is at 178 and unknown-class-in-import-type at 188, matching the claimed
  175-194.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Skip the lazy alias Type node. It would touch every type operation in the
> types crate, and nothing here needs it. Keep the substitution eager at
> registry-build time and make it complete and re-runnable:
>
> (1) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs,
> resolve_deferred_type_imports (line 674): when an alias is not in
> `src.type_aliases`, follow the source class's own `type_imports` recursively.
> Carry a visited set of (class, alias) pairs. Memoize the results so they come
> out in dependency order, or run the pass to a fixed point the way
> flatten_traits already does.
>
> (2) Stop throwing the import list away. Today `info.type_imports.clear()` at
> line 750 deletes it. Keep the raw imports, or mark them resolved, so that
> Project::update_file (project.rs:1029) can re-resolve a class that imports
> from a class whose alias just changed.
>
> (3) Record the import errors on ClassReflection
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs, next to type_imports at
> line 540) as a small enum: UnknownSourceClass, MissingAlias, CircularAlias.
> Also detect local `@phpstan-type` cycles (P = Q|int, Q = P|string) in the
> second pass of build_type_aliases.
>
> (4) Emit these errors from
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_unresolvable.rs (the alias handling near
> line 320) when the class's file is checked. Once an import is known to be bad,
> stop also reporting `class.notFound` for the imported name at each place it is
> used.
>
> Tests: a 3-level import chain resolves to int; a missing source class, a
> missing alias and both cycle kinds each give one diagnostic; an LSP
> update_file that changes A's alias updates the types in C.

#### K107. Dangling by-ref foreach variable diagnostic

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Catches a classic, silent PHP data-corruption bug: a second
  `foreach ($items as $item)` overwrites the last element of the array. Mago
  reports it (probe cf/c t.php:16) and phpstan-rs does not.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/assignment/mod.rs:607`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:253`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/unset.rs:57`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:534`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/strict_rules.rs:639`
- **Risks:** False positives are limited to deliberate reference reuse, which is
  rare. It could ship opt-in or at level 4.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with small refinements. Mago:
  expression/assignment/mod.rs:607-619 reports
  IssueCode::ReferenceReusedFromConfusingScope, code
  "reference-reused-from-confusing-scope" (code.rs:278/610).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a small reference-hazard side table to Locals, next to the existing side
> tables (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs; `container_field_facts_mut()`, used
> at checker/stmt/loops.rs:825, is the model). Name it `dangling_refs`: a
> persistent map from a variable name to (origin span, iterated-subject text).
> Populate it at the end of check_foreach (checker/stmt/loops.rs, near the
> `if by_ref` block at :809) for every by-ref value binding. That covers a bare
> `&$v`, and also each `&$x` inside a by-ref destructuring pattern, which
> check_by_ref_destructuring (:763) already walks. As a second step, also
> populate it for a `$x = &$arr[...]` / `$x = &$obj->p` written inside a loop
> body, which is the general case Mago's
> update_references_possibly_from_confusing_scope
> (analyzer/src/context/block.rs:253) covers.
>
> Clear the entry when:
>
> - `unset($v)` runs;
> - `$v = &...` rebinds it;
> - the function or closure scope ends (the side table is per-Locals, so this is
>   automatic);
> - the variable is captured into a closure `use` list. Here, only clear it for
>   a by-value capture.
>
> The loop's own fixpoint iterations must not see the entry for its own value
> variable. Branch merges (merge_scopes) should union the entries, so an `unset`
> on only one branch leaves a "possibly still references" hazard.
>
> Report `foreach.danglingReference` on every write to a name in the table:
>
> - a plain assignment or compound assignment (check_assignment_target /
>   bind_assignment_target);
> - `++`/`--`;
> - a later non-by-ref `foreach (... as $v)` or `as $k => $v`, which is the
>   headline case. Report it once, at the foreach, not per iteration;
> - list()/[] destructuring targets;
> - passing the variable to a by-ref parameter (e.g. `preg_match($p, $s, $v)`),
>   which uses the same by-ref-arg path the checker already uses to bind
>   out-params.
>
> Example message: "\$v still references the last element of \$items from the
> by-reference foreach on line N; this write modifies that element. Call
> unset(\$v) after the loop." Reads stay silent.
>
> Ship it on by default at a mid level, not only as a strict_rules opt-in. The
> write-through is observable at runtime
> (`php -r '$a=[1,2,3]; foreach($a as &$v){} foreach($a as $v){} print_r($a);'`
> prints [1,2,2]), and deliberate reuse is very rare. If the team wants caution,
> gate it in strict_rules.rs next to foreach.keyOverwrite/valueOverwrite
> (:639/:646) first.
>
> Fixtures to add:
>
> - second foreach reuse;
> - plain assignment after the loop;
> - unset clears the hazard;
> - unset on only one branch still reports (possibly);
> - `$v = &$other` rebind clears it;
> - nested by-ref loops;
> - by-ref destructuring;
> - by-ref out-param write;
> - a closure boundary.

#### K130. Unimplemented abstract property hooks

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** PHP 8.4 property hooks and interface properties are spreading in
  new code, and this is a guaranteed fatal at class load.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:988`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1612`
- **Risks:** A plain (non-virtual) property satisfies a get or set hook
  requirement. Mago models this at class_like/mod.rs:950-980 and it must be
  copied carefully.
- **Verification:** Every citation checks out. Mago
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs: the loop starts at about line
  930 and walks all_parent_classes, all_parent_interfaces and used_traits. It
  checks each abstract hook at lines 944-980 (a plain non-virtual property
  satisfies it at line 952;
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add per-hook abstractness to PropertyReflection
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:131-137 has only a
> property-level `is_abstract` plus `has_get_hook`/`has_set_hook`). Add
> `get_hook_abstract`/`set_hook_abstract`, set from `PropertyHookBody::Abstract`
> where the reflection is built (class_info.rs:~1168). Treat every hook on an
> interface property as abstract.
>
> Add
> `Registry::required_abstract_property_hooks(fqn) -> Vec<(owner, prop, Hook)>`
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs, beside
> `required_abstract_methods` (hierarchy.rs:822). It uses the same ancestor walk
> over extends and implements. Add a companion
> `has_concrete_property_hook(fqn, prop, hook)`, modelled on
> `has_concrete_implementation` (hierarchy.rs:867). The hook is satisfied if the
> class or some non-interface ancestor, including trait-flattened properties,
> declares the property with either: (a) no hooks and not virtual, or (b) a
> non-virtual (backed) hooked property, because a backed property gives PHP the
> implicit get/set, or (c) a concrete (non-abstract) hook of that same kind.
>
> Do not copy Mago's `p.hooks.values().any(|h| !h.is_abstract)` fallback (mago
> crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:958-960). It accepts
> `interface I { public string $name { get; set; } } class B implements I {
> public string $name { get => "x"; } }`
> (verified: Mago is silent here), but PHP 8.5 fatals with
> "(HasName::\$name::set)". The check has to be per hook kind and take
> virtuality into account.
>
> Run the check on the class's own AST view or on a pre-merge flag, not on the
> merged `has_*_hook` bits. `inherit_property_hooks_one_pass`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:381-419) ORs a parent's hooks into
> the child's, so an inherited abstract hook would look "declared" on the child.
> Extend `check_class_completeness` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1612)
> to report `class.abstractPropertyHookNotImplemented`, using the same
> exemptions (interfaces, traits and abstract classes skip) and the same "first
> 3, and N more" message style. Enums can't have properties, so they are
> irrelevant here. Add fixtures for:
>
> - the interface `{get;}` case, the interface `{get;set;}` case and the
>   abstract-parent case
> - a plain property satisfying the requirement
> - a backed hooked property with only `get` satisfying `{get;set;}`
> - a virtual get-only property failing `{get;set;}`
> - an implementation provided by a trait or by a grandparent

#### K135. Opt-in possibly-undefined offset check

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** This is exactly where 'Undefined array key' warnings come from in
  shape-heavy code. phpstan-rs already tracks optional fields precisely, so the
  data is there.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:1180`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:550`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:648`
- **Risks:** May be noisy where optional keys are assumed to be present. Opt-in
  shipping matches the 'ship opt-in' rule.
- **Verification:** Mago, crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs: the
  strict_array_index_existence gate is at about line 1185. Line 1180 is
  `*has_possibly_undefined = true;` just before it.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `check_possibly_undefined_offsets: bool` to `RulesSettings` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/rules_settings.rs, off by default. Add a separate
> predicate to crates/types/src/offsets.rs, e.g.
> `Type::offset_possibly_missing(&self, offset) -> bool`. Do not reuse the
> `has_offset_value_type` Maybe result, because that Maybe also comes from
> unsealed shapes, general `array<K,V>`, lists, non-literal keys and mixed. The
> predicate is true only when: the dim is a literal key (`literal_key`); every
> union member is a sealed `ArrayShape` (or an intersection that contains one);
> and at least one member has the key as an optional field or lacks it, while at
> least one other member, or the same field, can hold it.
>
> In `check_offset_existence` / `report_missing_offset`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:658-713), after the definite `No`
> check, report `offsetAccess.possiblyNotFound` ("Offset 'b' might not exist on
> array{a: int, b?: int}.") when the flag is on and the predicate holds. Also do
> this in `check_destructuring_offsets`, since `['b' => $v] = $s` warns at
> runtime too.
>
> One suppression is required. When locals hold a narrowed entry under
> `narrowing_key($x['k'])` whose type excludes null, the key must be present,
> because a missing key reads null. Skip the report in that case. This covers
> `if (!empty($s['b']))` and `if ($s['b'] ?? false)`, which today narrow only
> the element and not the shape: probe x4b shows the shape stays
> `array{a: int, b?: int}`. A better fix is to make truthy/`!empty`/`??`-truthy
> narrowing also make the field required on the container shape.
>
> isset/empty/?? already go through their own offset paths (isset.offset,
> empty.offset and nullCoalesce.offset in the probe) and never reach the
> read-site check. Writes never reach it either.
>
> A general-array tier (`array<string,int> $a; $a['x']`, which Mago also flags
> under strict_array_index_existence at array.rs:1180) could be a second,
> separate opt-in flag later. Keep it out of this one.
>
> Tests: `array{a:int,b?:int}` read of 'b'; the
> `$x=[]; if($c){$x['k']=1;} $x['k']` union; `preg_match('/(a)(b)?/')` then
> `$m[2]`, a true positive because PHP omits the trailing unmatched group;
> negatives for isset / array_key_exists / !empty / `?? false` guards, unsealed
> shapes and lists.

#### K164. PHPUnit/Pest rules and test-method recognition

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a real false negative in the existing risky-test check.
  Brings phpstan-phpunit-style assertion hygiene that can be type-aware, which
  Mago's syntactic versions aren't.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/consistency/assertion_style.rs:121`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/prefer_test_attribute.rs:105`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/strict_assertions.rs:114`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/utils/phpunit.rs:9`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/risky_tests.rs:36`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/phpunit.rs:13`
- **Risks:** Assertion-style fixes must respect PHPUnit 10+ static assertion
  methods. assertEquals to assertSame is behaviour-changing for objects/floats,
  so gate it on types.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially correct. The Mago line numbers
  point at or next to each rule's `fn check`. For assertion_style.rs, `fn check`
  is at about line 121 and gates on the `test` prefix plus `_` or an uppercase
  letter. prefer_test_attribute.rs has `fn check` at about line 105.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split into a core fix and a smaller optional part.
>
> Core fix (worth doing):
>
> 1. Add one shared helper in a new crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/phpunit_tests.rs
>    (or next to risky_tests.rs). It takes the ClassDef/method AST plus the
>    registry and classifies a method as one of:
>    - Test: a TestCase subclass whose method is non-abstract and public, and
>      either has the `test` prefix, carries
>      #[PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Test] (resolved via name resolution, so an
>      aliased `use ...\Test` also counts), or has a `@test` docblock tag.
>    - Lifecycle: the setUp/tearDown family, or methods with
>      #[Before]/#[After]/#[BeforeClass]/#[AfterClass]/#[PreCondition]/#[PostCondition]
>      or the matching @before/@after tags.
>    - DataProvider target: a method named by #[DataProvider('x')],
>      #[DataProviderExternal(C::class,'x')] or `@dataProvider x` on any test in
>      the class.
> 2. Replace the two duplicated prefix-only checks with this helper:
>    - crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/risky_tests.rs:35
>      (`f.name.starts_with("test")`). This fixes the false negative for
>      attribute-style tests.
>    - crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:160
>      `is_phpunit_test_method`. This fixes false positives: a #[Test]/#[Before]
>      method, or a data-provider method, is currently reported as an unused
>      member because PHPUnit reaches it by reflection.
> 3. Update both files' "Scope, disclosed" doc comments. Add fixtures under
>    tests/fixtures/checker/ for #[Test], @test, #[DataProvider] and a Pest-free
>    TestCase.
>
> Optional, as opt-in keys in PhpunitSettings in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/phpunit.rs, from most to least worth building:
>
> - `check_focused_tests`: Pest `->only()` on it()/test()/describe() chains. It
>   sits next to check_pest_risky_test, which is already hooked at the Pest call
>   site. A committed `->only()` silently skips the rest of the suite, which is
>   a real CI failure.
> - `check_strict_assertions`: assertEquals/assertNotEquals, only when both
>   argument types are known and == versus === cannot differ. A pure
>   int/string/bool/null of the same kind, or arrays of those, count; numeric
>   strings versus ints do not. Report with no fix. Never suggest it for objects
>   or floats.
> - `check_specific_assertions`: assertSame(null|true|false, \$x),
>   assertTrue(is_\*()), assertSame(n, count(\$x)) and similar rewrites, with a
>   safe autofix through the existing LSP code actions.
> - Skip assertion-style (static:: vs \$this->) and prefer-test-attribute. They
>   are pure house-style choices with no correctness value, and Mago's
>   formatter/linter already covers them for users who want them.

#### K173. Constant-expression validity checks

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Covers probes m61-m66 and n22. PHP rejects all of these at
  compile time ('Constant expression contains invalid operations'), and
  phpstan-rs reports none. It also stops downstream type inference from treating
  `const X = g()` as a legal constant.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/cst/cst/expression.rs:100`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/constant.rs:24`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/attribute.rs:31`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/constant.rs:120`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/includes.rs:46`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/reflection_attribute.rs:24`
- **Risks:** Version-dependent admissibility (new-in-initializer 8.1, enum-case
  fetch 8.2, closures in constant expressions 8.5) has to follow the project's
  version range. With an unknown version, fall back to the permissive latest
  rules to avoid false positives.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out. Mago:
  crates/syntax/src/cst/cst/expression.rs:100 is
  `Expression::is_constant(&self, version, initialization)`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a pure AST predicate, for example `crates/syntax/src/const_expr.rs`
> (`is_constant_expr(&Expr, ConstExprContext, version_range) -> Result<(), &Expr
> /*offending node*/>`),
> which returns the first offending sub-expression so the diagnostic points at
> it instead of the whole initializer. It accepts: literals, magic constants,
> global and class constant fetches (including `X::class`, but not on
> `static::`, and no dynamic class names or constant names), unary, binary and
> logical operators, `?:`, `??`, array literals with spreads, and `[...]` index
> reads on constant operands. Version-gated cases: `new C(const args)` from 8.1
> (PhpFeature::NewInInitializers, new), but only in parameter defaults,
> static-variable, global-const and attribute contexts, and never in class
> constants or property defaults. Enum-case `->`/`?->` property fetch from 8.2.
> Static closures and first-class callables from 8.5. Wire it from a new
> `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/constant_expressions.rs` that walks
> declarations: global `const`, class, interface, trait and enum constants, enum
> case values, property defaults (including promoted-property defaults),
> parameter defaults on functions, methods and closures (Mago skips these, but
> PHP rejects them: `php -r 'function f($a = g()){}'` is fatal), attribute
> arguments plus a separate no-unpacking rule for attributes, and
> `static $x = ...` only when the version range includes < 8.3. Since 8.3,
> arbitrary expressions are allowed there (verified:
> `php -r 'function f(){ static $s = g(); }'` runs on 8.5). If some versions in
> the range allow a construct and others don't, report it only when no version
> in the range allows it, and say which version is needed in the message.
> Identifier `constantExpression.invalid`, non-ignorable. Add fixtures under
> tests/fixtures/checker/ for each context and each version gate.

#### K285. Per-path readonly double-initialization in constructors and \_\_clone (definite error vs possible warning)

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: property-initialization-readonly)
- **Benefit:** Catches `Cannot modify readonly property` runtime errors on
  constructor paths. The probe `$this->n = 1; $this->n = 2;` and
  `if ($b) { $this->s = 'x'; } $this->s = 'y';` are both silent in phpstan-rs,
  and Mago reports an error and a warning. It also fixes the current \_\_clone
  model, which cannot tell a definite double assignment from a branch-dependent
  one.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:19`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:154`, `crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:128`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs:197`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:606`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:46`
- **Risks:** Loop handling must not flag a legitimate single write inside
  `foreach` that breaks right after. Using converge_loop_body's second pass (not
  a syntactic 'inside loop' flag as Mago does) avoids that. Adding two more
  persistent sets to Locals adds a little join cost; imbl sets with ptr_eq fast
  paths keep it small.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/readonly.rs:19-25 is the
  LocalInitializationState enum, and lines 111-128 seed it from
  block_context.definitely_initialized_properties and
  possibly_initialized_properties. In a constructor, promoted properties and
  properties in initialized_properties start as Initialized.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs, replace the single
> `clone_reinitialized: ReinitializedPropertySet` (line 46, accessors at
> 410-416) with two sets, `readonly_init_definite` and `readonly_init_possible`
> (the alias in checker.rs:65 can be reused). In control_flow.rs merge_scopes
> (the clone_reinitialized union is at 606-610), take the intersection for
> definite and the union for possible. Every multi-way join already goes through
> merge_scopes: if/else, switch, try end_states, catch entry from throw_states
> (stmt/try_catch.rs:231), and the loop next_entry. In property_assignment.rs
> native_readonly_assignment (lines 194-213), handle constructors,
> \_\_unserialize and \_\_clone (PHP 8.3+) in one place, only for a Direct write
> on \$this:
>
> - If the property is in definite, report `assign.readOnlyProperty` "... is
>   already assigned."
> - Else if it is in possible, report a new identifier
>   `assign.readOnlyPropertyPossiblyAssigned`.
> - Then insert the property into both sets. Skip `??=` on a non-nullable
>   readonly (it never writes once the property is initialized). Also skip
>   array-element mutation, which has its own existing path. At constructor
>   entry, seed promoted readonly parameters of the current class into definite.
>   That catches `$this->p = 3` on a promoted property, a definite runtime Error
>   that is silent today. Loops are where the proposal as written goes wrong.
>   Locals::eq (locals.rs:340-351) compares only `types`, so converge_loop_body
>   (control_flow.rs:302) keeps pass 0 whenever types are already stable. The
>   body is never re-walked, so relying on convergence alone would never catch a
>   write inside a loop. The fix is to make the fixed-point test also require
>   `readonly_init_possible` to be unchanged, or to force one more pass when it
>   grew. Earlier passes' diagnostics are already discarded by rewind_to(mark),
>   and break/return paths never reach the back edge, so a write followed by
>   `break`/`return` stays clean. Do NOT copy Mago's syntactic inside_loop flag
>   (analyzer/src/readonly.rs:128-133). parent::\_\_construct() effects are
>   optional: seed them only when the parent's constructor-written set is
>   cheaply known, and only for PHP 8.4 protected(set) readonly properties the
>   child may write. Drop the "initializer methods / exclusive private helpers"
>   part. A native readonly write outside a constructor is already reported as
>   property.readOnlyAssignNotInConstructor, so it adds nothing.

#### K149. Dead-store and unused-local detection via flow-sensitive pending writes/provenance

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness,
  dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** A common class of real bugs, such as a computed value never used
  or a typoed variable name. It is more precise than Mago because it reuses real
  flow-sensitive reaching definitions. | This check family is missing entirely
  today. Because it rides on phpstan-rs's real branch merging and loop
  convergence, it is stricter and more precise than Mago's straight-line-only
  dead-store rule (it also handles `if (c) { \$x = 1;
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_dead_store.rs:109`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_redundant_variable.rs:110`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_unused_global.rs:102`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_unused_static.rs:102`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/utils/variable_usage.rs:144`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_dead_store.rs:56` (+2 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:129`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1669`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused/var_usage.rs:18`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563`
- **Risks:** Provenance tracking costs memory and time (imbl sets per declare).
  Keep it opt-in and measure. Loop re-checking passes must union reads across
  passes. By-reference captures, `$this` and variables read inside string
  interpolation must count as reads. | References (&\$x), variables captured by
  arrow functions and `static fn` bodies need careful modeling. Try/finally
  paths need care too. A performance cost comes from one more imbl set per
  Locals, which is cheap to clone.
- **Verification:** The citations are correct. Two small precisions. First,
  Mago's bailout on `$$x` is in walk_in_indirect_variable and
  walk_in_nested_variable, which call rec.bail() at
  crates/linter/src/rule/utils/variable_usage.rs around lines 457-463, just
  before :460.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a dedicated pending-writes lattice rather than reusing the LSP provenance
> map as-is. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs, add
> `pending_writes: imbl::HashMap<String, ProvenanceSet>` to Locals. It is filled
> only when a new `Checker` flag (ext.extras.check_unused_variables, opt-in) is
> on. `declare()` (locals.rs:129) replaces the name's entry with {span}. The
> merge of pending writes in control_flow.rs merge_scopes (:563/:736) must be a
> union over the key set of BOTH sides, including names present in only one
> branch. It must not follow the `types` loop, which drops one-sided names (see
> the doc at control_flow.rs:458-461). Keep a per-function
> `live_sites: RefCell<FxHashSet<Span>>` on Checker. Everything that reads a
> variable adds that name's pending spans to live_sites: the Variable arm in
> expr.rs:1656, isset/empty/`??` operands, compound assignment, ++/--,
> by-reference arguments, `$a = &$x`, compact() literals, closure `use` captures
> (expr.rs:3592), arrow-fn free variables, string interpolation, list() sources,
> and `unset`. Treat these as live: writes to by-reference parameters,
> `global`/`static` bindings used after they are declared, and any function
> where saw_dynamic_var_construct or any_variable_may_exist is set
> (checker.rs:1660, function_decl.rs:1193) or that calls
> get_defined_vars()/include. Treat every write inside a try body as live when
> there is a catch or finally, unless the throw-state merge in try_catch.rs:231
> carries pending writes too. At the end of the function, in function_decl.rs
> around :1190, a declared site that is not in live_sites gives
> `variable.unused` if the name is never read at all, and `variable.deadStore`
> otherwise. Mirror the same walk for `global $x`/`static $x` as
> `global.unused`/`static.unused`. Exempt `$_`-prefixed names, parameters,
> foreach keys and values under by-ref, catch variables, and `list()`
> placeholders. Also emit an LSP `DiagnosticTag::Unnecessary` hint so unused
> locals render faded in the editor. Add fixtures for the one-sided-branch,
> loop-carried (`$prev`) and try/catch cases before turning it on by default.

#### K218. Incremental whole-program checks in the LSP

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Dead-code, unused-member, unused-enum-case and
  circular-dependency findings appear live in the editor, as they do in Mago's
  watch mode, instead of only in batch runs. Every re-check also stops
  re-running the checker over all other writer files for property facts.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:52`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:1481`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:459`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:914`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1275`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:754`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1356`
- **Risks:** Memory rises by the size of the per-file facts; they are small. The
  first whole-program run still needs Tier 2 member refs
  (ensure_member_index_built); seed it from the initial workspace check pass as
  check-project does.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are wrong. Precise locations: Mago's
  FileState struct is at incremental_analysis.rs:50-59. The late-reference
  rebuild from cached FileState for skipped files plus fresh per-file results is
  at about lines 1480-1488.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this in two independent parts. Part 2 depends on part 1; part 1 is useful
> on its own.
>
> (1) Cache each file's side outputs in the project, keyed by path. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs, add a per-path store (in FileState or a
> sibling map) for three things: escaped_enums, escaped_member_classes and
> named_argument_calls. Replace a file's entry whenever
> check_file_and_member_refs or run_checker re-checks it (update_file loop
> around l.1084, remove_files around l.1175). Drop the entry in the same place
> use_sites.remove_file(path) is called (l.811/848). The project-wide
> escaped_enum_cases and escaped_member_classes (l.200-205) become either a
> union built on demand or a refcounted map. seed_member_refs (l.914) then
> writes per path instead of extend-only. Session::analyze (project/session.rs
> ~l.700-754) should seed the same store, so check-project and the LSP share one
> path.
>
> Also cache property_assign_facts per file. Then judge_property_types
> (project.rs ~l.1356-1395) reads the cached facts for `others` and only falls
> back to run_checker when the cache is missing. That removes the extra Checker
> pass over each trait or co-declaring file on every re-check. The cache stays
> correct because any file whose facts depend on a changed symbol is already in
> update_file's transitive-dependents set, and re-checking it refreshes its
> entry.
>
> (2) In lsp.rs, after the debounce worker's update_files finishes, run
> project.check_whole_program(&merged_named_argument_calls) plus the other gated
> passes (dead enum cases, dead code, dead members, abstract classes, circular
> namespace deps) when their settings are on. Merge the results into the
> per-file published sets. Diff them against the last published whole-program
> set, so only files that changed get a new publishDiagnostics.
>
> Build the Tier 2 index (ensure_member_index_built, l.877) once, in the
> background, after the workspace loads, and only when a whole-program setting
> is enabled. Until it is built, publish no whole-program diagnostics rather
> than partial ones. Consider re-running the whole-program passes on save or
> idle instead of every debounce tick, so a method just typed is not flagged
> unused mid-edit.

#### K5. Configurable short open tag (\<?) support in the lexer

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Legacy templates and older applications that use `<? ... ?>` are
  currently analysed as pure HTML. Every bug in them is invisible, and their
  declarations are missing from the registry.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/settings.rs:10`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:231`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:418`
- **Risks:** Enabling it by default would misread `<?xml` headers in templates,
  so keep it opt-in and document it. The hint needs care to avoid noise in
  HTML-heavy files.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, apart from minor line offsets.
  Mago crates/syntax/src/settings.rs:10 declares `enable_short_tags` and
  documents it as matching the `short_open_tag` ini directive. Its Default impl,
  which returns `true`, is at lines 20-24.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs, add a `short_open_tag: bool` field to the Lexer
> and a builder `Lexer::with_short_open_tag(bool)`, next to the existing
> `with_interner` at line 146. In `lex_inline_html` (lines 418-458), when the
> flag is on, also stop the scan at a bare `<?`. The existing `<?php` and `<?=`
> branches keep priority. Any other `<?` consumes 2 bytes and sets in_php, with
> no whitespace requirement. PHP's zend lexer switches on `<?` directly:
> `php -n -d short_open_tag=1` runs `<?echo 1;?>` and prints `1`. The proposal's
> rule that a whitespace byte must follow is therefore wrong. It would miss real
> `<?if(...)` templates. It would also still misfire on `<?xml`, which PHP
> itself misparses when the setting is on, so that is correct behaviour. Add
> `parameters.shortOpenTag` (default false) in crates/config and pass it down
> through ProjectSession/Project to every place the project builds a file lexer.
> Stubs and vendor always use the default. Add a separate `phpstan.shortOpenTag`
> hint for files that are analysed with the flag off, contain a `<?` that is not
> `<?php`, `<?=` or `<?xml`, and are followed by something that lexes as a PHP
> statement start. Emit it once per file at the first occurrence. The hint turns
> silently skipped code into visible code, and it is arguably worth more than
> the setting itself.

#### K122. Report arithmetic that always throws

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Catches code that is certain to crash at runtime; cheap to add
  and has no false positives by construction.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs:954`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/math/intdiv.rs:37`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs:364`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:380`
- **Risks:** Only fire when every value is certain to fail, to avoid 'maybe'
  noise.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/arithmetic.rs:954
  definite_arithmetic_runtime_error is accurate, but narrower than the proposal.
  It only matches a literal int 0 / float 0.0 right operand for %, and a literal
  negative int for << and >>. It does not handle ranges or 0.5-style floats.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Rename crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs check_division_by_zero (line
> ~364) to check_certain_arithmetic_error and make it answer "is every finite
> value of the operand a certain failure after PHP's own coercion". (1) / and %:
> map each finite divisor value through PHP's numeric conversion before the zero
> test. For %, use int conversion (coercion::php_float_to_int for floats, so 0.5
> and -0.9 count; numeric-string '0' and '0.4' count; true/false/null follow
> (int)). For /, use the number conversion (float 0.0, -0.0, '0', '0.0', false,
> null count). The current test only compares against Type::int_literal(0) /
> Type::float_literal(0.0), which also misses `5 / '0'` and `$i % '0'`; php -r
> confirms both throw DivisionByZeroError. Keep the existing identifiers
> division.byZero and modulo.byZero. (2) << and >>: report "Bit shift by a
> negative number." (arithmetic.shiftNegative) when the right operand's int
> bounds after int conversion have max < 0. (3) intdiv in the function-call
> path, next to where throws/dynamic.rs:67 already special-cases intdiv for
> throw points: report intdiv.byZero when the divisor is certainly 0 after int
> conversion, and intdiv.overflow when the dividend is certainly PHP_INT_MIN and
> the divisor is certainly -1. Do NOT report PHP_INT_MIN % -1; php -r shows it
> returns int(0). Do NOT touch fmod, which returns NAN. Fire only on certainty,
> meaning a non-empty finite_types where every member fails. The expression's
> never result already marks the rest of the block dead, so the new diagnostic
> should sit on the operator/call span. The existing deadCode.unreachable report
> on the next line stays as it is.

#### K136. unset() legality checks

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Guaranteed runtime Errors, cheap to detect with reflection data
  phpstan-rs already has.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/unset.rs:373`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/unset.rs:388`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/unset.rs:87`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:571`
- **Risks:** A readonly property may be unset inside the class before
  initialisation (a lazy-init idiom). Scope the check to outside the declaring
  class, or treat that case separately.
- **Verification:** All cited locations are accurate. Mago
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/unset.rs: check_property_unset is called at line
  60; the scalar-container InvalidUnset message is at lines 83-90 ("Cannot apply
  `unset` to an offset of non-array type").
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the diagnostics to
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs::check_unset_target, which
> currently only walks the target quietly (check_expr_quiet_root) and updates
> narrowing and shapes. Put the property logic in a helper next to the
> readonly-assign scope code in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/property_assignment.rs (around lines 170-215),
> so both use the same scope rule.
>
> (1) Readonly properties. For ExprKind::PropertyAccess, or
> NullsafePropertyAccess if the parser allows it in unset, resolve the receiver
> with the same machinery used for assignment. Report `unset.readOnlyProperty`
> ("Cannot unset readonly property C::\$p.") when prop_sig.is_readonly() (see
> registry/class_info.rs:195) or the class is readonly, and the current scope is
> outside the declaring class. The one exception is PHP 8.4+ with a non-private
> write visibility, where a subclass also counts as inside, mirroring the
> `allowed_in_subclass` test in property_assignment.rs. Inside the declaring
> class or an allowed subclass, PHP permits unset while the property is still
> uninitialised. This is the lazy-init and ghost-proxy idiom, and phpstan-rs
> cannot track initialisation state, so stay silent there. Optionally report
> later inside a constructor after a definite assignment on the same path.
>
> (2) Hooked properties. Report `unset.hookedProperty` when the property
> declares any hook (has_get_hook or has_set_hook) or is_virtual
> (class_info.rs:227). This is unconditional: PHP throws even for a set-only
> hook on a backed property.
>
> (3) Offsets. For ExprKind::Index(base, _), infer base_ty. Report
> `unset.offset` only when every member of the union is certainly one of int,
> float, true or a non-empty/any string, using the existing
> certainty/failing_level machinery. null, false and array must not fire,
> because unset(\$null[0]) and unset(\$false[0]) are silent no-ops at runtime.
> For strings, the message is "Cannot unset string offsets". For the other
> scalars it is "Cannot unset offset in a non-array variable". A 'maybe' union
> such as array|int should report at most at the strict level, or not at all.
>
> Keep one identifier per case, and add fixtures for each PHP runtime case
> listed below.

#### K138. Direct trait constant access and self-referencing constants

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Two guaranteed Errors, and the cycle data is already computed and
  then thrown away.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/class_constant.rs:317`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/constant.rs:69`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:6098`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:599`
- **Risks:** Accessing a constant through self:: or static:: inside the trait
  itself is legal and must be excluded.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially right. Only small offsets
  differ. Mago's trait check is in find_constant_in_class at
  crates/analyzer/src/resolver/class_constant.rs:~294. It reports
  IssueCode::DirectTraitConstantAccess at line 317.
- **Refined proposal:**

> (1) Trait constant access, `classConstant.traitDirectAccess`: in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs `static_member_of_class` (around line
> 6080), after the class-exists and name-case checks and on the `!is_property`
> path, report "Cannot access trait constant T::C directly" when the registry
> kind of the canonical class is `ClassKind::Trait` and the reference was
> written as the trait's name (`written` is Some and names the trait).
> References written as `self`/`static`/`parent` inside the trait resolve to the
> using class and must be excluded. So must a class-string variable `$t::C`
> whose type only says it is a trait-string: PHP rejects that too, but reporting
> it risks false positives when the type is imprecise. Return the constant's
> type as the code does now, so the error does not cascade into other
> diagnostics. Put the new condition beside the existing trait-kind guards used
> by checker/resolve.rs:545 and checker/instantiation.rs:94, and don't add a
> separate walker. (2) Self-referencing constants, `classConstant.circular`: do
> not treat "still `contains_deferred()` after MAX_ROUNDS" as the definition of
> a cycle. A reference to a missing class or constant (`const m = Missing::Z`)
> also stays deferred, and it must not be reported as circular. Instead, in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs `resolve_class_constant_references`
> (line 590 onward), build a small graph before the final
> `unresolved_class_const_to_mixed` pass. Each still-deferred (class, const)
> gets edges to the ClassConstant references it holds, with self/static bound
> through `visible_class_consts`, and a DFS finds the strongly connected nodes,
> including `b = self::b`. Record them in a registry side table, e.g.
> `circular_class_consts: Vec<(Name, Name)>`. Report them from the
> class-constant declaration check in checker/oop.rs (next to the
> `classConstant.inTrait` rule near line 1382) at the constant's span, with the
> message "Cannot declare self-referencing constant". Keep the Mixed fallback.
> Add fixtures for the trait via name / self / static / using-class cases, a
> 1-cycle, a 2-cycle across two classes, and a missing-reference control that
> must stay silent.

#### K139. @method/@property without magic handlers

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Catches stale docblocks (magic handler removed in a refactor)
  that turn into runtime Errors while every call site still type-checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:1052`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/property.rs:1600`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:935`
- **Risks:** Frameworks put @method on interfaces or on abstract bases whose
  children add \_\_call. Only the final-class case is guaranteed; the non-final
  case should be opt-in.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:1052
  report_magic_call_without_call_method (IssueCode::MissingMagicMethod at 1067,
  Issue::error).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Ship only the @method half, and add it in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs
> next to check_method_tag_types (oop.rs:243). That function already loops over
> `info.methods().filter(|sig| sig.is_magic())` for each class.
>
> 1. Declaration-site check, level 0, on by default. For a concrete `final`
>    class, excluding enums, go through the magic @method signatures it owns or
>    inherits (skip the is_magic cases()/from()/tryFrom() that
>    registry/class_info.rs:1719/1770/1800 synthesise for enums). Report each
>    one that is not static when `registry.lookup_method(fqn, "__call")` is
>    None, and each static one when `__callStatic` is None. lookup_method
>    already follows parents and traits, the same way checker/expr.rs:1380 and
>    member_resolution.rs:460 use it. Report once per tag at the class span.
>    This finds a stale tag even when nothing calls it, and avoids repeating the
>    error at every call site.
>
> 2. Optional call-site variant, opt-in, for non-final concrete classes. The
>    receiver's static type is a non-abstract, non-interface class whose
>    resolved method is_magic() and has no handler. Keep it opt-in because a
>    subclass may add \_\_call. Always skip interface and abstract receivers.
>
> Use an identifier such as `method.magicWithoutHandler`.
>
> Do not build the @property/\_\_get/\_\_set half as proposed. A final class
> with @property and no \_\_get is valid PHP when the class is hydrated through
> dynamic properties (PDO::FETCH_CLASS, `$o->x = ...` before 8.2,
> #[AllowDynamicProperties], subclasses of stdClass), so it would produce false
> positives. If it is wanted at all, restrict it to classes where dynamic
> properties are a hard Error (readonly classes, enums).

#### K143. Missing PHP deprecations: case X; separator, class named _, by-ref return from void

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog,
  linter-catalog-correctness, linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** A cheap deprecation check with an autofix, ahead of removal in
  PHP 9. | Matches the deprecations PHP itself emits, and gives users an upgrade
  path. | All three are verified runtime deprecations on PHP 8.5.4 (`php -r`):
  'Case statements followed by a semicolon (;) are deprecated', 'Using "_" as a
  class name is deprecated since 8.4', 'Returning by reference from a void
  function is deprecated'.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:279`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/deprecation/deprecated_switch_semicolon.rs:110`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/deprecation/no_void_reference_return.rs:92`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/deprecation/no_underscore_class.rs:86`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/control_flow.rs:350`,
  `crates/types/src/php_version.rs:170`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/coercion.rs:142`,
  `crates/types/src/php_version.rs:214`
- **Risks:** None. It needs an AST field, so the parser and AST change. | None
  significant. Gate each one on the configured PHP version. | The AST change
  touches every SwitchCase constructor. Confirm the introduction version of the
  void by-ref deprecation (8.1 RFC) against the runtime before choosing the
  PhpFeature boundary.
- **Verification:** The citations check out, apart from small line offsets. -
  Mago analyzer: crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:279-281 checks
  is_deprecated(Feature::SwitchSemicolonSeparators) together with
  SwitchCaseSeparator::SemiColon and reports DeprecatedFeature.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Not refuted. Three small checks that match deprecations PHP itself emits.
>
> 1. **`case X;` / `default;` separator.** This is the only part that needs a
>    syntax change. In crates/syntax/src/parser/control_flow.rs:350 and :363,
>    `if !self.eat(&Token::Colon) { self.eat(&Token::Semicolon); }` accepts the
>    semicolon and throws away which separator was used. Add
>    `separator_semicolon: Option<Span>` to `SwitchCase`
>    (crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:180), recording the `;` token's span. Keep the
>    span, not a bool, so `--fix` can replace `;` with `:`. Add
>    `PhpFeature::DeprecatedCaseSemicolon` (8.5) next to
>    `DeprecatedBacktickOperator` in crates/types/src/php_version.rs (~:219 and
>    the version table ~:394). Emit `switch.caseSemicolonDeprecated` from the
>    switch walk, gated with
>    `registry.php_supports_somewhere(...) == Some(true)`, the same way as
>    `check_backtick_deprecation`
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/coercion.rs:146). This covers both brace and
>    alt-syntax switches.
>
> 2. **By-reference return from a void function.** No AST change is needed.
>    `FunctionDecl.by_ref` (ast.rs:266) already covers functions and methods.
>    `parse_closure` and `parse_arrow_fn` (parser/closures_and_match.rs:17, :74)
>    already read the `&` into `by_ref`. Flag when `by_ref` is true and the
>    native return type hint is exactly `void`. Checked on php 8.5.4, PHP flags
>    this even without a body: on interface methods, closures and arrow fns. Use
>    `PhpFeature::DeprecatedVoidByRefReturn` with an 8.1 boundary. It was
>    introduced in PHP 8.1; Mago gates it at 8.2, which is wrong. Do not include
>    set hooks: `&set` is a compile error, not a deprecation, so Mago covering
>    it adds nothing.
>
> 3. **Class named `_`.** Flag a class, interface, trait or enum declared with
>    the short name `_` only in the global namespace, via
>    `PhpFeature::DeprecatedUnderscoreClassName` (8.4). Checked on php 8.5.4:
>    `class _ {}` prints 'Using "_" as a class name is deprecated since 8.4',
>    but `namespace N; class _ {}` prints nothing. The namespace check keeps
>    this free of false positives, and Mago's rule may not have it.
>
> Identifiers, for example: `switch.caseSemicolonDeprecated`,
> `function.voidByRefDeprecated` / `method.voidByRefDeprecated` /
> `closure.voidByRefDeprecated`, `class.underscoreNameDeprecated`. Tests go in
> the checker's existing deprecation test module.

#### K146. Report break/continue out of finally

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Catches a real fatal compile error in PHP. The change fits into
  an existing walker.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/safety/no_unsafe_finally.rs:100`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs:100`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs:31`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs:195`
- **Risks:** Minimal. Only jumps whose target frame is outside the finally are
  errors; a loop nested inside the finally is fine, and the depth comparison
  handles that.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/linter/src/rule/safety/no_unsafe_finally.rs
  defines targets() at about line 93, and check() starts at about line 103. The
  loop that maps ControlFlow::Return/Throw/Continue/Break to an issue is at
  about lines 112-119, so the cited line 100 is close but not exact.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs, give each frame the finally
> depth it was entered at. Change `Scope.frames` to
> `Vec<(FrameKind, usize, usize)>`, push `self.finallies.len()` in the
> While/DoWhile/For/Foreach arm (lines 66-74) and the Switch arm (lines 75-82),
> and update `placement()` (line 45) to map `|(_, id, _)|`. In the
> Break/Continue arm (lines 100-128), look up the target frame
> `self.frames[len - level]` after the level and out-of-loop checks. If that
> frame's recorded depth is less than `self.finallies.len()`, push
> `("outOfFinally", span, "Keyword {keyword} jumps out of a finally block.")`.
> It goes through the existing reporting loop at lines 154-167, and since its
> kind is not "switch" it comes out level 0 and non-ignorable. Order it before
> the `continue`-targeting-switch hint, because the fatal error matters more.
> Only take the break/continue half of Mago's no_unsafe_finally. `return` and
> `throw` inside finally are legal PHP, so treating them as errors would be
> wrong. Add fixtures for: break/continue directly in a finally inside a loop
> (report); a loop or switch nested inside the finally breaking itself (no
> report); `break 2` from a loop inside the finally to a loop outside it
> (report); and nested try/finally inside a finally.

#### K158. Empty catch detection

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Finds swallowed errors that make debugging hard.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_empty_catch_clause.rs:97`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:458`
- **Risks:** An intentional empty catch with an explanatory comment is common.
  The comment exemption requires the lexer to keep comment spans.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/no_empty_catch_clause.rs:97 is `fn check`.
  It walks each Try's catch_clauses and reports "Do not use empty `catch`
  blocks." when are_statements_empty holds.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `catch.empty` inside `check_catch_hygiene`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:458), so it stays behind
> `ext.extras.check_exception_hygiene` (gate at try_catch.rs:264, flag in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs:33). The check fires when `c.body`
> (ast.rs:191, `CatchClause.body: Vec<Stmt>`) is empty or holds only no-op
> statements, meaning empty statements and nested empty blocks, as Mago's
> `are_statements_empty` does. The message names the swallowed type(s), e.g.
> "JsonException is caught and silently discarded." Both bare-variable and
> `catch (Foo)` forms are reported.
>
> Suppression: skip the report when a comment lies inside the clause span. The
> comments already exist. `syntax::ParsedFile.comments`
> (crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:27) is sorted by position, but it is only used by
> `ignore_comments::scan_parsed` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_comments.rs:48)
> and never reaches `Checker`. So keep the comment start positions in the
> per-file parse result (project.rs `Parsed`, around line 1947) and give
> `Checker` a slice. `check_catch_hygiene` then binary-searches for a comment
> between the clause's `{` and its end. The lexer needs no change.
>
> De-duplicate: when `catch.baseWithoutRethrow` already fires for the same
> clause (empty `catch (Exception $e) {}`), send one report instead of two,
> preferably the `catch.empty` wording, which says more.
>
> Split out the proposal's "dead catch" half. `call_throw_types` does not exist.
> The comment at try_catch.rs:132-140 says the per-callee "never thrown" model
> is missing. `catch_live` (try_catch.rs:241, from `try_throw_states` and
> `may_catch`) already works out reachability, but reporting unreachable catches
> is a separate feature with its own false-positive profile around unannotated
> and implicit throws. It should not be bundled into this check.
>
> Fixtures: `catch (JsonException $e) {}`, `{ ; }`, `{ /* intentional */ }`
> (silent), `// ignore` on its own line inside the body (silent), a multi-type
> catch, `catch (Exception) {}` (single report), and a body that has a statement
> (silent).

#### K170. Modifier sequences in AST with duplicate/conflict checks

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Probes m01-m05, m14, m15 and m16 are all PHP fatals, and
  phpstan-rs reports nothing for any of them. With modifier spans, the LSP can
  also offer a precise 'remove modifier' quick-fix.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/method.rs:46`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/constant.rs:37`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:144`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs:98`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:199`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:354`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:294`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:508`
- **Risks:** An AST field change touches every ClassDef/MethodDecl constructor
  (parser, anonymous class, stubs) and increases AST memory slightly; a
  SmallVec<[_;3]> keeps that minimal. Stub files may contain odd modifier
  orders, so run the check only on analysed files.
- **Verification:** Mago citations check out. method.rs:40-50 is the
  duplicate-`static` check, and 65-72 is final-after-abstract. The
  readonly-on-method, duplicate-visibility and "`X` modifier is not allowed on
  methods" issues sit in the 148-200 range.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't add a `modifiers: Vec<(ModifierKw, Span)>` field to the AST. Do the
> checks inside the modifier loops that already exist in
> crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:
>
> - the member loop at about lines 199-270;
> - the class-level loop in parse_class_decl at about lines 505-527;
> - the promoted-constructor-parameter modifier loop.
>
> In each loop, keep a small local record of what has been seen: the first
> visibility's span, and the spans of static, abstract, final and readonly. When
> a modifier token arrives that conflicts with that record, report it right
> away, pointing at the token (the same pattern as the anonymous-class check at
> classes.rs:61-70, which returns a ParseError "Cannot use the {word} modifier
> on an anonymous class"). The checks:
>
> - repeated visibility ("Multiple access type modifiers are not allowed"), and
>   `var` combined with any other modifier;
> - repeated static, abstract, final or readonly;
> - abstract together with final, on a method or on a class;
> - readonly on a method;
> - static, abstract or readonly on a `const`, checked after `self.eat(Const)`
>   at about line 276. The loop already knows is_static, is_abstract_member and
>   is_readonly_member at that point; they are just thrown away.
>
> If the parser can collect recoverable errors, report through that. Otherwise
> follow the anonymous-class precedent and return Err: PHP itself refuses to
> compile these files (`php -l` fails), so a hard parse error is accurate.
>
> Stubs need no special case. PHP refuses these files, so correct stubs never
> contain these combinations. The only cost is a few bool/Option locals in the
> loop, with no AST memory growth. If a "remove modifier" LSP quick-fix is
> wanted later, the offending token's span is already in the error.

#### K171. Abstract/interface/anonymous method body rules

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Covers probes m07, m09, n08, m12, m13, n06 and n12. All are fatal
  at class declaration time in PHP and all are currently silent.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/method.rs:350`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:467`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:689`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:1172`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1459`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1369`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:154`
- **Risks:** Low. Interface methods are bodiless by construction, so the body
  check must not double-report with method.nonAbstract; that rule already
  excludes interfaces (oop.rs:1503).
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate to within a line or two. Mago:
  crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/method.rs has "abstract and
  cannot have a concrete body" at about line 349 and "interface method
  implicitly abstract, cannot have a body" at about 363.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs check_method_declaration_sanity (line
> 1459, called from oop.rs:979 and checker.rs:1548), add four non_ignorable
> rules, each keyed on the declaring kind: (1) method.abstractBody:
> `m.is_abstract && m.function.body.is_some()` for every kind, traits and enums
> included, since PHP rejects it everywhere ("Abstract function A::f() cannot
> contain body"). (2) method.interfaceBody:
> `kind == Interface && m.function.body.is_some()`. Skip it when m.is_abstract
> so it does not double-report with (1). (3) method.interfaceAbstract:
> `kind == Interface && m.is_abstract`. (4) method.interfaceFinal:
> `kind == Interface && m.is_final`. In check_class_constant_modifiers
> (oop.rs:1369), add classConstant.interfaceVisibility:
> `kind == Interface && c.visibility != Public`. For anonymous classes, in
> check_anonymous_class (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:153), call
> check_method_declaration_sanity(name, ClassKind::Class, false, &def.methods).
> Branch its method.abstract message to "Anonymous class method z() must not be
> abstract", because "Non-abstract class class@anonymous/... contains abstract
> method" reads badly. Pass a flag, or check whether the name starts with
> class@anonymous. That same call also brings method.nonAbstract, finalPrivate
> and the other sibling rules to anonymous classes. Also call
> check_class_constant_modifiers for anonymous classes if it is not already
> called there. Add one fixture per identifier under tests/fixtures/checker,
> including a trait with an abstract method that has a body, and an interface
> method that is abstract and has a body (it must report once).

#### K246. @no-named-arguments support

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Precision: `$args` is known to be a list, so array_is_list,
  `$args[0]`, and passing it to list\<T> parameters stop producing false
  positives. The new check catches calls that break the library's API contract.
  The tag is widely used in real vendor code (e.g. several sebastian/comparator
  files in the vendored drupal tree).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:447`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:583`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/post_process.rs:124`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:521`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:750`
- **Risks:** Stubs may carry the tag for functions that do accept named
  arguments in practice. Keep the call-site check at an appropriate level, or
  make it opt-in for vendor callees.
- **Verification:** None needed. Mago:
  crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:447-449 (NoNamedArguments sets the
  flag), crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:582-590 (variadic
  becomes get_list when named args are forbidden, otherwise
  get_keyed_array(arraykey, T)), crates/analyzer/src/invocation/post_pro ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs apply_tag (~:750): add a
>    `no_named_arguments: bool` field set by `no-named-arguments`,
>    `psalm-no-named-arguments` and `phpstan-no-named-arguments`. A class-level
>    tag applies to every method of that class. 2) Carry the flag onto the
>    function/method reflection in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry
>    (function_sig.rs). Inherit it through Registry::flatten_phpdoc_inheritance
>    (registry.rs:293), because an override that drops the tag still breaks the
>    parent's contract. 3) crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs :521
>    and :595: when the flag is set, make the variadic's _phpdoc_ body type
>    `Type::list_of(T)` (crates/types/src/constructors.rs:282) instead of
>    `Type::array(unknown_array_key, T)`. Leave the _native_ type at :539 as
>    `array<array-key, T>`. PHP does not enforce the tag, so a caller the
>    checker never sees can still pass string keys, and the native,
>    runtime-truth layer must stay honest. 4) At the call sites
>    (checker/expr.rs, near the named-argument handling at :1442), report a new
>    identifier (e.g. `argument.named`) in two cases: an `Argument::Named`
>    passed to a flagged callee, and a spread `...$x` whose key type may contain
>    a string, because string-keyed unpacking becomes named arguments at
>    runtime. That second case is the one Mago misses. Make it a normal-level
>    check. The bundled stubs don't contain the tag, so the risk of stub false
>    positives doesn't apply.

#### K271. Unused protected members in final classes/enums

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** This is a sound local check with default-on potential, where
  today the only option is the noisy opt-in whole-program rule.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:95`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:231`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:228`
- **Risks:** Ancestor bodies must be available. A vendor ancestor whose AST is
  not loaded should make the check skip the candidate, not report it.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:95 sets is_final =
  final || enum. The protected-property gate is at 109 and the protected-method
  gate at 172. Method overrides are skipped at 184 via overridden_method_ids,
  and trait-provided methods at 187-194.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs check_unused_private_members
> (called once per class at crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1641), accept
> Visibility::Protected consts, methods and non-hooked properties as candidates
> too, but only when the class is sound to judge from its own file: (a) it is an
> enum, or a `final` class with no parent class (interfaces are fine). A class
> with a parent is skipped for now. The Checker only has the Registry's
> signatures and never sees another file's bodies, so the ancestor-body walk the
> proposal asks for cannot be done locally. (b) it uses no traits. A trait body
> is compiled into the host's scope and can reach any host member. The trait's
> AST may live in another file. (c) the member does not override or implement an
> ancestor or interface member. Move overrides_an_ancestor_method out of
> project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:178 into a shared helper, and add a
> property/const counterpart. (d) it is not magic, not \_\_construct or
> \_\_clone, and not a promoted protected ctor param unless the same rules pass.
> Keep the existing usage.escaped and rebind_target_classes/rebind_escape_all
> bailouts, which cover protected members exactly as they cover private ones.
> Word the message "protected method C::x() is unused (class is final)" and
> reuse the method.unused, property.unused and classConstant.unused identifiers
> with the same removal fix. Follow-up (M): extend the class entries in
> src/registry with a small per-class summary of member names accessed on
> \$this, self, static or parent in the class's own and its traits' bodies,
> gathered during collection. That lets (a) and (b) relax to "no ancestor or
> used trait accesses this name". Fix alongside: the same trait gap already
> causes a false positive in today's private check. Probe: trait T { function
> t() { return \$this->viaTrait(); } } used by C with private function
> viaTrait(). phpstan-rs reports "private method C::viaTrait() is unused"
> although `php` runs it. Condition (b), or the registry summary, should apply
> to the private candidates too.

#### K293. Run return.unusedType on closures and arrow functions

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** A closure with `: string|false` that always returns a string is
  the same misleading contract as a named function's, and callers such as
  array_map results and callbacks stored in properties inherit the too-wide
  type. The probe shows phpstan-rs reports nothing for
  `function (int $x): string|false { return 'a'; }` or the arrow-function
  equivalent.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:339`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:1168`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3838`
- **Risks:** A closure passed where the parameter's callable type expects the
  wider return (a callback that must be `callable(): string|false`) is declared
  wide on purpose. Consider skipping closures whose declared return equals the
  contextual parameter's callable return type.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out. One caveat and one detail the
  proposal leaves out: 1. Mago's check is opt-in. At
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:902-912,
  check_return_type_width returns early unless
  settings.find_overly_wide_return_types is set, and settings.rs:398 defaults it
  to f ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. Refactor crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/return_type_too_wide.rs
>    check_too_wide_return_type (lines 56-125) to take `return_points: &[Type]`
>    and `saw_explicit_return: bool` as parameters instead of reading
>    self.current_function_return_points / current_function_saw_explicit_return
>    (lines 74-99). Update the function_decl.rs:1168 call to pass the live
>    fields.
> 2. Closure literal arm in checker/expr.rs: after check_closure_missing_return
>    (~3860), when a native `return_type` is present, call it with
>    &closure_return_points / closure_saw_explicit_return (3838-3845),
>    is_first_declaration=true, is_private=true, subject "Anonymous function",
>    span e.span. It must run before those vectors are moved at ~3952.
> 3. Contextual-closure path in checker/calls/closure_context.rs (~289-330):
>    this path currently does not save or restore current_function_return_points
>    / current_function_saw_explicit_return at all. So a callback's `return`
>    statements are pushed (stmt.rs:529-530, 635-636) into the ENCLOSING
>    function's return points. Fix this first: mem::take both before
>    converge_loop_body, clear them at the start of each pass as
>    expr.rs:3832-3833 does, and restore them afterwards. Then run the same
>    too-wide call on the closure's own points.
> 4. ArrowFn arm (expr.rs:3959 onward): when a native return type is declared,
>    use the single inferred body-expression type as the only return point with
