>    saw_explicit_return=true. Skip when the body is a `never`/throw expression.
>    Subject "Arrow function".
> 5. Keep the declared-return gate native-or-@return only, as for named
>    functions. Add fixtures covering: a closure, an arrow fn, a contextual
>    array_map callback, and an outer function whose callback returns a member
>    the outer function never returns.

#### K59. Read builtin purity from stub #[Pure] data

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: stubs-prelude)
- **Benefit:** Catches the real bug class of discarded builtin results
  (`trim($s);`, `array_merge($a, $b);`, `str_replace(...)` whose result is never
  assigned). It also raises precision of transitive purity for user code, which
  feeds other rules and result stability.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/core.php:746`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:346`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:161`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/purity.rs:256`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/noop.rs:240`,
  `vendor/phpstorm-stubs/Core/Core.php:57`
- **Risks:** phpstorm-stubs' #[Pure] is IDE metadata. A few entries may be wrong
  or may hide exceptions (ValueError on bad arguments), which is why functions
  with @throws or by-ref parameters stay excluded. Cross-check the list against
  functionMetadata.php before enabling it by default; otherwise ship the rule
  opt-in.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small line
  offsets. Mago: crates/prelude/assets/extensions/core.php:740-745 declares
  strlen with @pure, and the @pure count in the assets is 885 as stated. In
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs, the FunctionCall arm starts at about
  line 331.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build this on phpstorm #[Pure]. Use the plan that already exists:
> CRATE_SPLIT_EVIDENCE.md:1602 embeds
> vendor/phpstan-src/resources/functionMetadata.php as the builtin purity
> source, and C9 reads it (see :4515-4540). Concretely: (1) Add
> resources/functionMetadata.php to crates/stub-sources/build.rs. The
> build.rs:65 comment shows resources/ is excluded today. (2) Parse it once into
> a name -> hasSideEffects map, including Class::method keys. (3) In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/purity.rs, change purity_gate_passes (the
> `if sig.is_stub { return false; }` at ~:256) so a stub listed with
> hasSideEffects=false becomes a pure leaf in the fixed point. Keep the other
> gates (no by-ref params, no asserts, no throws). (4) checker/noop.rs
> check_pure_call_without_effect (~:240) needs no change. It reads
> is_transitively_pure. Use #[Pure] (without `true`) only as a fallback, and
> only for functions functionMetadata doesn't list. That is about 25 top-level
> functions (the locale_\* family, password_verify, get_debug_type,
> get_parent_class, ...). #[Pure(true)] stays impure for result-stability
> purposes. Add a small denylist that suppresses the statement-level report when
> the call's effect runs user code:
>
> - iterator_count / iterator_to_array on a non-array argument (draining a
>   generator is a real idiom)
> - count() on an object that isn't an array
> - strval() and string casts of an object with \_\_toString
> - method_exists / class_exists with autoload, which trigger the autoloader
>   Both functionMetadata and #[Pure] mark some of these side-effect-free.

#### K72. Support missing PHPDoc pseudo-types (non-empty-literal-string, literal-int, non-empty-mixed, new\<T>, template-type, properties-of)

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: type-representation, phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Removes spurious class.notFound and unresolvable-type diagnostics
  on libraries that use these tags (factories returning new\<T>, DI containers)
  and gives callers real return types instead of error or mixed.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/type/keyword.rs:150`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/derived/mod.rs:21`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/derived/new.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/cst/type/mod.rs:77`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/builder.rs:339`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/parse.rs:868`,
  `crates/types/src/parse.rs:845`, `crates/types/src/parse.rs:612`
- **Risks:** Each deferred Repr needs relation and display arms. properties-of
  needs visibility-aware registry access. Start with the lowering-only ones
  (non-empty-literal-string, literal-int, new over literal class-strings). |
  template-type and properties-of must be deferred until the registry is
  complete. Simplifying non-empty-mixed or literal-int to their parent types
  loses some precision but is never unsound.
- **Verification:** Mago citations check out. keyword.rs has `new` at about line
  150, `literal-int` → UnspecifiedLiteralInt in lookup_len11,
  `literal-float`/`open-resource`/`properties-of`/`template-type` in
  lookup_len13 (lines 300-325), and `non-empty-literal-string` in lookup_len24
  (about line 422).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split this into three tiers, all in crates/types/src/parse.rs (the keyword
> table in parse_type_keyword_or_class, around lines 845-1060) and
> crates/types/src/late.rs.
>
> (1) Lowering only, cost S. Add these arms next to the existing
> string-accessory arms (parse.rs:923-934) and the int-mask degradation
> (parse.rs:877):
>
> - `non-empty-literal-string` becomes Intersection([String,
>   Accessory(NonEmptyString), Accessory(LiteralString)]).
> - `literal-int` becomes Type::int(). Only add an AccessoryKind::LiteralInt if
>   a consumer (SQL or injection rules) reads it.
> - `literal-float` becomes float.
> - `non-empty-mixed` becomes the truthy-mixed form if the Mixed repr already
>   has one; otherwise plain mixed.
> - `callable-object` becomes object & callable.
> - `callable-array` becomes callable & list{object|class-string, string}, or
>   callable & array.
> - `__benevolent<U>` becomes U.
> - `open-resource` and `closed-resource` become resource.
>
> (2) `new<X>`, cost M. At parse time:
>
> - a literal class name becomes Object(X);
> - `class-string<C>` becomes C;
> - anything else becomes a new late Repr::New(inner).
>
> Resolve Repr::New in late.rs. Add an arm to resolve_node (late.rs:183-190),
> and handle it in resolve_late_to_bounds and in resolve_class_references
> (late.rs:22-38), following the KeyOf pattern: operand ClassString(T) or Object
> gives the object, and a template gives its bound's object. It also needs
> display, map_children, contains_deferred and relation fallback arms.
>
> (3) Registry-time, cost M. `properties-of<T>` (and the public-, protected- and
> private- variants) and `template-type<Obj, Class, 'T'>` become deferred Reprs.
> Settle them in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs, next to
> resolve_deferred_value_of (resolve.rs:447), and at call sites through
> resolve_deferred_value_of_now (checker/resolve.rs:100). properties-of maps to
> an array shape over visible property types. template-type maps through
> class_template_bindings. Do tier 3 last; tiers 1 and 2 already remove the
> false positives.

#### K151. Loop hygiene: loop never iterates and O(n^2) array accumulation

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness,
  linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Finds misplaced return/break logic errors in loops. Using typed
  termination (never-returning calls, throw) makes it more complete than Mago. |
  Finds a real performance problem common in PHP code, with few false positives
  because of the self-reference requirement. | (a) catches real logic errors (a
  misplaced return inside foreach), a common bug. (b) is a genuine performance
  issue that type checkers never flag.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/loop_does_not_iterate.rs:101`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/no_array_accumulation_in_loop.rs:105`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:209`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:650`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:93`
- **Risks:** The first-element idiom is common, so ship it opt-in with that
  exemption. | Bounded loops over tiny inputs are harmless, so keep it opt-in. |
  (a) `foreach ($x as $first) { break; }` 'take first element' idioms are
  intentional, so exempt loops whose body is only a break, or offer an ignore.
  (b) small arrays make it harmless, so keep it opt-in.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. loop_does_not_iterate.rs:101 is
  `check`, which matches For/Foreach/While/DoWhile.
  get_loop_terminator_from_statement (~:179) accepts only a bare
  `break`/`break 1` and `return`. might_skip_terminator (~:196) bails on
  Continue/Goto found in nested blocks and ifs.
- **Refined proposal:**

> (a) loop.neverIterates, opt-in under ext.extras (the extras section already
> exists, see crates/config/src/tests.rs:41 check_boolean_trap). Do not reuse
> always_terminates as it stands: control_flow.rs:96-99 counts `continue` as
> terminating, so a body ending in `continue;` would be reported wrongly.
> exits_function_or_loop (control_flow.rs:209) is not a fit either, because it
> returns false for `break` (:227) and it is shaped for switch cases. Add a new
> predicate in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:
> `ends_iteration_without_continuing(stmt, depth)`. It is true for return,
> throw, a never-typed expression, `break N` with N >= 1 at this loop's level,
> and `continue N` where N is greater than the depth (the continue goes to an
> outer loop). It recurses through Block (any statement), If with an else (all
> branches), Try (body and all catches) and Switch (with a default, adding 1 to
> the depth). A separate syntactic walk rejects the loop if any `continue`
> anywhere in the body resolves to this loop, reusing the frame and level
> resolution already used for break/continue level checks. Call the predicate in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs once per loop, on the first
> convergence pass only so it is not reported again on each pass. Exemptions:
> (1) do { ... } while (false/0), the breakable-block idiom; (2) foreach/while
> whose body is a single `return <expr>;` or `break;` (take the first element or
> row), because reset()/array_key_first() is not always equivalent for iterators
> or fetch loops; (3) loops whose body contains yield. Message: "Loop body
> always exits during its first iteration." with a tip about a return or break
> placed inside the loop by mistake. Main target:
> `foreach ($xs as $x) { if (p($x)) { return true; } else { return false; } }`.
> That is a real bug which Mago's top-level-only scan misses. (b)
> loop.quadraticAccumulation, opt-in extras, in the Assign handling
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs), gated on self.loop_depth > 0
> (checker.rs:650). Report `$v = array_merge($v, ...)` / array_merge_recursive /
> `[...$v, ...]` / `$v = $v + [...]` only when the LHS plain variable appears
> directly as an argument or spread operand. Also accept
> `$v = array_merge(..., $v)`. Drop array_unique and array_values from Mago's
> list: `$v = array_unique($v)` inside a loop is a dedupe step, not
> accumulation, and it would only add noise. Tip: collect the chunks with
> `$chunks[] = ...` and call `array_merge(...$chunks)` once after the loop. Put
> both behind separate config keys and give each fixtures covering the
> exemptions.

#### K153. Type-aware loose ==/assertEquals hazard

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Reports the loose comparisons that really are ambiguous, not all
  of them. Tests stop passing because of type juggling, for example '1' == 1 or
  null == false.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/identity_comparison.rs:87`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/strict_assertions.rs:114`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/use_specific_assertions.rs:130`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/comparisons.rs:191`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/phpunit.rs:13`
- **Risks:** Some == usage in legacy code is intentional, so keep it opt-in.
  Mixed operands must be skipped, which loose_kinds already does by returning
  false.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are right to within a few lines. In
  identity_comparison.rs the flags are at :96, :108 and :120
  (BinaryOperator::Equal, NotEqual and AngledNotEqual). They fire on every
  operator with no types involved, and the rule's requirements are None.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the idea into two parts. The operator check is sound. The PHPUnit part
> only works if it models PHPUnit's comparator, not PHP's ==.
>
> (1) Add an opt-in `ext.extras.check_loose_equality` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs, registered in app.rs next to
> `check_loose_haystack_comparison` (app.rs:203). Wire it in the
> binary-expression dispatch next to `check_identity_vs_equals`
> (checker/expr.rs:416, checker/strict_idioms.rs:204). For `BinOp::Eq`/`NotEq`,
> and `<>` which parses as NotEq, run `loose_kinds` on both operands
> (checker/comparisons.rs:150). Report
> `equal.looseHazard`/`notEqual.looseHazard` when some kind pair differs. Don't
> reuse `loose_comparison_differs` (comparisons.rs:191) as it is. Give the
> operator check its own variant: (a) Object==Object and Array==Array are value
> equality, not coercion. `new DateTime(..) == new DateTime(..)` is true and is
> the intended use. Suggesting === there changes the meaning, so don't flag
> these pairs. At most flag arrays only when their value kinds differ, checked
> recursively. (b) Add String==String, and NumericString==String, when neither
> side is a known non-numeric literal. This is the magic-hash hazard:
> `"0e123" == "0e456"` is true (confirmed with php -r). Today the table falls to
> `_ => false` for (String, String), so the most security-relevant case is
> missed. (c) Keep the null/bool/int-vs-numeric-string pairs and the PHP 8 split
> between non-numeric and numeric strings as they are. (d) Skip it when
> narrowing.rs already relies on the loose form in the same condition? No, it
> only has to be reported. But don't report when `probe_checks.rs:360-385` has
> already reported `equal.alwaysTrue`/`alwaysFalse` for the same node. Put the
> variant in comparisons.rs as a sibling of `loose_comparison_differs`, with a
> mode flag or a second function, so in_array keeps its current behaviour.
>
> (2) Under crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/phpunit.rs add `check_loose_assertions`,
> which defaults to off even when the extension is active. For
> assertEquals/assertNotEquals, model sebastian/comparator's ScalarComparator,
> not PHP ==. When either side is a string it compares both as strings, so
> assertEquals(0, 'abc') fails where PHP 7's == would pass. The hazard pairs are
> int/float vs numeric-string ('1' vs 1, '1.0' vs 1.0), bool vs anything
> non-bool, and null vs ''/0/false. Never flag object or array operands:
> assertEquals on objects compares by value, and on arrays it ignores key order,
> which is why people use it. Add `method.specificAssertion` only for
> assertEquals(true|false|null, \$x). assertEquals(true, 1) passes but
> assertTrue(1) fails, so that part is a real strictness gain. Suggesting
> assertTrue in place of assertSame(true, ...) is purely cosmetic, and can be
> left out or put behind a separate style flag.

#### K172. Magic-method signature legality table

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** A probe with 8 declarations that PHP rejects (e.g.
  `__isset(): int`, `__get(int $n)`, `__set(): int`, `__clone(): int`,
  `__call($n, string $a)`, `__serialize(): string`, `__destruct(): void`,
  `__unset(&$n)`) got 0 phpstan-rs diagnostics; Mago catches only the
  \_\_destruct one. Probes m25-m27, m29, n01, n03 and n05 are also silent in
  phpstan-rs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/mod.rs:51`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/method.rs:214`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1587`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/native_type_hints.rs:231`
- **Risks:** PHP only enforces types that are declared. Untyped magic methods
  must stay legal, and a subtype/covariant spelling (e.g. `static` or `self` for
  \_\_set_state's object) must be accepted. Check with php -l for each table
  row.
- **Verification:** All the citations check out. Mago:
  crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/mod.rs:51 defines the type
  `MagicMethodSemantic = (name, Option<usize> count, must_be_public,
  must_be_static, can_have_return_type)`,
  and the MAGIC_METHOD_SEMANTICS table is at lines 53-71.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/magic_methods.rs with a single static
> table keyed by the lowercased name. Reuse the name list from
> is_magic_method_name (checker/oop/enums.rs:13), and derive has_fixed_signature
> (checker/native_type_hints.rs:231) and the missing_typehint.rs:90 list from
> the same table so the three copies cannot drift apart. Each row holds: exact
> arity (\_\_get/\_\_isset/\_\_unset 1; \_\_set/\_\_call/\_\_callStatic 2;
> \_\_unserialize/\_\_set_state 1;
> \_\_destruct/\_\_toString/\_\_debugInfo/\_\_sleep/\_\_wakeup/\_\_serialize/\_\_clone
> 0); static required (\_\_callStatic, \_\_set_state) or forbidden (every other
> magic method, including \_\_clone and \_\_construct); no by-ref parameters;
> public visibility, reported as a warning because PHP only warns; no return
> type on \_\_construct/\_\_destruct; and the type constraints PHP checks only
> when a type is written. Parameter types are contravariant: the declared type
> must accept string for
> \_\_get/\_\_set/\_\_isset/\_\_unset/\_\_call(1)/\_\_callStatic(1), and array
> for \_\_call(2)/\_\_callStatic(2)/\_\_unserialize/\_\_set_state. So
> `string|int` and `mixed` are legal, and a mismatch is reported only when the
> declared type is not a supertype. Return types are covariant: a declared
> return must be a subtype of bool for \_\_isset (`true` is legal), void for
> \_\_set/\_\_unset/\_\_clone/\_\_wakeup/\_\_unserialize, string for
> \_\_toString, array for \_\_serialize/\_\_sleep, ?array for \_\_debugInfo, and
> object for \_\_set_state (`static`/`self` are legal). Use
> registry.is_super_type_of on the native types, not exact-name comparison. Call
> it from the per-method loop that already holds constructor.returnType
> (checker/oop.rs ~1587), and fold that check and a new destructor.returnType
> into the table. Every error except visibility should be non-ignorable, like
> method.visibility in the same loop. Run it for classes, anonymous classes and
> traits (trait methods are checked at the trait declaration; PHP fatals when
> compiling the trait). Fixtures go under tests/fixtures/checker/, one legal and
> one illegal case per row, with the legal side taken from php -l.

#### K274. Opt-in unused-parameter check

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Finds genuinely ignored inputs (a common refactor leftover, and a
  bug when a caller's argument is silently discarded) in the code where the
  signature is under the author's control.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/unused_parameter.rs:21`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/unused_parameter.rs:231`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/method.rs:118`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:8`
- **Risks:** Framework hooks with fixed signatures that are not expressed as
  interfaces cause noise. `_` naming (next idea) and opt-in gating reduce it.
- **Verification:** One path is wrong and a few descriptions need tightening.
  The citations are relative to /home/torres/projects/mago and
  /home/torres/projects/phpstan-rs. (1) overrides_an_ancestor_method is at
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/dead_members.rs:178, not :193.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in `rules.check_unused_parameters` flag, run in the whole-program
> phase (new module
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/whole_program/unused_params.rs, called from
> Project::check_whole_program next to check_dead_code, around
> project.rs:1720-1745). It reports positions from `decl_locations`, the same
> way dead_members does.
>
> What it checks:
>
> - Free functions.
> - Closures and arrow functions that are not passed directly as a call
>   argument, or as the value of a callable/Closure-typed property or parameter.
> - Methods that are private, OR are in a final class or enum, OR are final, OR
>   have no descendant overriding them. For the descendant test, build a map
>   from each (class, method) to "overridden by some descendant" once per run by
>   walking `registry.classes` and `all_ancestor_names`.
> - In every case the method must NOT override an ancestor or interface method.
>   Reuse `overrides_an_ancestor_method` (dead_members.rs:178), moved into a
>   shared helper.
>
> What it skips:
>
> - Abstract methods and interface methods.
> - Magic methods (`__call`, `__set`, `__get`, `__isset`, `__unset`,
>   `__callStatic`, `__serialize`, `__unserialize`, and so on).
> - Constructors, which the existing constructor.unusedParameter rule already
>   covers.
> - By-ref, promoted and variadic-sink parameters, and names starting with `$_`
>   / `_`.
> - Bodies that are empty or only `throw`.
> - Functions or methods carrying an attribute (hooks registered by attribute).
>
> Usage detection: reuse `collect_var_usage` (checker/unused/var_usage.rs)
> unchanged, since it already handles func_get_args, compact, get_defined_vars,
> include and \$\$x.
>
> Identifier: `parameter.unused`, level 1, with a fix-it that removes the
> parameter only for private methods and free functions that have no call sites.
> For all other cases, report without an autofix.
>
> Defer the overwritten-before-read refinement until the dead-store dataflow
> exists. Do not add a separate walker for it now.
>
> Tests: base-class hook overridden in another file (not flagged); private and
> final methods (flagged); array_map callback (not flagged); `$_x` (not
> flagged); an LSP edit to a subclass flips the finding in the base class.

#### K155. Type-level taint tracking

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, L (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Finds security bugs. The Doctrine and SQL extensions already know
  where queries go.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/tainted_data_to_sink.rs:96`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/utils/security.rs:33`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/lib.rs:764`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:751`
- **Risks:** Hard to scope: taint across function boundaries needs summaries,
  and the accessory may multiply types. Start with intraprocedural taint and
  opt-in.
- **Verification:** All the citations are correct. One detail is slightly off:
  the check() dispatch that handles Echo, EchoTag, PrintConstruct and
  FunctionCall is at mago
  crates/linter/src/rule/security/tainted_data_to_sink.rs:96-120. It also
  handles EchoTag (`<?=`), which the claim does not mention.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do not add a Tainted accessory to crates/types AccessoryKind
> (crates/types/src/lib.rs:764). A kind bitset there would break hash-consing
> and type equality, and it would show up in every union, subtype and describe
> path. Instead, keep a parallel taint side-map in the checker's Locals
> (src/checker.rs, imbl map keyed like the narrowing entries). Join it at merges
> the same way narrowing states merge, and keep it opt-in behind a config flag.
>
> Sources: superglobal reads, which already go through checker/assignment.rs
> around line 751, plus sources configured in config.
>
> Propagation: concatenation, interpolation, sprintf, implode, array access and
> assignment.
>
> Clearing, with no false negatives from over-clearing:
>
> - casts to int or float, htmlspecialchars/htmlentities/intval/filter_var with
>   a sanitize filter, and bound prepared-statement arguments;
> - type facts the checker already proves, such as int, float, bool,
>   numeric-string or decimal-int-string, and a value narrowed to a finite
>   literal union through in_array or match;
> - functions listed in config or marked with an `@phpstan-rs-taint-escape`
>   phpdoc tag.
>
> Sinks: echo, print and short echo tags (taint.html); the SQL argument at the
> existing recognition points, checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:684 (mysqli_query)
> and checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:807 (mysqli::query), plus
> PDO::query/exec (taint.sql); exec, system, passthru, shell_exec and backtick
> (taint.shell); include/require (taint.include).
>
> Scope: intraprocedural only, meaning function parameters are untainted. A
> later step adds per-function summaries recording which parameters flow into
> sinks, cached in the registry the same way inferred return types are.
>
> A complementary, cheaper check is `sql.nonLiteral`, modelled on the
> non-literal-string check in checker/psr3.rs:95. It would flag query sinks
> whose argument is not provably literal-string, reusing the existing
> LiteralString accessory, as a strict opt-in.

#### K162. Type-aware SQL injection check

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, L (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** The single most impactful PHP security bug class, done more
  precisely than Mago's WordPress-only syntax check. It reuses phpstan-rs's
  unique SQL-sink knowledge.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/security/prepared_sql.rs:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:684`,
  `crates/types/src/concat.rs:87`
- **Risks:** A new accessory touches the type lattice and hash-consing. Escaped
  strings (real_escape_string, quote()) need to count as sanitized. Dynamic
  table/column names from allow-lists produce false positives, so a
  `@phpstan-sql-safe` escape hatch or ignore is needed.
- **Verification:** The Mago citation is accurate.
  crates/linter/src/rule/security/prepared_sql.rs:74-93 describes it as a check
  on `$wpdb` query methods and sets
  `requirements: RuleRequirements::Integration(Integration::WordPress)`. It is
  off by default (default_enabled false, around line 58).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Ship it as an opt-in check, `sql.nonConstantQuery` under [ext.sql]
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/sql.rs SqlSettings gets a
> `non_constant_query: bool`), built in two layers.
>
> Layer 1: an intraprocedural provenance walk at the sinks. Add a module
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/sql_reflection/injection.rs. The sinks are
> mysqli_query / mysqli::query / mysqli::real_query / mysqli::prepare,
> PDO::query/exec/prepare, and the DBAL Connection methods that
> resolve_dbal_sql_from_call (checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:869) and
> parameter_validation.rs:200 already dispatch on.
>
> - **When to skip:** if foldable_sql_string(), used at mysqli.rs:56, already
>   folds the argument to constant text, it's safe. This reuses the existing
>   folding and costs nothing.
> - **Otherwise, walk the concat, interpolation, sprintf and implode tree.** A
>   leaf is safe if it is:
>   - a literal or class constant;
>   - an expression whose inferred type has no string members, or only
>     literal-string / decimal-int-string members (AccessoryKind::LiteralString
>     and DecimalIntegerString, types/src/lib.rs:764). This is what makes
>     `'SELECT ' . $int` safe, even though the type becomes
>     non-falsy-uppercase-string, not literal (probe confirmed);
>   - a sprintf whose placeholders for non-safe arguments are all %d/%u/%f;
>   - a call to an escaping function: mysqli_real_escape_string /
>     mysqli::real_escape_string, PDO::quote, DBAL Connection::quote /
>     quoteIdentifier, intval/floatval/(int) casts, and a configurable
>     `safe_functions` list for project helpers like WordPress esc_sql or Piwigo
>     pwg_db_real_escape_string;
>   - a local variable whose reaching assignments are all safe.
>   Anything else gets reported. In particular that means string parameters,
>   properties, mixed values and array elements.
> - **Tip:** use prepare() with bound parameters.
>
> Layer 2, a follow-up: a parameter annotated `literal-string` or
> `@phpstan-sql-safe` counts as safe inside the function. Callers are then
> checked against that parameter with the same provenance walk, not with plain
> literal-string acceptance, because acceptance would reject safe int
> concatenation. This is what makes query wrappers like
> `function db_query(string $sql)` usable: without it the check fires once,
> inside the wrapper, and never at the call sites that actually build the
> injection.
>
> Do not add a new AccessoryKind::QuerySafe to the type lattice. It has no
> PHPDoc spelling, so it would be lost at every function, property and array
> boundary, while still costing hash-consing, subtyping, printing and
> concat/sprintf/implode propagation work in crates/types.

#### K37. Opt-in existence check for use imports backed by a namespace-prefix set

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Catches typoed imports (`use Typo\Namespaec;`) and imports left
  behind after a class is deleted or moved. Today these go unreported unless the
  alias is used in a checked position. Probe names-symbols/ui:
  `use Nonexistent\Thing;` and `use Typo\Namespaec;` produce no diagnostic. The
  same namespace set also enables namespace completion and validation in the
  LSP.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/symbol.rs:87`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/use_statement.rs:73`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:110`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:420`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/imports.rs:114`
- **Risks:** Imports of symbols from unscanned vendor code would false-positive,
  which is why the rule is opt-in and should be suppressed when a composer
  autoload root covers the prefix but was not scanned.
- **Verification:** Mago: all three citations are accurate.
  crates/codex/src/symbol.rs:87-90 add_symbol_name extends `namespaces` with
  get_symbol_namespaces (defined at ~186-190; it yields every `\`-prefix).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in `use.notFound` rule (config flag, default off) for plain
> `use X\Y;` imports. Put it inside the existing `check_use_class_imports` loop
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/imports.rs, which is already called from
> checker.rs:1433-1434 next to the function/const import checks. The rule
> reports when `registry.lookup_class(path)` fails (this covers the
> case-insensitive fallback) and `path` is not a known namespace prefix. Don't
> maintain a namespace set incrementally in registry/index.rs. Build a
> folded-prefix `FxHashSet` lazily (OnceLock / cached field) from the keys of
> `Registry::classes` (NameTable, registry.rs:85), `functions` (registry.rs:90)
> and `global_constants` (registry.rs:100). Drop the cache whenever
> `Project::update_file` changes the registry's declarations. Mago never prunes
> its set (codex/src/symbol.rs:87 only extends it), so a lazy rebuild avoids
> stale namespaces in the LSP. Add a did-you-mean from the existing class-name
> suggestion helpers. The same cached set can later back LSP namespace
> completion. Build an unused-import rule (`use.unused`) in the same place
> alongside it, or ahead of it. grep turns up only `closure.unusedUse` in
> checker/unused.rs:127, so there's no unused class-import check today. That
> rule covers "import left behind after the class was deleted" more broadly than
> an existence check does.

#### K156. Swapped needle/haystack detection

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Catches silent wrong results, e.g. explode returning the whole
  string, or strpos always returning false.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/suspicious_explode_arguments.rs:98`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls.rs:598`
- **Risks:** str_contains(\$ch, 'a')-style checks of a single character against
  a short literal can be legitimate. Keep it behind the existing opt-in flag.
- **Verification:** Mago: the check runs in
  crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/suspicious_explode_arguments.rs, lines
  ~98-157 (starting at `fn check`). It fires when the second argument is a
  string literal no longer than `cfg.threshold` and the first argument is not a
  literal of equal or shorter length.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a second heuristic next to check_swapped_argument_names
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls.rs:536), gated by the same
> `check_swapped_arguments` extras flag
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs:19). Report the same
> `arguments.possiblySwapped` identifier, with a message that names the
> separator position. Limit it to `explode()` at first. Fire when argument #2
> (the string) infers, through the scope, to a constant string, or a union of
> constant strings, that is non-empty and no longer than a small threshold
> (default 1–2 bytes), and argument #1 (the separator) is not a constant string
> of that length or shorter. This is Mago's rule
> (crates/linter/src/rule/correctness/suspicious_explode_arguments.rs:98-140),
> but it uses phpstan-rs's inferred constant types in place of bare literals, so
> `$sep = ' '; explode($s, $sep)` is caught too. Skip spread and named
> arguments, as the existing check does. Do not extend it to strpos, stripos,
> strrpos, str_contains, str_starts_with, str_ends_with or substr_count unless
> there is a much narrower trigger. `strpos('+-*/', $op) !== false` and
> `str_contains(',;', $ch)` are real set-membership idioms: a short literal
> haystack and a variable needle, exactly the shape the proposal would flag. If
> those functions are added at all, they need their own sub-flag and should fire
> only when the needle argument infers to a string whose minimum length is
> greater than the literal haystack's length, which makes the call provably
> always false or 0.

#### K175. Namespace declaration structure checks

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Covers probes m51 and m52 and the 'No code may exist outside of
  namespace {}' case. Mago misses the last one, and phpstan-rs silently resolves
  such code as belonging to the preceding namespace, which is wrong name
  resolution rather than just a missed error.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/statement.rs:93`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/statement.rs:137`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:326`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:113`
- **Risks:** Files that are templates with inline HTML before `<?php namespace`
  are also fatal in PHP, so reporting is correct. Keep declare() and leading
  comments/whitespace allowed.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are right.
  crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/statement.rs: the first-statement check
  runs from about line 68 and reports at 91-93. It lets Declare, Namespace,
  OpeningTag and a shebang come first.
- **Refined proposal:**

> No soft-error or checker plumbing is needed. PHP rejects every one of these
> cases at compile time, so the whole file fails like any other syntax error.
> The fix is to return a normal ParseError, the same way every other syntax
> error already reaches the user.
>
> (1) In crates/syntax/src/parser.rs, add state to parse_program (line 297) with
> these fields:
>
> - `saw_ns: Option<braced: bool>` — whether a namespace was seen yet, and
>   whether it was braced.
> - `saw_non_declare_stmt: bool`
> - `last_was_braced_block_end: bool`
>
> Change parse_namespace_stmt (line 325) to also return whether the namespace
> was braced. Then raise a ParseError at the offending span in each of these
> cases:
>
> - (a) A `namespace` comes after a top-level statement that is not a declare.
>   InlineHTML/`?>` with non-whitespace output counts as such a statement. PHP
>   says: "Namespace declaration statement has to be the very first statement or
>   after any declare call".
> - (b) Braced and unbraced namespaces are mixed, in either order.
> - (c) An unbraced namespace has no name (`namespace;`). An empty qualified
>   name with no `{`.
> - (d) Any statement other than declare or `__halt_compiler` comes after a
>   braced namespace block but outside one: "No code may exist outside of
>   namespace {}".
>
> (2) In crates/syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:173, the namespace arm of
> parse_statement is only reached for non-top-level namespaces, because
> parse_program intercepts top-level ones. It should return a ParseError
> ("unexpected namespace") instead of emitting a StmtKind::Namespace marker.
> Today `function h(){ namespace X; }` is accepted and the marker lands in a
> function body, where name_resolution.rs:417 calls set_namespace on it.
>
> A `braced: bool` on StmtKind::Namespace (ast.rs:113) is optional and is only
> needed if later consumers care.
>
> Add parser unit tests and one fixture per case. Check each against `php -l`.

#### K177. Missing statement-level compile errors

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Covers probes m32, m54, m56, m87, n10 and n18. All are PHP
  compile-time fatals; Mago misses unset(\$this) and top-level yield as well.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/try.rs:33`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/control_flow.rs:29`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/function_like/parameter.rs:144`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:16`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs:152`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/control_flow.rs:269`
- **Risks:** Top-level yield inside an included-file body is still a compile
  error, so there is no legitimate exception. Keep the duplicate-default check
  purely syntactic.
- **Verification:** Mago citations check out: try.rs:33 (try with no catch or
  finally), :50 (union in catch; the note in the code says "Before PHP 7.1", not
  8.0), :66/:76 (invalid catch hint, meaning anything that is not an identifier
  or a union); control_flow.rs:29 (duplicate switch default;
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the confirmed compile-time fatals to phpstan-rs's existing declaration and
> keyword passes. Checked with `php -l` (php 8.5) and probed in phpstan-rs,
> where every one of these was silent:
>
> (1) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_like_declarations.rs, inside the
> parameter loop next to `parameter.variadicNotLast` (lines 266-272), add
> `if p.variadic && p.default.is_some()` -> "Variadic parameter cannot have a
> default value." (parameter.variadicDefault).
>
> (2) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/keywords.rs, extend the `Scope` visitor's
> `walk_stmt` match and have `check_statement_keywords` (line 152) report:
>
> - `StmtKind::Try` with empty `catches` and `finally == None` ->
>   try.noCatchOrFinally.
> - a `Switch` with more than one case whose test is None ->
>   switch.duplicateDefault, reported at the second default.
> - for top-level bodies only, a yield / yield from reached without crossing a
>   closure or function boundary -> yield.outsideFunction. This needs an
>   expression walk that stops at closures, arrow functions and class bodies.
>   `body_contains_yield` / `expr_contains_yield`, used from
>   checker/expr.rs:3731/4010, may be reusable.
>
> (3) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs, `StmtKind::Unset` (line 778): a
> plain `$this` target -> "Cannot unset \$this." (unset.this). This mirrors
> `global.this` at stmt.rs:807.
>
> (4) Catch types, in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:
>
> - `catch (static $e)` is a compile fatal ("Bad class name in the catch
>   statement"). phpstan-rs currently resolves it to the enclosing class and
>   says "cannot catch C: it does not implement Throwable". It should instead
>   report catch.invalidType against the unresolved name reference.
> - Do NOT add a compile-error diagnostic for `catch (int $e)`. `php -l` accepts
>   it: PHP treats `int` as a class name there, so the existing class.notFound
>   is essentially correct. At most, reword the message.
>
> Keep all of these non-ignorable and level 0, purely syntactic, and add one
> fixture per identifier under tests/fixtures/checker/.

#### K178. Inheritance-declaration sanity (cycles, self-extends)

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Covers probes m70-m74 and the cycle and `class int` probes.
  Cycles also make every ancestor walk depend on ad-hoc seen-sets; reporting
  them makes the defect visible.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/inheritance.rs:48`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/inheritance.rs:28`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/inheritance.rs:72`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/mod.rs:87`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:553`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:121`
- **Risks:** PHP catches self-extension only at link time ('Class A not found'),
  but it is still always fatal. Cycle detection must run after all files load,
  and has to behave correctly under incremental update_file.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations check out. In
  mago/crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/inheritance.rs,
  check_extends reports "can only extend one other type" when extension_limit is
  set and extends.types.len() > 1 (about lines 26-40).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add these checks to the existing per-class legality pass,
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs check_inheritance_target_kinds (line 41;
> called from checker.rs:1509, oop.rs:996, expr.rs:155). A separate
> whole-program DFS is not needed. (1) Cycle and self-inheritance: starting from
> the class being checked, walk extends+implements through registry.lookup_class
> with a seen-set. If the walk reaches the starting class again, report
> `class.circularInheritance` on that class's name span, for example "Class A
> extends itself through A -> B -> A". `class C extends C` and
> `interface I extends I` are the one-step case of the same check. Because each
> class is checked on its own, every member of the cycle gets a report in its
> own file. It also stays correct under Project::update_file, since editing a
> parent already re-checks its transitive dependents. The walk can reuse the
> logic of Registry::class_extends_implements_closure
> (registry/hierarchy.rs:39), or read the ancestor_names map that
> precompute_ancestor_names already fills: the class is in a cycle if its own
> name appears in ancestor_names[class]. That lookup is O(1) and needs no new
> traversal. (2) Multiple extends on a class: if kind == Class and
> extends().len() > 1, report `class.multipleExtends`. PHP rejects this at parse
> time ("unexpected token ','"). Put the check in the checker rather than the
> parser, because the parser comment at
> crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:549-552 deliberately parses both kinds the
> same way. (3) Reserved names: a class-like declared with a reserved type name
> (int, float, bool, string, true, false, null, void, iterable, object, mixed,
> never, array, callable, static, self, parent, list is not reserved and must be
> left out) gets `class.reservedName`, checked case-insensitively on the last
> name segment. Also check extends/implements targets of self/parent/static, so
> that `extends self` reports "Cannot use 'self' as class name" and the
> misleading `class.notFound` it reports today (probe: "E extends unknown class
> self") goes away. Before fixing the list, confirm each name against `php -l`
> (php 8.5 is installed).

#### K247. Redundant inline @var tags

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Stale @var annotations hide later type changes; if the inferred
  type later becomes more precise, the redundant tag silently widens it back.
  Removing them keeps inference authoritative. Cheap to build on the existing
  machinery.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:341`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:488`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/var_tag_types.rs:593`
- **Risks:** Noise in legacy code, hence opt-in. Must skip tags whose job is
  IDE-only (such as generics the inference already matches), so equality must be
  exact, not just 'fits'.
- **Verification:** Mago: insert_variable_from_docblock starts at
  crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:306. Its is_redundant computation is at
  :341 (mutual is_contained_by, with no mixed, no generic parameter and no
  placeholder allowed), and it reports RedundantDocblockType in the else-if
  branch just after :376.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in `check_redundant_var_tags: bool` to `RulesSettings` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/rules_settings.rs, wired through the key table in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/app.rs:73. The proposal suggested a Registry setting,
> but the opt-in checks actually live in RulesSettings. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/var_tag_types.rs, add a `varTag.redundant`
> branch at the end of check_var_tag_against (:593). It fires only when all of
> these hold:
>
> - the setting is on;
> - the tag is not mixed, and `contains_phpstan_type(tag)` is false;
> - neither side contains a template, late-resolved (static/\$this) or
>   unresolved type;
> - the tag is structurally equal to value.doc (`*tag == value.doc`), which is
>   cheap because types are hash-consed. As an option, also fire on mutual
>   `registry.is_super_type_of == Yes` when the rendered strings match, so
>   aliases such as `array-key` vs `int|string` are not flagged;
> - the check runs on the final/fixed-point pass only, so a loop's first pass
>   (narrower types) never produces the report.
>
> Keep the `current == tag` early `continue` at :504, which currently skips
> re-tagging an existing variable to its identical type. Make it report under
> the setting instead of skipping silently, because that is exactly Mago's
> insert_variable_from_docblock case
> (crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:320-370). Message: "PHPDoc tag @var
> with type T is redundant: it's already the inferred type." Optionally add an
> LSP quick-fix that deletes the tag line.

#### K251. @must-use as #[NoDiscard] source

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Libraries that target PHP < 8.5 can mark immutable 'with'-er
  methods and result-returning functions today. Discarding their result is
  almost always a runtime logic bug (e.g. `$date->modify()` on
  DateTimeImmutable-style APIs).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:417`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:428`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:171`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/misc_rules.rs:9`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:750`
- **Risks:** Very low: it only fires where authors opted in.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate. Mago:
  crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:417-418 maps TagValue::MustUse to
  MetadataFlags::MUST_USE. crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:428-432 handles
  functions and :440-444 handles methods, each as
  `flags.must_use() || attributes contain NoDiscard`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `must_use: bool` field to `DocBlock` and a
> `"must-use" | "mago-must-use" | "psalm-must-use" | "phpstan-must-use"` arm in
> `apply_tag` (crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:750; the Mago parser normalizes the
> tag to `mustuse`, crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/tag/mod.rs:118). In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs, next to `no_discard` (:175,
> computed at :700-703) and `must_use_result` (:178, :704), add a third bit,
> `doc_must_use`. Do not OR it into `no_discard`. Merge it the same way at
> :789-790 (the trait/flatten merge), and have the phpdoc inheritance path carry
> it to overriding methods that have no docblock of their own. In
> `check_no_discard_statement`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/misc_rules.rs:73), also fire when
> `doc_must_use` is set, with three differences: (a) use its own identifiers
> (`method.resultUnused` / `function.resultUnused` /
> `staticMethod.resultUnused`); (b) leave out `.non_ignorable()`, because unlike
> `#[\NoDiscard]` a docblock marker has no runtime effect, so users must be able
> to baseline or ignore it; (c) word the message around "marked @must-use" and
> not the engine's NoDiscard wording. Add one fixture covering a function, an
> instance method, a static method and an inherited override, plus a negative
> case where the result is assigned or passed on.

#### K296. Honour @api in class.notFinal and add an opt-in require-@api-or-@internal check

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** Library authors can turn on the closed-classes check without it
  contradicting their documented public API. The companion check makes every
  extension point state its backward-compatibility intent, which is what the
  finality rule's @api exemption needs in order to be meaningful.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:414`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:433`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/class_shape.rs:156`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:704`
- **Risks:** Low. Projects that write @api at method level only still see the
  class-level report, and the existing registry does not parse method-level @api
  for classes (phpstan_api.rs:58-61).
- **Verification:** Mago: all three citations are correct.
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:414-431 is
  enforce_class_finality, which exempts final, abstract, is_public_api (@api)
  and classes with children. Line 433 is require_api_or_internal, limited to
  abstract classes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Part 1: in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/class_shape.rs closed_class_shape
> (the notFinal condition around lines 156-160), add `&& !info.is_api()` to the
> exemptions, and extend the fixture/test for class.notFinal with an @api
> non-final class that stays silent and an @api final class that still gets the
> method.protectedInFinalClass checks. Scope the @api exemption to
> class.notFinal only. Part 2, which is optional and lower priority: add
> `require_api_or_internal: bool` (default false) to ClassShapeSettings in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/parent_calls.rs:22-39, wire it in app.rs next to
> check_closed_classes (app.rs:146) and in session.rs:105/279, and make the file
> loop at class_shape.rs:112-124 run it independently of closed_classes. Add a
> sibling fn that, for abstract classes, interfaces and traits whose ClassInfo
> has neither is_api() nor is_internal(), emits `classLike.missingApiOrInternal`
> on the name span. The message should say which one it is (abstract class,
> interface or trait).

#### K83. Support @where / @psalm-if-this-is receiver constraints

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Lets libraries express `Collection<T>::sum()` only when T is
  int|float, `Option<T>::flatten()` only when T is Option\<U>, or
  `Result<T,E>::unwrap()` constraints. Calls that would fail at runtime are
  caught, and the method body gets the narrowed `$this`, so it type-checks
  without casts.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:696`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/resolver/method.rs:776`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:818`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/template_inference.rs:1099`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:164`
- **Risks:** This is a non-standard tag, so it needs documentation. Stubs will
  not carry it, so incidence depends on adoption; that affects sequencing only,
  not whether the feature is correct.
- **Verification:** All citations check out. In mago,
  crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs:695-735 loops over the
  TagValue::Where tags. It rejects a tag on a function or closure (there is no
  method metadata) and on a static method (InvalidWhereTag), and otherwise
  stores `where_constraints.insert(template_name, con ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add the receiver precondition as a whole receiver type rather than a
> per-template map. Parse `@psalm-if-this-is Type` and `@phpstan-if-this-is`,
> and accept Mago's `@where T is X` as sugar, in crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs.
> It goes next to `self_out`: add a `this_is: Option<TypeNode>` field, plus
> alias entries in the prefix table around lines 637/680 and the tag-name list
> around line 1205. Resolve it in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs
> beside `self_out` (line 166 field, the doc-mapping at ~748, map at ~259, merge
> at ~869). It also needs the same template/`static` fixups as `self_out` in
> registry/resolve.rs (lines 493, 731, 1247, 1750). A `@where T is X` desugars
> to the declaring class type with X in T's slot and the other templates left as
> their own params/bounds.
>
> Call site: in checker/expr.rs, next to the `apply_self_out` call (~line 1485),
> substitute the class templates on the constraint with the existing
> `substitute_class_templates` / `class_template_bindings`
> (checker/generics/substitution.rs:51). Then report `method.ifThisIs` only when
> `is_super_type_of(constraint, receiver).no()`. Stay silent on maybe, because
> an erased receiver whose templates fell back to bounds must not produce false
> positives.
>
> Method body: in checker/function_decl.rs:620, where `$this` is seeded as
> `Type::object(c, own)`, seed the intersection or the constraint type when the
> tag is present. Also report the tag on static methods and free functions,
> extending `check_self_out` in checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:525 as the model.

#### K154. Secrets/security hygiene: #[SensitiveParameter], timing-unsafe comparison, hard-coded secrets

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness,
  linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Adds a useful security check that phpstan-rs lacks entirely. |
  Adds a security category phpstan-rs lacks. Type awareness removes Mago's main
  false-positive sources (bool/int params, comparisons against literal
  sentinels). #[SensitiveParameter] keeps secrets out of stack traces and logs.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_insecure_comparison.rs:94`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/sensitive_parameter.rs:94`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_literal_password.rs:100`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/tainted_data_to_sink.rs:96`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1`, `ROADMAP.md:2646`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/banned.rs:26`
- **Risks:** Name heuristics produce some noise, e.g. `$tokenType === 'bearer'`
  is excluded by the literal rule. Keep it opt-in. | Name-based heuristics are
  inherently fuzzy, so ship opt-in with a configurable name pattern list. Taint
  needs careful sanitizer modelling (htmlspecialchars, intval, casts).
- **Verification:** One path is wrong. The secret-name helper is at
  crates/linter/src/rule/utils/security.rs:180 (is_password), not
  crates/linter/src/utils/security.rs. It also strips a leading `$` and a
  `get`/`get_` prefix, and skips strings that start with `--` (lines 180-203).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one opt-in key, `check_secret_hygiene`, to
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs next to the existing opt-in heuristics
> (check_boolean_trap, check_identity_vs_equals,
> check_loose_haystack_comparison, lines 13-41). Make the name pattern
> configurable, defaulting to names ending in
> password/passwd/secret/token/apikey/api_key, case-insensitive after stripping
> `_`. It covers three things. (1) `comparison.timingUnsafe`: `==`, `===`, `!=`
> or `!==` where both operands' resolved types are string subtypes and
> non-constant (not a ConstantString or a literal). One side must be a
> secret-named variable, property, parameter, array-dim key or getter, or a
> parameter carrying #[SensitiveParameter]. Suggest hash_equals(). Using types
> removes Mago's false positives
> (crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_insecure_comparison.rs:94 only matches
> names) on `$token === null`, int or bool counters, and comparisons with a
> sentinel. (2) `parameter.missingSensitiveAttribute`: a secret-named parameter
> whose declared or phpdoc type is string-like (not bool, int or float), gated
> on php-version >= 8.2. Offer an insert-attribute quick fix in the LSP. (3)
> `secret.hardcoded`: a non-empty string literal assigned to a secret-named
> variable, property or constant, or used as its default. Skip test directories
> by default, since fixtures produce noise. Leave out the proposal's item (d),
> XSS sinks and configurable sinks and sanitizers. That belongs in the design of
> the existing ROADMAP D4 (ROADMAP.md:2646), not in this check.

#### K159. Complexity and size metrics family

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Wanted by teams (tomasvotruba/cognitive-complexity is top-25 on
  Packagist, per TOP100_PHPSTAN_EXTENSIONS.md:39). Cheap on phpstan-rs's
  existing AST. Doing match arms and cognitive complexity correctly beats Mago's
  version.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/maintainability/cyclomatic_complexity.rs:195`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/maintainability/halstead.rs:181`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/maintainability/excessive_nesting.rs:122`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/maintainability/too_many_methods.rs:116`
- **phpstan-rs:** `ROADMAP.md:2589`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:900`
- **Risks:** Thresholds are opinionated, so ship opt-in. Baseline churn if the
  value is in the message: put it in a tip and keep the message constant.
- **Verification:** Only small corrections. In Mago's cyclomatic_complexity.rs,
  the rule targets functions and closures as well as class-likes (check at ~:195
  dispatches to check_function_like for Node::Function and Node::Closure), so it
  is not only a class-level sum.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build ROADMAP Phase 96 D1 as a purely syntactic, per-file, opt-in metrics
> pass. It should not hook into
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:900, which runs inside type
> inference and scope setup. Metrics need no types, so keep them out of the
> checker's hot path.
>
> - **Module:** a new crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/metrics.rs, alongside
>   banned.rs and class_shape.rs. It uses the Visitor/walk_\* helpers in
>   crates/syntax/src/visit.rs (walk_function_decl:421, walk_class_def:438,
>   walk_method_decl:478). The ROADMAP's cited src/ast_walk.rs does not exist,
>   so fix that reference too.
> - **Incremental and LSP:** results are per-file, so they cache and re-run with
>   the file's own update, with no transitive dependents.
> - **Config:** a `[rules.metrics]` section, off by default, with one optional
>   threshold key per metric. An unset key means the metric is not checked.
> - **Metrics, in priority order:**
>   1. Cognitive complexity (Campbell/SonarSource: nesting increments, sequences
>      of the same boolean operator counted once, recursion and labelled
>      break/continue increments). This is the one teams actually ask for
>      (tomasvotruba/cognitive-complexity).
>   2. McCabe cyclomatic. Count every non-default `case` and every `match` arm
>      (the default arm too, or document the choice). Mago counts only `default`
>      (mago
>      crates/linter/src/rule/maintainability/cyclomatic_complexity.rs:334),
>      which undercounts.
>   3. Maximum nesting depth. Closures and arrow functions are their own
>      measured bodies.
>   4. Parameter count, with a separate constructor threshold that can exclude
>      promoted parameters.
>   5. Class-size counts (methods, properties, enum cases), with toggles for
>      trivial getters/setters and property hooks.
> - **Skip Halstead:** its volume/difficulty/effort thresholds are not
>   actionable and produce noise.
> - **Diagnostics:** stable identifiers (`complexity.cognitive`,
>   `complexity.cyclomatic`, `complexity.nesting`, `function.tooManyParameters`,
>   `class.tooManyMethods`, ...). The message stays constant, e.g. "Method
>   Foo::bar() has cognitive complexity above the configured limit". The
>   measured value and threshold go in the tip, so baselines don't churn on
>   small edits.
> - **Later, optional:** LSP code lenses showing the metric value. D1b
>   (dependency-tree complexity) stays a follow-up.

#### K165. PHP-version-aware modernization suggestions

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Upgrade assistance with safe auto-fixes. The static-closure and
  FQ-call rules have real runtime value (no captured \$this, which keeps objects
  alive; opcode specialisation).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/clarity/str_contains.rs:107`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/prefer_first_class_callable.rs:107`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/best_practices/prefer_static_closure.rs:110`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/clarity/explicit_octal.rs:85`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/consistency/ambiguous_function_call.rs:110`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs:226`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs:193`
- **Risks:** Stylistic rules are noise for some teams, so keep each key
  separately opt-in. The compiler special-function list must be kept in sync
  with php-src.
- **Verification:** Mago: all five cited files exist, and each does what the
  idea says. clarity/str_contains.rs is gated on PHP80 at :91, and its check
  (around :107-130) takes only strict !==/=== false as safe.
  prefer_first_class_callable.rs:92 and explicit_octal.rs:69 are gated on PHP81.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/modernize.rs, registered like the other ext
> groups (for example ext/strict_rules.rs) under an opt-in `[ext.modernize]`
> config section in crates/config, with each key off by default. Each rule
> reports only when `registry.php_supports(feature).yes()` holds
> (registry.rs:226), and each attaches a DiagnosticFix
> (crates/diagnostics/src/fix.rs) that surfaces as an LSP quickfix
> (lsp/protocol.rs:305). Do them in this order:
>
> (a) `functionCall.unqualifiedOptimizable`: an unqualified call inside a
> namespace, not imported with `use function`, to a function from a fixed list
> of the compile-time-specialised functions from php-src (strlen, count, is_\*
> type checks, in_array, array_key_exists, chr, ord, call_user_func(_array),
> func_get_args, get_class, gettype, boolval/intval/strval/floatval, defined,
> constant, array_slice, sprintf, and so on). Only report when the registry
> resolves no `Ns\name` function. The fix prefixes `\`.
>
> (b) `closure.canBeStatic`: a non-static closure or arrow function inside a
> class-like, whose body uses no `$this`, `parent::`, `self`/`static` instance
> context, or `$this`-capturing nested closure. It also needs a use site the
> checker fully knows: immediately invoked, or passed directly as an argument to
> a function/method parameter from stubs or source that has no
> `@param-closure-this` and isn't `Closure::bind`/`bindTo`/`call`. Never report
> closures that are assigned, returned, stored, or passed to unknown or
> unresolved callees (this covers macro-style rebinding). Reuse the binding
> knowledge in checker/calls/closure_context.rs. The fix inserts `static`.
>
> (c) Low-value style keys, bundled last:
> `strpos.toStrContains`/`toStrStartsWith` (only when the comparison is strict
> against `false`/`0` and both arguments are typed `string`, so no coercion
> changes), `octal.implicit` (0777 to 0o777, PHP 8.1+), `instanceof.stringable`
> (`method_exists($x,'__toString')` becomes `$x instanceof \Stringable` when
> `$x` is an object).
>
> (d) `callable.firstClass`, only when a string or array callable literal is
> passed directly to a `callable`/`Closure` parameter, never when it's assigned
> to a variable.
>
> Add fixture pairs under tests/fixtures/checker/ for each rule, including
> negative cases: a closure passed to an unknown macro-registration method, a
> shadowing namespaced `strlen`, and a callable string used as an array key.

#### K168. Redundancy family checks

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Cheap signal on dead or copy-paste code. Type awareness removes
  the false positives in Mago's no-redundant-math (casting idioms).
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_final.rs:1`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_readonly.rs:1`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_duplicate_match_arm.rs:1`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_math.rs:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs:338`,
  `ROADMAP.md:2589`
- **Risks:** Some teams write final on methods deliberately in preparation for
  un-finalising the class, so keep these opt-in.
- **Verification:** 1) The proposal says `classConstant.protectedInFinalClass`
  should be added to complete the family. That is wrong: phpstan-rs already has
  it.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Ship the family as opt-in extras keys, with one part removed and several
> narrowed:
>
> 1. DROP `classConstant.protectedInFinalClass`. It already exists in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/class_shape.rs:216-233, next to
>    method/property.protectedInFinalClass (lines 184-213), so the proposal's
>    premise is stale here.
> 2. `method.redundantFinal`: goes in the existing `if info.is_final()` block in
>    class_shape.rs:171, using the method's `is_final` flag from
>    crates/syntax/src/ast.rs (the `is_final` fields around lines 327/396/404).
>    Also cover enums, which are implicitly final. Skip private final
>    constructors: that is the one form PHP does not warn about, so it cannot be
>    told apart from intent. Fix: delete the `final` token.
> 3. `property.redundantReadonly`: same block, keyed on the class's readonly
>    flag and the property's `readonly` (ast.rs:203/321). This includes promoted
>    constructor params. Fix: delete the modifier.
> 4. `match.duplicateArmResult`: build this as part of ROADMAP D3
>    (ROADMAP.md:2622, which already names Match/Switch). Don't ship it as a
>    separate check. Compare arm result expressions with the side-effect-free
>    structural helper `is_duplicate_side_effect_free_operand` used by
>    check_duplicate_operands
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs:307-331). Only flag arms that
>    are the same after spans are dropped. Suggest merging the conditions, but
>    skip the `default` arm.
> 5. Type-aware `binaryOp.identity`, placed next to check_duplicate_operands in
>    operators.rs:
>    - `$x * 1`, `$x / 1` and `1 * $x`: when the operand is int or float.
>    - `$x + 0` and `$x - 0`: only when the operand is int. For floats they are
>      not identities: `php -r` shows `-0.0 + 0` gives `float(0)` and loses the
>      sign. Mago's syntactic rule misses this too.
>    - `$x . ''`: only when the operand is string. For int/float/Stringable it
>      is a real conversion. Never flag numeric-string, mixed or union operands.
> 6. `static.inFinalClass`: flag `static::`/`new static` only directly in method
>    bodies of a final non-trait class. Leave out closures, because
>    `Closure::bind`/`bindTo` can change the called-class scope, and leave out
>    trait bodies. Do not touch `@return static` or the `static` return type,
>    which have their own meaning for the declared type. All keys stay off by
>    default. Reuse the existing diagnostic/extras plumbing. Add one fixture per
>    key under crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/, including negative
>    cases: float `+0`, `'5' * 1`, `$i . ''` for an int, a closure in a final
>    class, and a trait.

#### K157. Arithmetic/bitwise constant results

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness)
- **Benefit:** Catches a wrong literal or operand in math code, such as a
  mistyped modulus.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_math.rs:282`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs:630`
- **Risks:** Float `* 0` can give -0.0 or NaN, so limit it to int operands. Skip
  constant-folded macros.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_math.rs:282 is the Modulo arm
  ("Redundant modulo by `1`: the result is always `0`."), and the Some(-1)
  modulo arm comes right after it. Line 99 is the start of `check` (Node::Binary
  targets at :89).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a sibling to `check_division_by_zero` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs, e.g.
> `check_constant_arithmetic_result(op, l, r, l_ty, r_ty, span)`, called from
> the same BinOp site. Identifier `binaryOp.constantResult`, message like
> "Result of `$x % 1` is always 0." Ship it opt-in or at a high level, following
> the rule for correct checks with unproven broad value.
>
> Report only absorbing-element cases where one operand decides the result and
> the other operand's type is not itself a single constant:
>
> - `% 1` and `% -1` give 0. This applies to any number operand, since PHP casts
>   to int, but not to an array or object operand, which already fails
>   binaryOp.invalid.
> - `& 0` gives 0 and `| -1` gives -1, with int operands.
> - `* 0` gives 0 only when both operands are int. Skip floats because of -0.0
>   and NaN.
>
> Don't report shifts: `>> 64` gives 0 or -1 and depends on the platform.
>
> Decide which operand is the deciding one from the syntax, not from narrowed
> scope types. The deciding operand must be:
>
> - an int literal,
> - a unary minus of a literal, or
> - a fully literal constant-folded subexpression (e.g. `2 - 1`).
>
> Explicitly exclude class and global constant fetches, because named constants
> are often deliberate configuration or flags. Also exclude variables whose
> value comes from narrowing.
>
> Optionally, fix the missed inference in the same change: `$x | -1` should be
> `-1`, and `$x & 0` is already `0`. That improves precision whether or not the
> rule ships.
>
> Leave ×1, /1, +0 and -0 to a style or redundancy check. Add fixtures for each
> operator, plus negative cases for float `* 0`, `& self::NONE` and narrowed
> `$n % $one`.

#### K297. Boolean-literal comparison simplification (\$bool === true) with suggested rewrite

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** Style and readability for general PHP code. Limiting it to
  operands typed exactly bool keeps it sound: `$x === true` on bool|int or
  bool|null carries meaning and is left alone. It is distinct from redundancy
  checks, which concern always-true or always-false outcomes, not verbose
  spelling.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/comparison.rs:74`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs:37`
- **Risks:** Pure style, so it must stay opt-in. Some teams prefer `=== false`
  after functions that return bool, and the check has to follow the inferred
  type, not a PHPDoc-only bool on a mixed native type.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are wrong. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/comparison.rs:73-127 has the block
  itself. It is gated on `context.settings.no_boolean_literal_comparison`, which
  is declared at crates/analyzer/src/settings.rs:133 and defaults to false at
  :411.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in toggle, `ext.extras.check_boolean_literal_comparison`. It goes
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs next to check_identity_vs_equals (line
> 39, with a resolve line near line 78) and is registered in app.rs next to
> lines 203-208.
>
> The check itself goes in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/strict_idioms.rs,
> inside check_strict_expression_idioms, beside the existing identity-vs-equals
> block at lines 204-229. That block already matches
> `ExprKind::Binary(Identical|NotIdentical, l, r)` and infers both sides.
>
> What it matches:
>
> - Operators: Identical, NotIdentical, Equal and NotEqual.
> - One side is `Literal::Bool` (or a `true`/`false` constant fetch).
> - The other side's inferred type is exactly `bool`. Accept only the full bool,
>   not bool|null, true/false alone, or mixed. When the type is a single `true`
>   or `false`, the existing constant-condition rules already report the
>   comparison.
> - The operand's type must also be certain without PHPDoc: skip when the native
>   type is not bool and phpdoc-certainty is off, so that `=== true` used as a
>   guard on a `@param bool` parameter with a mixed native type is not flagged.
>
> What it reports:
>
> - Identifier `equal.booleanLiteral` (or `identical.booleanLiteral` for
>   ===/!==).
> - The message includes the rewritten expression. Negate when (`===`/`==` with
>   false) or (`!==`/`!=` with true).
> - Attach a `DiagnosticFix` (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:120, turned into an
>   LSP quick fix by crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs:311). The fix
>   replaces the whole binary span with the operand's source text, prefixed with
>   `!` when needed.
> - Wrap the operand in parentheses when `!` would bind differently: an
>   assignment, ternary, `??`, a binary operator weaker than `!`, or a
>   `print`/`yield`. Take the operand text from a source slice rather than the
>   printer, so formatting and existing parentheses survive.
> - Skip spans that the checker synthesizes (for example from match or switch
>   desugaring), as Mago does with its zero-span guard at comparison.rs:79.
>
> Put tests in checker/tests covering: bool operand, bool|null (not flagged), a
> PHPDoc-only bool on a mixed native type (not flagged), both negation
> directions, a literal on either side, and a fix that needs parentheses.

#### K163. Member naming conventions

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Common team requirement. Overriding-member awareness is something
  Mago's syntactic rule can't do, and it removes its main false positive.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/consistency/method_name.rs:111`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/consistency/class_name.rs:94`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:574`
- **Risks:** Purely stylistic, so opt-in only. Variable naming in legacy code
  produces volume.
- **Verification:** The Mago method-name rule is at
  crates/linter/src/rule/consistency/method_name.rs. The config struct with
  camel, either and use_snake_case_for_tests is at lines 34-44 and defaults to
  disabled (default_enabled false).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in `[rules.naming]` section, on by kind only when configured. Reuse
> NamePattern (crates/phpstan-rs/src/architecture.rs:97, the `/regex/`-or-text
> parser that should_be_named already uses) and add named presets (camelCase,
> snake_case, PascalCase, UPPER_SNAKE). Kinds: class, interface, trait, enum,
> enum_case, method, function, property, class_constant, constant, parameter.
> Each kind takes `pattern`, `exclude`, and an optional `namespace` selector
> that reuses the architecture selector matching. Methods get a `tests` pattern
> override for PHPUnit test methods, found through the registry's TestCase
> ancestry, not Mago's `test` prefix heuristic. Implement it as one
> declaration-level pass next to project/architecture.rs, walking FileState ASTs
> of analysed (non-vendor) files, with identifiers `naming.<kind>`. The one
> feature a syntactic linter can't match: skip any method, property, constant or
> parameter whose name is fixed by an inherited declaration (parent class,
> interface or trait from the registry, including vendor and built-in stubs),
> and blame only the root declaration in analysed code. Also skip magic methods,
> `$this` and superglobals. Leave variable naming out of the first cut, or keep
> it behind its own key: it produces a lot of noise in legacy code and has no
> runtime meaning.

#### K295. Opt-in impure-call-in-condition check backed by transitive purity

- **Value/cost:** 2/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** Finds evaluation-order hazards, for example
  `if ($it->next() && $it->current() > 0)`, where a side effect in one operand
  changes what another operand reads. It also marks conditions whose narrowing
  phpstan-rs may later drop because the call can invalidate property facts.
  Using transitive purity gives far fewer false positives than Mago's
  annotation-only version on unannotated code.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:162`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block_flags.rs:58`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/purity.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:532`
- **Risks:** Idioms such as `while ($row = $stmt->fetch())`,
  `if (!$file->open())` and `if (preg_match(...))` with by-ref output are impure
  on purpose. An exemption for an assignment-of-call as the whole condition is
  needed, and the check should stay opt-in.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:162-178 is
  accurate. It checks
  `!allow_side_effects_in_conditions && block_context.flags.inside_conditional()
  && !invocation.target.is_pure_or_mutation_free()`
  and reports IssueCode::SideEffectsInCondition ("side-effects-in-condition",
  code.rs:281/613 ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> If built at all, make it a small opt-in style rule and not a correctness
> check. Add a flag in crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/extras.rs, off by default. Add
> a condition-depth counter on the checker, next to `in_condition_position`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:532). That field is a flag cleared with
> mem::take and only covers the direct condition, so it can't be reused. Report
> a call only when its callee signature returns false from
> `is_transitively_pure()`, reusing the same lookup that
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/noop.rs:249-381 already does for function,
> method and static calls. Exempt calls with unknown or unresolved callees
> rather than flagging them. Also exempt these idioms: (a) a condition that is
> an assignment from a call: `while ($row = $stmt->fetch())`; (b) a condition
> that is exactly one call, possibly negated or compared to a literal:
> `if (!mkdir(...))`, `if ($stmt->execute() === false)`,
> `if (preg_match(..., $m))`. With those exemptions it would only fire on mixed
> conditions such as `if ($it->next() && $it->current() > 0)`. Build it only
> after higher-value work is done.

### 3.3 robustness (39)

#### K29. Key the incremental dependency graph by resolved, case-folded FQNs including PHPDoc and constant references

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, M (aspect: names-symbols, incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** A file that references a changed class as `\App\C`, `Sub\C`, an
  alias (`use App\C as Base`), or in another case currently never enters
  `dependents["C"]`. deps.rs records the written text, and project.rs:976 looks
  up `bare_name("App\\C")` = `C`. Editing C therefore leaves stale diagnostics
  in those files in the LSP until they are touched.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:706`,
  `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:485`, `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:68`,
  `crates/codex/src/signature_builder.rs:76`, `crates/fingerprint/src/lib.rs:66`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/deps.rs:53`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/deps.rs:61`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:976`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1230`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_updates.rs:199`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/deps.rs:55` (+4 more)
- **Risks:** Type-hint names inside docblocks resolve at registry time, not in
  the AST. deps must resolve them with the same NameContext or an
  over-approximation must be kept for them. A missed name in an incremental
  index means a stale diagnostic, so extend the tests before switching. | Every
  resolution path has to be covered: `self`, `static` and `parent` resolve
  through the enclosing class, which is already a dependency of the file.
  Dynamic names (`new $x`, class_alias) cannot be resolved statically.
- **Verification:** Mostly accurate. Mago: reference.rs:68 is the
