  SymbolReferences struct, which starts at about line 68 and holds the body,
  signature and overridden-member maps. reference.rs:482-487 is
  add_reference_for_method_call, which uses ascii_lowercase_word(class).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Rewrite crates/phpstan-rs/src/deps.rs so `referenced_names` returns resolved,
> case-folded keys instead of the `written` text. Classes in expressions,
> extends/implements/traits, catch, attributes and type hints
> (TypeHint::class_names() already returns &QualifiedName) record
> `name.resolved_class()`. Function and constant names record both halves of
> `name.candidates()`. Fold every key with registry::function_key/folded_key.
> Folding constants too is a safe over-approximation. self/static/parent resolve
> to Unresolved and are skipped, because the enclosing class is already a
> dependency. The resolution logic already exists in project/use_sites.rs
> `resolve_class_ref`/ClassFnRefWalker (line 113ff), so share it or mirror it.
>
> Add doc-comment references. Walk the file with
> syntax::name_resolution::for_each_in_context (name_resolution.rs:69) and scan
> each doc_comment on classes, functions, methods, properties and class
> constants for class-shaped identifiers. Either parse them with the phpdoc
> crate or tokenize them conservatively. Resolve each one through
> NameContext::resolve (name_resolution.rs:183) and insert it. Over-collecting
> here is harmless.
>
> In project.rs, drop `bare_name` (2142). Seed `changed_symbols` in
> update_file_cancellable (980-981) and unindex_file (816-817), and the frontier
> in transitive_affected_files_from (1248), with folded FQNs. For global
> constants, add a separate helper next to `declared_names` (2155) that collects
> Declared::Constant and Define keys. Keep `declared_names` itself unchanged,
> since registry removal relies on it. Rewrite the stale 'deliberately bare-name
> / over-approximating' comments in deps.rs:8-26 and project.rs:972-979,
> 1244-1246 and 2135-2141.
>
> Add tests in project/tests/incremental_updates.rs for `\App\C`,
> `use App\C as Base; extends Base`, relative `Sub\C`, `new app\c` (case
> mismatch), a reference only in PHPDoc (`@param \App\C`, `@var`, `@mixin`), a
> namespaced function with global fallback, and a global const/define edit.

#### K66. Tri-state resource type (unknown/open/closed)

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a runtime-incorrect alreadyNarrowedType/impossibleType
  diagnostic on common resource-lifecycle code (open, use, close, re-check), and
  makes `open-resource` meaningful.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/resource/mod.rs:10`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/comparator/resource_comparator.rs:12`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:257`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/lib.rs:170`,
  `crates/types/src/parse.rs:1012`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:371`
- **Risks:** Stubs that declare `resource` returns (fopen) become Unknown, so an
  immediate is_resource() check on a fresh fopen() result stops being 'always
  true'. That is correct at runtime but changes existing output. Consider
  treating a fresh function return as Open through the stub PHPDoc
  `open-resource`.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are correct. TResource { closed:
  Option\<bool> } is at crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/resource/mod.rs:10.
  resource_comparator.rs:12-14 returns true when the container's `closed` is
  None. combiner.rs:257-271 turns RESOURCE, or open plus closed together, into
  closed: None.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/types/src/lib.rs:170, change Repr::Resource { closed: bool } to a
> three-state `ResourceState { Any, Open, Closed }` (or `closed: Option<bool>`).
> Then update every site that matches on it. The grep turned up 11: lib.rs:375
> and :525 (eq/hash), intern.rs:215 and :342, constructors.rs:126
> (Type::resource), display.rs:109-110 (Any shows as `resource`, Open as
> `open-resource`, Closed as `closed-resource`), and parse.rs:1012-1013
> (`resource` becomes Any, `open-resource` becomes Open, `closed-resource`
> becomes Closed). In super_type.rs:486 (scalars_disjoint), only Open and Closed
> are disjoint; Any overlaps both. is_super_type_of treats Any as a supertype of
> Open and Closed. The union/normalization step folds Open|Closed into Any. In
> predicates.rs:371, is_resource narrows the true branch to Open; the false
> branch removes Open and turns Any into Closed. So `resource|false` becomes
> `closed-resource|false`, and the alreadyNarrowed/impossible logic sees Any as
> "maybe", not "always true". To avoid losing precision on fresh handles, treat
> a call's stub/native return of Any as Open when the call result is bound. A
> function never hands back an already-closed handle, so
> fopen()/curl_init()/proc_open() results stay Open and
> `if (!is_resource($f = fopen(...)))` narrowing is unchanged. Then declared
> types (params, @var properties) stay Any, which is the case that matters.
> Optional follow-up: an extension marks the argument of
> fclose/closedir/pclose/proc_close/curl_close/finfo_close/socket_close as
> Closed after the call, which makes the `use after close` →
> `fwrite(closed-resource)` mismatch detectable. Leave coercion.rs, queries.rs
> and kinds.rs as they are, since they use `..`.

#### K89. Stop stale condition-alias replay

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Closes a soundness hole in which a flag variable replays a
  condition against a changed world. The snapshot design also stops replay from
  paying re-inference cost.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/formula.rs:839`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:379`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:570`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1335`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:185`
- **Risks:** The snapshot design loses flow-sensitive refinement when the alias
  target is narrowed further between assignment and test, which is rarely
  useful. Keep the delta-intersection semantics: replay should narrow with the
  snapshot types, not overwrite them.
- **Verification:** The citations are correct. At narrowing.rs:562-581,
  condition_alias_targets returns
  `narrowing_key(l).or_else(|| narrowing_key(r))` for comparisons (line 581), so
  it keeps only one operand key. The Variable arm at narrowing.rs:1334-1337
  replays the stored alias Expr through apply_narrowing.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Two-step fix. Step 1 (S, does most of the work) has two parts: (a) In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs, `condition_alias_targets` (562),
> keep the current narrowing keys and also add every variable name that
> `syntax::visit::any_expr_in_scope` finds anywhere in the rhs. That is the same
> walk `cond_references_variable` already does at 158-163. It covers comparison
> operands on both sides (581), arithmetic operands (`$y + 1`), subscript
> variables and call arguments. `record_if_body_flag_alias` (1475) then picks
> this up automatically, because it calls the same function. The self-reference
> guard in `record_condition_alias` (1391) has to keep looking only at the
> narrowing keys. Otherwise `$flag = $flag || ...` would be rejected, which is
> fine anyway. (b) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs,
> `purge_condition_aliases_targeting` (185-189) compares with `t == key`. Change
> it to `narrowing::key_depends_on(t, key)` from narrowing/predicates.rs:308,
> which `purge_branch_implied_facts_depending_on` already uses. Then rebinding
> `$o` also purges an alias whose target is `o->p`. Add fixtures for the three
> probe shapes below. Step 2 (M, optional, for precision): at record time,
> snapshot the true and false deltas by running `apply_narrowing` on cloned
> locals and diffing the result against the current locals. Store them in
> `ConditionAliasMap` in place of `Rc<Expr>`. On replay, intersect the deltas
> with the current types instead of overwriting them. Purge only on a rebind of
> a delta key. This keeps Mago's `int(5)` answer after the other operand is
> reassigned, and replay no longer re-infers anything. Do step 2 only after
> step 1. Step 1 alone is sound; step 2 only gets back the precision that step 1
> gives up.

#### K103. Switch: keep nested break/continue states

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a soundness hole. Probe cf/f s1:
  `$x = null; switch ($k) { case 1: if ($c) { break; } $x = 1; break; default:
  $x = 2; }`
  infers `1|2` instead of `1|2|null`. In s2, a variable assigned only after an
  early break is treated as definitely defined after the switch, so misuse of
  null goes unreported.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/break.rs:204`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/scope/case_scope.rs:19`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:85`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs:104`
- **Risks:** Minimal. Cases that end in a break at switch level are then counted
  twice, via the frame and via reaches_after_switch; this is harmless because
  merge_scopes is idempotent, but the last-statement check can simply be
  removed.
- **Verification:** Small line fixes only. In Mago,
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/break.rs:204 is the `if target_is_switch`
  branch. It counts the switches between the break and its target, and the
  actual `case_scope.record_break(&block_context.locals, ...)` call is at :209.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/switch.rs check_switch: replace the
>    discarding `self.loop_break_states.pop(); self.loop_continue_states.pop();`
>    (lines 121-122) with
>    `let brk = ...pop().unwrap_or_default(); let cont = ...pop().unwrap_or_default();`
>    and push every state from both into exit_states. A bare `break`/`continue`
>    or `continue 1` at switch level exits the switch in PHP. Deeper levels
>    already land in outer frames through the depth arithmetic in
>    stmt.rs:945-958. Keep the `reaches_after_switch` fall-off-the-end logic for
>    the last case (and the `None => is_last` path). The direct-break arm
>    (`is_switch_break_equivalent`) can stay, since merging a duplicate state is
>    idempotent, or it can be dropped now that the frame records it. Also
>    rewrite the stale comment at switch.rs:69-84 that says the frame is
>    "discarded below, never read". 2) Fix the companion hole in the same
>    commit. The `StmtKind::Switch` arm of always_terminates in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:131-149 only inspects each
>    case's last statement, so
>    `case 1: if ($c) { break; } return 1; default: return 2;` is treated as
>    terminating. Add a helper `contains_switch_level_exit(stmts)` that walks
>    nested if/else/try/block statements, but not nested loops, switches,
>    closures or functions. It should return true for `break`/`continue` with
>    level 1 (or None), and for `break N` when N levels resolve to this switch.
>    When the helper returns true for any case body, the switch does not always
>    terminate. Fixtures: the assertType probe below, a missing-return case for
>    g(), and a no-unreachable case for h().

#### K120. Real types for string offsets

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a confirmed false positive (a stale literal after a string
  offset write) and turns `mixed` into `string` for the very common `$s[0]`
  idiom, which enables return and argument checks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:1483`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/assignment/array_assignment.rs:101`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:4436`,
  `crates/types/src/offsets.rs:328`
- **Risks:** Code that relied on the mixed result may now get argument.type
  findings (true positives). Be careful not to claim a literal when the write
  value isn't exactly one byte (PHP uses only the first byte and warns).
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:1483-1531
  handle_array_access_on_string matches the claim. It returns non-empty-string
  when the base string is non-empty, and string (marked possibly-undefined)
  otherwise.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. **Reads (`crates/types/src/offsets.rs`).** Add a string arm to
>    `offset_value_type` / `offset_value_type_at`:
>    - Literal string with a literal int (or int-like) key, negative indices
>      counted from the end: in range gives the exact 1-byte literal; out of
>      range gives `''`.
>    - Any other string-typed member gives `string`. Do not use
>      `non-empty-string`, because an out-of-range read returns `''`.
>    - This also lets the `Union` arm's `collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>` succeed for
>      `string|array`, which currently degrades the whole read to `mixed`.
> 2. **Writes (`set_offset_value_type` in the same file).** For a string
>    container:
>    - Literal base, literal in-range key, and an exactly-1-byte literal value:
>      return the rebuilt literal.
>    - Otherwise: return `non-empty-string`.
>    - Never return `None` for a string member. Unions map per member.
>    - `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs:508-519` then picks up the
>      new type with no change, which fixes the false `identical.alwaysTrue`.
> 3. **Diagnostics (`crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/offset_assignment.rs`).** It
>    already rejects a non-int dimension on a string write. Add:
>    - `$str[] = ...` on a string (fatal Error:
>      `[] operator not supported for strings`).
>    - Writing `''` through a string offset (Error: cannot assign an empty
>      string to a string offset).
>    - Invalid offset types (e.g. a non-numeric string) on string reads, through
>      the existing read-side `offsetAccess` invalid-offset path.
> 4. **Tests.** Cover:
>    - `'abc'[1]` → `'b'`; `'abc'[-1]` → `'c'`; `'abc'[5]` → `''`.
>    - `string $s` → `$s[0]` is `string`, and the `u()` return mismatch is now
>      reported.
>    - The write case: `'abc'` → `'axc'` with no always-true finding.
>    - A non-literal write → `non-empty-string`.
>    - A `string|array<int>` read.

#### K42. Track per-file declaration contributions so unindexing removes only what a file owns

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: codebase-model, incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** When two vendor packages ship the same FQN (a case already seen
  in this codebase, see the index.rs:416-422 comment), editing or deleting one
  file no longer makes the class disappear, or drops the other copy's members,
  until the next full reload. That prevents spurious class.notFound and
  method.notFound results in the LSP. | Fixes data-loss bugs confirmed by probe.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1422`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1479`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1438`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1079`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:919`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:423`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:810`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:800`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:469`
- **Risks:** Merge semantics (overload merge vs replace) must be reproducible
  from the stored sites, which pushes toward the order-independent resolution
  idea. Memory cost of keeping per-site entries is small, since duplicates are
  rare. | Keeping per-origin snapshots costs memory for names declared more than
  once (stub plus polyfill is common in vendor). Store the BuiltDecl only for
  names that actually collide, and a pointer for the rest. The merge path
  (existing.merge) has to become associative and deterministic.
- **Verification:** Mago line numbers are slightly off. The doc comment and
  function for extract_owned_keys are at
  crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1422-1470; the signature is at about line
  1437, and the span-equality filter is at 1439-1467. remove_entries_by_keys
  starts at about 1475.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Replace the name-only removal with "retract and replay". Don't keep per-origin
> snapshots.
>
> 1. Registry::remove_declarations (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:423)
>    becomes retract_names(names). For each affected FQN it drops the entry and
>    its markers (unconditionally_declared_\*, stub_provided_functions,
>    built_in_stub_classes, function_decl_sites, phpstan_class_files).
> 2. It then puts back the stub contribution for that name. Stub data is a
>    static LazyLock cache (registry/stubs.rs:954; generated_stub_classes, used
>    by merge_stub_classes and merge_stubs at index.rs:478/506), so this takes a
>    per-name lookup and no extra memory.
> 3. Project::unindex_file (project.rs:800-822) and update_file
>    (project.rs:~990-1004) then re-run insert_built_decl for that name only,
>    over every other loaded file that still declares it. FileState already
>    keeps each file's AST and its classes/functions lists;
>    project/duplicate_class_sites.rs and duplicate_fn_sites.rs already hold
>    per-path sites and can serve as the name-to-paths index, once extended to
>    cover anonymous and conditional declarations. The replay runs in the batch
>    load order: context files before analyzed files, then path order. The
>    edited file's new declarations go into that same sequence at their own
>    position, not last.
>
> The result is an incremental state equal to a fresh load for any edit order,
> and insert_built_decl's merge logic is reused unchanged. A differential test
> can then assert that update_file/remove_files state equals a fresh Project for
> polyfill, redeclared-builtin and duplicate-vendor-FQN cases.

#### K104. finally entry state includes return/break/continue/throw exits

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Fixes unsound narrowing inside finally. In probe cf/e f2,
  `$h = fopen(...); if ($h === false) { return; }` gives `$h` the type
  `null|resource` in finally, while at runtime finally also sees `false`. The
  same applies to cleanup code that checks handles or locks after an early
  return or continue.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/return.rs:127`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/throw.rs:34`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/break.rs:184`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/try.rs:383`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:294`
- **Risks:** Nested try/finally needs the frames chained so an exit passes
  through each finally. With many exits, the finally entry gets wider, which may
  add a few legitimate diagnostics.
- **Verification:** The phpstan-rs line is wrong.
  `let finally_entry = merge_scopes(&pre_try_locals, locals);` is at
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:301, not 294. Lines 286-300
  are the comment above it. The pre_try snapshot is taken at try_catch.rs:67.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a stack of exit-state frames in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs `check_try`, maintained the
> same way as the existing `try_throw_states`: push a frame only when
> `finally.is_some()`, and record the loop depth at push time. On `return` (in
> stmt.rs `check_stmt_impl`), push `locals.clone()` onto every active finally
> frame of the current function. Returns go through every enclosing finally, and
> recording the pre-inner-finally state in outer frames is a sound
> over-approximation. On `break N` / `continue N`, push onto each frame whose
> recorded loop depth is at least the current loop depth minus N plus 1, so only
> trys that the jump actually leaves. For uncaught throws, reuse the
> `throw_states` popped at try_catch.rs:87: the escaping ones, and all of them
> when there is a finally. Build `finally_entry` as merge(pre_try, completion or
> catch end states, every recorded exit state). When the try body always
> terminates, stop using `locals` as-is (today it is the pre-try state). Keep
> the current rule that only keys the finally body reassigns flow back onto the
> narrower post-try state. Take and restore the new stack at every
> function-boundary site that already does this for `try_throw_states`
> (expr.rs:3791/4023, function_decl.rs:919, oop/property_hooks.rs:230/525,
> calls/closure_context.rs:304). Add fixtures f6/f7/cf-f2/f3 from the probe
> below. The variable in f6 should come out as "might not be defined" rather
> than "undefined".

#### K105. By-reference sites create their target

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Removes 4 false positives on valid code seen in probe cf/j:
  `$r = &$undef;` (undefined variable twice) and `$node = &$cfg['a']['b'];`
  (offsetAccess.notFound twice). The latter is the standard way to build nested
  config and tree structures in PHP. PHP runs it without any notice (verified
  with php -r).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/unary.rs:83`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/variable.rs:185`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/array.rs:187`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:2021`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1656`
- **Risks:** The offset-creation path must not narrow a sealed shape wrongly;
  the created keys should get a `null` value, which the later write-through idea
  can then widen.
- **Verification:** All the Mago citations are correct. unary.rs:83-92 computes
  is_reference/is_variable_reference and sets
  inside_reference/inside_variable_reference before analysing the operand (line
  95).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a helper
> `define_reference_target(&mut self, target: &Expr, locals: &mut Locals) -> Type`
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/assignment.rs (next to bind_assignment_target
> at :293). Call it from: (1) The AssignRef branch of expr.rs:2013, replacing
> `check_expr(rhs)` for every lvalue-shaped right-hand side. Keep the existing
> `Index(base, None)` case, check_nullsafe_byref_target and
> check_property_assign_by_ref. (2) predefine_byref_or_unknown_args in
> checker/calls.rs:68, for by-ref parameters (or unresolved signatures) whose
> argument is an `Index(_, Some(_))` chain rather than a bare Variable. (3) The
> foreach `as &$v` subject, if it is evaluated as a read today. Closure
> `use (&$x)` is already exempt (expr.rs:3580), so leave it alone.
>
> Behaviour of the helper:
>
> - A missing root variable: `locals.declare(name, Type::null(), span)`, with no
>   variable.undefined report. Superglobals and `$this` pass through unchanged.
> - For each missing offset along an Index chain, when the container is a
>   constant shape, general array, null or undefined: create the key without
>   reporting offsetAccess.notFound. Bind it through bind_assignment_target
>   using the existing value for keys that definitely exist, value|null for
>   optional keys, and null for new keys. Consider mixed for created keys until
>   reference write-through or aliasing is modelled, to avoid follow-on
>   stale-shape false positives.
> - Keep every other diagnostic: non-array containers
>   (offsetAccess.nonOffsetAccessible), nullsafe.byRef, property checks, and
>   index expressions, which are still evaluated as reads.
> - Return the slot's type, so `$r` gets null for a fresh slot or the existing
>   value type.
>
> Optional: a help-level, opt-in `variable.referenceUndefined` note for
> `&$undefined`, off by default.
>
> Fixtures: `$r=&$undef; echo $undef;`, `$n=&$cfg['a']['b']` on `[]`, an
> optional key on a sealed shape, a present key keeping its type,
> `preg_match(.., $m['a'])`, and a non-array root still erroring.

#### K272. Count trait accesses to host private members

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Removes a false-positive class common in trait-heavy code, where
  traits call template hooks that the host implements as private.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:130`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:132`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:31`
- **Risks:** Trait `insteadof`/`as` aliasing renames methods, so it must be
  applied to the summary. A trait from vendor code with no AST loaded should
  escape the host.
- **Verification:** Minor line drift only. In Mago,
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs has the property
  name-collision skip at lines 134-141
  (`used_traits.iter().any(|t| codebase.property_exists(t, name))`) and the
  method one at lines 188-194 (`method_exists`).
- **Refined proposal:**

> The false positive is real and I reproduced it. Probe
> <scratchpad>/probes/traitpriv/t.php:
> trait T's run() writes \$this->hostProp and calls \$this->hostHelper(), and
> final class C { use T; private \$hostProp; private function hostHelper() }.
> Running check-project reports
> `private property C::$hostProp is never read, only written` and
> `private method C::hostHelper() is unused`. Both are wrong, because in PHP a
> trait's methods run in the host's scope and can reach the host's private
> members.
>
> Proposed fix:
>
> 1. Add a `TraitMemberUsage { consts, methods, reads, writes, escaped }`
>    summary to the trait's ClassReflection
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs). Fill it at registry-build
>    time by running the existing walkers from
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused/member_usage.rs
>    (walk_stmt_body_for_members at :274, walk_expr_for_members,
>    walk_property_hooks_for_members). Run them over the trait's method bodies,
>    property and const defaults, and hooks, using the same two-pass alias
>    approach as unused.rs:161-172. Those walkers probably need to move to a
>    place the registry can use, such as a shared `member_usage` module. The
>    per-body `aliases` set is not persisted. The walkers resolve
>    `self::`/`static::`, so the trait fqn works as the fqn argument (see
>    class_ref_is_self, member_usage.rs:52).
> 2. In check_unused_private_members
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:138), after the host's own walk,
>    collect every trait the class uses, directly or through other traits, by
>    following ClassReflection.uses with a seen-set. This is the reverse of
>    Registry::classes_using_trait (registry/hierarchy.rs:142). Merge each
>    trait's summary into `usage`. If a trait is missing from the registry or
>    has no body summary (unknown or stub-only), set usage.escaped = true and
>    suppress the check, which is the safe direction.
> 3. `insteadof`/`as` do not need special handling. They rename or hide the
>    trait's own methods, not the names the trait bodies use to call the host.
>    The worst case is that a method excluded by `insteadof` over-counts its
>    references, which can only hide a report, never create a false one.
> 4. Incremental/LSP: make sure a host's diagnostics are recomputed when a used
>    trait's file changes. The flattening in flatten_traits
>    (registry/resolve.rs:107) already makes the host depend on the trait, so
>    this is probably already covered. Confirm it in project.rs.
> 5. Add fixtures:
>    - a trait calling a private host method;
>    - an `abstract private function hook()` in the trait, implemented by the
>      host;
>    - a trait-of-trait chain;
>    - a dynamic access in the trait that suppresses the host check;
>    - a truly unused host private member that is still reported.

#### K98. Share match-arm false narrowing between check_expr and infer_expr

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Removes a class of false positives in which inference and
  checking disagree for the same match expression, and prevents future drift
  between the two walkers.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/match.rs:618`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:3364`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:4546`
- **Risks:** None meaningful. Check whether the remaining_subject_ty bookkeeping
  (3368-3375) should also be shared.
- **Verification:** No material corrections. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/match.rs lines 618-644 negate the arm's clauses
  with negate_or_synthesize (also the original arm clauses), then saturate them
  into running_else_context.clauses. Both inference and checking go through this
  one path.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs, add
> `fn narrow_match_arm_skipped(&self, subject: &Expr, conds: &[Expr],
> accumulated: &mut Locals, match_true: bool)`
> next to narrow_match_arm_conditions (expr.rs:6251). It is the counterpart of
> the existing true-branch helper and handles the false branch. For match(true)
> it calls apply_narrowing(c, accumulated, false) for every cond; otherwise it
> calls apply_equality_narrowing(subject, c, accumulated, false) for every cond.
> Call it from infer_expr's Match arm (expr.rs:4546-4557), replacing the
> `if let [only_cond]` block. In check_expr (expr.rs:3364-3380), call it first,
> then keep a separate loop there for the remaining_subject_ty bookkeeping. That
> bookkeeping only feeds the check-only `match.alwaysTrue` report and has no use
> in infer_expr, so it stays out of the helper. Add fixtures covering both
> multi-condition shapes on the infer path, such as an argument position: (1)
> `strlen(match(true){ is_int($x), is_float($x) => 'a', default => $x })` with
> int|float|string \$x, and (2)
> `strlen(match($y){ 1, 2 => 'a', default => $y })` with 1|2|'s' \$y. Both must
> be clean.

#### K147. try/finally: terminating finally fixes return.missing, and return in finally that swallows exceptions

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-correctness,
  linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Removes a false positive in a check that is on by default. The
  unreachable-code, never-return and variable-merge logic that depend on
  always_terminates become correct for these functions too. | Finds exceptions
  that are silently lost, which is a real runtime bug that PHPStan's rule
  misses. | Fixes a real false positive in core control-flow analysis and
  catches silently lost exceptions.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/safety/no_unsafe_finally.rs:100`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/safety/no_unsafe_finally.rs:112`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:162`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:254`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs:319`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/throws.rs:97`
- **Risks:** Code after a terminating try/finally becomes unreachable, which
  could newly report deadCode.unreachable. That is correct, but check it with a
  corpus diff. | Some code returns in finally on purpose, e.g.
  cleanup-then-return helpers. Gating on throw points in the try body keeps
  noise down. It could start under ext.extras if it turns out noisy. | Changing
  always_terminates affects unreachable-code and definite-assignment results
  downstream. Re-run fixtures. A `throw` inside finally is legitimate (it
  replaces the exception), so exclude it or give it a separate identifier.
- **Verification:** Mago: no_unsafe_finally.rs:100 is the start of `fn check`.
  It does not treat return as overriding the try. The actual loop is at :112
  (`for control_flow in find_control_flows_in_block(&finally.block)`), the
  message is at :121, and the "override control flows from try and catch blocks"
  note is at :13 ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> (1) The core fix. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs, both Try
> arms (always_terminates at ~162 and exits_function_or_loop at ~254) currently
> match `StmtKind::Try { body, catches, .. }`. Change them to destructure
> `finally` and return
> `finally.last().is_some_and(|s| self.always_terminates(s, locals)) ||
> <existing try+catches condition>`,
> with the same change in exits_function_or_loop. Update the comment at lines
> 158-161, which says finally "doesn't need to independently terminate". Add
> fixtures for three cases: the
> `function f(): int { try { echo 1; } finally { return 2; } }` return.missing
> false positive, code after such a try (now deadCode.unreachable), and
> never-return inference. (2) A lost-exception check in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/try_catch.rs, next to the finally.exitPoint
> block (~319). When `try_catch_exit_points.is_empty()` (the case
> finally.exitPoint deliberately skips) and the finally block contains a
> reachable `return` or `exit`, and the try body has throw points (an explicit
> throw, or a call whose throw type is recorded through throws.rs
> record_call_throw_point), report `finally.discardsException` at level 4: "This
> return in finally discards any exception thrown in the try block." Leave
> `throw` in finally out: PHP chains the original exception as getPrevious(),
> which I verified with php -r, so nothing is lost. A catch-all
> `catch (Throwable)` that already terminates also makes the warning moot. (3)
> Drop the proposed break/continue part of the swallow check. PHP rejects
> `break`/`continue` out of a finally at compile time ("jump out of a finally
> block is disallowed", verified with php -r for both). The right fix is a
> separate hard error at level 0, for example `finally.jumpOut`, reported when
> break/continue inside a finally targets a loop outside that finally. No such
> check exists today (a grep for the message or an in-finally flag finds
> nothing).

#### K43. Resolve duplicate declarations by an explicit total priority order

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** The same inputs always produce the same registry, whether loaded
  in batch, re-indexed incrementally, or scanned in a different order (for
  example a new scan path). This removes a class of LSP-only false positives and
  makes the collision policy readable in one function instead of the ~270-line
  branch in insert_built_decl.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1664`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1074`, `crates/codex/src/scanner/mod.rs:191`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:103`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:646`
- **Risks:** Current behaviours relied on by tests (the PHPUnit TestCase guarded
  fallback, the Imagick stub merge, the strtr overload merge) must each map to a
  rank rule. Overload merging for phpstorm-stubs built-ins must stay a merge,
  not a pick.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. should_replace_metadata is at
  crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:1664-1705: user-defined, then patch, then
  external, then built-in, then non-polyfill beats polyfill, then
  `new_span < existing_span`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep the goal, which is that the registry entry for a name depends only on the
> set of sites that currently declare it. Drop the rewrite of the batch
> collision policy into a new DeclRank. The actual bug is in the incremental
> remove/re-add path.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs FileState, keep each file's
>    `built_decls` (for example as `Arc<[BuiltDecl]>`) instead of consuming them
>    in `insert_parsed_file`. Also record global-constant names per file. The
>    `name -> declaring paths` index can come from `duplicate_fn_sites` and
>    `duplicate_class_sites`, which already store a path per site, or from a
>    small new `decl_sites` map.
>
> 2. Replace `Registry::remove_declarations`
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/index.rs:423) with
>    `recompute_names(names)`. For each touched function, class or constant name
>    it should:
>    - clear the slot and its side-set markers (`unconditionally_declared_*`,
>      `stub_provided_functions`, `built_in_stub_classes`,
>      `function_decl_sites`);
>    - re-apply the built-in stub entry for that one name (the per-name part of
>      `merge_stubs`, `merge_stub_classes` and `merge_stub_constants`, looked up
>      from the LazyLock stub tables in registry/stubs.rs);
>    - feed the remaining declaring files' BuiltDecls back through the unchanged
>      `insert_built_decl`, in the same batch order: context files sorted by
>      path, then analysed files.
>
>    This makes an incremental result equal a fresh load by construction. It
>    reuses the existing ~270-line policy that the tests pin (the PHPUnit
>    TestCase guarded fallback, the Imagick merge, the strtr overload merge,
>    `better_conditional_function_declaration`) instead of re-encoding each rule
>    as a rank.
>
> 3. Include global constants. Today `register_global_constant` (index.rs:706)
>    only ever adds entries or poisons them to mixed, and nothing ever removes
>    them.
>
> 4. Add incremental tests in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_updates.rs, each asserting
>    that update_file gives the same result as a fresh load:
>    - edit a `function_exists` polyfill file: the built-in must survive;
>    - edit one of two files that both declare the same class;
>    - change a constant's value, then delete the constant.
>
> Optional later step: pull the policy's decisions into one documented
> `fn collision_outcome(existing_origin, new_origin, conditional, analyzed)` for
> readability. Do this only if it stays behaviour-identical, not as a new total
> order.

#### K116. Named-argument-aware call-argument view for builtin/extension handlers

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis, plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Removes unsound inferences and spurious errors on named-argument
  calls to builtins. These calls are increasingly common in PHP 8 code
  (`json_decode(flags: ...)`, `array_slice(preserve_keys: true)`,
  `htmlspecialchars(double_encode: false)`).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/context.rs:353`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/math/intdiv.rs:72`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/context.rs:408`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/array/array_all.rs:50`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:21`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/misc_rules.rs:93`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:20`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:132`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/misc_rules.rs:98`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1058` (+3 more)
- **Risks:** Mechanical but touches roughly 100 match arms; each arm's arity
  guard has to be translated faithfully. The existing builtin tests catch
  regressions. | About 100 raw-index sites (84 in builtin_calls.rs alone, per
  grep) need mechanical rewriting, and some arms use `args.len()` to pick
  overloads (hrtime, array_filter, parse_url), which has to become a check on
  which parameter is bound. A named argument that doesn't match any parameter
  must still fall back to the stub type. Fixture coverage should add named and
  reordered variants for each migrated arm.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small line
  offsets. In Mago, `InvocationInfo::get_argument` is at
  crates/analyzer/src/plugin/context.rs around lines 352-354. It delegates to a
  free function `get_argument` at about line 406.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two steps, with the soundness fix first.
>
> Step 1 (size S, fixes the unsound and false-positive cases right away). In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:26
> `infer_builtin_call_return_type`, before the `match name`, check whether any
> arg has `name.is_some()` or `spread`. If one does, call
> `resolve_call_args(args, sig.params())`. When the bound slots form a
> contiguous prefix (no gap), rebuild a positional `Vec<&Expr>` and dispatch on
> it. Otherwise return `self.infer_call_return_type(sig, &resolved, locals)`,
> the generic stub-typed path that the polyfill branch at line 36 already uses.
> Apply the same guard to `check_random_int_call` (calls/misc_rules.rs:94,
> called from expr.rs:872), the in_array and array_key_exists narrowing arms
> (narrowing.rs:1058/1078), and `class_argument_return`
> (member_resolution.rs:420). They either map through `resolve_call_args` or
> bail. This removes the wrong `never` and the spurious random_int error, and
> stops array_slice(preserve_keys:) from being typed as a list and
> array_combine(values:, keys:) from being swapped.
>
> Step 2 (size M, gets precision back). Add a `CallArgs<'e>` view in
> checker/calls.rs next to `resolve_call_args` (line 829). It holds the raw
> slice plus the resolved slots, with `arg(i) -> Option<&Expr>`,
> `bound(i) -> bool`, `raw_len()` and `has_spread()`. Migrate the arms of
> `infer_builtin_call_return_type`, then throws/dynamic.rs, the narrowing arms,
> misc_rules/array_ops/format_string, from `args[i]` / `args.len()==K` to
> `call.arg(i)` / `call.bound(K-1)`. Where an arm picks an overload by arity
> (hrtime, array_filter, parse_url), the check becomes whether that parameter is
> bound. For an unbound optional param, arms can use
> `sig.params()[i].default_ty()` (registry/function_sig.rs:115) instead of
> assuming the literal default. Replace the doc comment at
> builtin_calls.rs:20-25, since its premise is false. Add fixtures with a named
> and a reordered variant for each migrated arm.

#### K237. Stale inherited docblock types in LSP; own vs inherited provenance

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a real incorrect-result bug in the LSP, the main
  interactive UX: editing a base class or interface docblock currently leaves
  every implementor's inherited types wrong until restart. A targeted re-flatten
  is also cheaper than today's whole-registry fixed-point pass on every
  keystroke-debounced update.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:46`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:202`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:529`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:1169`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1001`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:928`
- **Risks:** Resetting must also undo anything computed from inherited types
  (explicit_mixed_hint, reconcile_with_native results). The descendant set must
  include trait users and interface implementors. Needs an LSP-level regression
  test (edit parent, assert child).
- **Verification:** None of the citations are wrong. Mago:
  crates/codex/src/populator/docblock.rs:46-50 (the gate returns false only when
  `!m.inferred`), :202-225 (inherit_method_docblocks takes dirty_classes and
  adds all_class_like_descendants), :518 and :536 (TypeMetadata written with
  `inferred: true`).
- **Refined proposal:**

> This is a real LSP bug, but the reset-to-native part of the proposal is the
> fragile half. The fix I'd recommend reuses the re-indexing code phpstan-rs
> already has.
>
> **How the bug happens**
>
> - `Registry::flatten_phpdoc_inheritance_one_pass`
>   (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:964) sets `p.has_own_doc = true`
>   at :1169 and `sig.return_has_own_doc = true` at :1176 when it backfills a
>   slot. It also overwrites `ty`/`return_type` with the ancestor's type after
>   `reconcile_with_native`, and copies `explicit_mixed_hint`.
> - `Project::update_file_cancellable` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1001)
>   calls `self.registry.index(&ast, …)` only for the edited file, then reruns
>   `flatten_phpdoc_inheritance` (:1031).
> - A child class in another, unchanged file therefore keeps its stale
>   backfilled type. Its slot also looks "documented", so the flatten never
>   visits it again.
> - The same staleness happens when a parent removes its doc (the child keeps a
>   phantom type) and for grandchildren.
>
> **Recommended fix: two steps**
>
> (1) Correctness fix, reusing existing code.
>
> - In `update_file_cancellable`, before the flatten pipeline, gather every
>   class that transitively extends, implements or uses a class declared in the
>   edited file. The precomputed ancestor-name data
>   (`precompute_ancestor_names`) can supply this; include trait users and
>   interface implementors.
> - Re-run `self.registry.index(&file_state.ast, &origin, analyzed)` on those
>   classes' files, whose ASTs are already kept in `FileState`.
> - This restores each child's pristine own/native signature. The later passes
>   (`flatten_traits`, `resolve_method_tags`, `resolve_deferred_*`,
>   `flatten_phpdoc_inheritance`, `apply_assertion_table`, mixins, purity) then
>   rebuild everything derived from the inherited types in the usual way. That
>   covers `explicit_mixed_hint`, the `reconcile_with_native` results, and
>   assertion/throws/property inheritance, with no reset code to write.
> - Check that `record_phpstan_class_file`, `duplicate_fn_sites.index` and
>   `duplicate_class_sites.index` are keyed by path and idempotent when re-run.
>
> (2) Optional cleanup.
>
> - Add `doc_inherited: bool` (or `DocProvenance::{Own, Inherited}`) next to
>   `has_own_doc` in `ParameterReflection` and next to `return_has_own_doc` in
>   `FunctionReflection` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:58 and
>   :161).
> - The flatten would set `Inherited` instead of faking `has_own_doc`. The
>   ancestor gate at resolve.rs:1051/:1083/:1122 becomes
>   `has_own_doc || doc_inherited`.
> - The merge at function_sig.rs:832/:867 must combine the new flag too.
> - Payoff: hover can say "inherited from X", and rules can tell a real docblock
>   from an inherited one.
> - `has_own_doc()` / `return_has_own_doc()` have no callers outside
>   `registry/`, so the change stays local.
>
> Keep the whole-registry fixed-point flatten. A targeted flatten over dirty
> classes plus descendants is only an optimisation; do it later if profiling
> shows it matters, because already-filled slots are skipped cheaply.
>
> **Test:** add an LSP/`Project` regression test.
>
> 1. Parent P declares `@return list<int>`; child C in another file has no
>    docblock.
> 2. Call `update_file` on P changing it to `list<string>`, then assert C's
>    return type.
> 3. Also cover a grandchild through an interface, a trait user, and removing
>    the parent's doc.

#### K239. One docblock pre-processor and tag-selection path

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Fixes the confirmed statement-@var bug and removes a second
  precedence implementation that can silently drift from the first. It also
  lowers parse work (see the parse-once idea).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/mod.rs:44`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/docblock.rs:69`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:22`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:307`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_unresolvable.rs:67`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_unresolvable.rs:27`
- **Risks:** The two paths currently differ on invalid-tag handling
  (scratch-merge vs `tag.errors.is_empty()` skip). The fixture suite must pin
  varTag.\* and phpDoc.parseError output before merging.
- **Verification:** Every cited path and line checks out. Mago:
  crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/mod.rs:44 parse_with_span;
  crates/codex/src/scanner/docblock.rs:69 find_most_trusted_tag and :104
  for_each_tag_by_ascending_trust (the scanner's parse_docblock wrapper sits
  just above, around :59-66).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in three steps. Each step can be committed on its own.
>
> (1) Small, and it fixes the bug by itself. Pull the line pre-processor into
> one `pub(crate) fn tag_lines(raw) -> Vec<String>` in crates/phpdoc. It should
> use docblock.rs's rule: join continuation lines with '\n' and do not strip
> '//'. Use it in both crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:15-30 and
> crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:296-316. The grammar lexer already skips a '//'
> comment only where whitespace is allowed (grammar/lexer.rs:102-106), so quoted
> keys stay intact. The newline join also keeps a wrapped field's `// note` from
> swallowing the rest of the shape. The doc comment at parser.rs:9-14 already
> says the two paths match, but they don't. This fixes statement-level @var:
> `stmt.rs:155/371`, `var_tag_types.rs:286` and `phpdoc_type_compat.rs:597` all
> go through var_tag_nodes. It also fixes grammar::parse's other users:
> `generics/ancestors.rs:402` and `docblock::unknown_phpstan_tags` at
> docblock.rs:1228.
>
> (2) Move tag selection into the phpdoc crate. DocBlock already stores
> `params`, `param_out`, `return_type` and `var_type` as grammar `TypeNode`s.
> Add a `var_tags: Vec<(Option<String>, TypeNode)>` using var_tag_nodes' rule
> where unnamed tags win over named ones. Then delete
> `phpdoc_unresolvable::tag_type_nodes` and `var_tag_nodes`, and switch their
> callers (missing_typehint.rs:436, function_decl.rs:444,
> phpdoc_type_compat.rs:34/352/362/370/597, stmt.rs, var_tag_types.rs) to the
> DocBlock fields. One point needs a decision first. tag_type_nodes skips any
> tag with `!tag.errors.is_empty()`, while docblock's apply_tag_recording_errors
> keeps a lenient value. The unresolvable and compat rules need the strict view,
> so either keep a flag for each tag or store both the strict and lenient node.
>
> (3) Optional parse-once. Build docblock::parse from grammar::parse's PhpDocTag
> list instead of calling split_tag + parse_tag_rest again for each tag.
>
> Before step 1, pin the varTag.\*, phpDoc.parseError and phpDoc.phpstanTag
> fixture output. Keep it separate from this work, but also fix a bug the probe
> found. The @param path mis-parses a quoted shape key that contains ':'
> (`@param array{'a:b': int} $p` gives `array{0: 'a:b': int}` plus a bogus
> class.notFound). This looks like the string round-trip through
> crates/types/src/parse.rs:413 (split_once(':')). That points to a third
> type-text path, which this proposal does not unify.

#### K277. Bundle per-function-like checker state into one BodyContext swapped as a unit, so return points from contextual closures stop leaking into the enclosing function

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: hir-lowering-ir)
- **Benefit:** Removes a class of state-leak bugs, one of them confirmed: the
  missing return.unusedType. It also removes about 120 lines of mechanical
  save/restore, and makes any new per-body field automatically scoped correctly
  for all four closure-like entry paths.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/hir/src/lower/mod.rs:40`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/mod.rs:104`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/item/expression/closure.rs:47`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/item/member/method.rs:35`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:364`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:900`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs:289`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:529`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/return_type_too_wide.rs:78`
- **Risks:** Some fields are intentionally not reset for closures, e.g.
  current_method_attrs (checker.rs:325-332 documents that). The struct has to
  separate truly per-body fields from lexically inherited ones. Probably easiest
  as two structs: BodyContext, and a LexicalContext that is inherited.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/hir/src/lower/mod.rs:41-50 defines BodyEffects,
  and :104-110 has enter_function_like_body/leave_function_like_body using
  mem::replace. Both are confirmed. BodyEffects is small, though.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Step 1 is the bug fix. It is small and should land first as its own commit. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs, around lines 289-307,
> the contextual-closure entry must also take and restore these fields, exactly
> as the ExprKind::Closure arm in expr.rs:3801-3844 does:
> current_function_return_points, current_function_saw_explicit_return,
> current_function_by_ref_params, by_ref_exit_snapshots, by_ref_params_with_tag,
> byref_snapshot_names and current_declared_throws_type. Add a fixture with f1
> (array_map(function(int \$x){ return (string)\$x; }, [1]) inside
> `function f1(): int|string`) that expects return.unusedType. Also add a
> fixture for a by-ref param in the outer function combined with an inner
> contextual closure that returns.
>
> Step 2 is the structural change. Move the fields documented in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:355-510 into a
> `pub(crate) struct BodyContext` held as `Checker.body`. That covers
> current_function_is_generator, current_declared_return_type/throws, the
> throw_points, has_unannotated_call, explicit_throw_points, return_points,
> saw_explicit_return, the four by-ref collections, goto_targets,
> assigned_variables, saw_dynamic_var_construct and try_throw_states. Keep
> current_method_templates, current_method_attrs and current_class in a separate
> lexically inherited struct, or leave them as plain fields; checker.rs:325-332
> documents that they are deliberately not reset. Add
> `BodyContext::for_function`, `::for_closure(body, declared_return, class)` and
> `::for_arrow_fn`. Add
> `fn enter_body(&mut self, b: BodyContext) -> BodyContext` using mem::replace,
> plus `leave_body(prev) -> BodyContext`, which returns the finished body so
> callers can read return_points and throw_points afterwards. Then replace the
> hand-written save/restore blocks in function_decl.rs (~900 and 1199-1214),
> expr.rs (the Closure and ArrowFn arms), calls/closure_context.rs and
> oop/property_hooks.rs. The PassMark rewind in checker.rs:~1140-1160 then
> indexes `self.body.*` lengths. Build BodyContext with an exhaustive struct
> literal and no `..Default::default()`, so every new per-body field forces each
> constructor to decide.

#### K301. Static musl and old-glibc Linux release targets

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** The binaries run on the distros most PHP CI and production images
  use: Debian 11/12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 8/9 and Alpine. Today they fail there
  with a dynamic-loader error before analysis starts. Any Composer launcher or
  container image depends on this.
- **Mago evidence:** `.github/workflows/cd.yml:173`,
  `.github/workflows/cd.yml:270`, `.github/workflows/cd.yml:346`
- **phpstan-rs:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:33`, `README.md:29`
- **Risks:** musl's default allocator is slow for a multi-threaded
  allocator-heavy workload. The musl builds need mimalloc or jemalloc to avoid a
  large slowdown, which ties into the mimalloc idea. Any other C dependency has
  to cross-compile cleanly.
- **Verification:** Mago: the musl legs are at .github/workflows/cd.yml:175
  (aarch64-unknown-linux-musl) and :186 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl). The
  arm/armv7 musl variants are at :201-204, and musl-tools is installed at :228.
  The manylinux2014 (glibc 2.17) image selection is at :270-284.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Two parts in .github/workflows/release.yml, in order of payoff. (1) Lower the
> gnu glibc floor. Keep the x86_64 and aarch64 `-unknown-linux-gnu` legs, but
> build them with cargo-zigbuild (`--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.17` /
> `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.17`) or inside a manylinux2014 container. Add a
> step that runs `objdump -T` on the binary and fails if any `GLIBC_` version is
> above the chosen floor. Check that the mold setup in .cargo/config.toml
> doesn't conflict with zig's linker; the zigbuild legs may need mold turned
> off. (2) Add `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` legs
> so the binary also runs on Alpine and other php:\*-alpine images. On musl
> only, set `#[global_allocator]` to mimalloc behind a cfg or feature in
> crates/phpstan-rs. Without that, musl's malloc makes a multi-threaded,
> allocation-heavy analyzer much slower. Share this with any separate mimalloc
> idea rather than duplicating it. Then rewrite README.md:32-41 ("Linux glibc
> compatibility") to state the new floor and the musl option. Make
> editors/vscode/src/serverDownload.ts pick the musl asset on musl hosts or when
> glibc detection fails. Before any of this, do the first `workflow_dispatch`
> dry run the release.yml header comment asks for, because no leg has been run
> in CI yet.

#### K1. Error-recovering parser: statement/block-level recovery returning a partial AST plus an error list

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: lexer-parser, robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** A single syntax error, or unsupported syntax in one vendor file,
  no longer deletes that file's declarations. Today that causes cascading
  class.notFound or undefined-function noise in files that depend on it, and
  silently removes the file from analysis. The LSP gets current diagnostics for
  the rest of the edited file while it is mid-edit.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/mod.rs:86`,
  `crates/syntax/src/cst/mod.rs:27`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/internal/block.rs:12`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/internal/terminator.rs:48`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/internal/class_like/member.rs:87`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/internal/expression.rs:309` (+5 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:38`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:298`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:569`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/completion.rs:1`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:729`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2020` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Recovered trees can produce false positives. A Mago probe showed
  this: `$x = $this->` followed by `}` produced a spurious
  `impossible-assignment: right-hand side has type never` (probe under
  scratchpad/probes/lexer-parser/a). Error nodes must be `mixed`/neutral, and
  flow-sensitive rules must be gated in affected function bodies. Every consumer
  of `Result<.., ParseError>` has to change: project.rs, session.rs, stubs.rs,
  ignore_comments.rs and main/check.rs. Parse-time validation that is currently
  fatal (`pattern_only`, parser.rs:61-67) must turn into recorded errors.
- **Verification:** Minor line drift only. phpstan-rs
  crates/syntax/src/parse.rs: `parse` is at line 37 (not 38); the early
  lexer-error return is at line 70 (not 64); `parse_program()?` is at line 77
  (not 70). Mago's top-level loop starts around mod.rs:89, and the progress
  guard is at lines 111-119.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two stages, and ship the cheap, high-value stage on its own.
>
> Stage 1 (L): recover at the statement and member level only, with no
> placeholder expressions.
>
> - Change `syntax::parse` (crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:36) to return
>   `ParsedFile` with a new `errors: Vec<ParseError>` field.
> - A lexer error (currently an early return at parse.rs:68-73) is recorded
>   instead of aborting.
> - In `Parser::parse_program` (crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:298), the stmt-list
>   block loop in parser/stmt.rs and the class-body member loop in
>   parser/classes.rs: on Err, record it, restore the position, then skip tokens
>   until one of these, tracking brace depth:
>   - a `;` at depth 0;
>   - the matching `}` at the current depth;
>   - a statement or member start keyword
>     (function/class/interface/trait/enum/abstract/final/readonly/public/protected/private/static/const/use/namespace).
> - Always consume at least one token (a forward-progress guard like Mago's
>   parser/mod.rs:110-119).
> - The broken statement is dropped rather than represented by an Error node.
>   That keeps every downstream consumer unchanged: visit.rs, the printer and
>   the checker never see a new variant.
> - Wiring:
>   - `parse_file` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2019) always yields a
>     ParsedFile.
>   - `read_and_parse_file` (project/session.rs:569) stops returning None on a
>     syntax error.
>   - Context files (session.rs:655, `skipped_context`) keep their declarations.
>   - registry/stubs.rs keeps the parsable members of a stub instead of
>     `continue`.
>   - Each recorded error becomes a `parse.error`-style diagnostic on analysed
>     files.
>   - The checker suppresses flow-sensitive rules (unreachable, missing return,
>     always-true/false, undefined-variable) inside any function body whose span
>     contains a recorded error.
> - A fuzz invariant in fuzz/ checks that recovery terminates and that no error
>   is silently dropped.
>
> Stage 2 (L, done later and driven by the LSP): add `ExprKind::Error` and a
> missing-member-name form in PropertyAccess/MethodCall, so that `$x->|` parses.
> Only then retire `parse_standalone_expr`, `find_enclosing_names` and
> `truncate_before` in lsp/completion.rs (lines 172, 236, 690-691). Error exprs
> type as `mixed` and emit nothing.
>
> Do not do the "keep last-good AST only for span-stable LSP features" dual
> bookkeeping unless Stage 2 shows it is needed.

#### K3. Lexer halt mode for \_\_halt_compiler(); so trailing data is never tokenized

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Correctness on valid PHP. A probe file
  (`function f(): int { return "s"; } __halt_compiler(); 08 1e 0x /* \x01 "abc`)
  passes `php -l` and runs, but phpstan-rs skipped it
  (`1 file(s) skipped: parse error`), losing the real return.type error.
  Self-extracting installers, PHAR stubs and code generators in vendor trees
  (for example laravel/src/Illuminate/Console/GeneratorCommand.php mentions it)
  are affected.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:380`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:1039`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:391`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:64`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:239`
- **Risks:** The halt-stage tokens need care with whitespace and comments
  between `(`/`)`/`;` (PHP allows them). `__halt_compiler` inside a namespace or
  function is a PHP compile error, which the parser should still report.
- **Verification:** All citations check out, with small line offsets. In Mago's
  crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs, lines 378-380 set
  LexerMode::Halt(HaltStage::LookingForLeftParenthesis) when token_kind ==
  TokenKind::HaltCompiler. The `LexerMode::Halt(stage)` arm starts at line 1039.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a halt stage to the lexer in crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs. In the identifier
> branch of next_token (around lines 374-393), when the identifier matches
> `__halt_compiler` (case-insensitive) and the previous significant token is not
> `->`, `?->`, `::`, `function` or `const` (it is a semi-reserved name that is
> allowed as a member name), set `halt = HaltStage::LParen`. For the next
> significant tokens, skipping whitespace and comments as usual, require `(`,
> then `)`, then `;` or `?>`. After those, make run() (line 239) stop: move
> self.pos to src.len() and emit Eof, with no token for the trailing bytes. The
> parser only needs the statement to end, and dropping the data keeps it out of
> the doc-comment and code_line_starts collection in parse.rs:50-67. If the
> sequence does not match, clear the halt state and continue normally, so the
> parser reports the error. Update the arm at
> crates/syntax/src/parser/stmt.rs:391: it now consumes `__halt_compiler ( ) ;`
> properly instead of setting `self.pos` to the token count, and optionally
> reports a halt inside a function, class or braced namespace. Add parse.rs
> tests for trailing `08`, an unterminated `/*`, an unterminated `"`, non-UTF-8
> bytes, `__halt_compiler ( /*c*/ ) ?>`, and `$o->__halt_compiler()` (which must
> not trigger halt mode).

#### K198. One canonical project-relative file identity for output, baseline and ignore_errors

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** The same baseline and ignore_errors config work whether

  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:397`,

  handles. Paths outside the root need a fallback, such as keeping them
  absolute. | This changes the output path spelling people see and may grep for.
  Existing baselines keyed with './' prefixes need tolerant matching during a
  transition, so lexically normalize both sides.
- **Verification:** All citations check out, give or take a line or two. Mago:
  reporting/src/baseline.rs:157 is normalize_path, which replaces '\\' with '/'.
  baseline.rs:185 uses normalize_path(&file.name), the database's logical name.

> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs next to `absolute_path` (around line 588). It
> builds on `absolute_path`: strip `absolute_root` (the config dir, or cwd when
> there is no config), fall back to the absolute path when the file is outside
> the root, use '/' separators, and drop the leading "./". In
> `AnalysisResult::finalize` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:201-204),
> re-key `results` through this helper before `ignore_errors::filter` and
> `baseline::filter`, then map the keys back, as the LSP already does in
> lsp.rs:393-417. Then replace the LSP's own `to_relative`/`root.join` closure

#### K214. Symlink-loop-safe, deterministic (parallel) file discovery

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Probe: a single file with a `src/a/up -> ..` symlink was checked
  41 times ("41 file(s) checked") until the kernel returned ELOOP. Two sibling
  loops multiply the count exponentially, and duplicated declarations corrupt
  registry collisions. Parallel walking also speeds up discovery on large vendor
  trees. | Probe: a single `src/up -> ..` symlink made 1 file show up as 41
  checked files, each re-declaring the same class.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/database/src/loader.rs:446`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:516`, `crates/database/src/loader.rs:448`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:518`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2111`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:596`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2124`
- **Risks:** Whether to follow symlinks at all, which composer path repositories
  rely on, must stay the same; only loops are cut. | Following links outside the
  workspace can pull in unexpected trees. Combine this with the exclude matcher
  and report which symlinks were followed at debug verbosity.
- **Verification:** The cited Mago lines are about right. In mago
  crates/database/src/loader.rs, `rayon::join` is at about line 441. It splits
  into direct-path files and `directory_roots.into_par_iter()` at 444-446.
  `WalkDir::new(&root).follow_links(true)` with the `filter_entry` prune is at
  447-456.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep this small, and fix only the loop bug. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs, collect_php_files_excluding (line 2111)
> should get a private recursive helper that carries a HashSet of visited
> directory identities. Use (dev, ino) from std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt on
> unix, and fall back to fs::canonicalize elsewhere. A directory already in the
> set is skipped. Classify each child with entry.file_type() and only stat it
> when it is a symlink, so the extra per-entry is_dir stat goes away. Symlinks
> are still followed as they are today, so composer path repositories keep
> working.
>
> A skipped cycle should be reported: return it, or push it to a warnings vec,
> so Session can add a line to Session.warnings. The silent
> `let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(path) else { return; }` at lines 2124-2126
> should add a warning too, but only when the directory is a root the user
> named, so noise in vendor stays quiet.
>
> After this, the sort plus dedup in Session::load
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs lines 596-605) is enough, because a
> file reached through two different non-looping symlinks is rare. Canonical
> dedup there is optional.
>
> Do not add walkdir or ignore, and do not parallelize the walk. The output is
> already sorted at session.rs lines 599 and 604, so it is deterministic.
> Directory walking is negligible next to parsing and checking, so the parallel
> part of the proposal adds complexity for no measurable gain. Add one unix-only
> test: a tempdir holding a.php and an up -> .. symlink should collect exactly
> one file.

#### K221. Classify runtime-created files with loader rules

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** With `paths = ["src"]`, a newly created tests/Foo.php is
  currently analyzed and published. A new file under a scan_paths directory
  becomes analyzed and therefore overwrites same-name declarations instead of
  merging (insert_built_decl), so the incremental state diverges from what a
  restart would produce.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/database/src/watcher.rs:547`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:998`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:480`
- **Risks:** An explicitly opened file outside the analyzed paths may still
  deserve diagnostics (the user is looking at it). Keep the current behavior for
  didOpen of such files, but mark them analyzed only while open.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate. In Mago, `classify_added_file`
  starts at crates/database/src/watcher.rs:547, with its doc comment at 539-546.
  It takes the max specificity over the host, patch and include bases and hands
  it to `resolve_file_type`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `classify(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<FileRole>` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/workspace_config.rs on WorkspaceContextPaths, with
> `FileRole { Analyzed, Context }`. Use the same precedence load_workspace_files
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:480-530) already applies. A path under
> vendor.files, vendor.dirs or extra_dirs is Context, since context wins as it
> does in the load order. Otherwise, a non-empty analyze_paths is an allowlist:
> a path inside it is Analyzed and anything else is None. With an empty
> analyze_paths, a path under the workspace root is Analyzed unless it sits
> under a DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES directory, which makes it Context.
> Refactor load_workspace_files to use this one predicate so the two cannot
> drift apart. Then add a
> `Project::update_file_with_role(path, text, analyzed: Option<bool>)`, or pass
> the flag into the existing `update_file`/`update_file_cancellable`, used only
> when the path is not yet in `self.files` (project.rs:998). In
> handle_watched_files_changed (lsp.rs:792), a None role means skip the Created
> event: the file is not loaded, gets no diagnostics, and is not added to
> open_uris. In handle_open_or_change and handle_debounced_change, a file the
> user opened that classifies as None stays analyzed, which is the current
> behavior. A Context-classified file stays context. The Project fallback at
> project.rs:998 remains for non-LSP callers. Add LSP tests under the existing
> lsp test module for three cases: a watcher-created tests/Foo.php with
> paths=[src] is not published; a watcher-created file under a scanDirectories
> directory not named vendor is indexed with analyzed=false and merges instead
> of overwriting; a didOpen of an out-of-paths file still gets diagnostics.

#### K223. Restore default SIGPIPE

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Stops the panic backtrace and exit 101 when output is piped to

  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:59`

  other crates). Skipping it for lsp avoids silently dying if the editor closes
  stdout.
- **Verification:** mago/src/main.rs:101 is the definition of reset_sigpipe(),
  which calls libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL) at lines 102-105. It is called at
  mago/src/main.rs:133. A no-op version for non-unix is at line 110.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a small `reset_sigpipe()` helper to crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs,
> modelled on Mago's src/main.rs:95-110. Call it in the `Check`, `CheckProject`,
> `Demo`, `ConvertBaseline` and `IncrementalBench` match arms. Leave it out of
> the `Lsp` arm and do not call it at the top of main(). The LSP server talks

> BrokenPipe as exit 0. That covers more code: the println! calls at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:271-280, the `print!` of
> render_friendly just above them, and the other subcommands. It gains nothing,
> because on a broken pipe the right action is to stop quietly anyway. No new

#### K248. Ignore tags in fenced code blocks

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Documentation examples no longer silently change a function's
  parameter or return types, which is especially relevant for framework code
  that documents annotation usage inline.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/code.rs:20`,
  `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/element.rs:21`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:304`
- **Risks:** A malformed, never-closed fence would swallow the rest of the
  docblock. Close fences at end of comment and consider reporting the unclosed
  fence (Mago reports UnclosedCodeBlock).
- **Verification:** The citations check out. Mago:
  crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/code.rs:20-24 is at_code_block. It
  fires on a Backtick token at the start of a line whose run is at least
  FENCE_MINIMUM = 3. parse_code_span at :26 and later treats a block fence as
  opaque Code.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one shared helper in crates/phpdoc (e.g.
> `fn split_tag_lines(inner: &str) -> Vec<String>`) and use it for both of the
> tag-line loops that exist today. They are duplicates:
> crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:302-318 inside `parse`, and
> crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:19-25. The helper strips the `*` prefix
> exactly as both loops do now. It also tracks a fence state: a line whose
> trimmed text starts with ``` or ~~~ opens a fence, and the matching marker
> closes it. The fence line and every line inside it are dropped. They do not
> start a tag and do not join onto the previous tag's continuation. That second
> part matters as much as the first, because otherwise a fenced `@param` line
> would get glued onto the real tag's text as a continuation line.
>
> Unclosed fences: before treating a line as an opener, check that a matching
> closing fence appears later in the same comment. If there is none, treat the
> line as ordinary text, which is what happens today. That way a stray ``` can
> never swallow the real tags after it. Reporting an unclosed fence is optional
> and low value.
>
> Handle `<code>...</code>` (and `<pre>`) the same way, and only when the
> closing tag exists. This is the PHP-manual and Doctrine style of embedding
> examples, and it produces the same bug.
>
> Add unit tests in crates/phpdoc/src/tests.rs or docblock/tests: (a) a fenced
> `@param int $s` does not override a real `@param string $s`; (b) a `@return`
> placed after a closed fence is still read; (c) with an unclosed fence, the
> tags after it are still read; (d) an array-shape continuation line that
> contains a backtick-free string keeps working.

  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:1342`,
