- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:602`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/array_ops.rs:509`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:213`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:153`
- **Risks:** Scope strings are also read by check_variance and
  substitute_class_scoped_ancestor_templates (registry/generics.rs:171-182), so
  every producer and consumer must migrate together. Stubs in stubs.rs:432-549
  hard-code scopes.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out. One clarification:
  build_template_params itself is defined at
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig/generics.rs:146 and sets
  `scope: Some(scope.to_string())` (around line 196).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this in two steps, and commit each one on its own.
>
> Step A (cost S, most of the value): add `own_templates: Vec<TemplateParam>` to
> `FunctionReflection` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/function_sig.rs:153).
> Fill it in `from_decl` (function_sig.rs:600-603) from the
> `build_template_params` map before class templates are merged in. Then: (1) In
> checker/expr/array_ops.rs:505-509, replace the closure
> `!self.registry.classes.contains_key(scope)` with "tp.name is in
> sig.own_templates and tp.scope equals that entry's scope". (2) Make
> `Checker::current_function_template_params` (checker/resolve.rs:173-200) read
> `sig.own_templates` instead of re-deriving templates from the params and
> return type through `collect_scoped_template_params`. This also closes the
> documented gap where a template is used only in a body `@var`. (3) Extend
> `check_template_type_not_in_parameter` (checker/resolve.rs:219) with a second
> message for a declared template that nothing in the signature references. Skip
> names that start with `_`, as Mago does. (4) Optionally add a class-level
> check for a declared template that no member signature uses, modelled on mago
> crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/mod.rs:330. Ship it opt-in.
>
> Step B (cost M): make scopes unambiguous. Give a function template its FQN
> (use `ctx.declared_name(&f.name)` instead of the bare `f.name` at
> function_sig.rs:602). Give a method template a distinct form: either an enum
> in types/src/lib.rs:633 like Mago's GenericParent
> (analyzer/src/invocation/resolver.rs:50), or a `Class::method` string. Several
> consumers compare the bare method name and need to migrate:
>
> - checker/resolve.rs:674 and resolve.rs:168 (current_method)
> - registry/resolve.rs:887 (`template_param_scopes_all_safe_to_backfill`). This
>   one depends on an inherited method's templates matching by bare name across
>   the class hierarchy, so it needs a "method part matches" comparison, not
>   string equality.
> - registry/generics.rs:176 and checker/generics/ancestors.rs:336, which look
>   scopes up in class-keyed maps and so can currently collide with a method or
>   function of the same name.
> - the stubs that hard-code scopes (registry/stubs.rs). The types crate's
>   CALLABLE_TEMPLATE_SCOPE and OPEN sentinels stay as they are.

#### K109. Sound static/global variable typing

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Removes an unsound type on a real pattern (a memoising static
  reset to another type) and adds the enforcement Mago has for typed caches and
  globals (probe cf/g: Mago reports t.php:11 and :16, phpstan-rs reports
  nothing). It also fixes the stale local after a late `global`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/static.rs:77`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/global.rs:69`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:59`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:845`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:694`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:817`
- **Risks:** Some assigned types may themselves depend on the static (for
  example `$n = $n + 1`); a single pre-pass with the declared or initializer
  type, plus generalize, bounds this. The @var constraint could surface in
  legacy code, so it may be level-gated.
- **Verification:** Mago: the assignment-side check is in
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/assignment/mod.rs:563-599
  (ReferenceConstraintSource::Static/Global arms, reported as
  IssueCode::ReferenceConstraintViolation at :599), not
  statement/assignment/mod.rs, which does not exist.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Three separable pieces, ordered by value per cost.
>
> (A) The late `global $x` fix. Cost S, do it first. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:819-828, drop the
> `if !locals.contains_key(name)` guard. `global $x` should always rebind: call
> purge_stale_narrowing_for (checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:276), then declare
> the registry.global_variables type, or mixed when there is none. This matches
> runtime semantics, since the local slot is replaced by a reference to the
> global. Mago does the same at crates/analyzer/src/statement/global.rs:69-75,
> where it inserts into locals unconditionally. The probe confirms the bug:
> `$x = 1; global $x;` gives assertType actual "1".
>
> (B) Sound cross-call static typing. Cost M. Don't try to pre-type RHS
> expressions before the walk. PHP evaluates them in body order, and a pre-pass
> would have to use entry-scope types, so it would be imprecise or wrong for
> `$n = $n + 1` and for RHS values built from locals. The better model: the
> static's value on entry to a later call is whatever it held when an earlier
> call exited.
>
> - Treat the function entry as a loop head for statics only. After the first
>   walk of the body, join each static's type over every exit scope (returns
>   plus the fall-through end).
> - If that join is not a subtype of the declared entry type
>   (static_variable_type(init), stmt.rs:1391), re-walk once with the entry type
>   set to generalize(entry ∪ exit-join), with diagnostics suppressed on the
>   first pass, like the existing loop fixpoint does. Otherwise keep the single
>   pass.
> - Functions with no statics, or whose statics never widen, pay nothing extra.
> - Keep the null→mixed sentinel and the array→array\<mixed> rule.
> - Replace Checker::static_var_names (checker.rs:694) with a per-function-body
>   map, saved and restored in the same place loop_depth is. It only suppresses
>   checks today, and being file-wide is a latent leak across functions.
>
> (C) @var on static/global as an enforced declared type. Cost S-M.
> var_tag_types.rs:460-481 already makes the tag the static's type (probe:
> `/** @var list<int> */ static $c = []` gives `list<int>`), but a later
> `$c = 'x'` goes unreported.
>
> - Record the tag type in a Locals side map keyed by name: {name → (declared
>   Type, source Static|Global)}.
> - On a plain assignment to that name, check the RHS the way
>   by_ref_params.rs:62 check_param_out_assignment does, with new identifiers
>   staticVar.type and globalVar.type.
> - Clear the entry on unset or on a re-`global`.
> - Mago equivalent: crates/analyzer/src/statement/static.rs:74-83 and
>   global.rs:77-89, checked at
>   crates/analyzer/src/statement/assignment/mod.rs:529-599.
> - Ship it on by default. It fires only when the author wrote an explicit type
>   contract, so it has almost no noise source.
>
> Where phpstan-rs is already ahead: global types are inferred from the whole
> program (registry/global_vars.rs), not just mixed or superglobals, and @var on
> statics already shapes the type and is validated for name mismatch
> (stmt.rs:275-320).

#### K185. Case-insensitive extension dispatch

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Correctness for legal PHP, including legacy code bases that use
  odd casing. It also removes the inconsistency where some checks fire and
  others don't for the same call.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:1200`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/provider/method.rs:51`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/provider/function.rs:46`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:42`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1057`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:609`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:795`
- **Risks:** Very low, since only the dispatch key changes. It needs one fixture
  per dispatch site with a mixed-case call so the fix doesn't regress.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are accurate. registry.rs:1200-1201
  lowercases with ascii_lowercase_word before the function_exact lookup.
  method.rs:43-55 matches_class and matches_method use eq_ignore_ascii_case, or
  starts_with_ignore_case for a prefix.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Canonicalize the name once, at the call-resolution boundary, and don't patch
> each match separately. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs, at the two
> call sites of infer_builtin_call_return_type (around lines 1114 and 4721) and
> at the function-call check chain (around line 795), compute a lowercased bare
> name (trim the leading backslash, then to_ascii_lowercase; a small Cow or an
> interned lowercase name avoids allocating when the name is already lowercase)
> and pass it into infer_builtin_call_return_type in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, type_check_call_outcome,
> and the `match *name { "array_filter" ... }` chain. Keep the original spelling
> only for diagnostics text. Do the same in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs: bind one lowercased bare callee
> name at the top of the call-condition arm and use it for in_array,
> array_key_exists, is_\* and the other predicate arms. This matches the
> eq_ignore_ascii_case style already used at narrowing.rs:668/706/731. For
> methods, lowercase `method` once in
> member_resolution.rs::object_method_call_return_type (the `method == "format"`
> arm at line 609 and the Doctrine getResult family), then write its match arms
> in lowercase. Grep all `method == "` and `trim_start_matches('\\') == "`
> comparisons under src/checker/: there are about 17 method comparisons and 7
> function comparisons, plus the throws/dynamic dispatch. Registry lookups like
> builtin_function_extension (registry/stubs.rs:836) already lowercase and serve
> as the model. Add one mixed-case fixture per dispatch family (return type,
> narrowing, method return, strict-rules check). Optionally, add a debug_assert
> or a unit test that every string literal arm in these matches is lowercase, so
> a camelCase arm like "getScalarResult" can't silently become dead after the
> switch.

#### K197. Strip XML-forbidden characters in checkstyle/junit

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** One stray byte in a docblock, as found in legacy code or
  binary-ish fixtures, no longer makes the entire checkstyle/junit report
  unparseable in Jenkins or GitLab.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/formatter/utils.rs:137`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/utils.rs:312`,
  `crates/reporting/src/reporter.rs:371`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs:257`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs:196`
- **Risks:** Negligible: the dropped characters cannot legally appear in XML
  anyway.
- **Verification:** All citations check out. Mago:
  crates/reporting/src/formatter/utils.rs:137 xml_encode drops any char that
  fails is_xml_1_0_character (lines 169-175). The test at about line 313 asserts
  that "a\0\u{1}\u{B}\u{C}\u{1F}\u{FFFE}\u{FFFF}b\t" encodes to "ab\t".
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs, change xml_escape (line 257) to handle
> every char outside XML 1.0's Char production (anything other than \t, \n, \r,
> U+0020-D7FF, U+E000-FFFD, U+10000-10FFFF). That means C0 controls except
> tab/LF/CR, plus U+FFFE and U+FFFF. Replace each one with U+FFFD rather than
> dropping it, so the report still shows that a bad byte was there. Escaping it
> as &#N; is not an option, because XML 1.0 forbids even character references to
> these code points. Surrogates cannot occur in a Rust &str. Because
> render_checkstyle (lines 187-198) and render_junit (lines 221-241) send every
> file name, message, identifier and tip body through xml_escape, this one
> change covers both formats. Add a test in output/tests.rs that builds a
> diagnostic whose message holds "\0", "\x01", "\x0B", "\u{FFFE}", a path with
> '<' and CR/LF, and a tip. It should check that neither rendered report
> contains any forbidden char. A small hand-written well-formedness check is
> enough; no XML-parser dependency is needed. Leave the text, json and GitHub
> formats alone: JSON already escapes controls through serde.

#### K234. Honor composer vendor-dir

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Projects with a custom vendor-dir (e.g. `lib/vendor` in Drupal-
  and WordPress-style layouts) currently get no vendor context at all, so they
  see floods of unknown-class diagnostics. A silently ignored broken
  composer.json also changes results without any explanation.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/composer/src/schema.rs:433`,
  `src/commands/init.rs:472`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/composer/src/vendor.rs:47`,
  `crates/composer/src/manifest.rs:327`, `crates/composer/src/manifest.rs:132`
- **Risks:** Low. Paths must stay spelled consistently with the analyzed root
  (manifest_root vs canonical).
- **Verification:** All the citations check out. Details: mago
  crates/composer/src/schema.rs:432-434 declares
  `#[serde(rename = "vendor-dir")] pub vendor_dir: Option<String>`. Mago
  src/commands/init.rs:472 does `ComposerPackage::from_str(&composer_json)?`,
  which propagates the parse error.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. In crates/composer/src/manifest.rs, split the composer.json read out of
>    ComposerManifest::load (line ~129) and have it return
>    Result\<Option\<ComposerManifest>, String>: Ok(None) when composer.json is
>    missing, Err(msg) when serde_json fails (msg includes serde's line and
>    column). Add a `vendor_dir: PathBuf` field resolved from
>    `config.vendor-dir`: relative to root, absolute kept as-is, a leading `~`
>    expanded. Default to "vendor". 2) Replace the hardcoded root.join("vendor")
>    in read_installed (manifest.rs:302 and :327) with the resolved dir. 3)
>    Change vendor::discover_vendor_context(root) (vendor.rs:43-47) to take the
>    resolved vendor dir. PackageContext::load (lib.rs:32-36) resolves the dir
>    once from the parsed JSON and passes it to both. 4) In PackageContext, keep
>    the parse error. Push it into the existing Session `warnings` Vec
>    (project/session.rs:338), worded like "composer.json: \<serde error>;
>    composer-derived settings (PHP version, extensions, vendor context)
>    disabled". 5) When the resolved vendor dir is not a component literally
>    named `vendor`, add it as a path-prefix exclusion next to
>    DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES (project.rs:2093). Otherwise a default scan
>    analyzes the whole vendor tree (e.g. `deps/`). Skip the COMPOSER env var
>    for the manifest name, and treat COMPOSER_VENDOR_DIR as optional at most:
>    an LSP server or editor process rarely has the project's shell environment,
>    so env-derived results would differ between CLI and editor. If it is
>    supported, Composer's own precedence is env over config, not config then
>    env as the original proposal says. Add unit tests in
>    crates/composer/src/tests/vendor_context_discovery.rs for a custom
>    vendor-dir and for a malformed composer.json.

#### K249. PHPDoc parser recursion-depth limit

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** A single hostile or generated vendor file currently kills
  check-project and, more importantly, the long-running LSP server. The fix is a
  small local change.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/stream.rs:92`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:546`
- **Risks:** The limit must be comfortably above real-world nesting (shapes
  rarely exceed ~10 levels).
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate. In Mago, MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH is
  512 at crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/stream.rs:43, enter_recursion
  is at :92, it is called from parser/internal/type/composite.rs:24, and the
  'Type nested too deeply' message is at crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/error.rs:88.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `depth: u32` field to `TagParser`
> (crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:61-65). Increment and decrement it inside
> `parse_type` (:546), the one entry every nested position goes through: generic
> args, shape fields, callable params/return, conditional branches and
> parenthesized types. Past a fixed cap (256), push a PhpDocParseError "type
> nested too deeply", skip to the end of the tag, and return TypeNode::Error.
>
> Use a cap here rather than wrapping the recursion in `syntax::stack::guard`
> (crates/syntax/src/stack.rs:17). The guard only grows the stack for the frames
> it wraps. The TypeNode tree still has to survive every later recursive walk:
> `to_source_string` (ast.rs:207), the phpdoc-to-Type resolution in phpstan-rs,
> and the compiler-generated recursive Drop of the Box/Vec tree. Each of those
> would need its own guard or an iterative rewrite. A cap at parse time bounds
> all of them at once.
>
> Add a unit test in crates/phpdoc that parses a `list<` nested 100k deep and
> checks it returns an error without overflowing. The parser runs on every
> vendor file, and in the LSP it runs on every open buffer.

#### K250. Case-insensitive tag-name dispatch

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Legacy and hand-written codebases that capitalise tags (@Param,
  @Return, @Var, @Throws are common in older PEAR/Zend-style code) get their
  documented types used instead of silently falling back to mixed.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/tag/mod.rs:57`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:750`
- **Risks:** Stricter-than-PHPStan behaviour, since phpdoc-parser dispatches
  case-sensitively, so a previously ignored malformed `@Return foo bar` can now
  produce phpDoc.parseError. That is acceptable, but check it against the
  fixtures.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are wrong. Mago's dispatch_tag_value
  starts at mago crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/parser/internal/tag/mod.rs:56. Lines
  58-70 fold the name to lowercase and drop '-' into a stack buffer, and lines
  74+ match on the result ("param", "paramout", "return", ...).
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs, add a helper
> `fn canonical_tag_name(written: &str, rest: &str) -> Cow<str>`. It returns the
> name unchanged if the name contains '\\' (namespaced annotation) or if `rest`
> starts with '(' (Doctrine/Sensio annotation-call syntax such as `@Template()`,
> `@Method("GET")`, `@Type("...")`). Otherwise it returns
> `written.to_ascii_lowercase()`. Use it in the plain-tag loop (:331-351), the
> @phan-/@psalm- loop (:358-375; lowercase the prefix check too, e.g.
> `@PHPStan-`/`@Psalm-`), the @phpstan- loop (:376-383), and the unknown-tag
> check against KNOWN_PHPSTAN_TAGS (:1223-1237). Keep passing the as-written
> name as `written` to apply_tag_recording_errors so messages and
> InvalidTagValue keep the user's spelling. Skip hyphen folding (`@paramOut`),
> because it is not an established spelling anywhere and adds ambiguity for no
> gain. Optionally make the raw `doc.contains` scans for `@impure`/`@final`
> (checker/noop.rs:387, checker/oop/method_overrides.rs:219) case-insensitive
> for consistency. Add docblock unit tests for: `@Param string $s` typed as
> string; `@RETURN int`; `@Template("x.html.twig")` and `@Method("GET")` staying
> ignored with no parse error; `@ORM\Column(...)` unchanged.

#### K303. Apply stub-only availability transforms only to stubs, not first-party code

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** Removes a silent false-positive source on legitimate user code.
  Polyfill and compat libraries can declare which PHP versions their symbols
  exist on, and the analyzer enforces it for downstream projects that target
  older PHP.
- **Mago evidence:** `composer/src/AvailableSince.php:33`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/version_claim.rs:128`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/availability.rs:68`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1957`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/stub_attributes.rs:36`
- **Risks:** Some projects vendor JetBrains' own attribute on purpose for
  PhpStorm, and they would lose the current behaviour. That behaviour is wrong
  for user code anyway. The new attributes need a runtime class only when
  reflected, so the Composer package has to be optional for analysis.
- **Verification:** All citations check out. Mago:
  composer/src/AvailableSince.php:33 is `final class AvailableSince` with ctor
  `int $version`. composer/src also has AvailableUntil, OptionalSince/Until,
  RequiredSince/Until, TypedWithSince/Until and UntypedSince/Until.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep only the first half, and make it smaller than proposed. (1) In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/stub_attributes.rs:36 (`stub_attribute`), stop matching
> on the last name segment. Match the resolved FQN instead:
> `JetBrains\PhpStorm\Internal\PhpStormStubsElementAvailable`,
> `JetBrains\PhpStorm\Internal\LanguageLevelTypeAware`,
> `JetBrains\PhpStorm\Internal\PhpVersionAware`, compared case-insensitively.
> This also covers aliases, because `resolved_class()` already sees through
> them. With that change, a user's own `App\PhpStormStubsElementAvailable` (or
> an unimported bare name inside a namespace) no longer deletes declarations.
> (2) Also thread the `is_stub` flag, which `project::parse_file` already takes
> at crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2014-2017, into `parse_with_ignores`
> (project.rs:1949-1960). Skip the transform on analysed first-party files. Keep
> it for stub_paths files and for context/vendor files, so a vendored
> jetbrains/phpstorm-stubs copy still gets transformed. The LSP `update_file`
> path (project.rs:966) needs the file's stub flag, or it should re-apply the
> same FQN rule. Add a stub_attributes test for a user-namespaced look-alike
> attribute that must be left alone. (3) Drop the proposed
> PhpstanRs\AvailableSince/Until attribute family, or at most file it as a
> separate, low-priority idea. It needs a Composer runtime package, an attribute
> nobody in the ecosystem uses, and polyfill libraries won't adopt an attribute
> tied to one analyzer. Mago's own Mago\ family
> (codex/src/scanner/version_claim.rs) has the same adoption problem.

#### K174. Faithful property hook parsing

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Probes m78, m79 and m83 plus the hook-visibility probe are all
  PHP fatals and all silent. More importantly, today an invalid hook is silently
  re-typed as `get` or dropped, which can hide real errors inside the body.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs:978`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs:998`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs:632`,
  `crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs:699`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/property_hooks.rs:47`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/property_hooks.rs:109`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/property_hooks.rs:33`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:361`
- **Risks:** The AST change is local. Real PHP accepts get/set
  case-insensitively, so keep eq_ignore_ascii_case.
- **Verification:** Mago line numbers are close but a few lines off. In
  crates/semantics/src/internal/checker/class_like/property.rs, the empty hook
  list check starts at about line 629 (the `hook_list.hooks.is_empty()` test).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep it small and do it only as a cheap cleanup; it should not be treated as a
> robustness priority. In crates/syntax/src/parser/property_hooks.rs,
> parse_property_hooks (lines 10-117) should record a problem list on
> PropertyHooks (crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:361), such as
> `pub problems: Vec<(HookProblem, Span)>`, instead of silently normalising. It
> would record four things: (1) a hook name that is not get/set, compared
> case-insensitively (today line 47-49 skips any token and treats it as get);
> (2) a duplicate get/set (line 109-113 overwrites); (3) an empty `{}` list; (4)
> public/private/protected on a hook, which the loop at lines 33-44 silently
> skips. For duplicates, keep the first hook in `get`/`set` and push the later
> one into an `extra` vec so its body still goes through
> check_get_hook/check_set_hook. Emit all four as errors at the top of
> check_property_hooks in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop/property_hooks.rs:30, for both declared
> properties and promoted-ctor param hooks. Skip Mago's other compile-time
> checks unless they fall out for free.

#### K209. Hang watcher and slow-file reporting for check-project

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism, robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** Users report 'it hangs' with a file name instead of nothing.
  Infinite loops in fixed-point code (union merging, loop widening, the registry
  fixed point) get located immediately, and editor users see which file stalls
  diagnostics. | The super-linear cases seen earlier (&& chains, concat chains,
  nested loops) become visible on real projects without a profiler, and a user
  report can name the file that hangs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:214`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:304`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/analysis.rs:411`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:161`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:339`
- **phpstan-rs:** `ROADMAP.md:2564`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1308`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1309`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:672`
- **Risks:** The watcher thread must not hold slot locks while formatting, and
  must shut down cleanly on Drop (Mago uses a condvar with notify_all). There is
  a small cost of one mutex lock per file start and end. | The flag must stay
  off by default so output stays deterministic, and there is minor overhead when
  it is on.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially correct, with four nuances.
  (1) In Mago, the 5 s constants are at
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:198-199
  (HANG_INITIAL_THRESHOLD=5s, HANG_POLL_INTERVAL=2s).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep it to the minimum, and only if a hang or a slow file comes up again. Add
> one opt-in `--timings` flag to check-project. It wraps the closure in
> `Project::check_files` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1308-1313), and the
> writes-only pass in `judge_property_types`, with an `Instant` per file. It
> then prints the slowest N files, with milliseconds, to stderr. Add an
> in-flight slot per worker, indexed by `rayon::current_thread_index()` and
> cleared by a guard, plus a watcher thread on a `Condvar::wait_timeout`. With
> `--timings` on, that thread prints "still checking X after Ns". Don't turn it
> on by default, don't add an LSP window/logMessage path, and don't add
> exponential-backoff re-reporting. Put everything in a small
> `project/timings.rs`. A panicked file needs nothing new, because
> `catch_unwind` already reports it.

#### K306. Build-provenance attestations for release assets

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** Anyone who auto-downloads a native binary into CI (the Composer
  launcher, the editor, the container) can check it came from this repository's
  workflow at a given commit, a supply-chain guarantee a colocated checksum
  cannot give.
- **Mago evidence:** `.github/workflows/cd.yml:432`,
  `.github/workflows/cd.yml:100`
- **phpstan-rs:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:127`
- **Risks:** Only useful after a public GitHub remote exists (release.yml:3-9
  notes there is none yet).
- **Verification:** The citations check out. Mago:
  .github/workflows/cd.yml:15-16 grants `id-token: write` and
  `attestations: write`. Lines 100-108 attest the source tar.gz and zip with
  actions/attest-build-provenance@v3. Lines 432-435 attest the binary package,
  and lines 437-441 attest the WASM package.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Scope it to the workflow only. In .github/workflows/release.yml, add
> `permissions: { contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: write }` to
> the job that uploads releases. After the `sha256sum "$dest.gz"` step (line
> 127), add one `actions/attest-build-provenance` step with `subject-path` set
> to the `.gz` asset. Add one line to the install docs showing
> `gh attestation verify phpstan-rs-<triple>.gz --repo darktorres/phpstan-rs`.
> Leave out the optional verification step in the Composer launcher and VS Code
> downloader: it would mean shelling out to `gh`, handling auth and adding a
> fallback path, and that is ongoing maintenance for something few users would
> ever turn on.

#### K313. Replace demo with dump signatures built on the real Project pipeline, listing only declarations from the input file (not stubs)

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary

- **Benefit:** The existing debug tool stops giving answers that differ from

- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/cst.rs:138`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:85`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:127`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:56`
- **Risks:** Changing or removing `demo` breaks anyone's habit or scripts. Keep
  `demo` as a hidden alias for a while.
- **Verification:** The citations are close but a few details are off. In Mago,
  `configuration.parser.to_settings()` is at src/commands/cst.rs:144, inside
  CstCommand::execute (136-). Line 138 is not that call.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep it small. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs, record the function and
> class names that `Registry::build(&program)` produces (line 72) before the
> `merge_stubs*` calls (lines 73-76), and have the signature loop (lines 85-103)
> and the hierarchy loop (lines 105-118) print only those names. For the
> hierarchy, list each source class's ancestors from the registry's precomputed

> comparing classes within the file (lines 107-110). Delete the hard-coded
> strlen example (lines 120-123). Replace the `panic!` at line 56 and the parse
> `.unwrap()` at line 62 with an eprintln of the path and error, then
> `process::exit(2)`. Either drop the diagnostics section (lines 125-140) or

> Treat a `dump symbol <FQN>` command that reads merged Project reflection

### 3.4 performance (35)

#### K205. Dynamic largest-first work queue

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** This removes a straggler thread that currently holds up the check
  phase whenever file costs are skewed, which is the norm: generated code, large
  legacy files and big vendor classes. The perf probe showed one worker thread
  with 48.8% of samples and 7 idle. The worst case for wall time is roughly the
  total cost of the top len/(2N) files, and after the fix it drops toward
  max(largest file, total/N).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:345`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:673`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:288`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:626`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check.rs:25`
- **Risks:** Slightly more per-item overhead from one atomic fetch per file,
  which is negligible next to millisecond-scale checks. Byte size is only an
  approximation of check cost; a later refinement could use statement count or
  the previous run's timing.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with small offsets.
  In Mago, crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:345-347 is
  `host_files.into_par_iter().map_init(LocalArena::new, ...)`, and nothing sorts
  it by cost. A second, similar par_iter sits at pipeline.rs:479.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Step 1, which is one line and should be measured first: in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:288 (map_on_pool), change
> `items.par_iter().map(&f).collect()` to
> `items.par_iter().with_max_len(1).map(&f).collect()`. Do the same for the
> parse par_iter at crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:626-629. Rayon's
> LengthSplitter (rayon-1.12.0 src/iter/plumbing/mod.rs:315-322) then raises
> min_splits to len, so every item can be stolen on its own. Work-stealing then
> limits the tail to about one in-flight item per thread. Because collect() is
> indexed, output order stays the same. check_files (project.rs:1308) and the
> others pass of judge_property_types (project.rs:1369) are covered
> automatically.
>
> Step 2, only if step 1 still leaves skew: add a small
> `map_on_pool_lpt(pool, items, cost, f)` helper in project.rs. It sorts indices
> by descending cost, runs `pool.broadcast` (or `pool.scope` with
> current_num_threads workers) that pull the next index from an AtomicUsize, and
> writes each result into a `Vec<OnceLock<R>>` (or `Vec<Mutex<Option<R>>>`)
> slot. That gives true LPT order. Rayon steals the oldest job, which is the
> half holding the small files, so plain rayon cannot. Cost: source length for
> check, which session.rs:668-677 already computes, and file metadata length for
> parse.
>
> Optional: crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check.rs:25-30 is the parse-only `check`
> command. Replace its static par_chunks with
> `par_iter().with_max_len(1).filter_map(...)`, though that is a minor developer
> tool. Keep the largest-first sort at session.rs:673-676. It only helps once
> splitting is fine-grained, and under the current default splitter it actively
> puts all the big files on the calling thread.

#### K212. Incremental update: check affected files as a parallel, cancellable batch

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: pipeline-parallelism, incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Editing a widely used class re-checks N dependents in about
  N/cores of the time, and duplicate facts-only checker passes disappear.
  Cancellation still works at per-file granularity. | The probe (ws7) showed a
  scan_paths context file (lib/l.php) that was not published at startup get its
  'return type mismatch' diagnostic published after an unrelated edit to
  src/a.php.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:1337`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:1336`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:1315`,
  `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:731`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1080`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1286`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1233`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:849`
- **Risks:** Results must stay identical to the serial loop: check_files already
  merges facts in path order. The panic-poisoning issue in the debounce worker
  (CRASH_REPORTING_PLAN.md:141-146) becomes more reachable if it is not fixed
  first, but check_files' catch_unwind actually improves it. |
  judge_property_types runs per check_files batch, so the private-property
  judgement must see the same writers. Checking all affected files as one batch
  actually improves this over the current per-file calls. The Server lock split
  requires Project data to be shareable (Arc) during checks.
- **Verification:** Almost all of the citations check out. There are a few small
  corrections. (1) phpstan-rs project.rs: `check_one` is defined at line 1284.
  Line 1286 is its `check_files(&paths, None, ..)` call, so the claim is right
  about 1286.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Changes, all in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs and lsp.rs:
>
> 1. Add a shared helper, e.g.
>    `fn recheck_affected(&mut self, affected: FxHashSet<PathBuf>, pool:
>    Option<&rayon::ThreadPool>, should_abort: &(dyn Fn() -> bool + Sync)) ->
>    FxHashMap<PathBuf, Vec<Diagnostic>>`.
>    It should: (a) Keep only files that are `files[p].analyzed` or no longer
>    loaded (so a removed path still gets an empty clearing Vec). Context files
>    still take part in the transitive_affected_files_from BFS but are not
>    checked or returned. (b) Sort the paths and make one
>    `check_files(&paths, pool, self.member_index_built, false)` call. (c) Check
>    `should_abort()` inside the check_files closure before each `run_checker`.
>    An aborted item should get a distinct outcome, for example an `Aborted`
>    variant or a filtered-out Option, and be dropped from the results rather
>    than published as empty. (d) Then run `reindex_use_sites_for_file` serially
>    on each surviving result. update_file_cancellable (project.rs:1079-1092)
>    and remove_files (project.rs:1175-1187) both call this helper.
> 2. Change `should_abort` from `impl FnMut() -> bool` to
>    `impl Fn() -> bool + Sync`. The LSP closure already reads an atomic or
>    mutex generation, so it can be shared.
> 3. Give Project an `Option<Arc<rayon::ThreadPool>>`, set from the
>    `worker_pool()` the Server already holds (lsp.rs:143/299). A test or
>    `update_file` caller without a pool keeps using serial
>    `map_on_pool(None, ..)`.
> 4. Optional follow-up: check the edited `path` alone first and hand its result
>    to a callback, so lsp.rs can publish it before the dependents run.
> 5. Defer the Server lock split. It needs Project behind Arc/RwLock or
>    snapshotting, which is an L-sized change. Batching alone already shrinks
>    the time the lock is held by about 1/cores.
> 6. Skip Mago's EXPENSE_LIMIT fallback to full analysis. A single parallel
>    batch over the analyzed affected set already does what check_all would do.

#### K69. Precompute per-node type flags at intern time

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Turns O(size) traversals on hot paths (every union, every
  template substitution) into O(1). The largest win is on big shapes and nested
  generics, which are also the types that are expensive to traverse.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/flags.rs:5`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/expander.rs:170`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/late.rs:133`,
  `crates/types/src/queries.rs:143`, `crates/types/src/union.rs:303`,
  `crates/types/src/lib.rs:79`
- **Risks:** The constant nodes (intern.rs:48-94) must get correct flags too.
  Extension payloads (Repr::Extension) must report their own flags through
  ExtensionTypeData or be treated conservatively.
- **Verification:** Mago side is misdescribed.
  mago/crates/codex/src/ttype/flags.rs:7 `UnionFlags(u16)` is real, but it holds
  11 bits (bits 0-10), and none of them is a cached structural fact about the
  tree. The "(27)" and "(11)" in the idea are line numbers, not bit positions.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `flags: u16` to `Node` (crates/types/src/lib.rs:79-83) and compute it in
> `intern::insert` (crates/types/src/intern.rs, right before
> `Arc::new(Node { repr, hash, exact })` at ~line 113). Compute it only after a
> table miss, as the node's own tag bits ORed with its direct children's flags,
> using the same `for_each_child` walk that `any_child` uses
> (crates/types/src/traverse.rs:132). That way the flags match today's recursive
> answers by construction, including how `Repr::Extension` is treated (as a
> leaf, the same as now). The constant nodes (intern.rs:48-94) already go
> through `insert`, so they need nothing extra. Bits: HAS_TEMPLATE
> (TemplateParam, or a Conditional whose subject is
> `ConditionalSubject::Template`), HAS_LATE (KeyOf/OffsetAccess), HAS_VALUE_OF,
> HAS_CLASS_CONST. Then `contains_deferred` = LATE|VALUE_OF|CLASS_CONST.
> `is_single_value` can be cached as its own bit, but that one is not an OR of
> children: set it at insert from the repr plus the children's bits. Then: (1)
> Make `references_template` (late.rs:133), `contains_late` (late.rs:166) and
> `contains_deferred` (queries.rs:143) O(1) flag reads. (2) This is the real
> payoff: early-return `self.clone()` in `substitute` (templates.rs:410),
> `replace_templates` (templates.rs:339) and `resolve_late_to_bounds`
> (late.rs:~150) when the subtree has neither HAS_TEMPLATE nor
> HAS_LATE|HAS_VALUE_OF. The gate has to include late/value-of because `settle`
> (late.rs:120) also resolves template-free key-of/value-of/offset nodes. Today
> these functions rebuild every template-free subtree through `map_children`:
> each node is re-interned (exact hash, shard lock, exact_eq), and each union is
> re-normalized through `Type::union` reduce, which runs
> `absorb_contained_members`' O(n^2) structural checks again. (3)
> `absorb_contained_members` (union.rs:303) then gets its `settled` predicate
> for free. Add a debug_assert or unit test that each flag equals the old
> recursive computation over the existing types test suite.

#### K211. Parallel LSP workspace load

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Initial LSP load parse time drops by roughly the core count,
  because in the LSP today it runs serially on the thread that also serves
  requests. The CLI and LSP also share one load code path, removing a source of
  parity drift.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:364`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:427`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:480`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:625`
- **Risks:** The order-sensitive collision policy (lsp.rs:470-479 doc) must be
  preserved: insert context files first, then analysed files, each in sorted
  order. That is exactly what Session::load already does.
- **Verification:** The canonicalize calls in lsp.rs are at lines 495 and 526,
  not 494 and 537. In Mago, `into_par_iter().map_init(LocalArena::new, ...)` is
  at incremental_analysis.rs:363-365 inside `analyze()`, which starts at
  line 342.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one shared helper in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs (or
> project/session.rs), e.g.
> `Project::load_batch(&mut self, context: &[PathBuf], analysed: &[PathBuf],
> stub_set: &FxHashSet<PathBuf>, pool: &rayon::ThreadPool) -> LoadBatchReport {
> lex_warnings, skipped_context, skipped_analysed: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>, sizes
> }`.
> It parses all files with
> `pool.install(|| files.par_iter().map(read_and_parse).collect())`, wrapping
> `parse_file` (project.rs:2014) in `catch_unwind` the way session.rs:575-581
> already does, then calls `insert_parsed_file` (project.rs:669) serially:
> context files first, then analysed files. Session::load (session.rs:617-667)
> calls it without changing behaviour. lsp.rs:480 `load_workspace_files` becomes
> three steps. (1) Build the file lists as today. (2) Decide which files to keep
> before any parsing: canonicalize in parallel on `self.pool` (lsp.rs:145), then
> serially apply the `loaded` FxHashSet dedup and the
> `self.project.ast(&path).is_some()` skip, in the same sorted order, context
> before analysed. (3) Pass the kept lists to `load_batch`, and turn the skipped
> and parse-failed entries into the window/logMessage warnings that
> `load_one_file` (lsp.rs:427) produces today. Leave `finish_loading` where it
> is now: once per batch, in `add_workspace_folders`. Optionally pass the
> stub_paths files as `is_stub` so the LSP stops differing from the CLI on
> duplicate-class indexing (project.rs:648-652, 2029).

#### K216. Skip no-op updates by content hash

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** The probe (ws/drive.py) shows that a didOpen of an already-loaded
  file with identical text caused a full cascade, republishing dependent d.php.
  Opening files, saving with no edit, and the watched-file echo of every save
  each currently pay a full global registry recompute plus a transitive
  re-check. With the hash check this becomes a near-free lookup.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:545`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:601`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:53`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:966`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:721`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:827`
- **Risks:** If settings changed since the last check, the file's cached
  diagnostics could be outdated; key the cache on a settings generation counter,
  which reload_configuration already republishes through. The hash has to cover
  the exact bytes passed in, including the BOM.
- **Verification:** Mago: all three citations are accurate.
  FileState.content_hash is at
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:53. The xxh3 hash with
  the "hash match despite watcher hint" branch is at lines 546-556. The early
  return of cached issues when nothing changed is at lines 601-605.
- **Refined proposal:**

> You don't need a hash on the LSP path. In practice only the LSP calls
> update_file (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:721, :763 and :827; the other
> callers are tests and main/incremental_bench.rs:57). The LSP turns on
> retain_source, so FileState.source (project.rs:62) already holds the exact
> last-indexed text.
>
> (1) At the top of Project::update_file_cancellable (project.rs:944), before
> parse_with_ignores, add:
> `if self.files.get(path).and_then(|f| f.source.as_deref()) == Some(new_source)
> { let d = <check_file_and_member_refs or check_file, as the tail loop does at
> project.rs:1073-1083>; reindex_use_sites_for_file; return Ok({path: d}); }`.
> This re-checks only that one file and skips the parse, unindex_file, all ~20
> global finishing passes (project.rs:1017-1057) and the cascade
> (transitive_affected_files).
>
> For non-LSP callers, where retain_source is off, you can add a
> `content_hash: u64` field to FileState (project.rs:48). Fill it with FxHash or
> xxh3 of new_source.as_bytes() in insert_parsed_file (project.rs:669) and in
> update_file, and compare it when source is None. This part is optional.
>
> (2) In lsp.rs handle_watched_files_changed (lsp.rs:792-839), skip a Created or
> Changed event when `open_uris.get(&path)` has `Some(version)`. That means the
> editor owns the document and its buffer is authoritative. The current code
> also overwrites the entry with version None at lsp.rs:825 and overwrites
> latest_text with the disk text at :826. That is a correctness bug as well as
> wasted work: after an echo, publishes carry no document version, and code
> actions and formatting read disk text instead of the buffer.
>
> Tests:
>
> - project/tests/incremental_updates.rs: calling update_file twice with the
>   same text returns only that path and gives the same diagnostics.
> - An LSP test: a watched Changed event for an open document produces no
>   dependent republish and keeps the version.

#### K217. Batch update API for file bursts

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Branch switches, rebases, formatter runs over a directory, and
  codegen now cost one recompute and one cascade instead of N. With the cascade
  union, a file that depends on several changed files is checked once instead of
  up to N times.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:495`,
  `crates/database/src/watcher.rs:383`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:803`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:2267`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1160`
- **Risks:** Cancellation granularity changes: with several edits in one batch,
  abort should fire only when a newer generation exists for a path in the batch.
  A parse failure in one file must not block the others, so keep the
  last-good-AST behavior per file.
- **Verification:** Mago citations hold, with small line-number drift.
  analyze_incremental is at
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:495. It handles
  deleted files and the new_file_scans set in one pass.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs, add
> `Project::update_files(&mut self, changes: &[(PathBuf, FileChange)],
> should_abort: impl FnMut(&Path) -> bool) -> (FxHashMap<PathBuf,
> Vec<Diagnostic>>, Vec<(PathBuf, ParseError)>)`,
> with `enum FileChange { Upsert(String), Delete }`. Steps: (1) Parse every
> Upsert up front with parse_with_ignores, in parallel through the existing
> worker_pool/par_iter helper (project.rs:215/288). The interner is already an
> Arc\<Interner>. A file that fails to parse goes into the error list and is
> left completely untouched, which keeps the last-good-AST rule that
> update_file_cancellable documents at project.rs:950-965. (2) Call unindex_file
> for every Delete and every successfully parsed Upsert, collecting one
> changed_symbols set. (3) Index every new AST: registry.index,
> record_phpstan_class_file, duplicate_fn_sites and duplicate_class_sites,
> register_references, and the FileState insert. Only after all of them are in,
> run the finishing sequence once. That is either finish_loading() or the same
> sequence with the PendingFileBodies variant, and once the new FileStates are
> inserted, plain finish_loading() is enough. This also removes the finishing
> sequence that update_file_cancellable duplicates at project.rs:1037-1080. (4)
> Seed one transitive_affected_files_from call with the union of changed_symbols
> plus every changed path. Check each affected file once, and before each
> check_file call should_abort for the files in the batch.
> update_file_cancellable, update_file, remove_file and remove_files then become
> thin wrappers. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs, handle_watched_files_changed
> (line 792) already coalesces to last_by_path. Instead of looping
> update_file/remove_file per path, it builds one change list and makes one
> update_files call, then one publish. In run_pending_edits (line 2261), pass
> the whole expired `edits` vector as one batch. The abort closure fires when
> any batch path has a newer generation than the one recorded for it. The
> existing per-path still_current filter stays: publish a result only if every
> batch path whose edit could have caused it is still current. The conservative
> version publishes only when no batch path went stale, and otherwise lets the
> requeued newer edit republish.

#### K236. Changed-files mode

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Pre-commit hooks and PR CI get most of the value at a fraction of
  the cost, since checking dominates parsing on large repos. Using dependents
  makes this more correct than Mago's staged-only scoping: breaking a caller
  elsewhere still gets reported.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/analyze.rs:165`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:684`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2166`
- **Risks:** Shelling out to git needs clear errors outside a repo. Dependents
  are keyed by bare names (project.rs:2142), which over-approximates, but that's
  safe.
- **Verification:** Mago: src/commands/analyze.rs:165 is only the
  `pub staged: bool` field (doc comment at 158-164, "Fails if not in a git
  repository"). The logic is at analyze.rs:272-284.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `--staged` and `--changed-since <ref>` to CheckProjectArgs in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs (they conflict with `--fix`,
> `--generate-baseline` and `--dump-types`). Get the file list from
> `git diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACMRD` (with `--cached` for staged,
> `<ref>...HEAD` plus the worktree for changed-since), run through
> `git -C <root>`. Outside a repo, or if git is missing, stop with a clear
> error. Keep only files under the configured analyse `dirs`. If nothing is
> left, exit 0 early, as Mago does at src/commands/analyze.rs:160-165.
>
> Still load everything through Session::load (session.rs) so all type context
> is there. Then, in Session::analyse
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:684-690), pass a narrowed list to
> project.check_files. The seed is the changed files' own declared class and
> function names, as bare names. Expand it with a new pub(crate) wrapper around
> Project::transitive_affected_files_from (project.rs:1215), and add the changed
> files themselves.
>
> Deleted and renamed files need handling so broken callers still show up. For
> each D/R entry, parse the old blob (`git show <ref>:<path>`, or `:<path>` for
> the index) only to collect its declared names, and add those names to the
> seed.
>
> In partial mode, three things change: (a) Skip unmatched-baseline-entry
> reporting, since entries for files that weren't checked would show up as
> stale. (b) Skip the tier-2 and project-wide passes (dead members and enum
> cases, dead code, duplicate declarations, named-argument aggregation), or run
> them fully only if they're explicitly re-enabled. Print a one-line notice
> either way. (c) Print "checked N of M files (K changed + dependents)" so users
> know the scope.
>
> For `--staged`, also say that the working-tree contents are what gets
> analysed, not the index blobs. Reading staged content exactly would mean
> loading the index blobs, which can be a later refinement.

#### K50. Precompiled/serialized stub registry snapshot instead of parsing stubs every process start

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: codebase-model, stubs-prelude,
  build-structure)
- **Benefit:** Startup today is about 0.95s / 150MB on a one-line file against
  Mago's 0.07s / 96MB (measured facts in the task). Most of the difference is
  stub parsing. That matters for the LSP cold start, pre-commit hooks, editor
  'check this file' runs and the test suite. Dropping the duplicate copy lowers
  peak RSS in every run. | Measured here: a one-line file costs phpstan-rs
  1.1-1.6 s wall, 3.5 s user CPU and 148 MB;
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/src/lib.rs:1`,
  `crates/prelude/src/build.rs:26`, `build.rs:15`,
  `crates/prelude/src/lib.rs:64`, `src/consts.rs:109`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:953`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:789`,
  `crates/stub-sources/build.rs:109`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:346`,
  `CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:2537`, `GATE_SPEED_PLAN.md:49`
- **Risks:** Option A: serialising hash-consed Arc\<Node> types and interned
  Names is non-trivial, and a type-representation change requires regenerating
  the cache (build-time generation avoids staleness). Option B: whole-registry
  passes (flatten, precompute owners, and anything iterating registry.classes
  such as completion) must either tolerate partial materialisation or force the
  needed subset, and lazy loading must be thread-safe under rayon. | Serde
  across the reflection types is broad. Re-interning on decode still costs
  something, since Type interning takes locks.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. build.rs:15-24 runs
  Prelude::build() on a 36 MB-stack thread, encodes the result and writes
  OUT_DIR/prelude.bin. crates/prelude/src/build.rs:26-47 is
  build_prelude_internal: it runs populate_codebase and adds every class-like,
  function and constant to safe_symbols.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in three steps, cheapest first.
>
> (1) Stop keeping two copies of the stubs. Today
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:789 `generated_stub_classes()` returns
> `generated_stub_data().classes.clone()` (the function and constant accessors
> do the same), and Project::new (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:346-350)
> merges those clones while the static LazyLock copy stays resident for the
> whole process. Instead, keep the data behind Arc and share it (a shared base
> layer the Registry falls back to), or let a one-shot CLI take ownership once.
> This is S cost and lowers peak RSS on every run.
>
> (2) Make the stub layer lazy, as CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN C5
> (CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:2511) already plans. At build time, emit a name ->
> stub-file index from crates/stub-sources/build.rs. It already walks every file
> and needs no parser dependency, which respects Appendix F. Then parse, index
> and patch only the files a run touches, with thread-safe OnceLock slots per
> file. Whole-registry passes such as completion enumeration and owner
> precompute must force the full set explicitly.
>
> (3) Only after C5 defines the stub layer's snapshot type, add a runtime cache
> instead of a build.rs blob. Store serde-encoded resolved reflections, one
> entry per stub file or index entry. Key each entry on the binary identity F2
> already defines plus a stub-format version and the PHP-version key. Write with
> atomic rename. On a miss, parse as today. Add a `--no-stub-cache` switch, and
> a gate test that checks decoded equals freshly parsed. Type and Name need
> custom Deserialize impls that re-intern through Type::new and
> Interner::global() so hash-consing and sharing are kept.
>
> Do not copy Mago's build.rs route. It makes the parser, registry and types
> crates build-dependencies of the snapshot, so every edit to the reflection
> code reruns a full stub parse at compile time, which is worse in a debug
> build.

#### K53. Signature/body split (fingerprints and separate edges) to stop incremental invalidation cascading on body-only edits

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: codebase-model, incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Typing inside a method body (the common LSP case) would re-check
  one file instead of every transitive dependent. Namespaced same-name classes
  stop causing spurious cascades. | The probe (ws6) showed that changing
  `return 1;` to `return 2;` inside Foo::v() re-checked and republished all four
  files (b.php via Foo, c.php via Bar, d.php via g/Bar). Mago would re-analyze
  only a.php.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:68`,
  `crates/codex/src/reference.rs:706`, `crates/codex/src/differ.rs:115`,
  `crates/codex/src/signature.rs:28`, `crates/codex/src/differ.rs:118`,
  `crates/fingerprint/src/function_like/mod.rs:102` (+4 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/deps.rs:8`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1215`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:980`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1079`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/purity.rs:70`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1247` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Summaries derived from bodies (purity, property writes, global
  variable inference, and the inferred assertions idea) make some body changes
  signature-relevant, so they must be folded into the hash. Getting that wrong
  causes stale diagnostics, which is worse than the current over-approximation.
  | This is only safe if every cross-file fact derived from a body is included
  in the summary. Any fact left out causes a stale diagnostic. The differential
  test harness is the safety net.
- **Verification:** Only small line offsets. mago crates/codex/src/differ.rs:
  myers_diff starts at line 81, and the per-child
  `a_child.signature_hash == b_child.signature_hash` keep test is at line 118,
  not 115. The top-level check
  `has_child_sig_change || a.signature_hash != b.signature_hash` is at line 136.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't split deps.rs syntactically into signature and body references. Diff the
> finished registry output instead, and log which foreign bodies the checker
> reads. (1) In Project::update_file_cancellable
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:944-1083), the whole registry is already
> re-finished on every edit. That covers flatten_traits,
> flatten_phpdoc_inheritance, resolve_transitive_purity and
> resolve_constant_named_types.
>
> - After those passes, compute a summary hash for every class, function and
>   constant entry. The hash is a hand-written Hash walk over ClassReflection
>   and FunctionReflection with spans and provenance stripped. It includes the
>   purity results, purity_dependencies and the property-write facts from
>   registry/purity.rs:70-74.
> - Keep the previous map on Project and diff it by name.
> - The finished reflections already include inherited and flattened members. So
>   B's summary changes when its parent C changes, and the transitive BFS in
>   transitive_affected_files_from (project.rs:1215-1260) becomes a one-hop
>   lookup: dependents of each changed name. (2) Hash registry.global_variables
>   as a whole. infer_global_variables (registry/global_vars.rs:174) rebuilds it
>   from every file's top-level code, so a top-level edit can change `global $x`
>   types in other files (checker/stmt.rs:812-822). If the hash changes,
>   re-check the files that use `global` or \$GLOBALS. (3) Wrap Checker.bodies
>   (checker.rs:281, the BodySource trait in registry/bodies.rs:14) in a
>   recording adapter so each check_file records which other files' bodies it
>   read. Two readers do this: uninitialized_dataflow.rs:750 absorb_resolved and
>   project/class_shape.rs:293 parent_call_rules. Store this as a reverse map,
>   body_readers[file]. On an edit, also re-check body_readers[path]. (4) Key
>   `dependents` by resolved FQN rather than bare names. Resolve through the
>   file's NameContext in deps.rs, which currently collects written names only
>   (deps.rs:8-33). This stops spurious cascades between same-name classes in
>   different namespaces. (5) Add a differential test in the project tests:
>   apply random edits, then compare the incremental results with a fresh full
>   check. Result: when nothing changed, re-check `path` plus body_readers plus
>   global users only. Otherwise do a one-hop dependents lookup of the changed
>   names.

#### K24. Use mimalloc as the global allocator, adopted by measurement

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation, pipeline-parallelism,
  build-structure)
- **Benefit:** Probe measurements with LD_PRELOAD on the current release binary:
  on a one-line file, glibc takes 1.03-1.47 s at 146-150 MB, and mimalloc takes
  0.91-0.95 s at 184-194 MB. On a 300-file synthetic project, glibc takes
  1.14-1.34 s at 166-172 MB and mimalloc 0.93-0.99 s at 209-216 MB. jemalloc
  sits between the two. MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 gave the lowest RSS (131-145 MB) but
  about 2.2x the wall time.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/main.rs:79`, `Cargo.toml:316`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:16`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:19`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:981`
- **Risks:** Could raise peak RSS, the metric this aspect targets, so it should
  not be enabled by default without corpus numbers. Adds a C dependency; the
  pcre-validate feature already sets that precedent. | Peak RSS can rise or fall
  depending on the workload, so measure it; the 1.62 GB peak matters. Adds a C
  dependency (mimalloc-sys), and the crate already accepts C deps (pcre2-sys,
  bundled sqlite). | It adds a C dependency built with cc, conflicting with the
  'pure Rust except pcre' goal stated in the pcre-validate comment; making it a
  feature keeps `--no-default-features` pure.
- **Verification:** All the citations are accurate. Mago: src/main.rs:79-85 is
  `#[cfg(all(not(feature="dhat-heap"), any(macos, windows, musl, gnu)))] #[global_allocator]
  static ALLOC: mimalloc::MiMalloc`,
  and the dhat::Alloc alternative is at lines 87-89.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml, add an optional `mimalloc` dependency and a
> `mimalloc` feature. Leave it out of the default features until corpus numbers
> exist. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs, install
> `#[global_allocator] static ALLOC: mimalloc::MiMalloc` under
> `cfg(all(feature = "mimalloc", not(feature = "dhat-heap"), not(feature = "hotpath-alloc")))`.
> Extend the existing compile_error! at main.rs:16-17 so that at most one
> allocator is installed. The library crates stay allocator-agnostic. Only once,
> on the full corpus and in an LSP steady-state session, measure wall time and
> peak RSS for glibc, mimalloc and mimalloc with MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0
> (optionally also glibc with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4). You can do this with
> LD_PRELOAD on the existing release binary, without rebuilding. Make it the
> default only if it is faster and peak RSS stays at 1.62 GB or below. Otherwise
> keep it opt-in and drop the arena/purge tuning explorations.

#### K58. Build the stub layer in parallel with file discovery and parsing

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: stubs-prelude, pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Hides stub-build latency behind IO-bound work (directory walks,
  composer JSON, file reads) and the serial parts of setup. The effect is
  largest for small and medium runs and language-server start. It needs no
  structural change. | Hides the serial walk time (and composer vendor discovery
  if moved there) behind stub init, cutting startup latency on every run. It is
  cheap and output-neutral.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/analyze.rs:303`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:443`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:594`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:595`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:611`
- **Risks:** Both phases are CPU-parallel, so on a saturated pool the overlap
  gain is limited to the serial and IO portions. Care is needed so the warm-up
  thread doesn't compete with the rayon pool size setting. | Both tasks compete
  for the pool; the walk is I/O-bound, so the interference is small.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. At
  mago/src/commands/analyze.rs:303, `rayon::join` decodes the prelude
  (`Prelude::decode(PRELUDE_BYTES)`) in one branch while the other runs
  `orchestrator.load_database(...)`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split Session::load (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:594) into two
> concurrent halves using rayon::join or std::thread::scope. (a) Build the
> stub-backed project: Project::new() (project.rs:346) runs
> generated_stub_data()'s LazyLock (registry/stubs.rs:953), then clones the Vecs
> and runs the serial registry.merge_stubs / merge_stub_classes /
> merge_stub_constants. (b) Walk dirs and scan_dirs and stub_dirs, sort them,
> and par-parse context and analysed files on self.pool (lines 595-628). Right
> now the parse has to wait for Project::new because it uses project.interner()
> (line 612). Add a small Project::with_interner(Arc\<Interner>) constructor, or
> have Project::new take the interner, so the interner is made first and shared
> by both halves. The stub data uses owned Names and doesn't touch the project
> interner. After the join, run configure() and insert_parsed_file serially as
> now. Keep the analyze_files.is_empty() early error, raising it after the join
> or checking it before the join is spawned. The stub par_iter currently runs on
> rayon's global pool, because Project::new is called outside pool.install. Move
> it into self.pool.install so --threads and stack settings govern it too.
> Otherwise, while both halves run, 16 threads compete for 8 cores. In the LSP,
> Server::new (lsp.rs:289) builds Project::new synchronously before the
> handshake. Start that construction on a thread at process start, so it
> overlaps reading the initialize request and client round-trips. For the CLI,
> an even cheaper first step is a stubs::warm() that forces
> generated_stub_data() from a spawned thread at the top of main. That overlaps
> config and composer loading and the walk, and can land before the interner
> refactor.

#### K200. Precompile and validate ignore_errors patterns at config load

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Removes O(diagnostics x entries) regex compilation, which is
  significant with dozens of message patterns and thousands of diagnostics, and
  matters most in the LSP where it runs on every edit. Stale suppressions get
  surfaced and misconfiguration is caught.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/lib.rs:259`,
  `crates/reporting/src/lib.rs:66`, `crates/reporting/src/lib.rs:741`,
  `crates/database/src/matcher.rs:134`, `crates/database/src/matcher.rs:206`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:71`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:81`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:96`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:55`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:407`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:94`
- **Risks:** Unmatched reporting must stay opt-in: some entries may target
  identifiers phpstan-rs doesn't implement, so reporting them unmatched would be
  noise (the doc comment at ignore_errors.rs:43-55 explains this). | Changing
  the glob semantics from fnmatch-without-FNM_PATHNAME to globset could change
  matches. Keep `*` crossing '/' by building globs with
  literal_separator(false), as Mago's default does.
- **Verification:** Mago: CompiledIgnoreSet::compile is at
  crates/reporting/src/lib.rs:~258-300. It compiles the regex/ExclusionMatcher
  once, and a bad entry gets tracing::error! and is skipped. The IgnoreEntry
  enum (Code/Pattern/Scoped) is at lib.rs:~66-100, and `in` goes through
  one_or_many.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs add
> `CompiledIgnoreErrors { entries: Vec<CompiledEntry> }`, where
> `CompiledEntry { identifier: Option<String>, paths: Vec<String>, message:
> Option<regex::Regex>, source_index: usize }`,
> and a
> `compile(&[IgnoreErrorEntry]) -> (CompiledIgnoreErrors, Vec<String /*warnings*/>)`.
> When `regex::Regex::new` fails, keep the current posture and skip that entry,
> but return a warning that names the entry index and the regex error. Include
> the case of PCRE-only syntax Rust's regex rejects, e.g. lookarounds or
> backreferences, which today makes the entry silently match nothing. Also strip
> one pair of PCRE delimiters (`#...#`/`/.../` plus flags, mapping `i` to
> `(?i)`) so entries copied from phpstan.neon work unchanged.
>
> Build it once: (a) In project/session.rs, when `Finalize`/`Session` is built
> from settings (around line 531). Push the warnings into the existing
> `warnings` Vec at session.rs:338, which is seeded from `config.warnings()`.
> (b) In lsp/workspace_config.rs::resolve. Keep the raw `Vec<IgnoreErrorEntry>`
> in `ResolvedWorkspaceConfig`, because it derives PartialEq for
> reload_configuration's no-op fast path and `Regex` isn't PartialEq. Store the
> compiled set on the Server next to it (lsp.rs:223), and eprintln the warnings
> the same way other resolve failures already degrade.
>
> `filter` (line 134) and the LSP call at lsp.rs:410 take
> `&CompiledIgnoreErrors`.
>
> Accept `paths = [..]` as well as `path` (`#[serde(default)]`, OR semantics).
> Keep `glob_matches` as it is: its `*`-crosses-`/` fnmatch semantics are shared
> with restricted_symbols.rs:488/496 and checker/restricted_symbol_usage.rs.
> Don't bring in globset. If `?` is wanted, add it to the hand matcher for all
> three users at once.
>
> Leave count enforcement and unmatched-entry reporting out of this change, or
> make them a separate opt-in item. The key the proposal names
> (`report_unmatched_ignored_errors`) doesn't exist; the only related flag is
> `options.report_unmatched_ignores` for inline ignores (session.rs:200). The
> doc comment at ignore_errors.rs:43-55 still holds: entries for unimplemented
> identifiers would show up as permanent noise.

#### K7. Compact, zero-copy token representation with a single-pass token vector

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Measured gap on a synthetic 7.1MB file of 40k small functions:
  phpstan-rs `check` (lex+parse only) took 7.55s with a 602MB peak, while
  `mago lint -s` (parse and semantic checks) took 0.62s. perf attributes about
  35-40% of phpstan-rs parse time to malloc/realloc/mprotect, 8-12% to
  `Parser::new` and about 5-8% to `Lexer::run`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs:279`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/stream.rs:275`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:14`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:248`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:95`, `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:51`,
  `crates/syntax/src/token.rs:117`
- **Risks:** `Token` is matched in about 170 places (the keyword_raw comment at
  parser.rs:30-36) and is also used by lsp/completion.rs, output/codeframe.rs,
  stub_attributes.rs and the phpdoc crate's type lexer
  (phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:42). They need an adapter or migration. The fuzz
  target `token_stream_parse` builds `Token` values through `arbitrary`, so the
  harness must change too. Interpolated strings need a sub-token representation
  or lazy re-lexing of their byte range.
- **Verification:** One risk citation is wrong.
  crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:42 calls the phpdoc crate's own lexer
  (`use super::lexer::{Lexer, PhpDocToken}` at line 5), not the syntax crate's
  `Token`, so the phpdoc type lexer would not need migrating.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this in steps and measure each step with
> crates/syntax/benches/lex_parse.rs, plus a new bench that includes Parser::new
> and parse_program. Don't rewrite Token wholesale.
>
> (1) Have the lexer write doc comments straight into a side table: a Vec of
> (next-token index, Arc\<str>, start Position). It should also collect
> code_line_starts and the plain comments in the same pass. Then Parser::new
> (crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:95-140) stops copying every token into
> filtered/filtered_spans/filtered_keyword_raw, and stops building four
> FxHashMaps. The four maps become one sorted Vec (or one map) of per-token
> DocInfo. The re-walk in parse.rs:51-68, and its String copy of each doc
> comment at line 55, go away too: keep Comment.text as Arc\<str>.
>
> (2) Replace keyword_raw: Vec\<Option\<String>> (lexer.rs:384-388,
> parser.rs:37) with a byte offset/length per token. Keep src alive in the
> Parser, so take_name_segment slices the raw spelling instead of allocating.
>
> (3) Store per-token byte offsets rather than line/col, and resolve Spans
> lazily through a line-start table. Right now Lexer::run computes two
> line_col_at results for every token (lexer.rs:252-255): a binary search plus
> UTF-8 column counting, each time. Keep the public Span as it is at AST
> boundaries, so nothing outside the syntax crate changes.
>
> (4) Replace Keyword::try_from_bytes (token.rs:117+) with a table that
> dispatches on length and first byte. Compare case-insensitively with
> eq_ignore_ascii_case, and drop the from_utf8.
>
> Only after those, and only if profiling still points at token payloads, move
> StringLit/InterpString decoding from the lexer into the parser. Tackle the
> dominant malloc share separately, as its own idea: AST node allocation
> (Box\<Expr> everywhere in ast.rs), and stub startup, which a precompiled or
> cached stub index serves better than faster parsing. Don't count on either
> being fixed by this token work.

#### K51. Precompute descendant indexes, transitive ancestor sets and unresolvable-ancestor flags

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Removes O(classes)-per-call scans from checker hot paths (escape
  analysis runs per receiver type, trait checks per trait). Checking scales with
  project size plus stubs instead of project size × stub count. It also
  underpins targeted incremental invalidation, since descendants give the dirty
  set.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:287`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/merge.rs:118`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:780`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:142`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1322`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/native_type_hints.rs:170`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:655`
- **Risks:** More memory per class (descendant sets for widely used interfaces
  such as Traversable can be large). Store descendants only for non-built-in
  roots, or compute them lazily with OnceLock. Must be kept in sync by the
  incremental path.
- **Verification:** Mago: the citations are accurate. populator/mod.rs:286-300
  builds direct_classlike_descendants and all_classlike_descendants from
  all_parent_interfaces and all_parent_classes, but only when
  `!incremental || !class_likes_to_repopulate.is_empty()`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Extend the existing settle-point pass instead of adding a new one.
> `Registry::precompute_ancestor_names`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:67) already rebuilds
> `ancestor_names` from scratch in parallel. Add these alongside it: (1)
> `ancestors_with_uses: NameTable<Arc<FxHashSet<Name>>>`, the transitive closure
> over extends, implements and uses. `all_ancestor_names` (hierarchy.rs:112)
> then returns this cached set instead of running a new DFS. It has about 12
> call sites, including the type-relation path registry/relation.rs:30, which
> feeds types/src/relation/super_type.rs:382, plus resolve.rs:852/1644,
> unused.rs:91 and oop.rs:1810. (2) A per-class `hierarchy_fully_known` bool,
> meaning no ancestor is missing, computed once from (1). Use it to answer
> `has_unresolvable_ancestor` (hierarchy.rs:655), the `hierarchy_known` closure
> in super_type.rs:380-388 (add a `HierarchyFacts` trait method in
> types/src/hierarchy.rs), and `is_fully_known_class_type`
> (resolve.rs:1636-1646). (3) A reverse index
> `trait_hosts: NameTable<Vec<Name>>`, final non-trait hosts only, built by one
> pass over `uses`. This replaces the O(classes)-per-level scan in
> `classes_using_trait` (hierarchy.rs:142), which is used by
> checker/function_decl.rs:32 and checker/function_like_declarations.rs:220. (4)
> Build the concrete-descendant index lazily with a OnceLock, or only when
> `collect_member_refs` is on. This avoids storing large descendant sets for
> Traversable or Countable on every run. `escape_targets_for_class`
> (checker.rs:1309-1340) and the subclass scan in
> checker/native_type_hints.rs:170 then use it. Leave `class_is_immutable`,
> `find_final_ancestor_*`, `required_abstract_methods` and
> `has_concrete_implementation` as they are. Their walks follow short extends
> chains and run once per declaration, so a precomputed map would add memory for
