> (project.rs:775, project.rs:1048, registry.rs:299, and the test helpers), so
> incremental sync is handled already.

#### K57. Load phpstan-src stubs lazily through index.tsv

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: stubs-prelude)
- **Benefit:** Projects that don't write PHPStan extensions skip up to 42% of
  stub parsing work and the matching memory, which is most general PHP code in
  scoped runs. The index gains a real runtime consumer, as C5 anticipates.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/src/lib.rs:1`,
  `docs/content/en/guide/configuration.md:187`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:974`,
  `crates/stub-sources/index.tsv:1`
- **Risks:** Projects with PHPStan extensions in vendor (larastan and similar)
  still trigger the full load in composer runs, so the win is conditional. The
  finer closure step must not miss names only reachable through PHPDoc
  (templates, @mixin); fall back to the full layer on any unresolved PHPStan\\*
  lookup.
- **Verification:** These are small corrections. index.tsv has no separate `s:`
  rows. Each row starts with a kind column (class, function and so on), and `s:`
  is a prefix inside the declarations column (column 5). Exactly 1962 rows have
  an `s:` declaration, so the count is right.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split `generated_stub_data()`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:953-1027) into two LazyLocks: a
> builtin layer (PHPSTORM_STUBS_SOURCES plus the patches that touch builtins,
> including patch_phpstan_stub_classes for builtin classes) and a phpstan layer
> (PHPSTAN_SRC_SOURCES, Origin::Phpstan, merged with first-occurrence-wins
> against the builtin layer's seen sets, as the current single pass does).
> `Project::new` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:346-350) merges only the
> builtin layer. Add `Project::ensure_phpstan_layer()`. It runs once, before
> registry flattening/checking in check-project, and in the LSP on any
> `update_file`. It fires when any loaded file (analysed, context or vendor)
> contains the bytes `phpstan\` (ASCII case-insensitive memmem on the raw
> source). That catches docblock-only, string and `use` references with no
> name-resolution plumbing, and over-approximating is harmless. When it fires,
> it calls `merge_stubs`/`merge_stub_classes` for the phpstan layer.
> `merge_stub_classes` (registry/index.rs:506) already merges a class that was
> indexed first, so late merging is safe. After a late merge in the LSP, the
> whole project is rechecked once, because class existence changed. The
> index.tsv per-name closure is not worth building: PHPDoc, @mixin, templates
> and strings make it fragile, and the coarse gate already gets the win. Keep
> the full-load path for tests (generated_stub_coverage.rs,
> tests/stub_index.rs).

#### K254. Bound nested-loop convergence cost

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** Nested loops over growing array shapes go from exponential to
  roughly linear in depth. Option A costs no precision.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/settings.rs:17`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:599`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:328`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt/loops.rs:103`
- **Risks:** Memo keys must include everything that affects the pass: class
  context, by-ref and static vars, and loop_break_states. Option B trades
  precision on deep nests.
- **Verification:** Mago: the `while i <= assignment_depth` loop is at
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:598, not 599. The limit is not a
  flat cap.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep MAX_PASSES and WIDEN_FROM_PASS for a single loop, and cut the
> multiplication across nesting levels in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs converge_loop_body (line 302),
> in two parts.
>
> (1) Warm start instead of exact memoization. Add a map on Checker, keyed by
> the loop statement's span, that holds the last converged pass_entry for that
> loop. It is set when converge_loop_body returns and cleared when the enclosing
> function body finishes. When an inner loop is reached again on a later outer
> pass, it starts from merge_scopes(entry, cached_fixpoint) rather than from
> entry. The outer loop's entries only grow from pass to pass, because each is
> merged with the previous one, so the previous inner fixed point is contained
> in the new one. Warm starting therefore loses no precision, and the inner loop
> usually converges in 1 or 2 passes instead of up to 6. The zero_iterations and
> subject_exempt handling (around line 400) must still use the real entry, not
> the warm-started one. That handling is where the "may run zero times" union
> happens.
>
> (2) A per-function pass budget on Checker, as a backstop. Count total run_pass
> invocations. Past a threshold (for example a few hundred), every
> still-changing variable is widened from pass 0 and each loop is capped at 2
> passes. This mirrors Mago's DEFAULT_LOOP_ASSIGNMENT_DEPTH_THRESHOLD cap
> (crates/analyzer/src/settings.rs:17,
> crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:599), but it only applies once the
> budget is gone, so normal code keeps full precision.
>
> Leave out Option A (exact memo on Locals equality): each outer pass reaches
> the inner loop with a different whole-scope Locals, which is why the outer
> loop re-runs at all, so the memo would almost never hit. Replaying cached
> diagnostics and pass_mark side effects would also be fragile. Option C (making
> the constants configurable) is low value.

#### K307. Profile-guided optimization for native release legs

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** Faster check-project and LSP analysis at no source-code cost. PGO
  usually gives double-digit speedups on branchy interpreter- and
  analyzer-shaped Rust code.
- **Mago evidence:** `.github/workflows/cd.yml:320`,
  `.github/workflows/cd.yml:298`
- **phpstan-rs:** `Cargo.toml:43`, `.github/workflows/release.yml:100`
- **Risks:** Longer release builds. The profile has to come from a
  representative, general corpus or it biases toward one codebase. Cross legs
  cannot easily run the instrumented binary. It depends on llvm-tools for the
  pinned nightly.
- **Verification:** Mago: the PGO commands are at
  .github/workflows/cd.yml:321-330 (the `build` step; `cargo pgo build` at 324,
  `cargo pgo run -- -- --workspace corpus/ analyze --reporting-format count || true`
  at 325, `cargo pgo optimize build` at 326), not exactly at line 320.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Measure first, then add it to CI. (1) Add a local script under scripts/ (for
> example scripts/pgo-build.sh) that installs the llvm-tools-preview component
> for the pinned nightly in rust-toolchain.toml and builds with
> RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate=\<dir>". It then runs the instrumented binary
> with `check-project --no-composer` over inputs that are already in the repo:
> vendor/phpstan-src (a large general-purpose PHP codebase, and release.yml:~62
> already fetches it), the fixtures crate's PHP files, and one short LSP session
> replay if one exists. The script merges the output with llvm-profdata and
> rebuilds with -Cprofile-use=\<merged>.profdata -Cllvm-args=-pgo-warn-mismatch.
> Compare the result against the current thin-LTO/cgu=1 release profile
> (Cargo.toml:43-45) on wall time for check-project and for the one-line-file
> startup, which is dominated by parsing the stubs in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs. Use at least 2 codebases that were
> not in the training set, so the measured gain isn't just overfitting. (2) If
> the gain is at least 5% on the held-out codebases, add a matrix.native-gated
> branch to the Build step in .github/workflows/release.yml (currently a plain
> `cargo build --release --locked`, around line 100) that runs the same script.
> Cross legs keep the plain build. Mago uses a composer-installed corpus (mago
> .github/workflows/cd.yml:298-326); using vendor/phpstan-src instead avoids the
> PHP/Composer setup and the network fetch. (3) Consider BOLT only after that,
> on Linux only.

#### K10. memchr-accelerated scanning for inline HTML, comments and string bodies

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** This is the cheapest part of closing the throughput gap. Doc
  comments, templates and string literals are the long byte runs in real PHP
  (stubs are mostly docblocks). It is independent of the larger
  token-representation refactor.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:272`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:1924`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs:1742`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:427`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:530`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer/strings.rs:171`
- **Risks:** Minimal. Keep the existing semantics exactly (`/**/` is not a doc
  comment, lexer.rs:526; `?>` ends `#`/`//` comments). The existing lexer tests
  cover these.
- **Verification:** Mago (crates/syntax/src/lexer/mod.rs): the memchr2/memmem
  imports are at lines 8-9. `memmem::find(bytes, b"<?")` is at 232 and
  `memmem::find_iter(bytes, b"<?")` at 272. `read_literal_string` calls
  `memchr2(quote, b'\\', ...)` at 1751 (the claim said 1742, which is the
  function's start area).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `memchr = "2"` to crates/syntax/Cargo.toml. It is already in Cargo.lock at
> 2.8.3, so the dependency graph does not grow. Then replace the four
> byte-at-a-time loops, keeping their current semantics exactly: (1)
> `lex_doc_comment` (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:681-691) and the `/*` arm of
> `skip_whitespace_and_comments` (lexer.rs:527-535): use
> `memchr::memmem::find(&self.src[self.pos..], b"*/")`, and fall back to
> src.len() when nothing is found. The existing `(pos+2).min(len)` clamp stays.
> (2) The `#` and `//` comment loops (lexer.rs:490-497 and 502-510): use
> `memchr2(b'\n', b'?', rest)` and loop until the byte is `\n` or it is `?`
> followed by `>`. Do not add `\r` as Mago does: phpstan-rs stops only at `\n`
> today, so changing that would alter behavior and needs its own runtime check
> with `php -r` first. (3) `lex_inline_html` (lexer.rs:427-433): use
> `memmem::find_iter(rest, b"<?")`, and at each hit test
> `eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"<?php")` or `<?=`. (4) `lex_single_quoted`
> (crates/syntax/src/lexer/strings.rs:171-181): use
> `memchr2(b'\'', b'\\', rest)` to jump between candidates, keeping the
> run_start/extend logic. The same memchr2/memchr3 jump could also be applied to
> the literal-run scanning in `lex_interpolated_run` and to the heredoc/nowdoc
> body scanning. Measure before and after with the existing criterion bench
> (crates/syntax/benches/lex_parse.rs). Add a case to it that is heavy on stub
> docblocks, then check the result against the ~0.95s one-line-file startup. The
> existing lexer tests cover the `/**/` rule, `?>` ending comments, and `<?=`.

#### K32. Allocation-free case-insensitive NameTable lookups

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** This removes one heap allocation and free per case-insensitive
  lookup on the hottest registry paths: lookup_class (59 sites), classes.get
  (154), is_subclass_of (70, three lookups each), lookup_method (50) and
  lookup_method_with_owner (55). Nearly all real class FQNs contain uppercase,
  so today almost every lookup allocates. Expect a measurable share of
  registry-bound check time;
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/word/src/util.rs:265`,
  `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:438`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_table.rs:12`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_table.rs:66`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:22`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_table.rs:38`
- **Risks:** Hash consistency between the stored Folded and the lookup path must
  be exact, so add a unit test that inserts `Foo\\Bar` and looks up `FOO\\bar`
  through every API. There is no behavior change otherwise.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/word/src/util.rs:264-282 ascii_lowercase_word
  (STACK_BUF_SIZE=256 at util.rs:41); the stack buffer is then handed to
  Word::new (word.rs:86), which interns into a global sharded interner.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Two changes, both in crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_table.rs, done in
> this order.
>
> (1) Add Name-keyed lookups first, since they are nearly free. Add
> `get_by_name(&Name)` and `get_with_name_by_name(&Name)`. Both call
> `self.entries.get(name.lower())`. `Name::lower()` is cached
> (crates/syntax/src/name.rs:24-50), and `Folded: Borrow<str>` already returns
> `lower()` (name_table.rs:44-48), so hash and eq match without any folding.
> Switch the callers that already hold a `Name` owner:
>
> - `self.classes.get(&current)` in `class_extends_implements_closure`
>   (hierarchy.rs ~46)
> - `self.classes.get(owner)` in `lookup_method` (hierarchy.rs:380 and 392)
> - the same pattern in `lookup_method_with_owner` and the other owner-map
>   walks.
>
> (2) Make the `&str` path allocation-free. Add a private
> `with_folded(name, |key: &str| ...)` helper:
>
> - Fast path: if no byte is ASCII uppercase, borrow `name` unchanged. This
>   matches the current `function_key`.
> - Otherwise, if `name.len() <= 256`, copy it into a `[u8; 256]` stack buffer
>   with `make_ascii_lowercase`. Rebuild the `&str` with `std::str::from_utf8`
>   (or the unchecked version, since ASCII folding keeps UTF-8 valid).
> - Only longer names fall back to `to_ascii_lowercase()`.
>
> Route `get`, `get_with_name`, `get_mut`, `contains_key` and `remove` through
> this helper. The key passed to the map is a whole `&str`, so `Hash for str`
> produces the same bytes plus the `0xff` terminator that `Folded` hashes. No
> hashbrown or `Equivalent` switch is needed. Leave `function_key` and
> `folded_key` as they are for their 17 non-table callers.
>
> Tests: add a unit test in name_table.rs. Insert `Foo\Bar`, then look it up as
> `FOO\bar` through every API, including the new `by_name` variants. Also cover
> a name longer than 256 bytes.
>
> Measurement: before and after, use the existing `hotpath-alloc` feature
> (crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:37) to count allocations, and time a wall-clock
> run. Keep the change only if it measurably cuts allocations and time. Expect a
> low-single-digit percent at most.

#### K40. Single topological-order inheritance pass replacing fixed-point passes, with cycle reporting

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: codebase-model)
- **Benefit:** Removes the repeated whole-registry passes (each pass currently
  re-reads, and for traits re-clones, everything). Chains of trait-in-trait or
  undocumented overrides become linear rather than depth × N. The cycle
  diagnostics catch real fatal errors: `php` reports 'Class "P2" not found' for
  mutually extending classes, and likewise for interface and trait cycles
  (checked with php -r).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/sorter.rs:6`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:122`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:107`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:351`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:372`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:103`
- **Risks:** Parallelising per level is more complex than today's rayon over all
  classes. Mixins and type imports add edges that can form legal cycles (mutual
  @mixin), so those edges must be soft: order them if possible and ignore them
  in cycle reports.
- **Verification:** Mago: sorter.rs:6 sort_class_likes is correct. The
  `visiting` check that breaks cycles is at lines 47-49. The DFS follows
  direct_parent_class (54), used_traits (61), direct_parent_interfaces (67),
  require_extends (74), require_implements (80) and imported_type_aliases
  sources (86), then pushes the c ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the idea in two and drop most of the performance half.
>
> (1) Do NOT add registry/topo.rs or rewrite flatten_traits,
> flatten_phpdoc_inheritance and inherit_property_hooks around a topological
> order now. The crate-split plan's C4 already replaces these passes, and the
> other copy-down passes, with lazily memoized per-class resolution levels
> (ancestors, own, inherited, members, final), each a per-class OnceLock that
> reads only its ancestors' finished levels. See CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:370-380 and
> 2291-2300, and CRATE_SPLIT_EVIDENCE.md:1128-1133. Demand-driven memoization
> gives dependency order without a global sort or per-level parallel scheduling.
> It also fits incremental snapshots better than re-sorting the whole registry
> on each update_file. A topo pass would be built only to be deleted in C4. If a
> cheap interim win is wanted before C4, the smallest one is this: in
> flatten_traits_one_pass (resolve.rs:128-290), skip classes whose used traits
> did not change in the previous pass (a dirty set), so passes 2 and later stop
> re-cloning every trait's methods, properties and consts only to have them
> thrown away by the vacant-only insert.
>
> (2) Keep the cycle diagnostic, which is the part that adds something. Add one
> function, e.g. registry::hierarchy::inheritance_cycles(&Registry) ->
> Vec\<Vec\<Name>>. It runs a Tarjan SCC over hard edges only (extends,
> implements, uses; a self-loop counts). @mixin and @phpstan-import-type edges
> are left out. Report it as a declaration-level rule next to the existing
> extends checks in checker/oop.rs (~lines 85-110, class.extendsInterface /
> class.extendsFinal), or as a whole-program pass like
> project/whole_program/circular_namespace_deps.rs:50. Report each class in the
> cycle at its own declaration, e.g. "Class A extends itself through B" / "Trait
> T uses itself through U" / "Interface I extends itself", with identifiers such
> as class.inheritanceCycle, trait.useCycle and interface.extendsCycle. C4's
> ancestor level should later reuse the same SCC set for its specified 'drop
> every edge inside the cycle' step, so one function gives both the break and
> the report.

#### K112. Cheaper scope joins with ptr_eq fast path

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Every if, switch, try and loop pass joins through merge_scopes.
  Keeping structure shared and version-stable avoids re-inferring expressions
  after every join and cuts allocation in large functions. It can be verified
  with the existing hotpath measure on merge_scopes (control_flow.rs:472).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:62`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:298`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:340`
- **Risks:** Version reuse must be exact: only keep the version when the result
  is truly identical to one input. The equality change is purely internal.
- **Verification:** (a) The benefit line says the hotpath measure sits on
  merge_scopes at control_flow.rs:472. That is wrong. The `#[hotpath::measure]`
  at crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:472 comes right before
  add_implied_fact's doc comment, so it attaches to add_implied_fact (line 476),
  and merge_scopes ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Measure before building, then land it inside the planned merge_scopes rewrite.
> There are three parts.
>
> (a) Locals::eq (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:340). Replace the imbl
> `==` with
> `self.types.ptr_eq(&other.types) || (self.types.len() == other.types.len() &&
> self.types.iter().all(|(k, v)| other.types.get(k) == Some(v)))`.
> imbl's test_eq (imbl-7.0.1 src/hash/map.rs:484-504) builds a std SipHash
> HashSet of seen keys. With equal lengths and unique keys, that set adds
> nothing. Type::eq is already Arc::ptr_eq first
> (crates/types/src/lib.rs:343-348), so the new loop is only lookups. This part
> is about 10 lines and has no risk.
>
> (b) merge_scopes (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563-757).
> Start the `types`/`provenance`/`native` maps from then_locals' maps instead of
> fresh_scope(). If `then.types.ptr_eq(&else.types)` and the side maps are also
> ptr_eq, return then_locals.clone() unchanged, keeping its version (this is
> where the earlier guard/alias maps come in). Otherwise walk the keys. Remove a
> key the else side lacks. Leave a key alone when `then_ty == else_ty` and its
> provenance is identical. Insert the union only for keys that differ. This
> keeps unchanged imbl subtrees shared and avoids re-cloning every String key
> and ProvenanceSet (lines 737-752 clone both for every variable today). The
> guard-set intersections and alias filters can use the same ptr_eq shortcut.
>
> (c) Optional: a per-fork written-keys set, like Mago's assigned_variable_ids
> (mago crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:62,298), so a join visits only the
> keys written in either branch. This is only worth doing if (a) and (b) show
> merge_scopes is still hot.
>
> Sequencing: STAGE_B_FIX_REVIEW.md:40-50 already plans to replace Locals'
> separate side maps with one ExpressionHolder per key and to define
> merge_scopes once over holders. F5 (lines 275-295) also changes merge_scopes
> to keep one-sided variables as Maybe instead of dropping them. Write (b) into
> that rewrite, not into the current function. Before starting, profile a
> large-function PHP file under the existing #[hotpath::measure] on merge_scopes
> to confirm it is a real share of the time.

#### K206. Run all parallel phases on one worker pool

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Halves the thread count (2N plus the main thread becomes N plus
  the main thread). Registry passes and body walks get the 64 MiB stack instead
  of the default 2 MiB. Any thread-count setting (next idea) then covers every
  phase. Cross-pool futex and sched_yield traffic goes away;
  GATE_SPEED_PLAN.md:487 measured idle pool spinning at about 48% of fixture
  samples.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/main.rs:261`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:611`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:671`, `GATE_SPEED_PLAN.md:220`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:215`
- **Risks:** The stub LazyLock is process-global. If the LSP ever touches it
  from a thread outside the pool, it would run inline on that thread, so
  initialise it via pool.install at startup. No output change.
- **Verification:** Every citation checks out, with a few details to adjust: (a)
  Mago's single pool is built at mago/src/main.rs:260-264 (ThreadPoolBuilder
  with num_threads, stack_size, then build_global). Mago does not name its
  threads, so the thread_name suggestion is new and does not come from Mago.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs `Session::load` (lines 593-685),
> wrap everything from `Project::new()` (line 611) through
> `project.finish_loading()` (line 671) in a single `self.pool.install(|| ...)`.
> That covers the parse par_iter already in install at line 625, plus the stub
> LazyLock index par_iter (registry/stubs.rs:981-984), the hierarchy passes
> (registry/hierarchy.rs:71, 287, 303, 328), purity inference
> (registry/purity.rs:105, 123) and resolve (registry/resolve.rs:66, 142, 314,
> 973). In the LSP, run `self.project.finish_loading()` (lsp.rs:577,

#### K213. Parallelise infer_global_variables per file

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** This serial whole-program walk becomes parallel at load, and in
  the LSP each edit's cost drops from walking every file to walking one file
  plus a merge.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:227`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/global_vars.rs:182`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:783`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1058`
- **Risks:** WalkOutput borrows the AST (lifetime 'a). Caching it needs an owned
  form, which is more work. Merge order must stay identical to keep union member
  order deterministic.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:227-260 is
  the `source_files.into_par_iter().map_init(LocalArena::new, ...)` scan into
  per-file (CodebaseMetadata, capture) partials. Lines 264-300 merge them
  serially, in the order of the collected Vec: `for (partial, captured) in
  compiled { ...
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do the parallel half and leave out the per-file cache as proposed.
>
> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/global_vars.rs `infer_global_variables`
>    (174-205), replace the serial
>    `for (path, stmts) in files { walk_top_level(...) }` loop (182-185) with
>    `files.par_iter().map(|(path, stmts)| { let mut out =
>    WalkOutput::default(); walk_top_level(stmts, &FileCtx{registry, path}, &mut
>    out); out }).collect::<Vec<_>>()`.
>    Then concatenate `sites` and `include_sites` in `files` order. This keeps
>    the site order that `Type::union` sees in `GlobalAccumulator`, so the
>    output stays deterministic. Everything after that stays serial:
>    `resolve_global_scope_files` and the accumulator fold. This follows the
>    existing pattern in registry/hierarchy.rs:66-78
>    (`precompute_ancestor_names`: reborrow `&Registry`, par_iter, then assign
>    serially). Add `#[hotpath::measure]` so the gain can be measured.
>
> 2. If a per-file cache is wanted for the LSP, cache only the
>    registry-independent syntactic output: variable names, keys, gate, include
>    targets, and a way to find each RHS expression (for example, a stmt/expr
>    path into the file's own AST in FileState). Re-resolve every RHS against
>    the registry on every update. Do not cache resolved
>    `StagedSite.contribution` values. `resolve_static_expr_type`
>    (global_vars.rs:615-669) reads `registry.resolve_function`, `lookup_method`
>    and `lookup_const`, so a cached resolved site in file A goes stale when
>    file B changes a return type, method or class constant.

#### K215. Skip final Project teardown in the CLI

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Avoids a single-threaded free of a heap the size of the peak
  (about 1.6 GB on the corpus) at process end. That is pure wall time after the
  report prints, and it delays the exit that CI waits on.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:368`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:150`,
  `GATE_SPEED_PLAN.md:487`
- **Risks:** Must run after all output is flushed (BufWriter). dhat and hotpath
  profiling builds need the drop for their reports, so gate on those features.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate, with some caveats. Mago's
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:368 is `arena.reset();` inside the
  per-file `map_init(LocalArena::new, ...)` analyze closure. The same pattern
  also appears at lines 254, 498 and 605. It frees per-file scratch memory.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs, at the end of
> run_check_project_command, right after the `report(&run, &analysis, ...)` call
> (around line 150), add:
>
>     // The process is about to exit; the OS reclaims the heap faster than a drop walk.
>     #[cfg(not(feature = "dhat-heap"))]
>     {
>         std::mem::forget(analysis);
>         std::mem::forget(run);
>     }
>
> Use mem::forget rather than process::exit so main still returns normally. That
> keeps the #[hotpath::main] guard and std's stdout flush exactly as they are
> today. Leave the library (Project, CheckSession), the LSP, the tests and
> incremental-bench alone. Before adopting it, measure it once: time
> check-project on a vendor-heavy project with and without the forget (or perf
> the tail after the summary line), and keep it only if it saves a measurable
> amount.

#### K70. Stop interning throwaway probe types in type queries; add direct-repr fast paths

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Cuts global-mutex acquisitions and allocations from the most
  frequently called type queries in rules and narrowing. It is cheap and has no
  semantic change.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs:794`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/queries.rs:717`,
  `crates/types/src/queries.rs:643`, `crates/types/src/intern.rs:96`
- **Risks:** The fast paths must agree exactly with the relation's answers for
  intersections, templates and mixed~T. Keep the relation fallback for
  everything but trivially decidable reprs, and back it with property tests
  (tests/subtyping_properties.rs already exists).
- **Verification:** Mago: is_resource is at crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs:791,
  is_array at 795 and is_list at 799, not 794. Each one is
  `types.iter().all(TAtomic::…) && !self.types.is_empty()` and returns bool, not
  a trinary.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the proposal into a zero-risk half, worth doing, and a risky half, worth
> dropping or deferring until a profile justifies it.
>
> (1) Do this: cache the probe types in crates/types/src/queries.rs. Add private
> `static LazyLock<Type>` values, or one `OnceLock<[Type; N]>`:
>
> - ANY_ARRAY for the `Type::array(Mixed(false,None), Mixed(false,None))` built
>   in is_array (queries.rs:716-721)
> - ANY_LIST for `Type::list_of(Type::mixed())` in is_list (746-748)
> - SCALAR for the four-member Union in is_scalar (736-743)
> - NON_EMPTY_ARRAY for the Intersection in is_non_empty_array (751-759)
> - EMPTY_ARRAY for `array_shape(Shape::sealed(vec![]))` in is_empty_array
>   (762-764)
> - REFINED_STRING, indexed by AccessoryKind, for the
>   `Intersection([String, Accessory(kind)])` built in is_refined_string
>   (643-648)
>
> is_within (593-598) then takes `&*ANY_ARRAY` and so on. A static holds a
> strong Arc, so the table's Weak entry never dies and the node is interned only
> once. Equality and ptr identity are unchanged, so behaviour cannot change.
>
> Use statics here rather than widening intern::constant (intern.rs:50-94).
> constant() is matched on every intern() call, and adding composite patterns
> there would slow every construction.
>
> (2) Don't do this without profiling: the repr-level fast paths ahead of the
> relation. Relation::is_super_type_of (relation/super_type.rs:38-68) already
> starts with a cheap repr match: `sup == sub` is a ptr/hash compare, and there
> are early arms for mixed, never and Error. That leaves little to save.
> Meanwhile a second decision procedure for Intersection, Union, template,
> mixed~T, generic-list and accessory cases could drift from the relation.
>
> If you add any, limit them to reprs that are trivially decidable and never
> nested:
>
> - a Repr::Array or ArrayShape receiver answering is_array
> - a bare Int, Float, Bool, Null or String receiver answering No for the array
>   and list predicates
>
> Leave Union and Intersection to the relation, and cover each fast path in
> tests/subtyping_properties.rs with an equivalence property (fast answer ==
> relation answer).
>
> Verification: run `cargo test -p types`, and do an optional
> `--features hotpath` measurement before and after on a representative project
> to see whether the saved interning is even visible.

#### K86. Precompute each class's flattened ancestor template map

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Constant-time generic ancestor resolution on the hot relation
  path (every `Collection<User>` accepts check and every generic method call).
  Deep generic hierarchies (Doctrine Collections, Symfony Form, PhpParser node
  visitors) gain the most. It also creates one place to record diamond paths for
  interfaceConflict.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/populator/templates.rs:14`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/mod.rs:1585`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/generics.rs:81`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/relation.rs:90`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/generics/substitution.rs:78`
- **Risks:** Incremental LSP updates must invalidate the dependents' maps.
  Memory grows with the number of (class, ancestor) pairs, though only generic
  ancestors need entries.
- **Verification:** Mago: get_specialized_template_type begins at
  crates/codex/src/ttype/mod.rs:1548, not 1585. Line ~1585 is inside it, where
  it loops over the precomputed
  instantiated_class_metadata.template_extended_parameters.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build new machinery. Keep the per-class map that already exists.
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:850
> `ancestor_bindings(class_name, info)` already computes
> `{templated ancestor => class_template_bindings(class, own_template_args, ancestor)}`,
> with the class's own templates left as scoped TemplateParams
> (own_template_args is at resolve.rs:1474). Today it is only memoized in a
> transient `FxHashMap<Name, OnceLock<AncestorBindings>>` for the length of
> flatten_phpdoc_inheritance (resolve.rs:352-362, plan item S13 in
> GATE_SPEED_PLAN.md:496), then thrown away. The change: (1) After the fixed
> point, move those OnceLocks into an
> `ancestor_bindings: OnceLock<AncestorBindings>` field on ClassReflection
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs), or fill the field lazily on
> first query. (2) In Registry::class_template_bindings
> (registry/generics.rs:60), when class != target, look up the cached entry for
> target. If it exists, return its values with `substitute_templates` applied,
> using the zipped own bindings (templates zipped with type_args). If not,
> return an empty map, or fall back to the recursive walk when the cache is
> unset. (3) Every existing caller benefits with no change: relation.rs:90,
> checker/generics/substitution.rs:78/140/186, member_resolution.rs:367,
> property_assignment.rs:101, loops.rs:498/522 and generators.rs:60/119. (4)
> Invalidation: clear the field wherever the registry re-runs
> finish_loading/flatten for changed classes and their dependents. Leaving it
> unset falls back to the walk, so a missed invalidation costs speed, not
> correctness, as long as the field is cleared when any ancestor's declaration
> changes. Before merging, add a debug_assert or test that compares cached and
> walked results on the generics_and_templates fixtures, because
> substitute-then-substitute has to equal the one-pass walk. Missing args are
> the case to watch: a template with no argument must still come out as Mixed
> and not stay a TemplateParam. Optional extra from the Mago evidence: record
> every path during the precompute rather than stopping at the first DFS match,
> and use that for interface-conflict diagnostics. That is a separate feature
> and should be judged separately.

#### K240. Parse each docblock once and share it

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Cuts redundant parsing on the startup path (the stubs contribute
  many docblocks) and on every LSP re-check of a file. It also gives one place

  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:33`,

- **Refined proposal:**

> Skip the shared cache and remove the duplicate parses where they happen. (1)
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/class_info.rs:1077-1110: build the
> `final_properties_by_phpdoc` set inside the properties map, which already
> computes `doc_ty = p.doc_comment.as_deref().map(docblock::parse)` at :1110,

> docblock then gets parsed once instead of twice. (2)
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:726-770: in
> check_unknown_phpstan_tags_on, call `docblock::parse(doc)` once and pass the
> `&DocBlock` to report_invalid_doc_tag_values and check_doc_see_tag_targets. If

> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:33-34 and
> phpdoc_unresolvable::tag_type_nodes: let tag_type_nodes take an already-parsed

#### K33. Precomputed hash in Name and one interner per process

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Every `FxHashMap<Name, _>`/`FxHashSet<Name>` operation
  (ancestor_names, member-owner maps, function_decl_sites, …) and every type
  hash stops re-hashing string bytes. Equality between project and registry
  names hits the ptr_eq fast path. The shard-mutex traffic from the 111
  Name::from sites, including the ones inside precompute_\* rayon loops, drops.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/word/src/interner.rs:462`,
  `crates/word/src/interner.rs:652`, `crates/word/src/interner.rs:654`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:130`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:67`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:353`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:328`
- **Risks:** Adds 16 bytes per NameData. The Hash value changes from str::hash
  to write_u64, so any code relying on `Borrow<str>` lookups of
  `FxHashMap<Name, _>` by `&str` (name.rs:136-140) would break the Borrow
  contract. Audit those sites and give them a Name-keyed lookup or a `str`
  hasher shim. Merging interners makes one shared table live longer; it still
  sweeps.
- **Verification:** The Mago line numbers are wrong.
  /home/torres/projects/mago/crates/word/src/interner.rs has only 304 lines, so
  :462, :652 and :654 do not exist. The real locations are: Entry header
  `hash: u64, len: u32, _pad: u32` at interner.rs:12-27;
  `static INTERNER: OnceLock<Interner>` at interner.rs:212;
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the proposal and do it in this order.
>
> (A) Cheap, safe, worth doing (S). In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:353,
> replace `interner: Arc::new(Interner::new())` with
> `Arc::clone(Interner::global())`. Keep the `Project::interner()` accessor so
> the call sites stay as they are (project.rs:653/966, project/session.rs:612).
> Then change the module doc in crates/syntax/src/name.rs:11-14 so it no longer
> says "A `Project` owns its interner". After this, AST names, stub names
> (registry/stubs.rs:729, 919) and the 118 `Name::from` sites all dedup in one
> table.
>
> (B) Measure before building anything more. Build with `--features hotpath` and
> add timing around `Interner::name`, around the lexer's interning, and around a
> representative `FxHashMap<Name,_>` hot path such as the ancestor walk in
> hierarchy.rs. Go on to C or D only if name hashing or shard locking shows up
> as a real share of the time.
>
> (C) Precomputed hash, only if B justifies it. Add `hash: u64` and
> `lower_hash: u64` to `NameData`, filled in by `text_hash` inside
> `Interner::name`, which already computes that hash and currently throws it
> away. Implement `Hash for Name` as `state.write_u64(self.0.hash)`, and
> `Hash for Folded` (registry/name_table.rs:39) as `write_u64(lower_hash)`. You
> must also remove `impl Borrow<str> for Name` (name.rs:136) and
> `impl Borrow<str> for Folded` (name_table.rs:45). In their place, add a
> `#[repr(transparent)] struct NameStr(str)` whose `Hash` is
> `write_u64(text_hash(&self.0))`, and implement `Borrow<NameStr>` for both
> types. Removing `Borrow<str>` makes every `map.get(&str)` a compile error, so
> the audit is enforced by the compiler instead of lookups silently missing.
> `NameTable::get(&str)` then wraps `function_key(name)` in `NameStr`.
>
> (D) Drop the thread-local cache. `Weak::upgrade` is atomic anyway, the shards
> are uncontended mutexes, and the cache adds invalidation complexity on top of
> the weak sweep.

  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:275`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1018`,

  already-resolved ancestors). The global passes (infer_global_variables, purity
  fixed point) need their own incremental story or must stay global. Best done
  after the own/derived split, otherwise stale baked members defeat it. | A
  fixed point over cached per-file facts must see the same inputs a full pass
  would. Invalidate a file's cached classify_body result when a function it
  calls changes resolution (a dependency on callee names), or keep purity
  per-file but resolve targets during the global fixed point. Needs differential
  tests.
- **Verification:** Mago: all the cited locations check out.
  populate_codebase_targeted is at crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:49, with
  the O(dirty) doc comment at lines 43-47. One qualification: the targeted path
  is not strictly O(dirty).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build a dirty-set variant of the current passes. CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md C4
> (about lines 2186-2360) already replaces them with lazy per-class memos. Each
> memo records a read set that includes absent names, invalidation is by
> transitive readers, and memos for stub-only classes are shared through the
> stub layer. That is Mago's safe_symbols/targeted populate with a sounder

> The one piece the plan doesn't state explicitly is caching purity and

#### K68. Single-pass n-ary union builder

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Removes quadratic dedup and repeated normalization when building
  large unions (match arms, in_array haystacks, loop and branch merges,
  generalize over unions). It also avoids k intermediate interned nodes and k
  memo entries, cutting mutex traffic and memo churn (MEMO_CAPACITY clears
  everything at 65536 entries, intern.rs:469-471).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:165`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/combination.rs:230`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/constructors.rs:167`,
  `crates/types/src/union.rs:47`
- **Risks:** Binary union currently defines member order for display (first
  stays). Keep first-occurrence order to avoid snapshot churn. Pairwise-only
  rules such as merge_has_offset_value_pair (union.rs:535) need n-ary
  equivalents or a pairwise sub-pass.
- **Verification:** Mago: `combine` starts at
  crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:164, not 165. It loops once over all
  atomics into `scrape_type_properties` (defined at :446), then sorts and dedups
  the integers and floats and finalizes the sealed arrays once.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the part of crates/types/src/union.rs union_types_impl (lines 23-222)
> that runs after flattening into a
> `fn normalize_members(members: Vec<Type>) -> Type`. It covers error/mixed,
> never, bool folding, extension widening, void/null, benevolent, literal-base
> drop, merge_int_ranges, reduce_array_members, absorb_contained_members and the
> MAX_UNION_MEMBERS cap ladder. Binary `Type::union` becomes flatten-2 plus
> normalize_members, still memoized. Then rewrite `Type::union_of`
> (crates/types/src/constructors.rs:167) as follows: (1) flatten nested Union
> members once, deduplicating in first-occurrence order with an FxHashSet\<Type>
> next to the output Vec; (2) fold the HasOffsetValue intersections pairwise
> first through merge_has_offset_value_pair (union.rs:535), since that rule is
> binary; (3) call normalize_members once; (4) intern once, with no memo for
> more than 2 members, because the pointer-tuple memo key would rarely hit.
> Leave the checker's scope merges alone: merge_scopes
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563) and the loop joins
> (control_flow.rs:434-479) are inherently binary. Before switching, add a test
> that fuzzes union_of against `reduce(Type::union)` and checks both give the
> same result, including across the 64-member cap. Profile with the existing
> hotpath feature to confirm union building is actually hot before merging.

#### K253. Linear-time &&/|| chain narrowing

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** Per-chain cost drops from O(n^2) to O(n), which matters for
  generated validators and long guard conditions. Precision is the same, since
  each operand still sees exactly the narrowing of the operands to its left.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/settings.rs:327`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:334`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5293`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:749`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:812`
- **Risks:** Every arm that pattern-matches on Binary(And, l, r) has to see the
  same semantics (the or_chain and and_chain targets and the booleanAnd.always\*
  checks), and diagnostic spans for intermediate sub-expressions must be
  preserved.
- **Verification:** Mago: the setting is the `formula_size_threshold: u16` field
  at crates/analyzer/src/settings.rs:326, with its doc comment at 320-325. Its
  purpose is to cap CNF formula blowup in nested conditionals. It does not
  flatten a linear &&/|| chain.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Low priority. If it is ever done, keep it narrow. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs infer_binary (And/LogicalAnd arm at
> ~5293, and the Or/LogicalOr arm), flatten a left-associative chain of the same
> operator into a Vec<&Expr>. Then fold it with one running narrowed Locals:
> infer operand i in the running scope, then apply_narrowing(operand_i, running,
> true/false). Mirror this only in the narrowing.rs `&&` true arm and `||` false
> arm (~749-756), which are simple sequential compositions. Leave
> or_chain_narrowing_target, and_chain_narrowing_target and check_boolean_and_or
> unchanged. Those only pattern-match, and flattening them risks changing
> semantics for no measured gain. Do not add a Mago-style ConditionIsTooComplex
> cap or diagnostic. A new diagnostic for condition size adds noise, not
> correctness.

#### K55. Resolve stub classes once and skip already-derived stub classes in per-project finishing passes

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, L (aspect: stubs-prelude, pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Less time per load and much less per language-server edit: every
  keystroke-triggered update_file currently walks roughly 3500 extra classes
  several times. This works independently of the snapshot idea and combines with
  it, since the snapshot would then contain resolved data.

  `crates/prelude/src/build.rs:36`, `crates/prelude/src/lib.rs:63`,

  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:67`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1026`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:953`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:348`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:275` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Correctness depends on detecting every stub class whose resolution
  reads a project symbol (a project class named like a stub ancestor, or a
  project-declared trait). A missed case gives stale inherited members. Needs an
  equivalence test (full resolve against stub-resolved-plus-project) over the
  fixture suite. | The version-keyed stub attributes (C5) multiply the snapshot
  count, or would need a version-independent intermediate form. Type and Name
  use process-global interners, so a decoded snapshot must re-intern on load.
- **Verification:** All citations check out, with small offsets. Mago: at
  crates/prelude/src/build.rs:34, populate_codebase runs inside
  build_prelude_internal. The safe_symbols comment and the extend calls are on

- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build this as a standalone change. Put it into the already-designed
> CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN C4 and C5 work.
>
> - C4 (CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:2105-2230) replaces the eager passes in
>   Project::finish_loading (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:745-786) and
>   update_file (around line 1017-1050) with per-class, five-level OnceLock
>   memos.
> - C5 (CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:386-402, 2511) adds a process-wide, version-keyed
>   Arc\<StubLayer>. Its copy-on-merge rule covers a stub memo whose read set

>
> Together these give the proposal's step (a), "stub classes resolved once and
> skipped per project", as a side effect. They are also lazy, so an unreached
> stub class costs nothing, where the proposal would still eagerly resolve all
> ~3,500. The only new piece worth keeping is step (b), an optional build-time
> serialized StubLayer (bincode or rkyv, re-interned on load). It should be
> evaluated only after C5 lands, and only if measured startup still matters once
> lazy resolution from the stub-sources index is in place. If adopted it needs
> an equality test against the runtime-built layer, per PHP version key. Before
> measuring it, update the startup numbers: S14 already parallelized
> generated_stub_data (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:953, par_iter at
> line 983).

#### K8. Replace the recursive-descent precedence chain with Pratt precedence climbing

- **Value/cost:** 2/10, M (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Fewer calls and far fewer moves of `Result<Expr>` per expression:
  roughly 2 frames instead of about 22 for a literal or variable. It is a
  meaningful constant-factor speedup on expression-heavy code and stubs. There
  is also a single table to audit for precedence correctness instead of 22
  functions.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs:30`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/internal/expression.rs:114`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/expr.rs:8`
- **Risks:** Precedence and associativity regressions are subtle. Guard with the
  existing parser/tests/expressions_and_operators.rs (1170 lines) plus a
  differential test against php -l, or against real PHP evaluation (`php -r`) on
  generated operator mixes. The gain should be confirmed with
  benches/lex_parse.rs before committing to the rewrite.
- **Verification:** Minor corrections only. Mago: `pub enum Precedence` begins
  at crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs:31 (the derives are at line 28). It runs
  from Lowest to Highest and includes Pipe and ErrorControl. `Precedence::infix`
  is at :295 and `postfix` at :339.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this only after a measurement shows it is worth it, and treat it as a small
> cleanup, not a performance item. Step 1 (cost S): run
> crates/syntax/benches/lex_parse.rs ("lex and parse phpstorm-stubs") and do a
> perf run on a real project. Adopt the rewrite only if the precedence-chain
> functions (parse_low_precedence_or down to parse_pow in
> crates/syntax/src/parser/expr.rs:18-577) take a meaningful share of parse
> time, not just of total time. Step 2, if it goes ahead: in parser/expr.rs, add
> `enum Prec` and `fn infix_prec(&Token) -> Option<(Prec, Assoc)>`, and replace
> parse_low_precedence_or/xor/and, parse_coalesce_inner, parse_logical_\*,
> parse_bit_\*, parse_equality, parse_relational, parse_pipe, parse_concat,
> parse_shift, parse_additive and parse_multiplicative with one
> `parse_expr_bp(min)` loop. Keep these as they are: parse_ternary (the middle
> operand), parse_not/parse_instanceof/parse_unary_inner/parse_pow as the
> operand parser, and parse_assignment_tail applied to every operand. That last
> one is how the current parser models PHP's `variable '=' expr` wherever an
> operand may stand (expr.rs:60-66), so `false === $x = f()` and `$a ?? $b = 1`
> keep parsing as they do now. Enforce non-associativity for ==/\</etc. with a
> flag in the table. Put one stack::guard per recursive parse_expr_bp call.
> Verify with parser/tests/expressions_and_operators.rs plus a generated
> differential test against `php -r` on operator mixes. The work that actually
> pays for startup is different: the Interner::name lock contention and
> allocation shown in the profile, and precompiling or caching the stubs so they
> are not reparsed on every run.

### 3.5 memory (14)

#### K12. Freeze retained AST vectors to exact-size Box<[T]> slices

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: memory-allocation)
- **Benefit:** Every argument list, statement list and array literal in every
  retained file (14k files including vendor on a real project) stops carrying up
  to 3 unused slots of 128-168 bytes each. For the dominant 1-2 element lists
  that removes 50-75% of their bytes. This reduces the retained AST, likely the
  largest single component of phpstan-rs's peak, with no algorithmic change. It
  also speeds the Drop walk slightly.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax-core/src/cst/mod.rs:15`,
  `crates/allocator/src/arena.rs:441`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/postfix.rs:260`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1424`, `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:242`
- **Risks:** Wide mechanical churn in the parser and in any checker code that
  pattern-matches `&Vec<T>` (most uses take `&[T]` and are unaffected).
  into_boxed_slice costs one realloc per list at parse time, a small CPU cost.
  The shrink_to_fit-pass variant is lower churn but keeps the 24-byte Vec
  header.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/syntax-core/src/cst/mod.rs:15-28 is accurate.
  `Sequence { nodes: &'arena [T] }` and `Sequence::new` calls `nodes.leak()`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. **Measure first.** Add a test-only or debug walker in
>    crates/syntax/src/visit that visits every AST list and sums, per element
>    type, `(capacity - len) * size_of::<T>()` and `capacity * size_of::<T>()`.
>    Also print size_of for Expr, Stmt, Arg, ArrayItem, Param and Attribute. Run
>    it once over a large project and compare the result to the 1.62GB peak. If
>    the slack is under about 3-5% of peak, keep only step 3.
> 2. **Convert the retained lists to `Box<[T]>`** in crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:
>    args, ArrayLiteral, Destructure, Isset, Echo, Unset, Global, StaticVar,
>    Block, the bodies of
>    If/ElseIf/Else/While/For/Foreach/Try/Catch/Finally/Switch cases, params,
>    uses, attrs, match arms and conditions, ClassDecl members
>    (properties/methods/consts/trait_uses/enum_cases/extends/implements), Union
>    and Intersection TypeHint, and Interpolated. Change FunctionBody.stmts from
>    `Arc<Vec<Stmt>>` to `Arc<[Stmt]>`, which also removes one pointer hop, and
>    do the same for the matching `Option<Arc<Vec<Stmt>>>` body. Keep `Vec` as
>    the building type in crates/syntax/src/parser/\*.rs and finish each list
>    with `.into_boxed_slice()` (or `Arc::from(vec)`). Where the element count
>    is known up front, use `collect()` or `with_capacity`. Change project.rs
>    FileState.ast to `Box<[Stmt]>` after the stub and anonymous-class passes
>    run. In phpstan-rs/src/stub_attributes.rs, `strip` and `retain_stmts`
>    should take the Box, turn it into a Vec (`Vec::from(boxed)` or
>    `into_vec()`), call retain, and box it again. Change ast.rs:1554
>    `conditioned()` to return `&[Expr]`.
> 3. **Add `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Expr>() <= N)`-style asserts** for
>    Expr, StmtKind and Arg in ast.rs, so any enum-size win is locked in and
>    future size regressions are caught. This step is cheap and worth doing
>    whatever step 1 shows.

#### K13. Shrink Expr/Stmt node size by boxing rare large variants and moving doc comments to a side table

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: memory-allocation)
- **Benefit:** About 35% fewer bytes per Expr (136 to about 88) and about 20
  fewer bytes per Stmt, across every retained AST. Expr is the most numerous
  node type, so this scales directly with project size including vendor. It also
  improves cache density during checking.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/cst/cst/binary.rs:52`,
  `crates/syntax/src/cst/cst/identifier.rs:23`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1513`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1466`, `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1344`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:64`
- **Risks:** Many match arms on Closure/ArrowFn/StaticCall in
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/\* need a deref. The side-table doc comment
  requires threading the file's table to checker/stmt.rs::inline_var_annotation.
  The boxed-tuple variant avoids that at 8 bytes per Stmt. The replica sizes are
  estimates; confirm with size_of asserts once implemented.
- **Verification:** All the phpstan-rs citations check out. The ast.rs line
  numbers for StaticCall (1466), DynamicStaticCall (1468), Closure (1513),
  ArrowFn (1525) and Expr (1344, fields at 1345-1347) are right, give or take a
  line.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Start by measuring. Run the existing dhat-heap feature (README.md:92-98,
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:18-20) once, to confirm the AST's share of peak
> memory and to decide whether the Stmt half is worth doing at all. Then, in
> crates/syntax/src/ast.rs: (1) Box the rare large ExprKind payloads.
> Closure{..} (ast.rs:1513) becomes Closure(Box\<ClosureExpr>) and ArrowFn{..}
> (1525) becomes ArrowFn(Box\<ArrowFnExpr>), each a named struct with the same
> fields. Keeping the field names means `ExprKind::Closure(c)` plus `c.params`
> is a mechanical rewrite of about 81 match sites (44 Closure, 37 ArrowFn). (2)
> Shrink the static-access variants. Boxing only StaticTarget::Name's
> QualifiedName (ast.rs:807-810) is not enough. My replica shows that
> StaticCall(StaticTarget2{Box,Box}, Ident, Vec\<Arg>) still has a 64-byte
> payload, which with the tag keeps ExprKind at 72. So either give StaticCall
> and DynamicStaticCall (1466/1468) a single Box\<StaticCallExpr>, or make the
> target a thin Box (for example Box\<StaticTarget>, 8 bytes). ClassConstFetch
> and StaticPropertyFetch fit once StaticTarget::Name is boxed. That touches
> about 185 match sites. (3) Target sizes: ExprKind at most 64 (MethodCall's
> Box+Ident+Vec+u8 is the floor), Expr at most 88, Arg (ast.rs:666, which embeds
> Expr) at most 120. Add `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Expr>() <= 88);` next
> to the Expr definition, plus the same for ExprKind and Arg. (4) Stmt
> (ast.rs:64-67). Use the cheap form: a single
> `doc: Option<Box<DocComment { text: Arc<str>, line: u32 }>>` (8 bytes instead
> of 24). That touches about 95 doc_comment/doc_line sites. Skip the
> NodeId-keyed side table: it would mean threading a per-file table into
> checker/stmt.rs::inline_var_annotation and the other consumers, for only 8
> more bytes saved per Stmt. Update the parser construction sites and the
> checker/registry matches. No semantic change.

#### K22. Key scope maps (Locals, provenance, guards) by interned Name instead of String

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: memory-allocation, names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Every imbl node copy after a branch fork clones 8-byte Arc
  pointers instead of allocating Strings. That cuts transient allocation churn
  in the hottest checker path and lowers per-thread peak during deeply branching
  functions. It also removes the per-lookup String building for real variable
  keys. | Scope operations dominate the checker.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:58`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/expression/mod.rs:252`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:24`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:116`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:24`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:129`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:73`
- **Risks:** Many call sites (narrowing\*.rs, assignment.rs, control_flow.rs)
  build keys as String, so the change is mechanical but broad. Interning
  synthetic keys adds lock traffic unless a local interner or TLS cache is used.
  Ordering-sensitive output (for example --dump-types) must keep sorting by
  text. | This overlaps the scopes and narrowing aspect; coordinate with that
  work. The many call sites passing `&str` would need a lookup-by-str path,
  which is safe only if the Hash impl stays compatible, or else an explicit
  conversion.
- **Verification:** - The type aliases are in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs,
  not locals.rs. LocalsMap is at checker.rs:24-29 and ProvenanceMap at
  checker.rs:37-42. GuardedFunctionSet is at checker.rs:49-50, and it also types
  guarded_constants and guarded_classes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `ScopeKey` newtype in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs. It wraps
> a cheaply cloned shared string, and it must implement Hash by text and
> `Borrow<str>` so the existing `&str` lookups (`Locals::get`/`contains_key`,
> locals.rs:98-104) keep working unchanged. Switch these to it: `LocalsMap`,
> `ProvenanceMap`, `GuardedFunctionSet`, `GuardedMemberSet` (tuple becomes
> `(ScopeKey, ScopeKey)`) and `ReinitializedPropertySet` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:24-66, plus the `String`s inside
> `ConditionAliasMap` / `BranchImpliedFacts` (checker.rs:87,109). Make
> `insert`/`declare`/`insert_with_provenance` take `impl Into<ScopeKey>`, so the
> 58 `narrowing_key` call sites and about 134 locals write sites can migrate
> gradually, not in one big diff.
>
> Two ways to build the key; benchmark both behind the newtype: (a)
> `ScopeKey(syntax::name::Name)`. Plain variables reuse the lexer's
> `ExprKind::Variable(Name)` with no allocation (predicates.rs:73 currently does
> `name.to_string()`). Synthetic `a->b` / `a[k]` / `C::$p` keys go through
> `Interner::global().name(..)`. (b) `ScopeKey(Rc<str>)` from a per-Checker
> `FxHashMap<Box<str>, Rc<str>>`, dropped with the file. `Locals` already holds
> `Rc<Expr>` (checker.rs:87,109,149), so it is not Send and nothing is lost.
> This version avoids the global interner's shard mutex and weak-table growth
> for per-file synthetic keys. It also avoids cross-thread atomic refcount
> traffic on keys every file shares, like `this`.
>
> Keep `is_real_variable_key` (predicates.rs:165) as it is, or cache it as a
> bool in the key. Also have `narrowing_key` return `ScopeKey`, and have
> `may_have_member_narrowing` probes compare keys, not rebuild strings. Profile
> a branch-heavy file (for example with the existing hotpath feature) before and
> after. If the gain is under a few percent, keep only the
> `narrowing_key`-returns-`Name`-for-plain-variables part.

#### K14. Store resolved names (ResolvedName) as interned Name instead of per-occurrence Box\<str>

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation, names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Removes one heap allocation per class/function/constant reference
  in every retained AST (each `new Foo`, `Foo::bar()`, type hint, catch,
  instanceof). Deduplicates the long FQN strings that dominate namespaced vendor
  code, and shrinks QualifiedName, which is embedded in StaticTarget,
  InstanceofTarget, TypeHint and Attribute.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/word/src/interner.rs:152`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:58`, `crates/names/src/scope.rs:307`,
  `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs:296`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:395`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:409`, `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:856`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:193`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_context.rs:7`
- **Risks:** Adds interner lock traffic during parsing, so parallel parse
  contention is worth measuring; the name interner has only 16 shards
  (name.rs:216). A thread-local front cache (see the interner idea) mitigates
  this. ResolvedName's PartialEq semantics stay text-based. | AST construction
  must have an interner available at resolution time. The parser already has one
  (parser.rs:141). resolve_class_name is also called from LSP completion
  (lsp/completion.rs:700) and needs the interner passed through.
- **Verification:** Nearly all citations check out, with small offsets: -
  crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:391-397 is `resolve_class_name`, and it
  writes `ResolvedName::Exact(ctx.resolve(&name.written).into())` at line 395. -
  `with_fallback` at lines 406-411 does `.into()` on a String to get a
  Box\<str>.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:856-866, change `ResolvedName::Exact(Box<str>)`
> and `WithGlobalFallback(Box<str>)` to hold `crate::name::Name`. No interner
> plumbing is needed: the parser's interner is already the process-global one
> (`interner: Arc::clone(Interner::global())`, parser.rs:141), and
> `Name::from(&str)` interns into that same global (name.rs:154-158). So
> `resolve_names` (name_resolution.rs:285), `resolve_class_name`
> (name_resolution.rs:393) and `with_fallback` (name_resolution.rs:406-410) can
> build a Name directly, and LSP completion needs no signature change.
>
> The key refinement is to skip the lock entirely in the most common case. When
> the resolved text equals the written text (every unaliased name in the global
> namespace, which covers most non-namespaced PHP and most stub references), or
> equals `written` minus a leading `\`, use `name.written.clone()`, which is
> only an Arc bump. For the `\Foo` case, only intern the stripped suffix. To
> make this work, have `NameContext::resolve_as` (name_resolution.rs:193) return
> `Cow<str>`, borrowing when the input is already fully qualified. Only prefixed
> or aliased results then go through `Interner::global().name()`.
>
> `QualifiedName::resolved_class()` and `candidates()` keep returning `&str`
> through Deref, so the ~43 external callers compile unchanged. Also add
> `resolved_class_name() -> Option<&Name>` so that
> `registry::name_context::class_ref` (name_context.rs:7-9),
> `function_sig/type_resolution.rs:67` and `types/src/parse.rs:806` clone
> instead of re-interning.
>
> Rekeying `use_map` to avoid the `to_ascii_lowercase()` per lookup
> (name_resolution.rs:142 and 221) is a separate, optional micro-optimisation.
>
> Before and after, measure peak RSS and parse time with parallel parsing. The
> per-reference Mutex on 16 shards is the main performance risk, and the
> written-clone fast path is what keeps that risk small.

#### K17. Intern file paths as FileId and build incremental-only indexes (dependents, references) only when incremental updates are possible

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation, pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Replaces a heap PathBuf (24-byte header plus about 50-100 bytes
  of path) with 4 bytes in every reference edge, use site and declaration site,
  and drops the whole dependents map in batch runs. On a 14k-file project with
  dozens of referenced names per file that is hundreds of thousands of small
  allocations. Comparisons and hashing get faster as well.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/database/src/file.rs:18`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:99`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:254`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:2166`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:59`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/duplicate_fn_sites.rs:55`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:52`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:724`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1215` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Touches every API that takes &Path for lookups (project.rs, lsp.rs,
  whole_program/\*). A FileId must stay stable across remove_files/update_file
  (never reuse ids, or use a generation counter). Diagnostics output must still
  print paths identically. | A Project built with incremental=false must panic
  or rebuild if update_file is later called, so assert on it. The FileId table
  needs removal handling in remove_files.
- **Verification:** These are small corrections, and none of them changes the
  verdict. (1) Mago's FileId, at crates/database/src/file.rs:18, is not a
  sequential table index. Its doc comment (lines 10-13) says it comes from
  hashing the file's logical name, so it stays stable across runs.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split this into a cheap, clearly worthwhile part and an optional part. Do not
> do a crate-wide FileId migration.
>
> (1) Batch gate. Add a `track_dependents: bool` to ProjectSettings, following
> the same pattern as `retain_source` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:405,
> which the LSP Server sets). Leave it false in Session::resolve and in
> check-project, and set it true in lsp.rs and main/incremental_bench.rs, the
> only callers of update_file/remove_files (lsp.rs:608, 721, 827;
> incremental_bench.rs:57). When it is false:
>
> - skip `register_references` in insert_parsed_file (project.rs:724);
> - store an empty `FileState.references` (project.rs:52);
> - make `parse_file` (project.rs:2022) skip `deps::referenced_names` by passing
>   the flag in or returning an Option. Add a
>   `debug_assert!(self.track_dependents)` at the top of
>   update_file/remove_files so misuse is caught.
>
> (2) LSP only, optional. Re-key `dependents` (project.rs:126) as
> `FxHashMap<Box<str>, FxHashSet<Arc<Path>>>` and share each path's Arc from one
> place. `Origin::File(Arc::from(path))` is already built per file in parse_file
> (project.rs:2025), so no new FileId table or id-stability rules are needed.
> Apply the same Arc\<Path> sharing to use_sites.rs by_target/by_file
> (use_sites.rs:59).
>
> Leave DuplicateClassSites and DuplicateFunctionSites always populated. They
> cost one entry per declaration rather than one per reference edge. The
> always-on choice is deliberate (project.rs:157-163) so the check can be
> switched on incrementally.

#### K20. Reduce interner contention and overhead: flat open-addressed tables, more shards and a thread-local front cache

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation, stubs-prelude,
  type-representation)
- **Benefit:** Cuts per-unique-name overhead from about 4-5 allocations (Arc,
  text, lower, bucket Vec, map slot) to 1 allocation plus a 16-byte slot, and
  per-type-node table overhead from a bucket Vec plus map slot to a 16-byte
  slot. It also reduces mutex traffic in the hottest parallel paths (lexing
  every file, interning every computed type), which helps wall time on 8+ cores.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/word/src/interner.rs:122`,
  `crates/word/src/interner.rs:273`, `crates/word/src/interner.rs:113`,
  `crates/word/src/interner.rs:215`, `crates/word/src/interner.rs:54`,
  `crates/word/src/interner.rs:231` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:221`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:22`, `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:216`,
  `crates/types/src/intern.rs:23`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:919`, `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:328`
  (+3 more)
- **Risks:** A Weak still pins its ArcInner until swept. With the text inline,
  dead names keep their text until the sweep instead of only a 48-byte shell.
  Tune sweep_at, or sweep more eagerly when the table holds many dead entries.
  The unsafe DST Arc needs care, so prefer an audited crate. The TLS cache must
  not break the 'entry dropped on last strong ref' invariant. | Arc clones from
  a cache still bump shared refcounts on hot names, so some cache-line
  contention remains; a Lexer-local cache limits this per file. The test at
  syntax/src/name.rs:353 expects unreferenced names to be freed.
- **Verification:** Mago crates/word/src/interner.rs is only 304 lines, so
  several of the cited lines are wrong. Correct locations: - The Entry header
  (hash u64, len u32, _pad u32, 16 bytes, bytes stored inline after it) is at
  lines 18-27, not 77-86.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Measure before changing anything, then make the small changes first: (1) Put
> hotpath measurement on syntax::name::Interner::name/str
> (crates/syntax/src/name.rs:319-334) and types::intern::insert
> (crates/types/src/intern.rs:96) for the stub parse and a project run. (2) If
> lock time shows up, add a small direct-mapped cache keyed by the raw byte
> slice inside the Lexer (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:337-340 variables, :391-392
> identifiers). A hit returns a Name clone without the shard lock. It also skips
> the String::from_utf8_lossy(...).into_owned() / lex_ident_raw allocation that
> every identifier and variable token pays today. The cache dies with the lexer,
> so the test at name.rs:353 (unreferenced names are freed) still holds. (3)
> Raise name SHARDS from 16 to 64 (name.rs:216) and pick the shard from the high
> hash bits in Interner::shard (name.rs:310). The low FxHash bits also index the
> inner FxHashMap. (4) Replace the whole-memo clear at MEMO_CAPACITY (intern.rs
> ~469) with a two-generation swap so hot entries survive. (5) Separately,
> decide whether Project::new (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:353) should
> reuse Interner::global(), the interner stubs.rs:729/919 parse into. That
> removes the duplicate copy of every stub name and makes Name::eq's ptr_eq fast
> path (name.rs:59-63) hit across stub and project names. First check whether
> the separate interner exists on purpose, for test isolation or for freeing
> memory per project in the LSP. Defer these unless the profile shows table
> overhead matters: the hashbrown::HashTable<(u64, Weak)> rewrite and the
> single-allocation ThinArc NameData. Do not adopt: Mago's TUnion value-type
> model (codex/src/ttype/union.rs:36). phpstan-rs hash-conses types on purpose
> (Arc ptr_eq identity, the memo keyed by node address), so that part of the
> evidence does not apply.

#### K87. Merge same-class generic objects in unions through covariant slots

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: generics-templates)
- **Benefit:** Unions that grow in loops, branch merges and generators stay
  bounded (a `CoBox<1>|CoBox<2>|...` chain collapses). Hash-consed type count
  and memory drop, and diagnostics show far shorter types. Iterator, Generator,
  readonly value objects and Result/Option types are commonly covariant.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:1530`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/union.rs:298`,
  `crates/types/src/union.rs:23`
- **Risks:** The types crate is currently hierarchy-free in union.rs, so either
  the dependency or a variance cache must be introduced carefully. Merging must
  never happen through invariant slots.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/codex/src/ttype/combiner.rs:1530
  get_combiner_key is correct. It writes `*` only for `Variance::Covariant`
  slots (lines 1543-1545 and 1566-1567), not for bivariant ones, so the
  proposal's "or bivariant" goes beyond what Mago does.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Leave `Type::union` (crates/types/src/union.rs:14-21, 23) hierarchy-free. It
> is memoized in a thread-local table keyed by node pointers
> (crates/types/src/intern.rs:447-476), so a result that depends on a global
> variance table would stay cached after an LSP edit changes a class's
> `@template-covariant`. Putting the variance inside the interned
> `Repr::Object(Name, Vec<Type>)` node (types/src/lib.rs:165) is also a bad fit:
> equality and hashing would then depend on registry state that the types-crate
> parser does not have.
>
> Instead, add a hierarchy-aware normalization to the relation layer, for
> example `Relation::normalize_union(&self, ty) -> Type` next to
> crates/types/src/subtype.rs. It reads variance through the existing
> `effective_slot_variance` (crates/types/src/hierarchy.rs:64), which already
> honours call-site `VarianceArg` markers, backed by
> `ClassHierarchy::slot_variance`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/relation.rs:86, registry/generics.rs:21). It
> does two things: (1) Variance-aware absorption. Drop `CoBox<0>` when
> `CoBox<int>` is also a member. The current `absorb_contained_members`
> (union.rs:298) uses `Relation::structural()` and cannot do this. (2) Covariant
> merge. Two `Object(c, a)` and `Object(c, b)` members of equal arity merge into
> `Object(c, zip(a, b).map(union))` only when every differing slot is Covariant
> (or a `*`/bivariant call-site argument) and all other slots are equal. Never
> merge through an invariant or contravariant slot.
>
> Call it from the checker's join points that already have the registry:
> `merge_scopes` in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:563, the loop
> fixed-point widening, ternary/match results, and inferred return types.
> Optionally, the MAX_UNION_MEMBERS fallback could also run it before the union
> gives up to `mixed`. Today `generalize_members` (union.rs:346) leaves `Object`
> arguments untouched (queries.rs:478 `generalize` has no Object arm), so 64 or
> more distinct `CoBox<literal>` members turn into `mixed`.
>
> Tests should cover these cases, all confirmed as current output by the probe:
>
> - `$c ? new CoBox(1) : new CoBox('a')` is today `CoBox<1>|CoBox<'a'>`; the
>   target is `CoBox<1|'a'>`.
> - The loop case is today `CoBox<0>|CoBox<int>`; the target is `CoBox<int>`.
> - An invariant `InBox<int>|InBox<string>` must stay as it is.

#### K15. Batch mode: stop retaining context/vendor file ASTs after finish_loading

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, L (aspect: memory-allocation)
- **Benefit:** On a composer project the context files usually outnumber
  analyzed files several times over (about 11k of 14k on Piwigo). Their ASTs are
  dead weight during the parallel check phase, when per-thread checker state is
  added on top. Evicting them removes most of the retained-AST footprint, the
  component Mago avoids entirely, while keeping phpstan-rs's single-parse design
  for analyzed files.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:232`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:347`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:52`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:49`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:776`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/uninitialized.rs:123`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1866`
- **Risks:** Correctness depends on finding every post-load AST consumer (grep
  `.ast` / `bodies()` / `Project::ast`:
  project.rs:476,533,617,781,1055,1427,1509,1868). Missing one silently degrades
  results, so gate it with tests that run check-project with eviction on and off
  and diff the output. Lazy re-parse needs the file path and interner at lookup
  time and adds latency for classes with deep vendor ancestry. Pruning to
  ancestors/traits of analyzed classes is cheaper but must include traits used
  by vendor ancestors.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate.
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:231-254 uses
  map_init(LocalArena::new), then parse, resolve, scan_program, and
  arena.reset() at line 254. Lines 346-368 re-parse only host_files and reset
  the arena after each one.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Measure first, then evict in two tiers, and only in batch mode (retain_source
> off). (0) Measure with the existing dhat profile (README.md:86-98). Compare
> live heap right after Project::finish_loading (session.rs:671) with the global
> peak (t-gmax) inside check_files. If the peak is at load time, eviction after
> finish_loading cannot lower peak RSS. In that case the first win is streaming
> insert_parsed_file instead of collecting every (String, ParsedFile) pair
> (session.rs:627-632) before inserting any. (1) In a new
> Project::evict_context_asts(), called after finish_loading when
> !retain_source: set `ast` to an empty Vec for each non-analyzed FileState, and
> make Project::ast (project.rs:616) return None for evicted files. First run
> every post-load reader of context ASTs, or recompute its inputs at parse time:
> renamed_named_arguments (project.rs:1866, all files), composer_hygiene's
> declaring_files loop (composer_hygiene.rs:237), and rebuild_pest_config
> (project.rs:472-477; it already runs inside finish_loading). Skip eviction
> when check_renamed_named_arguments is on, or collect its per-file overrides in
> parse_file. (2) This step is where the real memory goes. FileBodies
> (registry/bodies.rs:32) holds Arc clones of FunctionBody.stmts
> (syntax/src/ast.rs:242), so step 1 alone frees only class/signature skeletons
> and top-level code. Prune each context file's `bodies` to the spans the
> checker can still reach: methods of registry.ancestor_names of every analyzed
> class, the traits those ancestors use (transitively), and the trait bodies
> that flatten_traits copies into analyzed classes. These are read by
> uninitialized.rs:123, uninitialized_dataflow.rs:750, class_shape.rs:293 and
> the per-use-site trait checks. Drop all other body Arcs. Purity and
> property_writes verdicts are already computed in finish_loading
> (project.rs:774, purity.rs:73), so they no longer need bodies. Add a test
> harness that runs check-project over fixtures with eviction on and off and
> asserts identical output. Add a debug_assert that no evicted ast or pruned
> body is read.

#### K16. Batch load: stop holding a String copy of every file's source alongside its ParsedFile

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation, pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Lowers the load-phase high-water mark by roughly the total source
  size of the project including vendor (tens to hundreds of MB on large composer
