  dhat profile. | Peak RSS during load drops by the total byte size of all
  loaded PHP files, vendor included;
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:232`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:575`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:625`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:735`
- **Risks:** Low. The streaming variant must preserve the
  context-before-analyzed insertion order that collision resolution depends on
  (session.rs:644-668). | Only index_class_fn_refs (project.rs:704) reads source
  text, under retain_source. Keep that path intact.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate apart from small line-number
  drift. In phpstan-rs, read_and_parse_file begins at
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:569; the
  `String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()` call is at 576, as cited;
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs, change
> SessionRun::read_and_parse_file (569-582) to return Option<(usize,
> ParsedFile)>, i.e. bytes.len() plus the parse, and stop building the
> from_utf8_lossy String. The Session always sets retain_source: false
> (session.rs:441), and the batch dead-code path uses
> index_class_fn_refs_without_source (project.rs:706-712), so batch never needs
> the text. Make combined_parsed a Vec\<Option<(usize, ParsedFile)>> (625) and
> feed the length into analyze_sizes (665). Change Project::insert_parsed_file
> (project.rs:669) to take source: Option\<String> and store
> `self.retain_source.then_some(source).flatten()`. Make the
> `if self.retain_source` branch at 706 use index_class_fn_refs only when a
> source is present, and fall back to the without_source variant otherwise. The
> batch callers (session.rs:653, 666) pass None. load_file_impl (project.rs:654)
> passes `self.retain_source.then(|| source.to_string())`, which also removes

#### K21. Make type-memo entries allocation-free and bounded so they do not pin types indefinitely

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: memory-allocation)
- **Benefit:** Removes one heap allocation per memoized operation. Bounds the
  number of otherwise-dead type nodes the memo keeps alive, which today can be
  hundreds of thousands pool-wide. That makes the weak interner's sweeping more
  effective and lowers steady-state RSS in both batch runs and the LSP.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:368`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/intern.rs:424`,
  `crates/types/src/intern.rs:436`
- **Risks:** A smaller or more frequently cleared memo can lose cross-file hits
  (common unions such as int|string recur across files), so tune it with
  measurements. Ptr-based Eq stays sound only while the key holds strong refs,
  which this design guarantees.
- **Verification:** phpstan-rs citations are accurate.
  crates/types/src/intern.rs:424 has `type MemoEntry = (Vec<Type>, Type)`.
  MemoKey stores addresses as usize at 429-434. MEMO_CAPACITY = 1<<16 is at 436.
  The thread_local FxHashMap is at 438-441.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/types/src/intern.rs, change the memo key so it holds the argument
> Types itself
> (`struct MemoKey { operation, first: Type, second: Option<Type>, rest:
> Box<[Type]> }`),
> with manual Hash/PartialEq that go through `Arc::as_ptr(&ty.0)`. The map then
> becomes `FxHashMap<MemoKey, Type>` and the `MemoEntry = (Vec<Type>, Type)`
> alias and the `kept` Vec (line 472) go away. On lookup, build the key from
> clones (refcount bumps, no heap for 1-2 args), or look it up with a borrowed
> address tuple through hashbrown's raw_entry/Equivalent so a hit costs no
> refcount traffic. Keep the 64k-entry wholesale-clear policy unless a hotpath
> measurement of hit rate and RSS shows a smaller cache (say 16k) loses no hits.
> Do not add a per-file `clear_memo()` from Project::check_files: it would throw
> away cross-file hits on common unions for little memory gain.

#### K34. Compact Name representation: inline small names and one allocation per entry

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Fewer allocations per interned name (from about 4 today to 1, or
  0 for short names with SSO), and a smaller table footprint. That helps the
  1.62GB peak and the roughly 0.95s startup, where around 2351 stub files are
  parsed and interned in every process. With SSO, interning short identifiers in
  the lexer becomes lock-free.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/word/src/word.rs:72`,
  `crates/word/src/interner.rs:452`, `crates/word/src/interner.rs:503`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:22`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name.rs:221`, `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:340`
- **Risks:** Unsafe DST layout code, or crates such as `triomphe::ThinArc` to
  avoid it. SSO changes `Name` from pointer-sized to 16 bytes, which grows AST
  nodes holding many Names; measure before adopting. Weak-table semantics
  (freeing unused names) must be preserved.
- **Verification:** Mago line numbers are wrong. crates/word/src/interner.rs has
  only 304 lines, so :452 and :503 do not exist. The entry header
  (`hash: u64, len: u32, _pad: u32` followed by the bytes) is `struct Entry` at
  interner.rs:13-27.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Scope this down to two small changes in crates/syntax/src/name.rs and nothing
> more. (1) Replace `WeakTable.buckets: FxHashMap<u64, Vec<Weak<T>>>` (line
> ~208) with `hashbrown::HashTable<(u64, Weak<T>)>`. Look entries up with
> `find(hash, |(h, w)| *h == hash && w.upgrade().is_some_and(is_it))`, and make
> `sweep` a `retain` on `strong_count() > 0` with the same 2x/MIN_SWEEP policy.
> hashbrown is already in Cargo.lock (0.16/0.17), so there is no new dependency.
> This drops one heap allocation plus a 24-byte Vec header per distinct text.
> (2) Optionally, fold `lower` into the same block by storing `text: Box<str>`
> as a single `Box<str>` of `text` or `text+lower` with a split length, or
> through `triomphe::ThinArc<(u32 split), u8>`. That takes a name from 2-3
> allocations to 1-2, or to 1 with ThinArc. Do not adopt the SSO `Name` enum. It
> would double `Name` from 8 to 16 bytes in every AST node, type and registry
> map that holds one, lose the `Arc::ptr_eq` fast path in `PartialEq` and
> `eq_ignore_case`, and add a branch to every `Deref`. Mago itself ships SSO
> only behind a non-default `sso` feature (crates/mago/crates/word/Cargo.toml
> `default = []`), and its default `Word` is a single pointer. Before either
> change, count distinct names and their bytes in one Piwigo-sized run (dhat or
> a debug counter in `Interner::name`). The change is only worth making if that
> count is a non-trivial slice of peak memory.

#### K19. Shrink the interned type Repr/Node: Arc the TemplateParam and Conditional payloads, intern template names

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: memory-allocation, type-representation)
- **Benefit:** About 40% smaller interned nodes (104 to about 64 heap bytes each
  including Arc counts), plus no slack in member lists and one fewer allocation
  per template/callable type. Registry types for every stub and vendor
  declaration are interned nodes, so this scales with the whole type population,
  not just the analyzed files.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs:38`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs:117`, `crates/codex/src/ttype/flags.rs:1`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/atomic/scalar/string.rs:29`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/lib.rs:621`, `crates/types/src/lib.rs:122`,
  `crates/types/src/lib.rs:680`, `crates/types/src/lib.rs:198`,
  `crates/types/src/lib.rs:192`
- **Risks:** TemplateParam is public API used widely
  (Checker.current_method_templates, generics code). Changing String to Name
  touches many construction sites. The Arc indirection adds one pointer chase
  when matching template/conditional types, which are rare compared to scalars
  and objects. Sizes are from a replica; verify with size_of asserts. |
  Mechanical but broad pattern-match churn (`Repr::TemplateParam(tp)` sites).
  The benefit should be measured on the 1.62GB peak before and after, since the
  number of distinct interned nodes may not dominate peak memory.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs:38-40 is
  `TUnion { types: Cow<'static,[TAtomic]>, flags: UnionFlags }`. UnionFlags is a
  u16 (flags.rs:7, `pub struct UnionFlags(u16)`), not u64-sized as the idea
  says. The flags.rs doc comment about going from 9 bytes to 2 bytes is quoted
  correctly.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two steps, and measure before the second one. Step 1 is cheap and
> worth doing anyway. In crates/types/src/lib.rs:
>
> - Change TemplateParam.bound from Box\<Type> to Type (line 629) and default
>   from Option\<Box\<Type>> to Option\<Type> (line 638).
> - Change CallableSig.return_type from Box\<Type> to Type (line 680). Type is
>   already Arc\<Node>, so the Box only adds a heap allocation and a pointer
>   chase.
> - Change TemplateParam.name and scope from String / Option\<String> to
>   syntax::name::Name (8 bytes, Arc\<NameData>). Clones in
>   CallableSig::with_own_templates (lib.rs:693+) and in generics rebinding then
>   become refcount bumps instead of String copies. CALLABLE_TEMPLATE_SCOPE
>   becomes a lazily built Name. Step 2 is layout. Store
>   Repr::TemplateParam(Arc\<TemplateParam>) and move Conditional's fields into
>   Arc\<ConditionalData>. Replace Vec\<Type> with Box<[Type]> in SelfRef,
>   StaticRef, Union, BenevolentUnion, Intersection and Object. Add a size test
>   such as `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Repr>() <= 40);`. Update exact_eq
>   and exact_hash in crates/types/src/intern.rs. The realistic target is 40
>   bytes, not the claimed 32. HasOffsetValue(ShapeKey, Type) is 24 + 8 bytes
>   before the tag, because PhpString is Arc<[u8]> (syntax/src/php_string.rs:9).
>   Getting to 32 would also need IntRange sentinels and a ShapeKey repacked
>   around the niche. Before committing to step 2, add a live-node counter under
>   a feature or debug flag in intern.rs. Multiply the node count by the ~32
>   bytes saved per node to see whether the churn pays off.

#### K11. Per-file arena or index slab for retained ASTs instead of one Box per node

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, XL (aspect: lexer-parser, memory-allocation)
- **Benefit:** The perf profile of phpstan-rs's parse-only run spends about
  35-40% in malloc, realloc and mprotect, and parse peak RSS is about 85x the
  source size (602MB for a 7.1MB file). Slab or arena allocation removes
  per-node malloc and free and the guarded per-node Drop. It also improves
  locality for the checker's repeated walks.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/mod.rs:34`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:254`,
  `crates/allocator/src/arena.rs:122`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/common/synthetic.rs:94`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1409`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1370`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:48`,
  `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1375`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:5960`
- **Risks:** This is a pervasive rewrite: visit.rs, VisitorMut and every checker
  pattern match on `Box<Expr>`. Mago does not show lower peak memory on the same
  synthetic file (805MB for `lint -s`), so the win is mainly CPU and
  fragmentation, not a guaranteed RSS drop. Mutating passes
  (apply_stub_attributes, name_anonymous_classes, completion's cloned bodies)
  need slab-aware equivalents. | Touches the whole syntax crate and every
  checker pattern match on Box\<Expr>. Self-referential structs complicate
  FileState ownership and incremental update_file.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/allocator/src/arena.rs:122 is not LocalArena.
  It is inside SharedArena (SyncBlinkAlloc, lines 25 and 119-126). LocalArena is
  declared at arena.rs:17 and wraps BlinkAlloc (66/73). Its reset is at 76-80,
  not 181-185. The Arena trait begins at arena.rs:248, not 353-406.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Measure a cheaper step first; the arena itself is optional and comes last.
> Step 1 (S): release builds use glibc malloc, since the only
> #[global_allocator] in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:19-20 sits behind the
> dhat-heap feature. Add mimalloc as the release global allocator, or an opt-in
> feature to start, and rerun the parse-only perf profile and the corpus wall
> time and peak RSS. A fast size-class allocator is where most of the reported
> 35-40% malloc/realloc/mprotect share would go, and it touches no AST code.
> Step 2 (S-M): the shrink ideas already queued ahead of this one (Box<[T]> for
> Vec fields that never grow after parsing, a smaller Expr/Stmt, evicting vendor
> ASTs from FileState). Step 3 (XL, only if 1 and 2 leave allocation or teardown
> clearly on top of the profile): an index-based per-file slab in crates/syntax.
> The file's node storage would be an Arc\<FileAst { exprs: Vec\<ExprNode>,
> stmts: Vec\<StmtNode> }>, keyed by the ids the parser already assigns in
> NodeId order (ast.rs:7-26). Function bodies would become (Arc\<FileAst>,
> StmtRange) handles instead of Arc\<Vec\<Stmt>> (ast.rs:242,
> registry/bodies.rs:17-60). Children would be ExprId(u32), and the checker
> would reach nodes through `&FileAst` accessors behind the visit.rs Visitor
> API. Synthetic nodes (checker/expr.rs static_call, NodeId::SYNTHETIC) would
> need a per-analysis overlay slab, because the shared file slab is immutable.
> VisitorMut passes (apply_stub_attributes, name_anonymous_classes) would run as
> parse-time fixups before the slab is frozen. Do not use the
> bumpalo+yoke/ouroboros variant: bodies are shared across files through Arc in
> the registry, and the LSP and update_file paths replace ASTs, so a lifetime on
> every AST type spreads self-referential lifetimes into Registry, BodySource,
> the checker and the LSP.

### 3.6 ux (37)

#### K194. Meaningful exit codes (0 clean, 1 diagnostics, 2 error) with configurable fail threshold

- **Value/cost:** 8/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Without this, check-project cannot gate CI: every pipeline has to
  grep the summary line or parse JSON totals to detect failures, and an analyzer
  crash (check_panics) currently looks like success. A distinct code for
  internal errors keeps 'tool broke' apart from 'code has issues'. This is the
  highest-value, lowest-cost item on this list. | This is the single largest
  CI-correctness gap.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/service/mod.rs:505`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:159`, `crates/reporting/src/reporter.rs:69`,
  `src/service/mod.rs:495`, `src/main.rs:94`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:165` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:159`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:69`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:136`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:137`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/cli.rs:39`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:201`
- **Risks:** Existing scripts that assume exit 0 will start failing, so this
  needs a release note and --no-fail as an escape hatch. The regression gates or
  fixture harness may invoke check-project and expect 0, so audit gates/ and
  xtask/ callers. | It's a breaking change for scripts that relied on exit 0.
  The fixture/gate harness uses the library Session, not the binary, so it isn't
  affected. Any corpus scripts that call the binary need `|| true`.
- **Verification:** Only small line-number drift. In phpstan-rs,
  Command::CheckProject is dispatched at crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:70,
  not 69. The analysis-Err `return` is at check_project.rs:139, not 136/137.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Core change, which is worth doing now: make `run_check_project_command` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs return `std::process::ExitCode`.
> Have `report()` return the code as well: 0 when no diagnostics remain after
> the level filter, inline ignores, ignoreErrors and baseline; 1 when some
> remain; 2 for tool failures. The tool failures are: config load or prepare
> errors (these call process::exit(1) at lines 116 and 123 today), a
> `Session::run` Err (the bare `return` at line 139), a non-empty
> `check_panics`, a baseline load failure (lines 201-208), a failed
> `--generate-baseline` write, and a failed fix or type-dump write. Change
> `fn main` in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs to return ExitCode, and use it for
> the Lsp and ConvertBaseline arms too. The `_profiler` and hotpath guards then
> drop before the process exits, which also removes the process::exit calls the
> comment at main.rs:60-63 has to work around. `--generate-baseline` exits 0 on
> success. With `--fix`, the code reflects the diagnostics that had no fix
> applied, not the pre-fix count. Change the assertion at tests/cli.rs:39 to
> expect exit 1, and add CLI tests for 0 (clean file), 2 (missing path or no
> .php files) and 2 (missing baseline). Add `--no-fail` (exit 0 on diagnostics,
> still 2 on tool errors) so wrapper scripts can tell 'broke' from 'found
> issues'. Treat the level-based fail threshold (`--error-on=<level>` plus a
> `fail_level` session key) as optional follow-up, not part of the core.
> Diagnostic already carries `level: u8` (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:101), so
> it would be easy. `--fail-on-stale-baseline` comes once stale-baseline
> reporting lands.

#### K2. Report parse errors and skipped/panicked files as structured, located diagnostics in the CLI and LSP (per path and reason, not a count)

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, S (aspect: lexer-parser, semantics-guard,
  robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** Users learn where and why a file was not analysed. Today a CI run
  silently drops a file with a syntax error, and an editor shows no marker at
  all. Tests can assert on error kinds instead of message strings. | Probes m53,
  m57, m75, m80-m82, n25-n27 and n40 each vanish into a bare count, and a CI
  user cannot tell which file failed or why. In the editor, the only feedback is
  an output-channel log line.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/syntax/src/error.rs:27`,
  `crates/syntax/src/parser/stream.rs:232`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/lint.rs:141`,
  `crates/syntax/src/error.rs:184`,
  `crates/syntax/src/cst/cst/expression.rs:95`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/analysis.rs:120` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/parser/tokens.rs:142`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:580`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:721`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:577`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:287`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:576` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** Once parse errors are reported diagnostics, vendor/context files
  with unsupported syntax need a policy: report only analysed files, and count
  context skips separately as now. Message wording is user-visible and may be
  baselined, so keep it stable once chosen. | Recovery is the large part (L to
  XL) because every checker walk must tolerate Error nodes. Surfacing is small
  and independent, so ship it first. A context (vendor) file with a parse error
  should stay a count, not a diagnostic. | Low. The JSON schema gets a new
  field.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with a few small
  corrections. - Mago crates/syntax/src/error.rs:
  `Expected { Exactly(TokenKind), OneOf(&'static [TokenKind]) }` sits at about
  lines 24-30.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split this into a small "surface it" change, which should ship now, and a
> separate recovery item.
>
> (1) crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:569-582: `read_and_parse_file`
> should return `Result<(String, ParsedFile), SkipReason>` with
> `enum SkipReason { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Panic(String) }`. The
> panic payload is downcast to `&str` or `String`. The `skipped_analyze` and
> `skipped_context` counters (session.rs:119-137, 648-668) become
> `Vec<(PathBuf, SkipReason)>` in Loaded and AnalysisResult.
>
> (2) For analysed files, each Parse skip becomes a normal Diagnostic at
> `ParseError.span` with its own identifier (e.g. `parse.syntax`), and it counts
> toward the exit code. The span is already reliable: all 29 `ParseError {..}`
> sites in crates/syntax/src set one. Io and Panic skips on analysed files are
> printed with their path and reason. For context and vendor files, keep a count
> in the summary at main/check_project.rs:287-289. Label them correctly
> ("skipped: N parse error, M unreadable, K parser panic") and list the paths
> under a verbose flag. Put the list in the JSON output too.
>
> (3) crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:721-735 and 763-778: in the `update_file` Err
> arms, publish `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` for that URI holding just the
> parse error (ERROR severity) in place of the logMessage. Replace the old
> diagnostics rather than merging them in: after an edit their ranges are stale
> and would point at the wrong code.
>
> (4) crates/syntax/src/parser/tokens.rs:142-150 `expect`: drop the
> `at token {pos}` suffix and the Debug-formatted token names. Use a small
> `Token::describe()` that returns PHP-style names (`variable "$x"`, `"}"`,
> `end of file`), giving `unexpected variable "$x", expecting ")"`. A full

#### K242. Docblock-aware LSP navigation

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Renaming a class currently leaves stale names in every docblock,
  so the next check reports class.notFound in @param/@return. With this change
  rename is complete. Go-to-definition and hover inside docblocks is expected
  editor behaviour.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/cst/type/mod.rs:144`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/redundancy/no_redundant_use.rs:389`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/navigation.rs:485`
- **Risks:** Depends on in-docblock spans. Aliases (@phpstan-type) and template
  names must not resolve to classes. Resolution must reuse the checker's
  alias/template scopes.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/cst/type/mod.rs:144 is
  `impl HasSpan for Type<'_>`, which dispatches to a span on each variant. That
  citation is correct.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Fix the target first. rename and references do not read
> lsp/navigation.rs::Walker. They read the Tier-1 use-site index,
> project/use_sites.rs::ClassFnRefWalker (index_class_fn_refs, line 124),
> through Project::use_sites() (lsp.rs:1297 references, lsp.rs:1343 rename).
> navigation.rs::Walker only serves hover, definition and documentHighlight. So
> the work touches both walkers, and it is best done as one shared docblock
> class-reference extractor that both of them call.
>
> Steps: (1) Byte anchors. The syntax AST keeps doc_comment only as Arc\<str>
> plus doc_line (syntax/src/ast.rs:64-67), so there is no byte offset. Add
> `doc_span: Option<Span>`, or a byte start, next to each doc_comment field on
> the Stmt, function, class, property and const nodes
> (ast.rs:64/233/268/330/465). (2) Positions inside the docblock. The phpdoc
> lexer already tracks a line/col Position per token
> (phpdoc/src/grammar/lexer.rs:73, 186-294). Add a byte offset to that Position,
> or record char offsets, so each Identifier/Generic-name token maps back to a
> source span. Alternatively give TypeNode::Identifier/Generic
> (phpdoc/src/grammar/ast.rs:112/122) a name span. Either way, map offsets back
> through the raw comment text. docblock::parse (docblock.rs:292) must keep
> offsets relative to the raw `/** */` text, not to lines stripped of their
> leading `*`. (3) A shared
> `doc_class_refs(doc_text, doc_span, name_ctx, template_names, alias_names) ->
> Vec<(Span, String /*fqn*/)>`.
> It walks
> @param/@return/@var/@throws/@property/@method/@extends/@implements/@use/@mixin/@phpstan-\*/@psalm-\*
> type nodes. It skips keywords and pseudo-types, @template names (class and
> method level) and @phpstan-type/@phpstan-import-type aliases, and resolves the
> rest through the same NameContext resolution the checker uses
> (registry/name_context.rs). It also covers class names in `Foo::CONST`
> const-fetch type nodes. (4) Call it from ClassFnRefWalker, recording
> RefTarget::Class, and from navigation::Walker, recording Resolved::Class.
> Hover, definition, highlight, references and rename then all cover docblocks.
> For a qualified name in a docblock, rename rewrites only the last segment, the
> same way the AST path does. (5) Only index_class_fn_refs, the LSP path with
> retained source, should emit docblock sites. Keep
> index_class_fn_refs_without_source (the dead_code existence path)
> docblock-free unless someone decides to change that on purpose. Otherwise a
> class that appears only in `@param Foo` stops being reported dead, which is a
> separate semantic change. (6) Tests go in lsp/tests/references_and_rename.rs:
> rename through `use` plus `@param`, generic arguments, template shadowing, and
> alias non-resolution.

#### K196. CI output formats (GitHub, GitLab, SARIF) with auto-detection

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Findings appear inline on GitHub PRs, in GitLab MR widgets and in
  GitHub code scanning without a third-party converter. The line-independent
  fingerprint gives stable MR diffs, and escaping closes a CI log injection
  vector. | Inline PR annotations are the most-used CI integration for
  analyzers, and today they need a checkstyle-to-annotation converter. Clickable
  paths improve local triage.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/formatter/mod.rs:71`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/github.rs:23`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/gitlab.rs:87`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/sarif.rs:49`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:243`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/github.rs:1` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs:41`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:256`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:155`
- **Risks:** Auto-detection changes default output inside CI, which could
  surprise scripts that parse text output; document it and make --format text
  explicit. Fingerprints must stay stable across versions. | Auto-switching the
  format could surprise scripts that parse text output in GitHub Actions.
  PHPStan does the same auto-detection, and `--format text` restores the old
  output.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with minor drift: -
  Mago crates/reporting/src/formatter/mod.rs: the ReportingFormat enum starts at
  about line 69-70, not exactly 71. Gitlab, Json and Sarif are behind
  #[cfg(feature = "serde")].
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs: add `OutputFormat::Github`, `Gitlab` and
>    `Sarif`. `Emacs` is optional and adds little, because Text is already
>    `path:line:col: msg (id)`.
>    - `github`: print
>      `::error
>      file=<escape_property(path)>,line=L,col=C,endLine=..,endColumn=..,title=<escape_property(identifier)>::<escape_data(message
>      [+ "\n" + tip])>`.
>      Both escapers copy Mago's crates/reporting/src/formatter/github.rs:23/45
>      (% then CR/LF, plus : and , inside properties). Add unit tests for a path
>      with `,`/`:` and for a message with a newline or `%`. The message keeps
>      its real newlines as %0A, unlike `diagnostic_line`'s single_line
>      (output.rs ~66).
>    - `gitlab`: output a Code Quality JSON array built with serde_json, with
>      description, check_name=identifier, severity="major" (the diagnostics
>      crate has no severity field today, so use a constant rather than
>      inventing a mapping), location.path relative to the project root with
>      forward slashes, and location.lines.begin/end. The fingerprint should
>      hash identifier + normalized path + message + the finding's occurrence
>      index among identical (path,id,message) triples. Leave line/col out of
>      the hash so it survives code shifts. This is better than Mago's
>      gitlab.rs:87, which hashes line and column. The hash must be stable
>      across Rust versions and platforms. std DefaultHasher is not, so add a
>      small dependency (sha2 or blake3) or hand-write FNV-1a/xxh64.
>    - `sarif`: hand-built SARIF 2.1.0 via serde_json, with \$schema, version,
>      runs[0].tool.driver{name:"phpstan-rs", version: CARGO_PKG_VERSION,
>      rules[] = distinct identifiers}, and results[] {ruleId, level:"error",
>      message.text (+tip), locations[0].physicalLocation{artifactLocation.uri
>      relative with uriBaseId "%SRCROOT%",
>      region{startLine,startColumn,endLine,endColumn}}, partialFingerprints
>      from the same stable hash}.
> 2. crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs: add the three arms to the
>    dispatch around line 256, and update the `--format` doc comment at line 86,
>    which is already stale (it lists only text/json/checkstyle). When
>    `args.format` is None (line 155), pick Github if GITHUB_ACTIONS is set and
>    GitLab... Actually, only auto-select `github` under GITHUB_ACTIONS. Do NOT
>    auto-select `gitlab` under GITLAB_CI: Code Quality JSON on stdout replaces
>    all human-readable job log output and is only useful when redirected to an
>    artifact file. GitHub annotations, by contrast, still show up readably in
>    the log. Document that `--format text` restores the old output.
> 3. Optional follow-up with separate value: an OSC 8 hyperlink option (config
>    key or PHPSTAN_RS_EDITOR_URL) for Friendly output only, gated on the same
>    is_terminal/NO_COLOR check already at check_project.rs:263. Keep it opt-in

#### K125. Explain argument/return mismatches with reasons and structural diffs

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: expression-call-analysis)
- **Benefit:** Much faster triage of shape and callable mismatches, which are
  the hardest findings to read. The LSP diagnostics become directly actionable.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/utils/mod.rs:33`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/arguments.rs:387`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/analyzer.rs:677`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/relation.rs:38`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:309`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:447`
- **Risks:** Reason text has to stay deterministic for snapshot and corpus
  diffs; keep it off the main message line so existing message matching isn't
  disturbed.
- **Verification:** Every citation checks out; three details need adding. (1)
  Mago: crates/analyzer/src/utils/mod.rs:33 get_type_diff returns None unless
  both types are complex (is_complex), then runs diffy::create_patch on
  get_pretty_id().
- **Refined proposal:**

> Three pieces, in order of value per effort. Each is independent, so each can
> be its own commit.
>
> (1) Did-you-mean on argument.unknown (cost S). At
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/parameters.rs:447, switch from self.report
> to report_builder. Add .tip(format!("Did you mean \${s}?")) using
> checker/suggest.rs::suggest_similar_name over the names in the by_name map /
> sig.params(). This follows the pattern already used at
> checker/expr.rs:1389-1393. suggest_similar_name already breaks ties
> deterministically.
>
> (2) A failure-only rejection explainer in crates/types/src/relation/accepts.rs
> (cost M). Add
> `pub fn explain_rejection(&self, accepting: &Type, accepted: &Type) -> Vec<String>`
> and fill AcceptsResult.reasons from it only when rule_level_accepts is not
> yes. Do not thread a reason collector through accepts_type or
> rule_level_accepts_rec. Those return bool on the hot path and are called
> everywhere; a Vec per call would cost time on every check.
>
> The explainer mirrors the structural arms and re-runs the existing boolean
> accepts_type / rule_level_accepts_rec on each component. That way a reason is
> emitted only when its own component check actually fails:
>
> - ArrayShape vs ArrayShape, per shape_accepts_fields (line 663) and the
>   unsealed-tail logic (lines 399-419):
>   - "Offset 'k' (T) does not accept U." — recurse for nested shapes, prefixing
>     a path such as 'a'.'b'
>   - "Offset 'k' is missing."
>   - "Offset 'k' might not exist."
>   - "Offset 'k' is not allowed by the sealed shape."
> - list vs array: "array might not be a list."
> - Generic object args: the Nth template argument, with its variance.
> - Callable vs callable: parameter #N and return type.
> - Union accepted by a non-union: name the first member that is rejected at the
>   rule level. The explainer must call rule_level_accepts_rec at the same
>   level, so it respects checkNullables/checkUnionTypes gating.
>
> If no component can be pinned down, return an empty Vec. Never guess. Sort the
> output by field declaration order, not hash order, so snapshots and corpus
> diffs stay deterministic.
>
> (3) In parameters.rs:309 and the return.type sites (checker/stmt.rs:615,
> checker/expr.rs:4090), plus the property/assign equivalents, pass the reasons
> as .tip(...). tip_text in crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:126 already renders
> several tips as a bulleted list. The message line does not change.
>
> Drop the diffy-style unified diff, or make it last and optional. phpstan-rs
> prints each type on one line, so a line diff of two one-line strings says
> nothing. It would first need a multi-line pretty-printer for types, and even
> then it only adds value over the per-offset reasons in the rare case where no
> reason could be computed.

#### K160. Severity model separate from level, with per-identifier overrides and fail threshold

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other, reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Lets teams adopt the opinionated checks proposed here without
  all-or-nothing CI failure. Editor squiggles match what the team cares about. |
  Gives CI and editors a meaningful notion of severity: an unused private
  constant can stop blocking a merge while an undefined function still does.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/mod.rs:42`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:28`, `crates/reporting/src/lib.rs:176`,
  `crates/reporting/src/reporter.rs:55`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/github.rs:74`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:499`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs:264`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs:193`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:159`,
  `crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:101`
- **Risks:** Two axes (PHPStan level and severity) may confuse users. Document
  level as 'which checks run' and severity as 'how loudly they're reported'. |
  Choosing defaults for about 565 identifiers is judgment work; a prefix-based
  default table keeps it manageable. Could be confused with `level` unless
  documented clearly.
- **Verification:** Nothing material is wrong. Small precision notes: - Mago
  crates/linter/src/rule/mod.rs:42 is the `Config` trait.
  `fn level(&self) -> Level` is a few lines down (about :49).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Two parts. (A) The failing exit code is the priority and is already planned in
> CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:816 (0 clean, 1 remaining errors, 2 untrusted result).
> Land that first in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs report(), which
> today returns without a failing status (the only exit(1) calls are at lines
> 116 and 123, for setup failures). (B) Make severity a property of the
> rule/identifier metadata, not a Diagnostic field. CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:731
> already says "Diagnostic.level goes" and "the LSP severity comes from
> rule-declared severity", so add `Severity {Error, Warning, Info, Hint}` to
> that per-identifier metadata table, with a default of Error for every
> identifier (today's checkstyle and CI behaviour) and lower defaults only for
> the few advisory families that phpstan-rs actually emits. Then add a small
> `[severity]` section in crates/config with exact identifier or `prefix.*`
> keys, and resolve it once when output is produced (one lookup: identifier to
> effective severity). Consumers: lsp/protocol.rs level_to_severity (line 264),
> which gets deleted; output.rs render_checkstyle (line 193, hard-coded
> severity="error"); the json/junit/github renderers and the summary counts; and
> the exit code, through `--fail-on error|warning|any` (default any, so the exit
> code stays strict). Leave out a separate `--min-severity` display filter,
> because ignoreErrors/identifier ignores already hide output. Leave out a
> hand-curated severity for all ~565 identifiers. Defaults stay Error unless a
> rule explicitly declares otherwise.

#### K199. Baseline lifecycle commands

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Fixing old debt shrinks the baseline without --generate-baseline
  silently absorbing newly introduced issues. CI can enforce that the baseline
  has no dead weight. Partial runs such as pre-commit on changed files stop
  printing hundreds of false 'no longer matches' lines, and teams can see what
  their baseline consists of.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/service/mod.rs:849`,
  `crates/reporting/src/baseline.rs:526`, `src/service/mod.rs:486`,
  `src/commands/args/baseline_reporting.rs:75`,
  `src/commands/inspect_baseline.rs:40`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/baseline.rs:422`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:177`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:181`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/baseline.rs:157`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/baseline.rs:397`
- **Risks:** Prune must follow includes and the per-identifier split layout
  carefully. Scoped staleness needs the analysed-file set threaded into
  finalize.
- **Verification:** All the citations check out, with small line offsets: - Mago
  src/service/mod.rs:849 verify_baseline: correct. It prints JSON
  VerifyBaselineOutput {new_issues, removed_issues} under --format json. On a
  scoped run with no new issues it logs the stale entries as info and passes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Changes, in priority order:
>
> 1. Scoped staleness (the biggest real fix). Pass the set of report paths
>    analysed in this run into baseline::filter
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/baseline.rs:370), threaded through FinalizeOptions /
>    Report in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:157-203. Report an entry
>    as stale only if its normalized `file` is in that set. Any file analysed
>    with zero diagnostics must count as analysed, not be dropped because it is
>    missing from `results`. Once this is in, LSP
>    (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:377-413) can show stale entries for the files
>    it just re-checked, where today it throws `_stale` away.
> 2. `prune-baseline <path>` subcommand, or `check-project --prune-baseline`.
>    Write a `prune_into` that follows the same include walk as the existing
>    `convert_into` (baseline.rs:342-361). Do not reuse `Baseline::load`: it
>    merges entries across the whole tree (merge() at baseline.rs ~130), so it
>    loses which file each entry came from. Instead, count per-key occurrences
>    from this run's unfiltered results. Then walk the include files in load
>    order, handing out min(recorded, remaining) to each entry, dropping entries
>    that reach zero, and keeping the `includes` lists and the per-identifier
>    split layout. The prune must never add entries, and it only touches entries
>    whose file was analysed (reuse the set from item 1).
> 3. `--fail-on-stale-baseline` (exit 1 when there are scoped stale entries;
>    today notices at check_project.rs:210 never affect the exit code) and
>    `--ignore-baseline`. The second is useful because the baseline can come
>    from the config file, not only the CLI. Add a JSON body {new, stale} when
>    `--format json` is used.
> 4. Make write_file (baseline.rs:157) atomic: write a sibling temp file, then
>    fs::rename. This also protects `convert-baseline` and generate.
> 5. Decide non_ignorable consistently. filter (baseline.rs ~397) currently
>    absorbs them, while ignore_errors.rs:141 exempts them. Either exempt them
>    in both generate and filter, or document why the baseline is allowed to
>    absorb them.
> 6. Optional, lowest value: inspect-baseline (counts by identifier and by
>    file). The baseline is plain JSON, so jq already covers most of this.

#### K220. Watch composer/config/baseline and rebuild in-process

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** After `composer require` or `composer update`, or an edit to
  phpstan-rs.toml's scan paths, the editor currently shows stale 'class not
  found' errors until a manual window reload. Mago's watch mode picks these
  changes up automatically.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/analyze.rs:563`,
  `src/commands/analyze.rs:400`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:1799`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:1860`
- **Risks:** A full rebuild pays startup cost again (about 0.95s plus a project
  parse). Diff-based application keeps it proportional to what changed. It has
  to coexist with debounced edits, so take the same Server lock.
- **Verification:** Mago's citations are accurate. In src/commands/analyze.rs,
  run_watch_loop is at line 400. On WatchOutcome::Restart it calls
  Configuration::load again and keeps the old config if that fails.
  setup_restart_watcher is at line 563.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs: (1) Widen request_watched_files_registration
> (lsp.rs:1803) with more watchers: phpstan-rs.toml, or the config_path_override
> path; the resolved baseline path; composer.json; composer.lock; and
> vendor/composer/installed.json. Split handle_watched_files_changed
> (lsp.rs:788) so these non-PHP paths go to a new `Server::rebuild_workspace()`
> instead of update_file. (2) rebuild_workspace calls workspace_config::resolve
> again (lsp/workspace_config.rs:59) and compares it with last_applied_config,
> the same way reload_configuration already does at lsp.rs:1887. If only the
> settings, baseline or ignore entries changed, it applies them hot through
> apply_resolved_config (lsp.rs:353) and republish_known_files. If
> vendor_context, extra_context_dirs or analyze_paths changed, it diffs the file
> set that load_workspace_files would collect (lsp.rs:480) against
> project.loaded_paths(). Removals go through the existing Project::remove_files
> batch (project.rs:1160). Additions and changed context files need a batch load
> without a per-file registry recompute, like load_one_file in
> load_workspace_files followed by one finish_loading, as add_workspace_folders
> does (lsp.rs:555). The last step is one republish. (3) The same path replaces
> the "reload the window" warning in reload_configuration (lsp.rs:1897-1905).
> (4) While a rebuild is pending, coalesce **/\*.php watcher events under
> vendor/ (or any excluded dir) into the rebuild instead of sending them one at
> a time to update_file. Debounce on installed.json or composer.lock, which
> Composer writes last. Take the Server lock, as other mutating paths do.

#### K276. Whole-program dead code in the LSP

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Dead-code findings become interactive (greyed-out declarations
  that update live) instead of a batch-only report.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/analysis_result.rs:51`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:318`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:754`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/use_sites.rs:79`
- **Risks:** The first build of the Tier-2 index is expensive and must stay
  lazy. Diagnostics for a file the user did not edit change as other files are
  edited, so publishing needs debouncing.
- **Verification:** All citations check out; nothing needs correcting. Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/analysis_result.rs:50-80 defines
  LateSymbolReferenceIssueReconciler.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an LSP whole-program pass that reuses the batch machinery. Skip the
> per-target delta and candidate-set design.
>
> 1. After each debounced update_file / remove_file (lsp.rs
>    handle_open_or_change ~721/763, and the watched-files path ~809/827) and
>    after the initial check_all_analyzed_paths, call a new
>    Project::check_whole_program_lsp(). It runs the cheap
>    registry-plus-use_sites scans already in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1714-1890: dead_code::find_dead_functions
>    / find_dead_classes, dead_enum_cases, dead_members, dead_abstract_classes
>    and circular_namespace_deps. Leave out renamed_named_arguments, which needs
>    the batch-only named_argument_calls. Each scan is a pass over registry
>    declarations with hash lookups into UseSiteIndex
>    (project/whole_program/dead_code.rs:48-80), so recomputing everything is
>    simpler than tracking reference-count deltas and costs about the same.
> 2. In Server, keep last_whole_program: FxHashMap\<PathBuf, Vec\<Diagnostic>>
>    separate from last_diagnostics. Diff the new result against it, and only
>    for declaring files whose set changed, publish the union of
>    last_diagnostics[p] and whole_program[p]. publish_diagnostics_for
>    (lsp.rs:849) replaces a file's whole set, so both parts must be merged at
>    every publish.
> 3. Tier 2: when check_dead_members or check_dead_enum_cases is on, seed it
>    from the LSP's own initial check_all_analyzed_paths pass (run_checker with
>    member refs, then seed_member_refs / mark_member_index_built, as
>    session.rs:700-746 already does for check-project).
>    ensure_member_index_built (project.rs:877) then never pays a second full
>    pass.
> 4. Fix a real staleness bug this surfaces: escaped_enum_cases and
>    escaped_member_classes (project.rs:200-205) are project-wide sets that only
>    ever grow (extend at project.rs:914-915). update_file
>    (project.rs:1084-1090) and remove_file never refresh them. Key them per
>    file (FxHashMap\<PathBuf, FxHashSet\<String>>) and replace a file's entry
>    in reindex_use_sites_for_file / remove_file.
> 5. Emit these as DiagnosticSeverity::HINT with DiagnosticTag::UNNECESSARY.
>    Nothing in lsp.rs or lsp/ sets DiagnosticTag today. They stay behind the
>    existing opt-in rules.check_dead_\* settings, and whole_program_diagnostic
>    (project.rs:1659) keeps filtering non-analyzed and vendor files and inline
>    ignores.

#### K299. Distinguish harmless trailing control flow from unreachable code; optionally suppress diagnostics in dead code

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** `break` after `return` in a switch is a different, harmless smell
  than genuinely dead logic, and separate identifiers let teams ignore one and
  keep the other. The knob lets users silence diagnostics computed from a scope
  that can never occur (for example type errors on variables that a preceding
  throw made irrelevant) without losing the unreachable-code report.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:239`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:267`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:58`
- **Risks:** Turning analysis off hides real bugs inside dead code that a later
  edit could make live again, so the default must stay 'analyse'. A new
  identifier changes baselines for the break-after-return case.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:225-273
  (analyze_statements). The is_harmless match is at lines 239-244: Break,
  Continue, or Return with value None gives IssueCode::UselessControlFlow; any
  other non-declaration gives UnevaluatedCode.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do this in two parts, most important first.
>
> (A) Correctness fix, found while probing this idea. Many termination checks
> look only at a case's or body's last statement. Add a helper in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs, e.g.
> `fn reachable_end<'s>(&self, stmts: &'s [Stmt], locals) -> Option<&'s Stmt>`.
> It returns the first statement that `always_terminates`, or the last statement
> when none does. Use it in place of `.last()` at:
>
> - control_flow.rs:135 and :144 (the Switch arm of `always_terminates`)
> - control_flow.rs:163-167 (the Try arm)
> - control_flow.rs:50 (`is_switch_break_equivalent` on a Block)
> - control_flow.rs:232 and :255 (`exits_function_or_loop`)
> - stmt/switch.rs:101-111 (`case_terminates` and `reaches_after_switch`)
> - stmt/try_catch.rs:105, :118, :269 and :272
>
> After this, `case 1: return 'a'; break;` counts as terminating. It no longer
> pushes a dead exit state into the switch merge, and it no longer produces
> return.missing. A leading `break; return;` still counts as a break, because
> the first terminator is the break.
>
> (B) UX split in `check_block` (stmt.rs:58-75). When the first unreachable
> statement is `break`, `continue`, or a `return` with no value, report it under
> a separate identifier, `deadCode.uselessControlFlow`, with a message like
> "Unreachable break/continue/return after a terminating statement has no
> effect". Keep the level and the one-report-per-run gating, and keep
> `deadCode.unreachable` for everything else. Update any fixtures that expect
> `deadCode.unreachable` on `return x; break;`.
>
> (C) Optional and low priority: an opt-in `analyze_unreachable_code` setting
> (default true). When it is false, dead statements still run through
> `check_stmt`, so side state like return points, throw points and goto targets
> stays the same. Only the diagnostics they emit are dropped, by truncating
> `self.diagnostics` to its pre-dead-run length, the same way
> function_decl.rs:1193 does.

#### K113. Did-you-mean hints on undefined-variable diagnostics

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Typo'd variables are the most common cause of this diagnostic; a
  'did you mean \$userId?' tip makes it immediately actionable in the CLI and
  the LSP. The ranking is already deterministic in suggest.rs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/variable.rs:225`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1656`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/suggest.rs:35`
- **Risks:** None significant. The suggestion must use the stable ordering
  already built into suggest_similar_name.
- **Verification:** The Mago citations are correct. In
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/variable.rs, the UndefinedVariable issue is
  built at lines 223-226. It calls generate_confusable_character_note (defined
  at :378) and find_similar_variable_names (defined at :303), and adds the
  results as notes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a variable-specific suggestion helper to
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/suggest.rs, for example
> `suggest_similar_variable(target, candidates)`. Do not reuse
> `suggest_similar_name` as it is. Three changes: (a) Compare case-sensitively.
> If exactly one candidate matches the target case-insensitively, return it
> first, since `$userid` against a local `$userId` is the most common variable
> typo. The existing helper filters out that exact case with
> `!c.eq_ignore_ascii_case(target)`. (b) Scale the distance cap with name
> length, e.g. `max(1, len/3)` capped at 3, so that `$a` does not suggest `$b`
> and `$i` does not suggest `$x`. (c) Keep the same lexicographic tie-break for
> determinism.
>
> Candidates are `locals.iter()` keys that are plain variable names. Filter with
> `narrowing::is_real_variable_key` (checker/narrowing/predicates.rs:165), or a
> looser check that also allows bytes >= 0x80, since PHP allows non-ASCII names.
> Either way this drops the synthetic `a->b`, `a[k]` and `C::$p` narrowing keys
> stored in the same map. Also add the superglobal names, so `$_PSOT` suggests
> `$_POST`.
>
> Wire it into all three `variable.undefined` sites, switching each from
> `self.report` to `DiagnosticBuilder` with `.tip("Did you mean $x?")`:
>
> - checker/expr.rs:1656 (`ExprKind::Variable`)
> - checker/expr.rs:3580 (closure `use`)
> - checker/calls/closure_context.rs:222 (closure `use`)
>
> Also attach `.fix(span, "$x", "Rename to $x")`. The LSP then offers a
> one-click quickfix through the existing DiagnosticFix-to-CodeAction path
> (lsp/protocol.rs:305). Tips already render in the LSP message
> (lsp/protocol.rs:241).
>
> Optionally, when the name contains a non-ASCII alphabetic char and an ASCII
> candidate matches after normalizing common homoglyphs (Cyrillic а/е/о/р/с,
> Greek ο), give that as the tip. This is a small table, like Mago's
> generate_confusable_character_note (mago
> crates/analyzer/src/expression/variable.rs:378), but it produces an actual
> suggestion rather than just a note.
>
> Add unit tests to suggest.rs for the case-only match, the short-name cutoff
> and synthetic-key exclusion, plus one fixture.

#### K202. Identifier-level reporting filters and statistics (--only-identifier, --stats)

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Makes triage of large legacy codebases much faster (which
  identifier dominates? which fixes can I apply right now?) and lets a dev loop
  focus on one rule without editing config. | Adopting the tool on a large
  codebase means triaging by category ('show me only argument.type'). Today that
  needs grep on text output.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/formatter/code_count.rs:18`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:73`, `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:55`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/rich.rs:129`,
  `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:196`, `src/commands/args/reporting.rs:74` (+1
  more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:282`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:23`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:15`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:194`
- **Risks:** None significant. Keep --only-identifier a reporting filter (not
  rule selection) and document the difference, as Mago does at
  reporting.rs:186-191. | A static identifier catalogue has to be kept in sync
  with emitting code. A test that scans emitted identifiers against the
  catalogue can enforce that.
- **Verification:** All the Mago citations check out, give or take a few lines.
  crates/reporting/src/formatter/code_count.rs:16-40 (CodeCountFormatter) counts
  issues per code (a missing code counts as "\<unknown>"), keeps the highest
  Level seen for each code, and sorts by count descending with ties broken by
  code name.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Core (S). All changes go in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs and
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs. The analysis/Session Finalize path stays
> unchanged, because this is a CLI reporting concern and the LSP has no use for
> it.
>
> 1. Add `--only-identifier <PATTERN>` (repeatable) and
>    `--exclude-identifier <PATTERN>` to CheckProjectArgs. A pattern is either
>    an exact identifier or a `prefix.*` glob; that covers the dynamic families
>    built with format!, such as `unionType.*`, `impure.*` and
>    `requireExtends.*`. Apply the filter in `report()` right after
>    `analysis.finalize(...)` (line ~208) and BEFORE the `apply_fixes` block.
>    That way `--fix --only-identifier X` applies only X's fixes, which is a
>    real workflow gain Mago blocks with a clap conflict. The filter must NOT
>    apply on the `generate_baseline` branch (lines 181-197). Either reject the
>    combination in clap (`conflicts_with = "generate_baseline"`) or ignore it
>    there; otherwise the tool writes a partial baseline that silently drops
>    real findings.
> 2. Add `--fixable-only`: keep only diagnostics with `d.fix.is_some()`, applied
>    at the same place.
> 3. Add `OutputFormat::Stats` in output.rs, plus a `--stats` alias that
>    conflicts with `--format`. It prints a table of identifier -> count sorted
>    by count descending with ties broken by name (deterministic), then level,
>    fixable count per identifier and a total line. Also extend the
>    Text/Friendly summary (check_project.rs ~282) with `, K fixable with --fix`
>    when K > 0.
> 4. Document in the --help text that these are reporting filters and every
>    check still runs. Optional follow-up (M, separate): a
>    `phpstan-rs identifiers` listing plus validation of
>    `ignore_errors.identifier`. That needs a catalogue that has both exact
>    literals and prefix families, because Identifier is `Cow<'static, str>`
>    with a `From<String>` path (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:17,44). It also
>    needs a test that scans the source's identifier literals and format!
>    prefixes against the catalogue. Only the unknown-identifier warning on
>    ignore_errors has correctness value (it catches typos that silently ignore
>    nothing). Build that part first if the catalogue is built at all.

#### K203. Friendly renderer robustness

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Correct caret placement in tab-indented PHP (very common), frames
  that always show the analysed text, and click-to-open file links in modern
  terminals.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/formatter/rich.rs:157`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/rich.rs:107`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/utils.rs:227`, `src/config/mod.rs:1239`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output/codeframe.rs:152`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output/codeframe.rs:171`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output/codeframe.rs:193`
- **Risks:** OSC 8 sequences must only be emitted when colour is enabled, since
  some consumers mangle them. The tab width is a convention that differs from
  what a given editor shows.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are materially wrong. Mago:
  crates/reporting/src/formatter/rich.rs has
  `term::emit_to_write_style(&mut buffer, codespan_config, &files, &diagnostic)`
  at about line 107.
- **Refined proposal:**

> All changes are in crates/phpstan-rs/src/output/codeframe.rs and
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs. (1) Caret alignment
> (codeframe.rs:145-155): build the underline prefix from the source line itself
> instead of `" ".repeat(col-1)`. Take the first col-1 chars of `text`, keep
> each '\t' as '\t', and turn every other char into ' '. For the '^' run, copy
> tabs the same way. The terminal then expands tabs identically on both lines,
> whatever its tab width. This needs no fixed tab-width convention, paint() is
> untouched, and the "tab width differs from the editor" risk goes away. Span
> cols are already UTF-8 character counts (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:176-182),
> so char-indexing is correct. An optional refinement is a unicode-width count
> for CJK/emoji. (2) Stale source after --fix (check_project.rs:215-244 applies
> fixes and rewrites files before render_friendly is called at :266, and
> codeframe.rs:171 re-reads from disk): render the friendly or text output into
> a String before the fix loop and print it afterwards. The alternative is to
> have the fix loop keep a map of pre-fix sources and give render_friendly a
> `sources: &FxHashMap<PathBuf, String>` parameter, falling back to disk. Either
> way the frames show the text that was analysed. (3) Non-UTF-8 files: replace
> `fs::read_to_string(...).ok()` with `fs::read` + `String::from_utf8_lossy`, so
> a frame always renders. If the analyser also works on lossy text, byte and
> char offsets can drift. That is a minor, pre-existing inaccuracy and still
> better than no frame. (4) Optional, lower priority: when `colour` is true,
> wrap the `path:line:col` header (codeframe.rs:189-199) in an OSC 8 link. The
> target is `file://<abs path>` by default, or an `editor_url` template
> (%file%/%line%/%column%) from a PHPSTAN_RS_EDITOR_URL env var or a config key.
> Skip Mago's TERM_PROGRAM/__CFBundleIdentifier auto-detection unless asked for,
> because it adds guesswork for little gain. Add a test in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/output/tests.rs next to the existing render_friendly
> tests (lines ~225/247) for a tab-indented line and for a non-UTF-8 byte.
> Secondary frames for related locations stay deferred until diagnostics carry
> related spans.

#### K207. Configurable thread count (CLI, config, env) with LSP default

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Users can limit CPU in CI containers, where cgroup quotas are
  often below the host core count and cause oversubscription, and in editors.
  Contention can be measured, and the gate harness can size pools explicitly
  instead of through an env var nobody documents. | CI runners with CPU quotas
  (cgroups) often report more cores than they have, which causes
  oversubscription.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/config/mod.rs:203`, `src/config/mod.rs:683`,
  `src/consts.rs:69`, `src/config/mod.rs:197`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:215`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:15`
- **Risks:** Minimal. available_parallelism already respects cgroups on Linux in
  modern std. | None of note.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate. In Mago,
  src/config/mod.rs:203-209 defines the `threads` field, and its doc says 0
  means logical CPUs and that it can be overridden by MAGO_THREADS or --threads.
  `stack_size` follows at about line 211.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Change `worker_pool()` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:215) to
> `worker_pool(threads: Option<NonZeroUsize>)`, which calls `.num_threads(n)`
> when a value is set. Pick the thread count in this order: the `--threads N`
> flag on CheckProjectArgs (src/main/check_project.rs:16) and on the `check`
> subcommand (src/main/check.rs:24), then the documented `PHPSTAN_RS_THREADS`
> env var, then a new `threads` key in SessionSettings
> (src/project/session.rs:44). The default stays rayon's (available_parallelism,
> which respects cgroup quotas).
>
> Apply the same count to rayon's global pool, either with
> `ThreadPoolBuilder::build_global()` once at startup or by running the whole
> prepare/registry phase inside `pool.install`. Otherwise the bare `par_iter()`
> calls in registry/hierarchy.rs (lines 71, 287, 303, 328) and registry/stubs.rs
> still run on the global pool at the default width, and the flag would not
> really limit CPU.
>
> For the LSP (src/lsp.rs:299), read the workspace setting and default to max(1,
> available_parallelism - 1) so the editor keeps a core free. Keep
> WORKER_STACK_SIZE fixed and don't add a stack-size setting. Tests and benches
> pass None.

#### K298. Per-type exemptions for strict boolean conditions (e.g. allow array truthiness)

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** `if ($items && $user)` on an array is idiomatic PHP with
  well-defined semantics (empty array is false). Today teams must turn the whole
  strict-boolean family off to allow it, and in doing so lose the reports that
  catch real bugs, such as an object that is always truthy or a nullable int
  where 0 is valid.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/logical.rs:735`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:1512`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/strict_rules.rs:14`
- **Risks:** Configuration surface grows, and the identifiers stay the same, so
  baselines are unaffected.
- **Verification:** Mago: the citation is correct.
  crates/analyzer/src/expression/binary/logical.rs:703-765
  check_logical_operand: mixed is an error, null is a NullOperand warning, and
  array is an InvalidOperand warning that is skipped when
  `context.settings.allow_array_truthy_operand` is set (line 735).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add one field to StrictRulesSettings in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext/strict_rules.rs:
> `boolean_conditions_allow: Vec<String>` (config key
> `[ext.strict-rules] boolean_conditions_allow = ["array"]`). Accept only a
> closed set of kinds: "array", "null", "int", "string", "float". Reject
> "object" and "resource" at config load, because they are always truthy and the
> check exists to catch them. Resolve the list once into a `Type` union, e.g.
> `array<mixed>|null`, and store it on the resolved settings. Apply the
> exemption in only two functions in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/operators.rs:
> check_non_boolean_condition (line 254) and check_non_boolean_and_or_operand
> (line 280). All 11 call sites go through these two, covering
> if/elseif/while/do-while/ternary/`!`/`&&`/`||`. After the existing mixed/bool
> early return, compute `rest = ty.without(&allowed)` using the existing
> Type::without (crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:195). If `rest` is never or
> `rest.is_bool().yes()`, skip. Otherwise report as today with the full type in
> the message, so `?array` with only "array" allowed still reports because of
> null, and `array|Foo` still reports. Keep the identifiers unchanged. Also
> route check_logical_xor (checker/control_flow/boolean_conditions.rs:144)
> through the same helper if it does its own operand check. Add fixtures:
> allowed array; ?array still reported; object never exemptable; int allowed
> while float is not.

#### K311. In-source dumpType/dumpNativeType/dumpScope intrinsics reported as informational diagnostics

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary
  commands)
- **Benefit:** For narrowing work this is the biggest win. It shows the actual
  state after a branch, a loop join or a condition alias, including the
  side-tables that assertType can never observe (e.g., why a `defined()` guard
  or an alias replay leaked). It speeds up the stale-alias, clause and
  loop-convergence investigations already on the roadmap. The workflow is the
  same as today's probes (check-project --no-composer .).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:174`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:529`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:153`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:457`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:29`
- **Risks:** A user function or method named dumpType must not be swallowed.
  Only intercept when no user-declared function with that resolved name exists,
  or require the namespaced forms. dumpScope output on large scopes can be long,
  so sort it and cap each type's rendering. This overlaps with the queued
  Composer no-op runtime stub idea, which covers runtime definitions only; this
  idea is the checker side.
- **Verification:** These are minor line offsets only. In phpstan-rs, the
  assertType check is at crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:457-458: the
  comment starts at 446 and the `name == "assertType"` test is on line 458.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs, next to the assertType arm (~line
>    457), intercept `PHPStan\dumpType`, `PHPStan\dumpNativeType`,
>    `PHPStan\dumpPhpDocType`-style names and `PHPStan\dumpScope`, plus the
>    `phpstanRs\` equivalents. Match them case-insensitively. A bare `dumpType`
>    should match only when `self.registry.resolve_function(name)` finds no user
>    or stub declaration, so a real user function is never swallowed.
> 2. For each argument of dumpType, report `Dumped type: {infer_expr}` at the
>    argument span with identifier `phpstanRs.dumpType`. dumpNativeType should
>    render the native type: `locals.native(name)` for a plain variable,
>    otherwise the native inference of the expression when one exists, and
>    otherwise say it is unknown instead of guessing. Still run check_expr on
>    the arguments, and return null.
> 3. Add `pub(crate) fn debug_render(&self) -> String` to Locals in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs. List the plain variables sorted as
>    `$x: T (native: N)`, then the synthetic narrowing keys (property chains and
>    indexes), then each non-empty guarded_\* set, condition_aliases,
>    branch_implied_facts, container_field_facts, discriminant_array_facts,
>    query_builder_aliases, clone_reinitialized and any_variable_may_exist, all
>    sorted. Cap each rendered type at about 200 characters. dumpScope() emits
>    that text as one multi-line diagnostic with identifier
>    `phpstanRs.dumpScope`.
> 4. Make these diagnostics bypass ignoreErrors and the baseline, and exclude
>    them from the exit-code and fail count. Mark them as informational/hint
>    severity, so the LSP shows them as hints rather than errors.
> 5. Keep the hidden `--dump-types` flag for whole-file regression snapshots.
>    Share the variable-line formatting between record_type_dump
>    (checker.rs:1185) and debug_render so the two cannot drift. Skip
>    `@phpstan-trace` docblock parsing; it adds nothing over `dumpType($x)`.

#### K201. Unmatched inline ignores reported at the comment with removal fix

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Stale suppressions are one-click or --fix removable instead of
  manual archaeology, and the report points at the text to delete. Scoped
  suppression avoids sprinkling dozens of per-line ignores through generated or
  legacy functions. A suppress quickfix is a common editor workflow that is
  missing today.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/collector/src/pragma.rs:66`,
  `crates/collector/src/lib.rs:441`, `crates/collector/src/lib.rs:480`,
  `crates/collector/src/walk.rs:37`, `crates/collector/src/pragma.rs:390`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_comments.rs:15`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:536`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:59`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:511`
- **Risks:** Scoped suppression is a new, non-PHPStan syntax, so keep it opt-in
  and namespaced to avoid ambiguity with real PHPStan. Removal edits inside
  docblocks must preserve surrounding tags, which is why Mago checks for
  non-pragma content.
- **Verification:** Only small offsets are wrong. In Mago, finish() starts at
  crates/collector/src/lib.rs:404. Line 441 is inside it, in the partial-count
  edit branch (the edit is built around 445).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Core (worth doing): (a) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_comments.rs, have
> IgnoreComments record provenance for each ignore: the comment's start and end
> Position (syntax::parse::Comment at crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:15 has only
> `start`, and the end can be computed from `text`), the byte range of each
> identifier inside the text, the range of the marker, and whether the comment
> is alone on its line (code_line_starts is already in the scan). Keep the
> existing `lines`/`identifiers` maps for matching and add a parallel
> Vec\<IgnoreSite>. (b) In Project::apply_inline_ignores
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:500-570), report
> ignore.unmatchedLine/unmatchedIdentifier at the identifier's span, or at the
> marker's span for -line/-next-line, rather than the zero-width (line, col 1)
> span. Attach a diagnostics::DiagnosticFix (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:173)
> that removes the identifier and its comma when a sibling identifier matched,
> removes only the directive line when a docblock has other content, and
> otherwise removes the whole comment, plus the line when the comment stands
> alone. Port the case split from mago crates/collector/src/lib.rs:554-659.
> Because check-project already applies fixes
> (src/main/check_project.rs:215-230) and the LSP already turns fixes into
> quickfixes (src/lsp/protocol.rs:305-324), both pick this up without extra
> work. (c) Add an LSP code action "Ignore \<identifier> on this line" that
> inserts or extends a `// @phpstan-ignore <id>` comment. It has to merge into
> an existing ignore comment on that line. Optional: (d) turn
> report_unmatched_ignored_errors (src/project/session.rs:59) on by default.
> Leave out scoped declaration-level ignores and `id(N)` counts, or keep them
> far behind an opt-in: they add new non-standard syntax and make matching more
> complex for little gain.

#### K210. Progress output for CLI and LSP

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Users can tell a slow run from a hung one. The editor shows real
  progress during the initial scan, which on big monorepos is the longest wait.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/progress.rs:414`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:215`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:133`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:2668`
- **Risks:** Output must never go to stdout, where it would corrupt json,
  checkstyle or junit. Throttle LSP notifications. It is an extra dependency
  (indicatif), or a small hand-rolled line renderer.
- **Verification:** Mago crates/orchestrator/src/progress.rs has only 182 lines,
  so the cited line 414 is wrong. create_progress_bar is at progress.rs:66. It
  adds the bar to GLOBAL_PROGRESS_MANAGER, which is a LazyLock\<MultiProgress>
  at line 44.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a small `Progress` trait in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs (or a
> new project/progress.rs):
> `fn phase(&self, name: &'static str, total: Option<usize>)` and
> `fn tick(&self)`, with `Sync` bounds, defaulting to a no-op. Keep the rest of
> the pipeline as it is.
>
> - Session::load (session.rs:594): call phase("parsing",
>   Some(combined_files.len())), then tick() inside the
>   `combined_files.par_iter().map(..)` closure (session.rs:625-629).
> - Session::analyse: call phase("analysing", Some(n)) around its per-file
>   parallel check loop. The serial or project-wide steps
>   (project.finish_loading(), the tier-2 dead-member and dead-enum-case passes,
>   the reporting step) each get a phase(name, None) call, so the display
>   switches to a spinner and a label instead of sitting at 100%.
> - Project::map_on_pool (project.rs:281) is used by the LSP and incremental
>   paths. Give it an optional `&dyn Progress` argument, or wrap f.
>
> CLI (crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:133): write a hand-rolled
> renderer to stderr that redraws one line with `\r` at most every ~100 ms,
> driven by an AtomicUsize, and clears the line before the report prints. This
> avoids adding indicatif as a dependency. Enable it only when
> stderr.is_terminal() (the file already uses IsTerminal at :263 for stdout
> colour), the format is text or table, and --no-progress, CI and NO_COLOR are
> not set.
>
> LSP (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:2663-2690): the scan runs synchronously
> inside handle_notification, and add_workspace_folders (lsp.rs:555) returns a
> Vec\<Message> after the fact, so Report messages cannot be emitted mid-scan
> without passing a sink down. Make the sink forward (done, total) over a
> crossbeam/std channel, or through a Mutex'd writer handle, and throttle to at
> most one message per 200 ms or 1% step. Send WorkDoneProgressBegin with
> percentage Some(0) and message "parsing 0/N", Reports with "parsing i/N" or
> "analysing i/N", then End. Extend the existing tests in
> lsp/tests/protocol_and_session.rs:299-363 so they accept 0..k report messages
> between begin and end.

#### K222. check-project --watch mode on the incremental Project

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp, config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Gives fast, persistent incremental checking in the terminal and
  in CI-like dev loops without an editor, using work the LSP already paid for.
  Only affected files are re-checked, whereas re-running check-project reloads
  about 2351 stub files and the whole project every time.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/analyze.rs:136`,
  `src/commands/analyze.rs:529`, `crates/database/src/watcher.rs:467`,
  `src/commands/analyze.rs:149`, `crates/database/src/watcher.rs:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:928`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:43`
- **Risks:** Batch mode with retain_source off still keeps ASTs, so long
  sessions keep peak memory at the batch figure (1.62GB on Piwigo).
  Whole-program checks need the per-file fact caching above to stay correct
  across edits. | Project must keep retain_source for incremental re-parsing,
  which raises memory. Whole-program passes need re-running or should be skipped
  in watch mode.
- **Verification:** Mago: the `watch` flag field is at
  src/commands/analyze.rs:136-149. Its doc comment says it watches mago.toml,
  baseline, composer.json and composer.lock, and the `#[arg]` is at line 148.
  The watch loop is at analyze.rs:~523-550.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add `--watch` to `check-project` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs,
> `run_check_project_command` at line 97), plus a `Session::analyse_retaining`
> in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs. It should run the same passes as
> `analyse` (line 689) and return the `Project` together with the per-file
> result map, instead of consuming the Project.
>
> Watch loop: (1) Watch `session.dirs()` and the scan dirs with `notify` (a new
> dependency; no crate has it today). (2) Debounce about 200-300ms and coalesce
> to the last event per path, the way `handle_watched_files_changed` does at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:783. Keep the 10ms stable re-read from Mago
> crates/database/src/watcher.rs:467. `lsp::debounce::DebounceQueue` is
> `pub(super)` and generation/cancel-oriented, so reuse or share it only if that
> is cheap. (3) Filter new paths through the session's own `collect_php_files`
> include/exclude logic. `update_file` already keeps an existing file's
> analyzed/context flag (project.rs:984-998). (4) For each path, call
> `Project::update_file` or `remove_file`. Merge the returned per-file maps into
> the retained full map, replacing keys. (5) Re-run the cheap project-wide
> passes that are pure functions of the registry: `check_class_shapes`,
> `check_banned`, `check_architecture` and `check_mock_hygiene`. (6) For
> `check_whole_program`, either rerun a full `check_files` when any
> whole-program rule is enabled, or mark those results stale in the summary
> line. The per-file facts they use are not maintained incrementally:
> `named_argument_calls` is gathered only in `analyse`, and `seed_member_refs`
> at project.rs:903 only extends the `escaped_*` sets. (7) Rebuild the
> post-filters through the existing
> `analysis.finalize(&run.finalize_options(baseline))` path and re-print. Clear
> the screen for text output. Print a delta and summary line to stderr. (8)
> Restart in-process when phpstan-rs.toml, the baseline, composer.json or
> composer.lock changes, as Mago does at src/commands/analyze.rs:524 and
> 572-586. Handle Ctrl-C cleanly.
>
> Reject `--watch` together with `--fix`, `--generate-baseline` and
> `--dump-types`.

#### K229. list-files and config introspection commands

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Configuration problems are the top support issue for analyzers
  ('why isn't X analyzed?', 'is doctrine active?'). phpstan-rs now has
  auto-activated extensions, composer-derived PHP ranges, path-repo promotion
  and moved keys, so the effective configuration isn't visible anywhere today.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/list_files.rs:112`,
  `src/commands/config.rs:1`, `src/config/mod.rs:628`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:33`,
  `crates/config/src/lib.rs:47`
- **Risks:** Showing the effective config needs Serialize on each Section, a
  mechanical change. Keep output stable if scripts come to depend on it.
- **Verification:** Mago: the citations are accurate. In
  src/commands/list_files.rs, execute at line 112 adds per-command excludes with
  --command (lines 113-120) and prints each database file (lines 124-126). The
  -0/--zero-terminate flag is at line 79.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `phpstan-rs show-config` subcommand, and `--list-files` on
> check-project, both built on the existing resolve step without parsing
> anything.
>
> 1. Split crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs `Session::resolve`
>    (line 265) into two parts. The first is a pure resolution that returns a
>    `ResolvedPlan` holding dirs, scan_dirs, scan_files, stub_dirs, composer
>    roots, `composer_php_versions` and the effective php_version with its
>    source (CLI, config or composer), the promoted path-repo packages, the
>    per-extension activation from src/ext.rs:47-65 (`is_active`) along with the
