>    reason (explicit `enabled` or the installed package that triggered it), and
>    the warnings. The second is the part that builds the Session. `Loaded` and
>    `prepare` in src/app/check_project.rs:60 would then take the plan.
>
> 2. `show-config [--config F] [--set K=V]... [--format toml|json]` prints
>    ConfigFile's merged toml::Value, after moves and --set. This value already
>    exists, so no `Serialize` derive is needed on the Section structs. After it
>    comes a "derived" block with the plan's values. Printing defaults can come
>    later: it needs `Serialize` or a defaults table per Section, because
>    crates/config/src/lib.rs:47-60 `Schema`/`RegisteredSection` only stores
>    field names and a check fn.
>
> 3. `check-project --list-files [-0]` runs the same file walk as `Loaded` and
>    prints each path with its tier (analyze, scan/vendor context, stub). With
>    `--verbose` it also prints the root that matched and the rule that dropped
>    a file (exclude, promotion, dedup). It then exits without parsing.
>
> 4. If discovery yields zero files, report whether no paths were given (resolve
>    already errors on this at session.rs:311) or every file was excluded, and
>    exit non-zero.
>
> Optionally, the LSP can expose the same plan through an executeCommand so
> editor users can check which extensions are active.

#### K232. Default paths from composer autoload and init command

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Zero-config first run on any Composer project, the common case,
  and a smooth path from PHPStan. Avoids Mago's silent 'nothing analyzed' result
  by being explicit.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/init.rs:779`, `src/commands/init.rs:771`,
  `src/config/source.rs:22`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:300`,
  `crates/composer/src/manifest.rs:20`
- **Risks:** A composer autoload that points at vendor-like or generated dirs
  would include them. Printing the chosen paths and supporting excludes covers
  that. A NEON import only needs the scalar and list subset.
- **Verification:** The citations are accurate, with three small
  clarifications. - Mago src/commands/init.rs:779-791
  (extract_paths_from_composer) reads only the psr-4 maps from autoload and
  autoload-dev. It ignores classmap and files.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build one shared resolver for "no paths configured" and use it in both front
> ends. Suggested home: a `default_analyze_paths(root, manifest)` next to
> `composer_roots` in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs, or in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/app/check_project.rs.
>
> (1) CLI config discovery. `load_config`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/app/check_project.rs:35-40) falls back to
> `ConfigFile::empty()` when there is no `--config`. It should first look for
> `./phpstan-rs.toml`, the same way the LSP already does in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/workspace_config.rs:64-66. Without this,
> "zero-config" never happens on the CLI even when a project has a config file.
>
> (2) Default paths. When `dirs` is empty (session.rs:289-302) and cwd holds a
> root composer.json, load it with `ComposerManifest::load`
> (crates/composer/src/manifest.rs:129). Take `autoload` plus `autoload_dev`:
> their psr4 dirs, classmap entries and files, deduplicated, keeping only paths
> that exist and are not under `DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES`. Drop any file
> where `manifest.excludes(section, file)` (manifest.rs:250) is true. Print
> `analyzing composer autoload paths: src, tests` to stderr.
>
> If there is no composer.json, or the autoload section is empty (common for
> legacy non-PSR apps), fall back to what the LSP already does with no
> configured paths: walk cwd with
> `collect_php_files_excluding(root, DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES)`
> (lsp.rs:503-508), and print that choice too. This replaces the hard error. The
> LSP's empty-`analyze_paths` branch should call the same resolver so the editor
> and CI analyze the same set.
>
> (3) A small `Init` subcommand in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:33 (the Command
> enum). It writes a commented phpstan-rs.toml with `paths` from the resolver.
> It prints the PHP range as a comment, taken from `declared_php_versions`
> (session.rs:225), and notes that the range is already applied automatically.
> Drop the proposed phpstan.neon import: baseline.rs:11-12 says baselines are
> JSON and there is no NEON parser, so the claim that "baseline.rs already reads
> NEON-shaped baselines" is false.

#### K241. Precise in-docblock diagnostic spans

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Squiggles land on the offending `@param` type rather than the
  function name, which matters most in the LSP. Precise spans are also required
  for docblock quick fixes (remove a stale tag, fix a param name) and for
  docblock-aware navigation.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/phpdoc-syntax/src/error.rs:63`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/mod.rs:209`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs:366`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:760`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:52`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs:40`, `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:64`
- **Risks:** Baseline/ignore matching keys on line numbers. Moving reports from
  the declaration line to the docblock line changes identity, so gate it or
  migrate baselines (convert-baseline exists). Multi-line joins need a careful
  offset map.
- **Verification:** Nearly all citations check out. Mago:
  phpdoc-syntax/src/error.rs has note() at ~:18 and help() at ~:46, and
  `impl HasSpan for ParseError` at ~:63. analyzer/src/context/mod.rs:204-238
  (get_parsed_docblocks) calls PHPDocParser::parse_with_span(trivia.span).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build it in two steps, and keep where a diagnostic is identified separate from
> where it is shown.
>
> (1) Record the docblock's start position on the AST. Add a
> `doc_start: Option<Position>` (or a span) next to each declaration's
> `doc_comment` in crates/syntax/src/ast.rs, filled from the
> `Parser::doc_comment_starts` map that already exists
> (crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:56, :102-115, :175). Change `take_doc_comment` to
> return the text and its start together. `Stmt.doc_line` (ast.rs:67, used in
> checker/stmt.rs:366) then becomes a special case of this field.
>
> (2) Give each tag its own position inside the comment, at line granularity. In
> crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/parser.rs (~:25-55), keep the source line index and
> the column of '@' for each entry in `tag_lines` before continuation lines are
> joined. Then offset `Lexer::new(rest)`'s relative spans by that index, which
> is exact for the first physical line of a tag. Do not put spans on every
> TypeNode yet. A tag-level span covers phpDoc.parseError, parameter.notFound,
> @param unresolvableType / phpDocType and varTag.\*, and it is enough for
> tag-level quick fixes such as deleting a stale `@param` or renaming its
> `$name`. That second one uses the existing
> `DiagnosticFix { span, replacement }` (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:173).
>
> (3) Keep ignore identity stable. Do not move `Diagnostic.span`. Existing
> `// @phpstan-ignore` comments and the report line are keyed to the declaration
> line, which is where checker/oop.rs:726-760 (`check_unknown_phpstan_tags_on`,
> `report_invalid_doc_tag_values`) and checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:52 report
> today. Moving the primary line would silently break those ignores. Add an
> optional `precise_span: Option<Span>` to `Diagnostic` (lib.rs:98) and a
> builder setter. The LSP uses it as the diagnostic range, with a
> relatedInformation entry pointing back at the declaration. CLI and table
> output can show it as a secondary location, or move the primary location later
> behind a config flag. Baselines are unaffected either way, because they match
> on message, file and count, not line (baseline.rs;
> tests/baseline_filtering.rs:282 merges entries that differ only by location).
>
> (4) Per-TypeNode spans, for pointing at an inner `Foo` in `array<int, Foo>`
> for class.notFound, are a later step. Put them in a side table filled during
> TagParser, not on the TypeNode enum, which is hash-consed and compared
> structurally.

#### K282. Add a dedicated diagnostic for a type alias used without import, with a did-you-mean import hint, no cascading errors, and optional program-wide aliases set in config

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: hir-lowering-ir)
- **Benefit:** The report turns into one actionable error instead of a
  misleading 'unknown class' plus follow-on noise. It also gives free functions
  and templates a supported way to share aliases.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/hir/src/lower/settings.rs:14`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/item/annotation/mod.rs:57`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/resolution/type.rs:173`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:606`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/var_tag_types.rs:289`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:686`
- **Risks:** The short-name match may be ambiguous when several classes declare
  the same alias; list all candidates. Configured aliases must not shadow real
  classes.
- **Verification:** The Mago lines are accurate, but they need context.
  crates/hir/src/lower/settings.rs:14-17 declares program_wide_type_aliases, and
  it defaults to true at :63. crates/hir/src/lower/item/annotation/mod.rs:57-64
  calls add_alias and, when the flag is set, add_program_alias.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split this into three independent pieces and ship them in this order.
>
> (1) Did-you-mean hint on the existing class.notFound report. Cost S. In
> Registry::resolve_deferred_type_imports
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:~674) or right after it, build an
> FxHashMap\<short alias name, Vec\<declaring class FQN>> from every ClassInfo's
> type_aliases. In Checker::check_type_class_names_exist
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:606), look up each unknown name's
> short form in that index and, when it matches, report a distinct identifier
> (typeAlias.notImported, or class.notFound plus a DiagnosticBuilder tip): "Row
> is a type alias declared on P\A. Import it with @phpstan-import-type Row from
> A." List every candidate class when several declare the same alias. Apply the
> same lookup at the other sites that report an unknown name through
> collect_unknown_class_names (@var tags via check_statement_var_tag_classes,
> and property/return subjects).
>
> (2) Cascade suppression. Cost S-M. When a PHPDoc @param/@return/@var type
> still contains an unresolvable class name after alias substitution, do not use
> that PHPDoc type for the parameter.phpDocType / return.phpDocType
> compatibility check
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:~116). Either skip the
> check or fall back to the native type. Do the same for the resolved variable
> type. Apply this to every unknown class, not only to aliases, because the
> cascade has the same cause for a misspelled class.
>
> (3) Program-wide aliases from config. Cost M. Add a type_aliases map to
> crates/config, parse the entries once into Types, and merge them as the
> lowest-precedence layer wherever class aliases are substituted today. There
> are at least eight such sites: registry/function_sig.rs:596-698
> build/substitute, checker/var_tag_types.rs:289,
> checker/phpdoc_unresolvable.rs:322, checker/generics/bounds.rs:229/551,
> checker/function_decl.rs:381, checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:194/330,
> checker/oop.rs:295, checker/generics/ancestors.rs:407. It must also cover the
> current_class == None path, so free functions get aliases. A configured alias
> whose name collides with a real class should be a config error (or the class
> should win, reported once). It must not be flagged as class.notFound.

#### K141. Default report level vs CLI help mismatch

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Users who trust the help text currently miss the whole
  nullable/union-safety class of bugs, the most common PHP runtime error.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/code.rs:680`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:38`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:23`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/rule_level_helper.rs:34`
- **Risks:** Changing the default increases output for existing users. The
  'hidden findings' note avoids that.
- **Verification:** All the phpstan-rs citations are accurate.
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:36-38 has the doc comment "every
  level this project's diagnostics are tagged with" on
  `DEFAULT_REPORT_LEVEL: u8 = 6`, and session.rs:303-307 uses it as the fallback
  when neither the CLI nor the config sets a level.
- **Refined proposal:**

> The half of this proposal that fixes the docs is already planned, so it adds
> nothing new. CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:2029-2031 (item C1, "Tests and docs") already
> says the check-project help will be corrected to "`--level` unset caps at
> `DEFAULT_REPORT_LEVEL` 6". Two small pieces are new and worth adding to that
> same C1 item.
>
> (1) Fix the other stale doc comment in the same pass. At
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:36-37, DEFAULT_REPORT_LEVEL's comment
> says "every level this project's diagnostics are tagged with". That is false:
> RuleLevelHelper::failing_level at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/rule_level_helper.rs:33-49 tags diagnostics at
> levels 7 and 8. The comment should say 6 is the default cap and that
> union-member (7) and nullable (8) findings sit above it.
> crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:80-95 lists the levels only up to 6, so extend
> it with 7 and 8.
>
> (2) Show a hidden-findings note. Session resolves the level at
> session.rs:303-307. Where the report is filtered, count the diagnostics
> dropped only because diagnostic.level > level (after ignore/baseline
> filtering, so ignored ones are not counted). When that count is non-zero and
> nobody set a level (report_level and configured_level are both None),
> check-project prints one line to stderr: "N findings above level 6 not shown
> (nullable/partial-union checks); pass --level 8 or set level in config". Skip
> the note for machine-readable output formats and in the LSP.
>
> Keep DEFAULT_REPORT_LEVEL at 6. Raising the default is a policy decision for
> the maintainer, not a bug fix.

#### K191. Extension introspection command

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Auto-activation from composer packages is convenient but opaque,
  and users can't easily tell why Doctrine typing or PSR-3 checks are or aren't
  running. This makes it self-explanatory and debuggable.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/plugin.rs:7`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/mod.rs:21`,
  `docs/content/en/extensions/analyzer/overview.md:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext.rs:30`,
  `crates/config/src/lib.rs:25`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:33`
- **Risks:** None of substance; the output format isn't a stable contract.
- **Verification:** All the phpstan-rs citations are accurate.
  crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext.rs:30 has ActiveExtensions as 13 bare bools, and
  resolve at :50 throws the reason away. crates/config/src/lib.rs:25-38 defines
  the Extension trait with PACKAGES, enabled() and is_active(), which returns
  only a bool.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep it minimal and reuse what already exists rather than adding NAME consts:
>
> 1. crates/config/src/lib.rs:25-37 (trait Extension): add
>    `fn activation(&self, installed: &dyn Fn(&str)->bool) -> Activation`
>    returning `Explicit(bool)` when `enabled()` is Some,
>    `Package(&'static str)` for the first matching entry of `Self::PACKAGES`,
>    else `Inactive`. Reimplement `is_active` on top of it so the two can't
>    disagree. The display name comes from the existing `Section::PATH` (e.g.
>    ["ext","doctrine"] prints as `ext.doctrine`). A one-line doc string is
>    optional, and only worth it if it also feeds a `--help`-style listing.
> 2. crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext.rs:47-78: add
>    `ActiveExtensions::explain(config, installed) -> Vec<(dotted path,
>    Activation, &'static [&str] packages)>`
>    built by the same generic helper as `resolve`, so the extension list stays
>    in one place (or build a single table that both `resolve` and `explain`
>    iterate).
> 3. crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:33: add
>    `Extensions { dir: Option<PathBuf> }`, which runs the same config discovery
>    and root-manifest loading as project/session.rs:429 (pull that small piece
>    out into a helper instead of copying it) and prints one line per extension:
>    path, active/inactive, and the reason ("enabled = true in phpstan-rs.toml",
>    "package phpstan/phpstan-doctrine installed", "no package from [..]
>    installed; set enabled = true to force"). Leave resolved per-check flags
>    out of the first version.
> 4. Optional: log the same summary once in the LSP `initialize`
>    (lsp/workspace_config.rs:157), sent at log level so it doesn't nag. Out of
>    scope: the non-Extension `[ext.sql]` section and Mago-style plugin aliases.

#### K204. Richer JSON output

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Tools such as reviewdog, custom bots or editor plugins without
  LSP can highlight exact ranges and apply suggested fixes themselves, without
  re-running the analyzer or parsing text.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/reporting/src/internal/mod.rs:59`,
  `crates/reporting/src/formatter/json.rs:24`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs:82`
- **Risks:** Only additive schema changes, so existing consumers keep working.
- **Verification:** Mago: ExpandedIssue is at
  crates/reporting/src/internal/mod.rs:58-76 and serializes level, code,
  message, notes, help, link, annotations and edits. The file/offset/line claim
  needs one correction.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Make only additive changes to crates/phpstan-rs/src/output.rs JSON rendering,
> and only for data that already exists on diagnostics::Diagnostic
> (crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:98-121):
>
> 1. JsonMessage gets `end_line`/`end_column` from d.span.end. The span is
>    already there; codeframe.rs:147 uses it, but JSON drops it.
> 2. JsonMessage gets `tips: Vec<&str>` (keep the joined `tip` so existing
>    consumers still work) and `non_ignorable: bool`, left out when false.
> 3. JsonMessage gets
>    `fix: Option<{description, start_line, start_column, end_line, end_column,
>    replacement}>`.
>    The span is resolved through diagnostics::fix::resolve_span
>    (crates/diagnostics/src/fix.rs:35), the same way lsp/protocol.rs:318 does
>    it. That means render_json needs each file's source text, which
>    check_project.rs already reads for --fix (lines 215-230), so pass a source
>    lookup in. Say plainly in the output that columns are 1-based character
>    counts, not bytes.
> 4. Fix a real gap in the JSON output: the Json arm in
>    main/check_project.rs:302-304 leaves out `check_panics` (internal errors)
>    and the parse-error skip counts, which the Text arm prints (lines 278-297).
>    Add `errors: [{file, message}]` and `totals.files_skipped_parse_error`, so
>    a CI consumer can't read a crashed run as clean.
> 5. Add a top-level `"version": 1`. Leave out `severity` and `related`:
>    Diagnostic has neither field, and adding them is separate diagnostics-model
>    work, not an output change. Extend the tests in output/tests.rs.

#### K252. Docblocks that drop native union members

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Surfaces docblocks that do not mean what their authors think: the
  author believes the parameter is int, while phpstan-rs, correctly, still types
  it int|string. The fix is to widen the doc or tighten the native type. This
  keeps phpstan-rs's sound choice and adds the UX Mago gets from a riskier
  approach.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:420`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/decide.rs:13`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs:106`
- **Risks:** `@param Foo` on `?Foo $x = null` is extremely common and
  intentional, so exempt null when the native default is null
  (apply_implicit_nullable_default), or keep the check opt-in.
- **Verification:** The Mago citation is accurate. In
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs, lines 386-420 hold the
  incompatibility branch (DocblockTypeMismatch).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a helper in crates/types/src/decide.rs, for example
> `pub fn native_members_kept_uncovered(doc: &Type, native: &Type) -> Vec<Type>`.
> It must reuse the exact backfill predicate that reconcile_with_native already
> uses (decide.rs:57-73): the native member is `native_member_addable`
> (decide.rs:114), no surviving doc member is its subtype, and it applies the
> same skip conditions (deferred value-of, conditional, template-referencing
> members, empty `kept`). Sharing the predicate means the diagnostic names
> exactly the branches inference keeps, with no second, drifting membership
> logic.
>
> In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/phpdoc_type_compat.rs, next to the `@param`
> call to report_phpdoc_native_mismatch (~line 106), call the helper when
> `registry.is_super_type_of(native, doc)` is Yes. That is the case
> report_phpdoc_native_mismatch at line 632 returns early and says nothing. If
> the helper returns anything, report `parameter.phpDocDropsNative`, for
> example: "PHPDoc tag @param for parameter \$x with type int does not cover
> string from native type int|string; string is still accepted and kept." Skip
> these cases:
>
> - null, when the parameter's default is null (implicit/explicit
>   `?Foo $x = null`)
> - overriding methods, where the native type may be widened because the parent
>   requires it
> - variadic element rewrites
>
> Optionally do the same for `@return`, where a dropped native branch means the
> reconciled return type silently widens. Gate it behind an opt-in
> Registry/config flag, following the existing opt-in-check pattern. Add
> fixtures for:
>
> - `int|string` with `@param int` (reported)
> - `?Foo $x` with no default and `@param Foo` (reported)
> - `?Foo $x = null` (not reported)
> - a template doc (not reported)
> - `string|array` with `@param array<int,string>` (not reported, because the
>   doc refines array)

#### K264. Fixture harness multiplicity-aware diff and orphan detection

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** Duplicate-diagnostic regressions, a real class of bugs where the
  same check fires twice from two paths, get reported correctly. Forgotten
  .expect files can no longer leave a fixture untested without anyone noticing.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/tests/framework.rs:175`,
  `crates/analyzer/tests/mod.rs:2785`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:270`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:54`
- **Risks:** Minimal. The orphan check must skip files inside directory
  fixtures, which collect() already tells apart through
  with_extension("expect").
- **Verification:** Mago: verify_reported_issues is defined at
  crates/analyzer/tests/framework.rs:174, and the BTreeMap\<String, usize> of
  counts per code is at lines 179-186. It isn't a comparison of expected against
  actual, though.
- **Refined proposal:**

> In crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs, replace diff() (lines 270-289) with a
> positional line diff: either a small LCS/Myers over the two line vectors (~40
> lines, no new dependency) or the `similar` crate as a dev-dependency
> (TextDiff::from_lines with unified_diff and a few lines of context). Print
> expectation line numbers so a reviewer can see where the change is. Drop the
> "(same lines, different order)" fallback; a positional diff already shows
> reorders. In collect() (lines 43-71), gather the stems of every .php/.toml
> file that is neither next to an X.expect nor inside a directory whose sibling
> X.expect exists, which is the same with_extension("expect") test the dir
> branch already uses. For each such stem, push a Trial::test("orphan/\<name>",
> || Err("no .expect; run PHPSTAN_RS_BLESS=1 to create one"))). Also consider
> having bless create a missing X.expect for an orphan X.php, so the one-command
> workflow still works.

#### K294. Anchor return.unusedType at the return-type node and check docblock and native declarations separately

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: analyzer-behaviour-settings)
- **Benefit:** LSP users see the squiggle on the type they need to edit, and a
  redundant `|false` in the native hint is reported even when the docblock is
  already accurate. Removing `false` from the native signature is what fixes the
  runtime contract, because native types are what the engine enforces.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:967`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:1035`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:1173`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:632`
- **Risks:** Checking both declarations can report the same member twice when
  both carry it. Dedupe per member, preferring the native span.
- **Verification:** Mago: the second check of the native declaration when the
  docblock overrides the return type is at
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/function_like/mod.rs:953-962, not 967.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep only the anchoring half. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:1168-1174, pass
> `f.return_type.as_ref().map(|h| h.span).unwrap_or(f.span)` into
> check_too_wide_return_type instead of `f.span`. This is the same expression
> return.neverCandidate already uses at function_decl.rs:1093, and it also
> appears at function_like_declarations.rs:68, internal_usage.rs:499 and
> restricted_symbol_usage.rs:912.
>
> Optional refinement: when the native hint is a TypeHintKind::Union
> (crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:1003-1015, where every child TypeHint carries its
> own span), anchor each unused member at the child hint whose native type it
> narrows. That puts the squiggle on `false` in `string|false`. Fall back to the
> whole hint's span for members that only come from the docblock, because phpdoc
> TypeNodes carry no source spans (crates/phpdoc/src/docblock.rs:20).
>
> Do the same for check_too_wide_throw_type (function_decl.rs:1141, also
> f.span), anchored at the function name or the doc comment.
>
> Drop the second half, the separate native pass. It adds nothing, as the
> reasoning below explains.
>
> A message that includes the narrowed type ("...; declare it as `string`") is
> cheap to add in return_type_too_wide.rs:115-122 by filtering
> declared.union_members(). Only do that if a fix engine will actually consume
> it.

#### K302. No-op runtime definitions for assertType and a dumpType probe shipped in the Composer package

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** Users can see what the analyzer infers without an LSP hover: in
  CI logs, in bug reports and while writing extensions. Probe calls no longer
  crash at runtime, and the handler stops capturing unrelated user functions.
- **Mago evidence:** `composer/src/functions.php:8`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:174`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:457`
- **Risks:** The dump diagnostic has to be excluded from baselines and fail
  thresholds, or it will break builds. Reusing PHPStan's own namespaced names
  could clash with phpstan/phpstan if both are installed; the function_exists
  guards handle that.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. composer/src/functions.php:9-22
  defines Mago\inspect and :24-39 defines Mago\confirm, both as empty void
  functions behind function_exists guards. composer.json:22-25 in the Mago repo
  root puts that file in autoload "files".
- **Refined proposal:**

> Drop the "ship a Composer package" part. phpstan-rs has no Composer package
> (the repo has no root composer.json, and distribution is the binary plus
> editors/vscode), and the PHPStan names already have runtime definitions:
> vendor/phpstan-src/composer.json:157 autoloads src/dumpType.php and
> src/Testing/functions.php, so any project with phpstan/phpstan installed has
> them. A first-party `PhpstanRs\` namespace is not needed. Keep the two
> analyzer-side changes in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs, around line
> 457: (1) Resolve the callee through `self.registry.resolve_function` (the same
> way the code a few lines below does for `resolved_name`). Fire the assertType
> handler only when the resolved FQN case-folds to `phpstan\testing\asserttype`.
> Those stubs are already indexed (crates/stub-sources/index.tsv:14951-14958).
> Keep a bare global `assertType` only if fixtures depend on it; otherwise
> switch the fixtures to the FQN. (2) Add `phpstan\dumptype`, and also
> `dumpnativetype`/`dumpphpdoctype`, which are indexed too. These report
> `Dumped type: <T>` at the argument's span with their own identifier (e.g.
> phpstanRs.dumpType) and evaluate to void/null. Exclude that identifier from
> baseline generation and from the exit code / fail threshold. That fits the
> per-call report path already used for assertType. The same resolver can add
> assertNativeType, assertSuperType and assertVariableCertainty later.

#### K167. Scoped and counted suppression pragmas

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** Finer-grained, self-documenting suppression than baselines.
  Counted and expect pragmas stop suppressions from silently covering new bugs.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/collector/src/pragma.rs:58`,
  `crates/collector/src/pragma.rs:98`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_comments.rs:1`
- **Risks:** A new pragma syntax diverges from PHPStan, so use a distinct
  prefix. Scoped ignores can hide too much, so pair them with unmatched-ignore
  reporting.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate. In
  crates/collector/src/pragma.rs, `PragmaKind { Ignore, Expect }` is at about
  lines 55-63. The `Pragma` struct follows at about lines 66-96, with
  `scope_span`, `count_span`, `expected_matches`, `matches` and `description`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build only part (a), with an optional count, and fold it into the machinery
> that already exists. Drop part (c) as a user-facing pragma.
>
> 1. crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_comments.rs: add
>    `scoped: Vec<ScopedIgnore { start_line, end_line, ids: Vec<(String,
>    Option<u16>)> }>`
>    to `IgnoreComments`. Fill it from a `@phpstan-rs-ignore <ids>` tag, which
>    needs a distinct prefix, reusing `parse_identifiers` so the
>    `ignore.parseError` path and its messages carry over. The tag sits in the
>    docblock of a function, method, class-like or property, and optionally on a
>    statement. The span comes from the declaration's AST node, the way
>    `trait_line_ranges(&file.ast)` in project.rs already gets line ranges, not
>    from comment position heuristics. An id may carry a `(N)` suffix.
> 2. crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs `apply_inline_ignores` (~l.499-583): after
>    the line and identifier checks, match the diagnostic's identifier against
>    the innermost enclosing scoped entry and count per (entry, id). With
>    `report_unmatched`, report `ignore.unmatchedIdentifier` for a scoped id
>    that matched nothing, and a new non-ignorable `ignore.countMismatch` when a
>    counted id's match count differs from N. Keep the existing trait exclusion.
> 3. Also enforce `IgnoreErrorEntry::count` in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs:43-55, the same count-mismatch idea
>    applied to config entries. It is parsed today but not enforced, and the
>    same count code can serve both.
> 4. Leave PHPStan's `@phpstan-ignore*` syntax unchanged. Skip
>    `@phpstan-rs-expect`: the project's own regression tests already use
>    .php/.expect fixtures, and in user code an unmatched-reporting counted
>    ignore already flags a suppression that went stale.

#### K182. Architecture config ergonomics

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Replaces long lists of pairwise rules with one layering line,
  makes common policies (Contracts namespace holds only interfaces, controllers
  expose only \_\_invoke) one-liners, and gives precise ignore/baseline
  granularity.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/guard/src/settings.rs:39`,
  `crates/guard/src/perimeter/checker.rs:100`,
  `crates/guard/src/settings.rs:103`, `crates/guard/src/report/breach.rs:30`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/architecture.rs:61`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:405`
- **Risks:** Config-surface growth. Keep the new keys orthogonal and validated
  at startup through ArchitectureRule::validate. Identifier changes affect
  existing baselines, so keep architecture.dependency as the prefix.
- **Verification:** Mago citations check out. mago
  crates/guard/src/settings.rs:39 is PerimeterSettings { layers:
  HashMap\<String, Vec\<Path>>, layering: Vec\<NamespacePath>, rules,
  restrictions }. StructuralRule is at :103, must_be at :111 and
  only_public_methods at :129.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Split the proposal and ship it in this order.
>
> (1) Layers and layering in crates/phpstan-rs/src/architecture.rs. Add
> `[[rules.architecture_layers]] { name, selectors = [...] }` and
> `rules.architecture_layering = [...]`. Let a Selector carry `layer = "x"`,
> which is resolved at config load. Expand the layering list into one synthetic
> ArchitectureRule per layer: `classes` = that layer's selectors,
> `can_only_depend_on` = the same layer plus every lower layer, and a name like
> "layering: domain". Existing ArchitectureRule::validate (architecture.rs:139)
> then checks these rules, and Project::check_architecture
> (project/architecture.rs:257) needs no change. Reject at load time any unknown
> layer, any duplicate layer, and any `layer` key combined with other selector
> fields.
>
> (2) Kind assertion `should_be_kind = ["interface", "enum", ...]` in
> check_rule. It reuses the ClassKind tests already in Context::matches
> (project/architecture.rs:208-233). This is simpler than a new selector because
> Selector already has is_interface, is_enum and so on (architecture.rs:49-56).
> Only the assertion side is missing.
>
> (3) `allowed_public_methods = ["__invoke"]` next to
> should_have_only_one_public_method. It checks decl.public_methods
> (project/architecture.rs:616) with a case-insensitive match.
>
> (4) Lowest priority: dependency vectors. class_dependencies
> (project/architecture.rs:317-381) keeps one Dependency per target and the
> first span it sees; `constructed` is the only kind it tracks. Signature types
> from the registry are all reported at decl.name_span. Per-vector identifiers
> would therefore need one Dependency per (target, vector). Treat the vector as
> rule policy first: add an optional
> `dependency_kinds = ["new", "static_call", "extends", "type", "attribute", "phpdoc"]`
> filter on should_not_depend_on / can_only_depend_on. Put the vector in the
> message. Keep the identifier architecture.dependency, adding an optional
> suffix only if users ask. That way existing baselines stay valid.
>
> Leave function and constant structural rules out until class-level rules have
> users who need them.

#### K255. Surface complexity cap hits

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: robustness-limits)
- **Benefit:** Explains precision loss that currently looks like a false
  positive or negative, and gives the hang and slowness report something
  actionable.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs:356`,
  `crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:22`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/union.rs:10`,
  `crates/types/src/offsets.rs:8`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:330`
- **Risks:** Could be noisy if turned on by default, so ship it opt-in.
- **Verification:** All cited paths and line numbers are correct, with one
  caveat about how Mago is described. Mago: - In
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/loop/mod.rs, the report is at lines ~358-375,
  not 356.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep only the loop part, and make it a developer trace rather than a user
> rule. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs converge_loop_body
> (MAX_PASSES=6, WIDEN_FROM_PASS=2, exit at line 368
> `if next_entry == pass_entry || is_last_allowed_pass`), when the loop exits
> because `is_last_allowed_pass` is true and `next_entry != pass_entry`, print a
> debug-only note with the loop span and the names of the locals that are still
> changing. The `changing` Vec is already built just above for widening, so the
> names are available. Gate it behind an existing verbose/debug switch or an env
> var, not a `loop.notConverged` diagnostic identifier. Do not add a union/shape
> cap counter in crates/types. MAX_UNION_MEMBERS (crates/types/src/union.rs:10)
> is applied inside `intern::memoized(Operation::Union, ...)`, so a cache hit
> skips the cap path and a counter would undercount. Reading it back per
> statement would also put new state on the hot interned-type path to report
> something the user can't act on.

#### K275. Honour _ prefix for intentionally unused names

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: dead-code-references)
- **Benefit:** Gives a local, self-documenting suppression without a baseline or
  ignore entry, which matters once opt-in unused checks are enabled.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:113`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs:509`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs:62`
- **Risks:** Renaming a parameter breaks callers that use named arguments, so
  for public methods the fix should be marked unsafe or offered only for private
  methods, closures and constructors.
- **Verification:** All the Mago citations check out. In
  crates/analyzer/src/statement/class_like/unused_members.rs, line 113 skips
  `$_` properties, line 176 skips `_` methods and line 436 skips `$_` properties
  in a second check.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Apply the `_` opt-out only where the unused name is part of a signature the
> author has to keep. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/unused.rs::check_unused_constructor_parameters
> (line 39), add `p.name.starts_with('_')` to the skip condition next to
> `usage.contains(&p.name)` at line 63. Any future unused
> function/method-parameter or unused-local-variable check should use the same
> shared helper, e.g. `fn is_intentionally_unused(name: &str) -> bool`. Do NOT
> apply it to check_unused_closure_uses (line 109) or
> check_unused_private_members (line 138). A `use($x)` capture is never dictated
> from outside, so removing it is always the right fix. A leading `_` on private
> methods and properties is the PHP4/PEAR/Zend1/CodeIgniter way of marking them
> private, not a way of marking them unused, so honouring it would silently hide
> real dead code in legacy projects. A quick fix that inserts `_` should come
> only with the constructor-parameter diagnostic, which today has no fix at all
> (report(), line 77). Mark it as a non-preferred/unsafe fix, or skip it when
> the project has a named-argument call site that passes that parameter
> (`new Foo(name: ...)`), because renaming the parameter breaks those callers.
> Add fixture tests covering `$_unused` in a constructor, and showing that a
> `_legacyPrivate()` method that is never called is still reported.

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary

- **Benefit:** Flags such as those on check-project, and the new dump

> Add `clap_complete` to crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml, pinned to the release
