### 3.7 architecture (12)

#### K91. Persistent CNF clause set in Locals

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Adds real reasoning between variables: generalized disjunctive
  syllogism, guard clauses with two variables, compound flags, and nested &&
  inside ||. It is also the base for paradox/redundancy diagnostics and a single
  engine for if, match and ternary.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:92`,
  `crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:111`, `crates/analyzer/src/statement/if.rs:393`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/if.rs:168`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/block.rs:379`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:174`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:1161`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs:29`
- **Risks:** Loop fixpoint equality must include clauses, or convergence may
  oscillate; Mago strips clauses with mixed variables in loops
  (formula.rs:1030-1047). There is a performance cost on condition-heavy code,
  so caps are needed. Clause key identity must match narrowing_key exactly. The
  change is large and touches check_if, loops, match and merge; ship it after
  the cheaper merge-based idea.
- **Verification:** All citations were checked and are correct. Mago:
  block.rs:92 `pub clauses: Vec<Rc<Clause>>`. The caps are at
  algebra/src/lib.rs:21-31. `saturate_clauses` is at lib.rs:111, and its
  literal_index fast path is at about lines 129-146.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep the goal (disjunctive facts that live on in Locals past the if statement)
> but drop the Mago-style Atom enum and the full resolution/consensus engine.
> Reuse phpstan-rs's own narrowing as the literal semantics.
>
> 1. New `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing/formula.rs`:
>    - `Literal { leaf: Rc<Expr>, positive: bool, keys: SmallVec<[String; 2]> }`.
>      The `keys` come from `narrowing_key` over the leaf's subjects.
>    - Leaves are normalized so a comparison and its negation share one leaf:
>      `!==` becomes the negated `===`, `!=` becomes the negated `==`, and `!e`
>      flips the polarity.
>    - Equality on a literal is structural and ignores spans. Two `===` leaves
>      against different literals are different leaves, so the unsoundness that
>      `disjunctive_syllogism_atom_key` guards against (narrowing.rs:166-184)
>      cannot happen.
>    - `Clause = Rc<SmallVec<[Literal; 4]>>`.
>    - `cnf_of(cond) -> Option<Vec<Clause>>`: `&&` concatenates, `||` is a
>      capped cartesian product, `!` is De Morgan with a cap. Past the cap it
>      returns None and nothing is recorded, so today's behaviour stays
>      unchanged.
> 2. Add `clauses: imbl::Vector<Clause>` to Locals (locals.rs:29), next to the
>    existing side maps. Like `condition_aliases`, leave it out of `PartialEq`
>    (locals.rs:340).
> 3. Propagation is semantic, with no resolution step. After any narrowing
>    (`apply_narrowing` in check_if, ternary, match arms, and the `&&`/`||`
>    rhs), walk each stored clause:
>    - A literal is refuted when applying it through
>      `apply_narrowing(leaf, scratch, positive)` on a scratch clone drives one
>      of its keys to never.
>    - A clause is satisfied when applying the negated literal drives a key to
>      never. Satisfied clauses are dropped.
>    - When exactly one literal is left, apply it to the real locals through
>      `apply_narrowing`.
>    - Iterate to a small fixpoint (a cap of 2-3 rounds).
>    Every existing narrowing arm (is_\*, instanceof, isset, null comparisons,
>    truthiness, `(bool)` casts) then takes part automatically, with no second
>    atom vocabulary to keep in sync with apply_narrowing.
> 4. Recording facts:
>    - check_if pushes cnf(cond) into then_locals and cnf(!cond) into
>      else_locals, before each body is checked.
>    - Because stmt.rs:1235-1237 already keeps only the surviving branch's
>      locals, the guard `if ($a===null && $b===null) return;` leaves the clause
>      (a!==null ∨ b!==null) with no extra work.
>    - `$ok = <cond>` records the clauses under the flag's truth: extend
>      `record_condition_alias` (narrowing.rs:1370) to store the CNF,
>      conditioned on the flag's literal. That covers the compound-flag case.
> 5. Invalidation: `Locals::declare` (locals.rs:129) and
>    `purge_stale_narrowing_for` (narrowing/predicates.rs:276) drop every clause
>    with a key that satisfies `key_depends_on` (predicates.rs:308).
> 6. `merge_scopes` (control_flow.rs:563) keeps only clauses present in both
>    inputs.
> 7. Loops: at loop entry `converge_loop_body` (control_flow.rs:302) strips
>    clauses that mention any variable assigned in the body, as Mago's
>    remove_clauses_with_mixed_variables does (formula.rs:1030). Clauses only
>    ever shrink, so the types-only fixpoint equality stays sound.
> 8. `pending_or_disjunctions` (stmt.rs:1161-1190) and
>    `apply_disjunctive_syllogism` (narrowing.rs:273) then become redundant and
>    can be deleted. Condition-alias replay can later collapse into the same
>    store, in line with the recent design direction of one holder instead of
>    more side maps.
>
> Tests: fixtures for the five probes, which I confirmed today. For the guard,
> the `||` case and the compound flag, phpstan-rs reports `int|null` where Mago
> proves int. Negative fixtures: any reassignment inside a branch kills the
> clause; `===1`/`===2` stay separate leaves; clauses do not leak out of loops.

#### K228. Shared workspace resolver and membership matcher

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Fixes a class of CLI-vs-editor divergences in one place:
  different diagnostics for the same file, new files classified wrongly, and
  path-repo packages analyzed in the CLI but not in the LSP. Every future config
  key then works in both front ends automatically.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/utils/mod.rs:69`,
  `crates/database/src/membership.rs:33`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/workspace_config.rs:59`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1000`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:504`
- **Risks:** The LSP needs Degrade behaviour, where a bad key must not kill the
  session. The resolver should return (value, Vec\<warning>) instead of
  early-returning. It also touches the load-order invariants documented in
  lsp.rs:470-479.
- **Verification:** Mago: - src/utils/mod.rs:69 is correct. create_orchestrator
  builds the single OrchestratorConfiguration (lines 93-112), and analyze, lint,
  list-files, guard, format and cst all call it. -
  crates/database/src/membership.rs:33 overstates things.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/workspace.rs holding a `WorkspaceSpec` that
> both front ends build from. Move the body of `Session::resolve`
> (project/session.rs:265 onward) into
> `WorkspaceSpec::resolve(config, config_dir, root, overrides, mode)`. `mode` is
> Fail for the CLI and Degrade for the LSP. It returns
> `(WorkspaceSpec, Vec<String> warnings)`: in Fail mode the first warning
> becomes an Err, and in Degrade mode each section error falls back to
> `S::default()`, the way the local `section()` helper does at
> lsp/workspace_config.rs:81. The spec holds:
>
> - the ProjectSettings
> - analyzed dirs after path-repository promotion
> - context dirs and files, built from `composer_roots` for each path
>   (session.rs:236, 385-414)
> - stub dirs, the baseline and ignore entries
> - the checker-side rule sets: banned_constructs, parent_call_rules,
>   architecture_rules and mockstan (session.rs:316-324, 471)
>
> `Session` then becomes a thin wrapper around the spec plus the thread pool.
> lsp/workspace_config.rs::resolve (lines 59-227) is deleted, and
> `Server::configure_from_workspace` (lsp.rs:338, 1882) consumes the spec. The
> LSP-only fields, `retain_source: true` and `defer_inline_ignores`, are applied
> afterwards.
>
> Also add a
> `WorkspaceMatcher { analyzed_roots, context_roots, excluded_dir_names }` with
> `classify(&Path) -> Option<Tier>`. Store it in ProjectSettings and use it in
> three places:
>
> - `Project::update_file` for paths it has never seen (project.rs:996-1001), in
>   place of the bare `DEFAULT_SCAN_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` test. A new
>   tests/foo.php stays context when paths=["src"].
> - `Server::load_workspace_files` (lsp.rs:480-540).
> - `Session::load` (session.rs:594).
>
> Either both walks share one file-discovery function that does the canonical
> dedup (lsp.rs:494, 529), or the matcher encodes the difference on purpose.
> Keep the context-before-analyzed load order that lsp.rs:470-479 documents: the
> spec only supplies the file lists, and the caller keeps the order. Add a test
> that resolves one config through both modes and asserts the two specs are
> equal, which guards against future drift.

#### K238. Lower TypeNode directly to Type

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, L (aspect: phpdoc)
- **Benefit:** Correctness: removes a whole class of text-splitting bugs (quoted
  keys containing ':' / ',' / '|', escaped quotes, callable return types inside
  shapes); the quoted-key bug is already confirmed. Performance: one parse
  instead of parse, print and re-parse for every docblock type, including the
  ~2351 stub files parsed at every startup. Maintainability: one type grammar
  instead of two.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/ttype/builder.rs:91`,
  `crates/codex/src/ttype/error.rs:6`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/type_node.rs:8`,
  `crates/types/src/parse.rs:412`, `crates/types/src/parse.rs:612`,
  `crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/ast.rs:207`
- **Risks:** types/src/parse.rs holds a lot of accumulated special-casing
  (callable templates, DNF groups, value-of deferral, int bounds), and all of it
  must be ported case by case. The existing unit tests of parse_type_string are
  the oracle, so run both paths side by side during migration and diff the
  results.
- **Verification:** Nearly every citation is accurate. One small correction on
  Mago: crates/codex/src/ttype/error.rs:6 is
  `pub enum TypeError { UnsupportedType(String, Span), InvalidType(String,
  String, Span) }`.
  The variants hold the type text, a message and a Span.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a structural lowering
> `lower(node: &phpdoc::grammar::TypeNode) -> types::Type` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/type_node.rs. It goes there because
> crates/types/Cargo.toml depends only on rustc-hash and syntax, not phpdoc, and
> adding that crate edge is optional. The lowering matches every TypeNode
> variant (crates/phpdoc/src/grammar/ast.rs:105ff): Identifier, Nullable, Union,
> Intersection, Generic, Wildcard, VarianceArg, ArrayOf, OffsetAccess,
> ArrayShape (with the typed ShapeKey::{Int,String,Identifier} at ast.rs:367, so
> no quote stripping is needed), Callable (with templates), IntRange, the
> literals, ConstFetch, Conditional and Paren.
>
> Split crates/types/src/parse.rs so the semantic half is public and works on
> already-structured input. Today parse_type_keyword_or_class(bare, original,
> generic_args: &[&str]) at parse.rs:845 takes its arguments as text. Change it
> to take `&[Type]`, or a small arg enum for int bounds and key-of/value-of
> deferral, and put canonical_int_key, mark_callable_templates and the int-bound
> handling behind that API. Then both the text path and `lower` call the same
> keyword resolver.
>
> Change parse_type_node and mentions_mixed (type_node.rs:8,14) to use `lower`,
> plus a structural mentions-mixed walk. Keep `to_source_string` for its other
> users (mock_hygiene.rs:183/416, docblock.rs:747).
>
> The 251 internal parse_type_string/parse_written_type call sites are mostly
> literal strings in stubs.rs, predefined_constants.rs, class_info.rs and so on.
> Leave them on the text parser at first. Move them in a second step to
> `phpdoc::grammar::parse_type(..)` + `lower`, and only then delete
> split_top_level, looks_like_shape_key, try_parse_array_shape and the other
> text heuristics.
>
> During migration, run a debug-assert or test harness that lowers every
> docblock type both ways and diffs the results, over the fixtures and the stub
> corpus. Also check that the grammar parser covers every input the lenient text
> parser accepted, and decide what an unparseable node lowers to.

#### K39. Separate declared (own) class state from derived/inherited state and rebuild derived data from scratch

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: codebase-model, incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Fixes the documented incremental staleness in
  project.rs:1105-1136 (a removed parent, trait method or mixin keeps its
  effects), which is a correctness problem for the LSP. Removes the O(hosts ×
  trait members × passes) cloning of FunctionReflections, cutting both memory
  (stub traits and vendor traits are copied into every host) and build time.
  Makes derived state reproducible, so incremental and batch results match.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:72`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:111`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/methods.rs:31`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:109`,
  `crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs:93`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:943`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:175`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:784`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1105`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:750`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:107`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1018`
- **Risks:** Very wide blast radius: every checker site that reads
  info.methods() directly as 'all methods including trait ones' (for example
  checker/function_decl.rs:31 trait-host checking and checker/oop.rs
  trait-conflict checks) must switch to the resolved view. Trait methods
  specialised per host (static/self binding, `@use` template args) need care.
  Needs a migration step where both views are checked against each other. | This
  is a large change to the registry data model; many lookup helpers read
  `methods` directly.
- **Verification:** Almost every citation matches the code. Small corrections:
  (1) phpstan-rs resolve.rs: the vacant-only insert of flattened trait methods,
  properties and consts is at lines ~254-275 (Entry::Vacant then slot.insert).
  It is not at 280-303, which is where abstract_methods and static_methods get
  merged.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't split ClassReflection. Instead, rebuild derived state by re-indexing the
> affected descendants from their retained ASTs, and treat the memory saving as
> a separate change.
>
> **Step 1: staleness fix (M), in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs, both
> update_file_cancellable and remove_files**
>
> - Compute the reverse-ancestry closure of the classes the edited or removed
>   file declared, both before and after the edit. Invert registry
>   ancestor_names and extends/implements/uses, and add a reverse index for
>   `@mixin` (the ClassReflection.mixins field).
> - Map that closure to the files that declare those classes, taken from
>   FileState.classes.
> - For each of those files other than the edited one:
>   - unindex_file(p) with the existing function at line 800.
>   - Then self.registry.index(&state.ast, &Origin::File(p), state.analyzed),
>     the same call as line 1003.
>   - The FileState must be kept or re-inserted, so reuse the AST instead of
>     re-parsing it.
> - Then run the existing finishing-pass sequence (lines 1015-1060) once.
> - Add those files to the transitive_affected_files seed so they get
>   re-checked.
> - Update the KNOWN LIMITATION doc (project.rs lines 1105-1136).
> - Add regression tests:
>   - A method removed from a trait makes `(new C)->m()` report an undefined
>     method.
>   - A mixin whose method is removed.
>   - A removed `use T;` in the host's parent.
>   - An incremental result equals the batch result.
>
> **Step 2: separate small fix, in the registry's
> class_extends_implements_closure / precompute_ancestor_names**
>
> - Record an ancestor only if it still resolves to a class in `classes`. This
>   fixes the documented case where a removed Base leaves
>   `is_subclass_of(Child, Base)` true.
>
> **Step 3: optional memory and time work (S-M), in registry/function_sig.rs and
> registry/resolve.rs**
>
> - Store methods as Arc\<FunctionReflection>, or make the heavy fields Arc, so
>   flatten_traits_one_pass and resolve_deferred_mixins share trait and mixin
>   signatures instead of deep-cloning them.
> - Build the addition lists only for slots that are still vacant, so later
>   fixed-point passes don't re-clone.
> - Change the per-signature mutators (resolve.rs lines 1724-1753) to
>   copy-on-write through Arc::make_mut.
>
> **Later, only if profiling shows the finishing passes dominate LSP latency**
>
> - Scope the passes to the recomputed subset in topological order, as Mago's
>   populator does (crates/codex/src/populator/mod.rs lines 93-120).
> - The full own/derived struct split is not needed for correctness.

#### K132. Derive impossible/redundant diagnostics generically from narrowing

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog)
- **Benefit:** Every narrowing extension added later gets redundancy and
  impossibility diagnostics for free, and the existing hand-written rules can
  converge on one engine.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:1443`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:1535`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/probe_checks.rs:582`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1077`
- **Risks:** Soundness depends on narrowing never producing a too-narrow type
  (see the Relation::narrow precision idea). Such a bug would turn into a false
  'always false'. Stage it behind a flag and run corpus diffs.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate. Mago:
  trigger_issue_for_impossible is at crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/mod.rs:1443.
  HasArrayKey/DoesNotHaveArrayKey map to ImpossibleKeyCheck at about 1534-1545
  and to RedundantKeyCheck at about 1607-1615.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't add a generic "diff every key apply_narrowing writes" mode. Generalize
> the per-call outcome oracle that already exists instead. Rename
> `type_check_call_outcome`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/probe_checks.rs:617, currently single-arg
> predicates plus is_numeric only) to something like
> `call_condition_outcome(name, args, locals) -> Option<bool>` and add arms that
> reuse the narrowing primitives already in place: (1)
> array_key_exists/key_exists with a literal key (`literal_shape_key`):
> outcome=false when `current.with_key_presence(key, true)` is never, and true
> when `with_key_presence(key, false)` is never
> (crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:422 already returns never both ways and handles
> unsealed shapes soundly). (2) strict in_array with a literal haystack
> (`in_array_target_type`, checker/narrowing/assertions.rs:113): false when
> `Relation::disjoint(needle, target)`, true when the needle type is accepted by
> the target. (3) is_a/is_subclass_of with a literal class string: reuse the
> logic of the instanceof outcome in impossible_instanceof.rs. (4)
> method_exists/property_exists: report only when the object type is a final or
> known class and the member provably exists (always true) or provably doesn't
> exist with no \_\_call/\_\_get and a final class (always false). Otherwise
> stay silent. Wire all of them through the two existing consumers:
> expr/builtin_calls.rs:40, so infer_expr returns a constant bool and
> ternary/&&/while get it for free, and check_impossible_type_check_call
> (probe_checks.rs:582), which reports function.impossibleType /
> function.alreadyNarrowedType with the last-condition exemption. Then extend
> should_skip_constant_condition (control_flow/boolean_conditions.rs:201) so
> if.alwaysFalse does not double-report. Add fixture tests for sealed and
> unsealed shapes, unions, and optional keys.

#### K35. Case-folded symbol ids as the registry identity model, with display spelling separate

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Case-insensitive symbol identity becomes enforced by construction
  instead of by convention. The confirmed bugs in the member, assert-tag,
  use-site and dependents ideas are all instances of one root cause: a
  Name-keyed container used for a case-insensitive PHP identity. A registry pass
  and many linear scans go away, and every identity hash becomes a u64 write.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/src/metadata/class_like.rs:42`,
  `crates/codex/src/symbol.rs:14`, `crates/codex/src/metadata/mod.rs:85`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/resolve.rs:49`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry.rs:197`, `crates/types/src/lib.rs:373`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/hierarchy.rs:433`
- **Risks:** Wide churn across registry, checker and types. It must be staged:
  the container type first, then migrating field by field with the existing
  fixture suite and corpus diff after each step. Property and class-constant
  maps must stay exact-case, so the type system should distinguish `Folded` from
  `Name` to prevent accidental folding there.
- **Verification:** All cited lines check out. Small corrections: (a) Mago
  mod.rs:85 is a doc comment. The class_likes field is at line 86, constants at
  101, and all_class_like_descendants/direct_classlike_descendants at 103/105.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Take the idea in stages, and leave the parts that already work alone.
>
> 1. Make `Folded` public (it is now private in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/name_table.rs:27-48). It can move into
>    crates/syntax/src/name.rs next to `Name`, which already caches `lower()`
>    (syntax/src/name.rs:48). Also add a `FoldedSet` (`FxHashSet<Folded>`,
>    looked up with `Borrow<str>` via `function_key`).
>
> 2. Change the registry's identity containers to folded keys and values:
>    - `ancestor_names: NameTable<FoldedSet>` (registry.rs:197).
>      `is_subclass_of` (hierarchy.rs:22-31) then no longer needs its two
>      `lookup_class` canonicalization calls.
>    - Method owners: `method_owner_by_class` and
>      `ancestor_method_owner_by_class` become `NameTable<NameTable<Name>>`,
>      because PHP method names are case-insensitive. This removes the O(n)
>      `eq_ignore_ascii_case` fallback scans in `lookup_method` /
>      `lookup_method_with_owner` (hierarchy.rs:472-476).
>    - `property_owner_by_class` and `const_owner_by_class` stay exact-case,
>      because those names are case-sensitive in PHP. The distinct types enforce
>      this.
>    - `names_with_assert_tags`, `unconditionally_declared_*`,
>      `stub_provided_functions` and `function_decl_sites` also become folded.
> 3. Rewrite `find_case_mismatched_ancestor_method` (hierarchy.rs:433). Look up
>    the folded key, then compare the stored declared spelling (the key's
>    `.display()`) with `method`. It no longer needs two spellings stored as
>    separate keys.
>
> 4. Once `ClassReflection.extends/implements/uses/mixins`, `trait_aliases` and
>    `type_imports` are only read through `NameTable` lookups or folded sets,
>    delete `canonicalize_class_name_case` (registry/resolve.rs:49-86) and its
>    three call sites (registry.rs:281, project.rs:746, project.rs:1018). The
>    LSP incremental path then stops paying for a whole-registry rewrite on each
>    update.
>
> 5. Leave crates/types alone. `Repr::Object`/`EnumCase` equality is already
>    case-insensitive (types/src/lib.rs:373, 376). Precomputing the hash is only
>    a micro-optimisation and can be done separately.
>
> Migrate one field per commit, with the fixture suite after each and a corpus
> diff at the end.

#### K102. Reachability computed during analysis instead of syntactic always_terminates

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, L (aspect: control-flow-scope)
- **Benefit:** Removes false positives found in probe cf/f, where Mago is
  correct on a2 and a3 and phpstan-rs reports return.type and assertType
  failures on all five: `do { throw } while (false)`,
  `try {...} finally { throw }`, an exhaustive enum switch where every case
  throws, `if (true) { throw }`, and `foreach ([1] as $_) { throw }`.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/context/block_flags.rs:945`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/context/scope/control_action.rs:47`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/switch.rs:258`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/statement/mod.rs:234`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/control_flow.rs:93`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:57`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:1228`
- **Risks:** Every construct needs correct dead propagation; a mistake there
  would silently skip diagnostics. Dead code should still be analysed for other
  rules, as today, by continuing from a non-dead snapshot. The goto-target
  exception in check_block must keep working.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/context/block_flags.rs:945 is
  wrong. The file has 256 lines. HAS_RETURNED is defined at :20, has_returned()
  at :128 and set_has_returned at :228. The loop citation holds:
  loop/mod.rs:282-283 inserts ControlAction::End and calls
  set_has_returned(true).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a reachability bit to `Locals` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/locals.rs),
> for example `unreachable: bool`, that `merge_scopes`
> (checker/control_flow.rs:563) treats as the identity: dead ⊔ X = X. Set it in
> `check_stmt_impl` (checker/stmt.rs) for Return and Throw, and for Expression
> when the inferred type of the checked expression is `never`, reusing the type
> `check_expr` already computed instead of calling `infer_expr` a second time.
> Break and Continue also set it, and they push the pre-jump state onto the
> loop's or switch's exit and continue lists. `converge_loop_body`
> (control_flow.rs:302) already folds `continue_states`, so break states become
> a sibling list. Propagate it through each construct:
>
> - Loops: the exit state is the merge of the break states, plus the state where
>   the condition is false, but only when the condition is not a constant truthy
>   value. For do-while and foreach over a non-empty constant array, the body's
>   first pass is mandatory.
> - try: a dead `finally` forces the result dead. Otherwise the result is the
>   merge of the body and catch results.
> - switch: when the subject's remaining type is `never` after the case
>   narrowings (the enum-exhaustive case), drop the implicit no-match path. The
>   same rule gives correct merged scopes for non-terminating exhaustive
>   switches (probe g3: `null|1|2` should be `1|2`).
> - if: a condition with a constant truthy or falsy value prunes the impossible
>   branch.
> - Label: a `goto` target clears the flag, which replaces the special case at
>   stmt.rs:63.
>
> With that in place:
>
> - `check_block` (stmt.rs:57-75) reports `deadCode.unreachable` on the
>   false-to-true transition.
> - `check_if` (stmt.rs:1228-1233) drops the three `always_terminates` calls and
>   relies on the merge identity.
> - Missing-return and never-verification in function_decl.rs:982-1023 and 1537,
>   the closure check at expr.rs:3849 and property_hooks.rs:278 read
>   `locals.unreachable` from the body's end state.
>
> `always_terminates` and `exits_function_or_loop` stay only as syntactic
> helpers where no scope exists. The uninitialized_dataflow.rs:326 mirror can
> then be retired or fed from the same result. Land it in phases:
>
> 1. Add the flag and the merge identity, and switch `check_if` and
>    `check_block` over, with a differential assertion that the flag agrees with
>    or exceeds `always_terminates` in debug builds.
> 2. Loops, try/finally and switch exhaustion.
> 3. Move the function-exit consumers over.
>
> Fixtures: probes f1-f5, g2 and g3 below, plus goto labels, `continue 2` inside
> a switch, a nested switch, and a `never` call inside a closure.

#### K280. Build one lexical TypeScope (class, method and closure templates, aliases, self) at body entry instead of rebuilding it for each PHPDoc resolution

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: hir-lowering-ir)
- **Benefit:** Fixes the body-only method-template false positive and loses no
  class template defaults. It removes a per-@var allocation of two hash maps and
  gives one place that decides precedence and static-context rules, instead of
  3-4 slightly different chains.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/hir/src/lower/resolution/type.rs:23`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/resolution/type.rs:147`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/type/annotation.rs:323`,
  `crates/hir/src/lower/type/mod.rs:25`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:89`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:152`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:193`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/var_tag_types.rs:286`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/function_decl.rs:852`
- **Risks:** Resolution order must stay 'resolve names, then substitute aliases'
  (generics.rs:14-24 explains why substituting first double-qualifies). A
  template shadowing a real class name has to keep today's behaviour of
  template-wins.
- **Verification:** - The "31 checker call sites go through the resolve_\* entry
  points" figure is wrong. resolve_type_hint and
  resolve_type_hint_with_case_refs (resolve.rs:56-78) only do native_type and
  never reach resolve_written_type. resolve_written_type has one caller,
  resolve_type_node (resolve.rs:82-84).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two steps. The bug fix is the part worth doing; the rest is optional
> cleanup.
>
> (1) Correctness fix, cost S. In
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/resolve.rs:161-200,
> current_function_template_params returns the signature-derived templates when
> a sig exists, and falls back to self.current_method_templates only when there
> is none. Change it to always start from current_method_templates (already
> parsed from the docblock at function_decl.rs:852-862) and extend it with the
> signature-derived entries. The sig entries should win, since they carry
> resolved bounds. Then add a template frame for closures and arrow functions:
> parse their docblock's @template with registry::build_template_params
> (generics.rs:146), save and restore it around the closure body the way
> function_decl.rs:862/1214 does for methods, and merge it innermost-wins in
> resolve_written_type. Also fill TemplateParam.default in
> class_template_params_for (resolve.rs:152) from info.template_defaults()
> (class_info.rs:692) instead of None.
>
> (2) Optional cleanup. Replace the three fields (current_class plus
> class_template_params_for, current_method_templates, and the new closure
> frame) with one checker::TemplateScope stack. Each frame holds an
> FxHashMap\<String, TemplateParam> built at class, method or closure entry.
> Build the class frame once on class entry rather than once per resolve.
> resolve_written_type then reads the merged view. Keep the current order: mark
> templates, resolve names, then substitute aliases (generics.rs:14-24). Keep
> template-wins over a real class name. Don't fold statement_var_tags' alias and
> pseudo steps into this unless they already share a code path. It's a small
> tidy-up and not needed for the fix.

#### K6. Byte offsets in Position/Span with lazy line/column and exact UTF-16 conversion

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: lexer-parser)
- **Benefit:** Several gains: - Removes per-token char counting from the lexer's
  hot path. - Fixes become O(1) to locate. - LSP positions become exact for
  non-BMP text. - Mixed-encoding sources get unambiguous edit ranges. - It lays
  the groundwork for a token table and for trivia-based doc lookup.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/span/src/lib.rs:19`,
  `crates/database/src/file.rs:149`, `crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs:798`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/token.rs:13`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:252`, `crates/diagnostics/src/fix.rs:8`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs:277`
- **Risks:** `Position` is used everywhere: Hash/Eq on Span keys (`Locals`
  provenance sets), baselines and ignore lines. A dual-field transition keeps
  behaviour identical but temporarily grows Span from 16 to 24 bytes.
  Interpolation fragments re-lexed via `new_in_php_at` (lexer.rs:153) must carry
  a base offset as well as a base line/col.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/span/src/lib.rs:19-21 is
  `Position { offset: u32 }` (repr(transparent)). `Span { file_id, start, end }`
  is at line 29, not 19. crates/database/src/file.rs:149-150 `line_number`
  binary-searches `lines: Vec<u32>` (field at line 80, built by `line_starts` at
  102/291).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do not migrate the whole codebase to offset-only positions. Make three
> targeted changes:
>
> (1) Add `offset: u32` to `syntax::token::Position`
> (crates/syntax/src/token.rs:13) and keep line/col. `Lexer::line_col_at`
> (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:161) already receives the byte position, so it
> fills the offset at no extra cost. For re-lexed interpolation fragments,
> `new_in_php_at` (lexer.rs:153) takes a base offset alongside `base: Position`,
> and `line_col_at` adds it.
>
> (2) Expose the lexer's existing `line_starts` (lexer.rs:27) as a `LineIndex`
> on the parsed file / `FileState`, so consumers can convert without rescanning.
>
> (3) Fix the LSP position encoding at the boundary in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs. `to_lsp_position`/`from_lsp_position`
> (lines 287 and 349) take the document text plus the negotiated encoding. For
> UTF-8 they return the byte column (`offset - line_start`). For UTF-16 they sum
> `len_utf16` over the line prefix. This fixes emoji/astral lines under the
> UTF-16 default. It also fixes a real bug: lsp.rs:2350-2355 echoes
> `PositionEncodingKind::UTF8` but keeps sending character counts. LSP's utf-8
> counts code units (bytes), so every non-ASCII line is currently off under that
> negotiation.
>
> (4) Rewrite crates/diagnostics/src/fix.rs `byte_offset`/`position_at` (lines 8
> and 24) to use `span.start.offset` directly. Keep `within`: it exists because
> checkers hold AST spans, not source text, and offsets alone do not remove that
> need.
>
> Keep line/col in `Position` permanently. Baselines, ignore comments, CLI
> output and ~22 LSP call sites are line-based, and the lexer already amortizes
> column counting.

#### K60. Move PHPDoc-expressible Rust special cases into embedded overlay stubs

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: stubs-prelude)
- **Benefit:** One patch mechanism for built-in, user and config overrides.
  Patches become reviewable PHPDoc, and drift from upstream stubs is caught by
  validation instead of silently no-oping.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:2261`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:2244`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/standard.php:3990`,
  `crates/prelude/assets/extensions/core.php:746`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:1007`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:43`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/assertion_tables.rs:34`
- **Risks:** Some Rust arms encode non-obvious behaviour (argument-count guards,
  list preservation) that a naive PHPDoc port could lose. Port them one arm at a
  time with fixture parity. Overlay application order against phpstan-src .stub
  overlays and the future functionMap layer must be specified.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate: standard.php:2240-2243
  (getenv), 2257-2260 (microtime), 3985-3990 (version_compare) and
  core.php:743-746 (strlen `int<0, max>`). Grepping for `@return ($` finds 103
  conditional returns, not 112; the claim may count other spellings. The 145
  `@param-out` count matches.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build a separate mechanism. Fold this into CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md C6 (lines
> 2567-2590). C6 already plans to apply the phpstan-src `.stub` PHPDoc overlays
> in general: all 146 functions and all method PHPDoc, not only class templates.
> It also plans "declarative patch entries replacing the Rust patch functions"
> (line 2585) but leaves their format open. Settle that format as
> phpstan-rs-owned PHP files, `crates/stub-sources/overlays/*.php`. Embed them
> the same way `PHPSTAN_STUB_SOURCES` is embedded, list them in index.tsv, and
> run them through the same engine C6 builds for the phpstan-src stubs, which
> today is the class-only `patch_phpstan_stub_classes` (registry/stubs.rs:727).
> Apply them last: phpstorm-stubs, then the functionMap layer, then the
> phpstan-src .stub files, then the phpstan-rs overlays.
>
> The engine needs two modes: (a) refine: PHPDoc must be a subtype of the native
> type. Use this for debug_backtrace's list shape, the Reflection/SPL
> `@template`s, DateTime's `static` returns, the array-callback `$rest` union,
> and conditional returns. (b) an explicit replace marker, e.g. a
> phpstan-rs-only attribute handled by stub_attributes. Use this for patches
> that widen or change by-ref: usleep's `int<0,max>` becomes `int`
> (stubs.rs:127), printf values go back to native (141), array_multisort drops
> by-ref (79). A refine-only engine cannot express these, so without (b) they
> would stay in Rust.
>
> A validation test should fail when an overlay names a function, class, method
> or parameter that the upstream stubs do not declare. That replaces today's
> silent no-ops, such as the `let Some(..) else continue` at stubs.rs:734.
>
> Port only the builtin_calls.rs arms that are pure type mappings:
>
> - microtime (1302), as
>   `($as_float is true ? float : ($as_float is false ? string : string|float))`.
> - version_compare (1294), as `($operator is null ? -1|0|1 : bool)`. This fixes
>   an explicit `null` operator, which is `int|bool` today but `int(-1)` at
>   runtime, and tightens `int` to `-1|0|1`.
> - hrtime (148), as
>   `($as_number is true ? int|float : ($as_number is false ? list{int,int} : ...))`.
> - Delete the strlen arm (53) outright. phpstorm-stubs Core/Core.php:54 already
>   declares `@return int<0,max>`, and the probe confirms `strlen(string: 'x')`
>   is already `int<0, max>`, so the arm does nothing.
>
> Keep the count-, value- and list-dependent arms (sprintf, array_column,
> array_search, str_replace, the preg family, etc.) in Rust. Keep the
> assertion_tables.rs TOML as the user-facing config format, and have C6 compile
> it into the same entries internally, as the plan already says (line 2079).

#### K126. Name-keyed typed provider registry (return type, assertion, throw) replacing by-name chains

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, L (aspect: expression-call-analysis, plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** One place per function holds its return type, callback context
  and argument checks. Arity and named-argument handling is correct by
  construction, the code is easier to review and test per function, and
  extension (ext/) crates can register providers for their own functions.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/mod.rs:39`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/invocation/return_type_fetcher.rs:15`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/context.rs:353`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:104`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:407`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:1358` (+2 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:26`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:579`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/calls/closure_context.rs:79`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:555`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/throws/dynamic.rs:53`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/narrowing.rs:1056` (+1 more)
- **Risks:** A large mechanical move. Do it family by family and run each
  family's existing tests; watch for arms that depend on evaluation order inside
  the big match (early returns that fall through to later arms). | This is a
  large mechanical migration touching the most central inference code. Behavior
  must stay identical, so snapshot the fixture suite and a corpus run before and
  after each batch. Some arms currently need `&self` access to many Checker
  helpers (doctrine_query_builder_source, foldable_sql_string), so `ProviderCx`
  must expose enough of them or those providers stay crate-internal.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate. Details: -
  builtin_calls.rs is 3257 lines in total. The ~1800 figure is the function's
  own span: infer_builtin_call_return_type runs from line 26 to its closing
  brace at line 1800. - The array_map arm is at builtin_calls.rs:374.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two stages, and don't start with the trait machinery.
>
> Stage 1 (M, most of the value). Add a `CallCx` in a new
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/builtins/ module. It holds the lowercased bare
> name (computed once), the slots resolved through the existing
> `resolve_call_args` (checker/calls.rs:829) keyed by parameter name/index, and
> a lazily memoized per-slot `infer_expr` result. Switch
> `infer_builtin_call_return_type` (checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:26), the
> call-predicate narrowing in checker/narrowing.rs (~1045-1075, e.g.
> `in_array`), `dynamic_function_throw_type` (checker/throws/dynamic.rs:53) and
> the check-side chain at checker/expr.rs:~860 (define/random_int/filter_var,
> which repeats `rsplit('\\')`+`eq_ignore_ascii_case`) from raw positional
> `args[i]` to `cx.arg("needle")`/`cx.arg_ty(...)`. Then pull the
> callback-context knowledge into one
> `fn builtin_callback_param_overrides(&CallCx) -> Option<(usize, Vec<Type>)>`.
> Two places use it: `contextual_callback_override`/`array_map_elem_override` in
> expr.rs:579ff, and the array_map/array_filter/usort/... arms in
> builtin_calls.rs (~374). That way the infer path and the check path cannot
> drift apart.
>
> Stage 2 (L, maintainability). Replace the big `match name` arms with a static
> `FxHashMap<&'static str, &'static dyn BuiltinFn>`, where `BuiltinFn` has
> `return_type`, `callback_overrides`, `assertions` (sure/if_true/if_false keyed
> by slot), `throw_type` and `check`. Group the providers into family files
> (array.rs, string.rs, pcre.rs, date.rs, math.rs, filter.rs). Providers take
> `&Checker` directly, since they need `doctrine_query_builder_source`,
> `foldable_sql_string` and similar helpers, so a narrow `ProviderCx` facade
> would just be ceremony. For methods, split member_resolution.rs:555
> `object_method_call_return_type` into per-library tables keyed by lowercased
> method name, each entry naming a class and run through `is_subclass_of`. Build
> those tables once per Project from `ActiveExtensions` (src/ext.rs:46-79), so
> the Doctrine entries only exist when Doctrine is active. Migrate one family at
> a time, snapshotting fixtures around each batch. Watch for arms that return
> early and fall through, and for the `type_check_call_outcome` pre-pass and
> polyfill guard at builtin_calls.rs:36-43, which must stay in front of the
> lookup.
>
> Leave out the public "extension crates register providers" part. The ext/
> modules live inside the main crate, and there is no external consumer yet.

#### K192. Move in-tree extension checks onto Rule registrations

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Makes each extension self-contained, which is the 'one module per
  extension crate to be' goal stated in src/ext.rs:1-2. It also exercises the
  public Rule API so it doesn't rot, and moves extension on/off logic to
  registration time.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/mod.rs:68`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:903`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr.rs:414`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/stmt.rs:90`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/rule.rs:61`
- **Risks:** Some of these checks read Checker internals (loop_depth,
  static_var_names, provenance) that Scope deliberately hides, so either widen
  Scope with care or keep those checks inline. Diagnostic ordering could change;
  the determinism gate (emission_order) must stay green. The performance gain is
  negligible.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/stdlib/mod.rs:68-71 registers
  SetCookieHook, SessionSetSaveHandlerHook, SessionSetCookieParamsHook and
  IntdivHook via register_function_call_hook. That is accurate.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Only for the checks that truly are observational over (expr, locals,
> registry): current_time (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/current_time.rs:154)
> and psr3 (checker/psr3.rs:107), plus magic-number expression/statement checks
> (checker/magic_numbers.rs:94,186). Before moving anything, widen `rule::Scope`
> (src/rule.rs:106) with read-only accessors those checks actually need and that
> a third-party rule would also want: `infer(&Expr) -> Type` (delegating to
> `Checker::infer_expr`, checker/expr.rs:4448, which is already `&self`),
> `registry()`, `settings()` and a `resolve_class_name` helper. Then build the
> first-party rules as a `Vec<Box<dyn Rule>>` from `CheckSettings` when the
> Checker is constructed, and chain them with `external_rules` in
> `dispatch_expr_rules`/`dispatch_stmt_rules` (checker/expr.rs:391,
> checker/stmt.rs:387). Leave the magic-number property/param checks inline
> (checker.rs:1535), because Rule has no class-member hook. Also leave
> strict_idioms, strict_rules and match-void inline: they read take()-style
> position flags (in_bare_statement_position, in_condition_position) and
> Checker-private state. Add a fixture that pins the order of same-position
> diagnostics.

### 3.8 testing (12)

#### K99. Runtime-oracle differential soundness tests for narrowing

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: narrowing-algebra)
- **Benefit:** Systematically catches unsound narrowing: the loose-== or-chain,
  stale aliases, and future merge/CNF work. Being stricter than PHPStan is only
  safe when it is sound.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:407`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/formula.rs:1057`
- **phpstan-rs:**
  `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/narrowing/an_or_chain_of_equality_comparisons_narrows_directly_to_the_union.php:4`
- **Risks:** Needs a php binary in CI, so keep the test ignored by default. The
  value universe is finite, so it gives evidence, not proof. Needs a small debug
  hook to dump branch types, or reuse assertType with generated expectations.
- **Verification:** 1. Mago crates/algebra/src/lib.rs:407-483 is not test code.
  It is clause-combination logic (conflict_clause construction around line 417,
  then find_satisfying_assignments at line 471). lib.rs has no `mod tests`.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in differential test target,
> crates/phpstan-rs/tests/narrowing_oracle.rs, registered with `test = false`
> like fixtures (or with every trial marked ignored unless `PHPSTAN_RS_ORACLE=1`
> is set and `php` is on PATH). It uses the same libtest-mimic and
> `Session::for_fixture` in-process driver as
> crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:74-83, so there is no subprocess and no
> release binary.
>
> Generator: build the cross product of (a) parameter types, for example ?int,
> int|string|null, bool|int, string, float|int, array|null, ?Foo and mixed; (b)
> condition shapes: ===, !==, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= against literals 0, 1, '',
> '0', null and false, plus isset, empty, !\$x, (bool)\$x, is_\*, count(\$x) >
> 0, strlen(\$x) > 0, instanceof, `?->`, and nested &&/||/! combinations of two
> arms, in both the if and the else branch; (c) a fixed value universe: null,
> false, true, 0, -1, 1, 1.0, 0.0, '', '0', ' 1', '1.0', 'a', [], [0], new Foo.
>
> For each case, emit one PHP function per condition. Inside each branch, add
> one probe per universe value: `if ($x === <v>) { r(<id>); }` (use
> `$x instanceof Foo` for the object). This needs no new debug hook. Run the
> file once under `php` with a driver that calls f(v) for every value the
> parameter type accepts, and record which probe ids ran. Run phpstan-rs once
> and collect every `identical.alwaysFalse`, `instanceof.alwaysFalse` or
> equivalent diagnostic on the probe lines.
>
> A failure means phpstan-rs called a probe impossible but php executed it. That
> is unsound narrowing, and the harness prints the minimized snippet. A second,
> non-failing report can flag values the type still allows but no runtime value
> reached. That is only a precision hint, since the universe is finite.
>
> Seed a handful of the generated failures as ordinary fixtures under
> tests/fixtures/checker/narrowing/ so the default suite pins them.

#### K219. Differential incremental vs full-load tests

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: incremental-watch-lsp)
- **Benefit:** Each of the five stale-result bugs these probes confirmed (alias,
  fully-qualified or PHPDoc dependents; constants; polyfill deletion;
  duplicate-class deletion; stale trait members) would have failed such a test.
  It is the safety net needed before any of the precision and performance ideas
  here (body-only skip, dirty-scoped passes) can land safely.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:2668`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:2680`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:2195`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_updates.rs:7`
- **Risks:** Tests are slower because each step does a full rebuild; keep the
  fixtures small. Ordering differences inside diagnostics need normalization
  (sort by path, line and message).
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/incremental_analysis.rs:2668
  `assert_matches_full` does what the idea says. It calls
  service.collect_all_issues(), builds a fresh service with
  make_watch_service(db), runs analyze(), and asserts that diff_issues finds
  nothing on either side.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add
> `assert_incremental_matches_full(project: &Project, files: &[(rel, contents)],
> ctx: &str)`
> to crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/helpers.rs. It builds a fresh Project
> in a new TempProject with the same file map and settings, calls
> finish_loading, then compares `check_all(pool)`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1642) on both projects. Before comparing,
> normalize each side by stripping the temp-dir prefix and sorting by (path,
> line, col, identifier, message). This compares whole-project state, not the
> cascade map that update_file/remove_file return, so stale diagnostics in files
> outside the cascade are caught. Call it after every step of a new
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_differential.rs module. That
> module ports Mago's scenario categories: parent/child signature change, trait
> method add/remove, class moved between files, delete then re-add, polyfill and
> duplicate-class deletion, class_alias target change, FQ, `use` alias and
> PHPDoc-only references, constants, and rapid edit/revert cycles. proptest is
> already a dev-dependency (crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:59), so also add a
> small proptest that applies random edit/remove/re-add sequences over a pool of
> 4-6 snippets and runs the differential after each step, with a bounded case
> count. As a separate, lower-priority test, check that the dependents and
> use_sites (project/use_sites.rs) sizes return to baseline after edit/revert
> cycles. Do not run the differential inside existing hand-written tests. Keep
> it in the new module so failures are easy to attribute.

#### K259. Property tests for type algebra

- **Value/cost:** 7/10, M (aspect: testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** Unsound union or narrowing results cause wrong types everywhere
  downstream. The narrowing completeness property directly checks runtime
  correctness, since a value that can exist must not be narrowed away. Proptest
  shrinking gives minimal counterexamples, as the existing NaN and intersection
  regressions show.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/codex/tests/property_combiner_comparator.rs:223`,
  `crates/codex/tests/property_combiner_comparator.rs:74`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml:82`, `crates/codex/tests/combiner_megatable.rs:20`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/types/src/tests/subtyping_properties.rs:65`,
  `crates/types/src/tests/subtyping_properties.rs:20`,
  `crates/types/src/constructors.rs:167`, `crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:195`,
  `crates/types/src/intersection.rs:23`
- **Risks:** Some properties will fail on purpose-built design choices (for
  example documented ClassString/String non-transitivity). Each needs a reasoned
  exclusion rather than a weakened generator, and the first run may turn up real
  bugs that need triage.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially correct. There are small
  off-by-one line numbers on the Mago side: in
  crates/codex/tests/property_combiner_comparator.rs the fn lines are
  combine_self_is_idempotent at 340 (not 339) and combine_with_never_is_identity
  at 358 (not 357).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add crates/types/src/tests/union_algebra_properties.rs as a sibling of
> subtyping_properties.rs, registered in crates/types/src/tests/mod.rs. Move the
> generator (leaf_type/any_type) into a shared tests/generators.rs and extend it
> with int ranges (IntRange incl. open ends), list and shape types with optional
> keys, callables, generic objects (Type::object with args), templates,
> Mixed(lacks) and BenevolentUnion. Define
> `equiv(a,b) = is_subtype(a,b) && is_subtype(b,a)` and assert these properties.
>
> - Union soundness: a <: union(a,b) and b <: union(a,b). This is the must-hold
>   one, because widening may lose precision but never values.
> - Union identities: union(a,never) ≡ a, union(a,a) ≡ a, and union(a,b) ≡
>   union(b,a) up to mutual subtyping. Also Type::union_of on a permuted vector
>   is ≡.
> - without: t.without(e) <: t, t.without(never) ≡ t, and narrowing completeness
>   t <: union(t.without(e), intersect([t,e])). The last one checks directly
>   that the false branch never drops a value that can exist at runtime.
> - intersect (Relation::intersect via Type::intersection_of): intersect([a,b])
>   <: a and <: b, and intersect([a,mixed]) ≡ a.
> - Memo agreement: Type::without and Type::union results equal the uncached
>   result. without_uncached is private in crates/types/src/narrowing.rs:201, so
>   the test goes in the same crate, or a #[cfg(test)] accessor is added.
>   union_types_impl is in crates/types/src/union.rs:23. Each known deliberate
>   non-law, such as ClassString/String non-transitivity (documented in
>   subtyping_properties.rs:7-15) or benevolent-union asymmetry, gets a named
>   `prop_assume!` with a comment giving the reason, not a narrower generator.
>   Pin every shrunk counterexample as a deterministic #[test], as the existing
>   NaN and intersection regressions are pinned. Keep the cheap existing 5
>   properties in the default run. Gate the new, heavier properties behind a
>   `property-tests` cargo feature on the types crate, or use PROPTEST_CASES /
>   #[ignore], so the per-fix `cargo test --lib` loop stays fast, and run them

> Add a static, build-free gate `cargo xtask idcov` in xtask/src/ (a new

> xtask/src/main.rs:1411, next to the existing "arch" and "module graph" steps.

>    - `requireExtends.{}` at checker/oop.rs:470

>    - `impure.{}` at checker/noop.rs:506

  and `clone` with arguments), so pin the expectation to the installed PHP

  files is slow, so check only the files phpstan-rs rejects, plus the curated
  invalid set.
- **Verification:** Mago's crates/syntax/tests/fixtures.rs has the PHP-Parser
  comment at lines 42-45. The fixture list (error_handling_\*,

> Add an `xtask syntax-oracle` subcommand in
> /home/torres/projects/phpstan-rs/xtask/src/ (new syntax_oracle.rs, wired into

> phpstan-src and PHP-Parser-style test fixtures hold many deliberately broken

#### K38. Case-variant fixture matrix for every symbol kind and reference site

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: names-symbols)
- **Benefit:** Locks in the fixes from the other ideas in this report and

  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution/tests.rs:1`
- **Risks:** None beyond fixture maintenance. The fixtures should assert PHP
  runtime behavior, not PHPStan messages.
- **Verification:** Both Mago citations are correct. mago
  crates/word/tests/util.rs:54-57 checks that
  ascii_lowercase_constant_name_word(b"Foo\\Bar\\MY_CONST") gives
  b"foo\\bar\\MY_CONST". Line 60 covers the no-backslash case and line 66 the
  long-input case.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a case-variant name-identity fixture set. Make it multi-file fixture
> directories, which the harness already supports (for example
> crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/receiver_type_checks/clone_non_object/
> is a directory). Put them under
> crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures/checker/name_identity/, one directory per
> symbol kind: constants_const_and_define, functions, classes_interfaces_enums,
> methods_static_instance_and_overrides, class_constants_and_static_props,
> namespace_prefixes_and_aliases. In each, one file declares the symbol in a
> mixed-case namespace and another references it at every site (call, new,
> instanceof, catch, param/return type, PHPDoc @param/@var, static prop, class
> constant, assert-tagged call). Use these spellings: declared, lower, upper,
> leading `\`, a `use` / `use function` / `use const` alias written in a
> different case, `namespace\`, and the unqualified global fallback. Add
> negative cases where PHP is case-sensitive: the constant's short name, a
> define() without the case-insensitive flag, and property and variable names.
> Those must still report not-found. The negative cases matter as much as the
> positive ones, because a blanket lowercase fix would silently accept
> `\foo\bar\my_c`. Each .expect encodes PHP runtime truth, checked once with
> `php -r` while writing it. Do not use PHPStan messages. Separately, add
> case-variant tests beside the existing
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_updates.rs and
> declarations.rs. They should check that editing a file declaring `Foo\Bar\X`
> re-checks a dependent that references `foo\bar\x`, and cover dead-code and
> reference lookups the same way. Land each fixture together with the fix that
> makes it pass, not as a failing batch up front. Drop Mago's word-level unit
> test style: phpstan-rs's folding lives in resolution and registry code, so
> project-level fixtures are the right granularity.

#### K263. Fixture determinism, load-order and incremental-equivalence checks

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** It catches order-dependent declaration merging,
  hash-iteration-order leaks and stale incremental state across the 3768
  targeted scenarios, not just Piwigo's shapes. Incremental equivalence directly
  protects LSP correctness, and the only cost is harness code.
- **Mago evidence:** `tests/suite.rs:111`
- **phpstan-rs:** `xtask/src/main.rs:716`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:81`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/tests/incremental_updates.rs:1`
- **Risks:** It roughly triples fixture run time in stress mode, which is why it
  is opt-in. Some legitimate order-sensitivity (such as which duplicate class
  wins) may need the expected output rules pinned down first.
- **Verification:** Mago tests/suite.rs:111-118 is accurate. After both first
  verify_baseline runs pass (lines 96-109), it runs verify_baseline for analyze
  and lint a second time "to catch non-determinism". These are two separate
  process invocations, and each is compared to the snapshot, not to the other
  run.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add an opt-in stress mode to crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs, enabled by
> an env var such as PHPSTAN_RS_FIXTURE_STRESS=1. Run it in the full xtask gate
> only, not in normal `cargo test`.
>
> 1. Incremental replay (the main value; directory fixtures, plus single files
>    that have a scan context). Split the steps inside run_fixture by calling
>    session.load() and session.analyse() separately; both are already pub on
>    Session in crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs. Snapshot the per-file
>    check_files diagnostics in emission order. Then call
>    Project::update_file(path, same_source) for every loaded path, context
>    files included, in sorted order and again in reverse. Re-run check_files
>    over all analysed files. Require the per-file diagnostics to match the
>    snapshot. This needs a small pub(crate) or test-only accessor that exposes
>    Loaded.project and the per-file results before the project-wide passes run.
>    Do not compare the output of check_whole_program, check_class_shapes,
>    check_banned, check_architecture or check_mock_hygiene (session.rs:748-760)
>    unless those passes are re-run on the replayed project. Re-running them is
>    a good second step, because it also checks that update_file keeps
>    duplicate_fn_sites, duplicate_class_sites and use_sites consistent.
> 2. Emission-order rerun, which is cheap: run the fixture twice with
>    Overrides.emission_order=true and require byte-identical output from both
>    runs. This catches rayon scheduling dependence and lazy shared-cache races.
>    Hash-seed leaks are out of scope because FxHash is unseeded.
> 3. Optional, lowest priority: a Session::for_fixture flag that reverses the
>    load order within the context group and within the analysed group
>    (session.rs:599-667), never across the two groups, so the rule that an
>    analysed declaration beats a context one still holds. Fixtures whose
>    expected output depends on which duplicate wins opt out through their
>    .toml.
>
> Report a failure as a unified diff naming the mode (replay, rerun or reverse)
> and the file whose update produced the mismatch.

#### K184. php -l differential gate for compile-time errors

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** It is the ground truth for this whole category. It keeps the ~40

- **Verification:** All cited locations check out. mago
  crates/semantics/src/lib.rs:51 is `SemanticsChecker::check`, which runs
  CheckingWalker. Its tests are in crates/semantics/tests/
  (enum_magic_methods.rs, instantiation.rs, trailing_comma.rs,
  trait_use_adaptation.rs).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build a separate gate runner. Reuse the existing fixture harness
> (crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs, 3919 .php fixtures under
> tests/fixtures/checker and tests/fixtures/project) in two ways.
>
> (1) Regression guard: add tests/fixtures/checker/compile_errors/, with one
> construct per fixture, for each php -l fatal the parser or checker should
> reject. Each gets an .expect that records the non-ignorable diagnostic or
> parse error on the offending line. Examples: `class C extends A, B {}`
> (crates/syntax/src/parser/classes.rs:549-559 accepts it for classes and
> interfaces alike), same-file `function f(){} function f(){}`,
> `function(){}();`, `new A->b`, `const`/`use` in a function body, `isset(1+1)`,
> `class int {}`, try without catch or finally, and a duplicate switch default.
> Add each fixture together with its fix, not as an allowlist of known gaps.
>
> (2) Discovery and truth check: add a small optional script at
> gates/php-lint-oracle/sweep.py. It runs `php -l` over every fixture and every
> probe snippet and reports two cases. (a) php -l fatals but the fixture's
> .expect has no diagnostic or parse error on that line: this is a
> silent-acceptance gap. (b) A fixture's .expect claims a compile error but php
> -l passes: this is a stale or wrong expectation. The script records `php -v`
> in its output and is never a required CI step, because results depend on the
> installed PHP version. Run it when the parser or checker changes, not per

#### K265. Inline expectation markers in fixtures

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** Each fixture states in place what it is meant to prove. Reviewing
  a bless becomes safe, because the core assertions cannot be overwritten.
  Line-shift edits to a fixture no longer break the intent-level check.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/collector/src/lib.rs:471`,
  `crates/analyzer/tests/framework.rs:175`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:97`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:554`
- **Risks:** Two sources of truth, so the rule should be that markers state
  intent and .expect is the detail snapshot. Markers change a fixture's line
  numbers when added to existing fixtures, so apply them only to new fixtures or
  with a single re-bless.
- **Verification:** All citations are essentially accurate. Details: - Mago
  crates/collector/src/lib.rs: the unfulfilled-expect handling runs across
  roughly lines 470-500 (not only 471).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Change only crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs. The product crates stay
> untouched: no reuse of the ignore code in project.rs.
>
> (a) Bless guard (do first, about 10 lines). After render(), if the output
> contains a diagnostic with identifier `phpstanRs.assertType` (and
> `assert.unresolvableType`), fail the fixture even when PHPSTAN_RS_BLESS is
> set. The exception is a fixture whose X.toml sets a harness-only key,
> `expect_assert_failures = true`. fixture_config() removes that key before
> schema validation, the same way it already handles `requires_feature`. Only
> the 2 fixtures that test assertType's own failure message need the key. This
> alone keeps all ~430 assertType fixtures from being blessed into accepting a
> type regression.
>
> (b) Inline markers. Scan each subject .php file (every file of a multi-file
> fixture) for comments of the form
> `// @phpstan-rs-expect ident[, ident2][ (N)]`:
>
> - A marker at the end of a line applies to that line. A marker alone on its
>   line applies to the next line that is not a comment.
> - Using the diagnostics from report.results, check that the targeted line has
>   exactly N diagnostics with that identifier (N defaults to 1). If not, report
>   "unfulfilled expect: fulfilled X of N" together with the file and line.
> - If a file contains any marker, a diagnostic in that file that no marker
>   claims also fails the test (Mago's framework.rs:175 rule). A "must not fire"
>   line therefore needs no `none` marker.
> - Markers are checked before the bless write, and a bless never touches .php
>   files, so an asserted diagnostic cannot be blessed away.
> - .expect stays the full snapshot of spans, messages, tips and fixes.
> - Update the module doc comment at the top of fixtures.rs.
> - Use markers in new fixtures. Add them to existing ones only together with a
>   single re-bless, because of line shifts.

#### K256. Checker-level fuzz target, actually run and seeded from fixtures

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: robustness-limits, testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** Finds panics in the checker, narrowing and type operations, where
  most of the code lives. Currently those surface only as check_panics on real
  projects. | Robustness for editor use: in the LSP every keystroke produces

  `fuzz/src/lib.rs:64`, `crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs:91`
- **Risks:** Stub loading costs about 1 s per process, so the project must be
  shared across iterations. Throughput is lower than the parse targets. | The
  checker target is slower per execution because stubs load once per process.

  conclusion. (a) crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs: the check_panics test is

> Keep the change small and local. The CI part adds ongoing time without much
> return, which matches the user's concern. (1) Add
> fuzz/fuzz_targets/check_php.rs with a new helper, guarded_check, in
> fuzz/src/lib.rs, next to guarded_parse (fuzz/src/lib.rs:53).
>
> - It takes raw bytes, UTF-8-lossy decoded, so fixture seeds are mutated
>   directly. structured_php's generator only draws names from a 12-entry
>   IDENT_POOL (fuzz/fuzz_targets/structured_php.rs:10), so it reaches very
>   little checker code.
> - A static LazyLock holds a template Project with the stubs already loaded, so
>   the ~1s stub load happens once per process. Each input then replaces a

> - It calls Project::check_paths_isolating_panics
>   (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1609) on the 64 MiB WORKER_STACK_SIZE
>   worker thread and aborts if the panics vector is not empty.
> - The target should find three kinds of bug: caught panics, stack overflows

>   while check_paths_isolating_panics, used from

> Build a smaller version than the one proposed:
> `cargo xtask smoke [project...]` in xtask/src/main.rs, next to corpus_dir()

> reactphp-http), it runs the release binary's
