> aarch64). It runs the built binary's `check-project --no-composer .` on a tiny
> checked-in probe directory: two files, one include, one CRLF-terminated file,
> one known diagnostic. It then compares the result against an expected output
> that uses '/' separators. This stops a broken Windows or macOS artifact from
> shipping, at almost no cost in CI minutes. (2) Add a separate `portable-tests`
> job to .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml. It uses a matrix of windows-2025-vs2026
> and macos-26 (the same pinned images as release.yml), fetches only the
> vendor/phpstan-src submodule, and runs `cargo test --workspace` plus
> `cargo test --test fixtures`. It skips mold, hack, deny and machete, which
> stay on Linux. Run it on push to master and on a schedule rather than on every
> PR, so it doesn't slow PR feedback. Before it can pass,
> crates/phpstan-rs/tests/fixtures.rs has two fixes. render() (around line 202)
> has to join the components of `strip_prefix(base)` with '/', not use
> `.display()`. portable() (around line 252) has to handle both separator
> spellings of the base path. Also note that one_line() (line 248) turns '\'
> into '\\', which makes Windows paths inside messages even harder to match. Any
> CLI or baseline output that echoes relative paths should also render them with
> '/'. The component-join approach already used in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs path_to_uri_path_string (lines 148-175)
> is the model to reuse.

### 3.9 tooling (12)

#### K208. Runtime per-phase timings behind a flag

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: pipeline-parallelism)
- **Benefit:** Users can report which file or phase is slow on their own
  codebase from a release binary, and regressions become visible in CI logs. It
  also exposes the straggler effect from the first idea directly.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:19`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:159`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/pipeline.rs:395`,
  `crates/orchestrator/src/service/analysis.rs:344`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:36`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/profiling.rs:11`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:594`
- **Risks:** Needs discipline to keep it off the hot path when disabled (branch
  on a bool captured once, as Mago's trace_enabled does).
- **Verification:** Mago citations are accurate or off by only a few lines.
  crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:19 is the measure! macro: when
  trace_enabled is false it runs the body with no clock read.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a hidden `--timings` flag to check-project, also settable as
> PHPSTAN_RS_TIMINGS=1. Read it once into a `bool` on `Session`, and send all
> output to stderr so the diagnostics stream stays unchanged. (1) Phase wall
> times, with each phase wrapped in `if timings { Instant::now() }`:
>
> - in `Session::load` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:593): file
>   discovery (collect_php_files), `Project::new()` with stub init, parallel
>   parse, serial insert, and each finish_loading pass;
> - in `Session::analyse` (session.rs:689): the check pass, the
>   judge_property_types re-check pass, and each whole-program pass. (2) A
>   slowest-files list. In `Project::check_files`
>   (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1301), when the flag is set, wrap each
>   `run_checker` call (project.rs:1447) in an Instant. Collect (Duration,
>   PathBuf) pairs through the rayon map, or a Mutex\<Vec> sink, sort them, and
>   print the top 20 along with a count and the total. Use one small
>   `macro_rules! timed!(enabled, label, body)` in a new
>   crates/phpstan-rs/src/timings.rs, modelled on mago
>   crates/orchestrator/src/service/telemetry.rs:19. Leave `measure_outermost`
>   and the hotpath feature (crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/profiling.rs,
>   Cargo.toml:37) alone for deep profiling. Skip Mago's per-file sub-phase
>   AtomicU64 counters (analysis.rs:344). phpstan-rs parses everything in load,
>   not per file during analysis, so the phase times plus per-file check time
>   already cover what matters.

#### K142. Central identifier/rule metadata catalog (list-identifiers, --explain, config validation, docs)

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: analyzer-issue-catalog, linter-catalog-other,
  reporting-fixes)
- **Benefit:** Makes the catalog discoverable for users and LSP code actions,
  catches config typos, and makes coverage audits like this one mechanical. |
  Discoverability of ~600 identifiers and ~60 opt-in checks spread over 9 ext
  sections. Offline docs. Examples that are guaranteed correct. Answers 'why
  didn't check X run'.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/code.rs:1`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule_meta.rs:6`, `crates/linter/tests/rule_examples.rs:20`,
  `src/commands/lint.rs:399`, `docs/src/rules.rs:47`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/code.rs:12` (+2 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/oop.rs:1900`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:54`,
  `crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:98`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:33`,
  `ROADMAP.md:5328`, `crates/diagnostics/src/lib.rs:17` (+3 more)
- **Risks:** format!-built identifiers need an enumerated expansion. Pure
  plumbing with no behaviour change. | Retro-fitting ~600 identifiers is a lot
  of writing. Start with families and opt-in checks. Examples must be
  self-contained, with no vendor context. | Dynamic identifiers need pattern
  entries. The catalog could drift unless the xtask runs in a gate.
- **Verification:** Mago: `impl std::str::FromStr for IssueCode` starts at
  crates/analyzer/src/code.rs:1012, not 1015 (1015 is inside that impl). The
  enum starts at line 12 and the file is 1384 lines, which is correct.
  `--list-codes` is at src/commands/analyze.rs:156 (flag) and :237 (handler).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build a separate catalog or xtask scanner. The enumerable set is already
> planned: CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:4483-4490 (D6) has each rule declare its
> identifiers as prefix × suffix families, has the dispatcher debug-assert every
> emitted error against that declaration, and turns the ~40 format!-built sites
> into family members. Hang the metadata off that declaration. Add a static
> `RuleMeta` in crates/diagnostics with: family pattern, default level, one-line
> summary, gating (extension key, PHP range, opt-in flag), whether a fix exists,
> and optional bad/good snippets. Consumers, in value order: (1)
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/ignore_errors.rs: enforce `count` and the
> unmatched-entry report. The doc comment at ignore_errors.rs:45-56 names the
> missing ability outright ("tell 'unmatched because stale' apart from
> 'unmatched because never implemented'"), and D6 already names that rule. (2)
> `phpstan-rs list-identifiers [--json] [--enabled]`, where --enabled resolves
> the config and says why each family is on or off, plus
> `phpstan-rs explain <id>`, both in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs. (3) A test
> that runs each snippet through check-project and asserts the identifier
> appears in the bad snippet and not in the good one. This keeps Phase 185's
> rule reference (ROADMAP.md:5309+) honest. (4) LSP: completion of known
> identifiers inside `@phpstan-ignore`, and codeDescription only if a docs URL
> template is configured (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/protocol.rs:244-251 sets
> only `code`). Typo detection must NOT warn on every identifier outside our
> set. Converted phpstan.neon configs legitimately name PHPStan and third-party
> identifiers phpstan-rs doesn't implement (dba.\*, shipmonk.\*). Only emit a
> did-you-mean hint when an unknown identifier is within edit distance 1-2 of a
> known one and is not a known upstream identifier. Otherwise leave it silent,
> as D6 specifies.

#### K230. Config JSON Schema and did-you-mean

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** There are many keys (dozens of ext.\* toggles), so typos and
  discovery are real friction. A schema gives completion, hover docs and inline
  validation in editors at zero runtime cost, and the suggestion fixes the most
  common error in one step.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/config/mod.rs:151`, `src/commands/config.rs:1`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/config/src/lib.rs:168`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/app.rs:31`
- **Risks:** Every Section type, including nested ones such as IgnoreErrorEntry
  and SQL config, needs the derive. Custom Deserialize impls need hand-written
  schemas.
- **Verification:** Mago: the Configuration struct is at
  src/config/mod.rs:166-167 (`#[derive(... JsonSchema)]`, with
  `deny_unknown_fields`). The `$schema` key is at mod.rs:169-171, as
  `#[serde(rename = "$schema")] _schema: Option<IgnoredAny>`. Line 151 in the
  claim is a compile-time const assert, not the struct.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Ship this in two steps.
>
> (1) Did-you-mean, cost S. In crates/config/src/lib.rs `Schema::check_table`
> (lines 145-173), when a key has no owner, collect these candidates:
>
> - the `fields` of every RegisteredSection whose `path == path`;
> - the next segment of any section path that extends `path` (for example
>   `ext.extra` should suggest `ext.extras`);
> - at the top level, the `old` names from `self.moves`.
>
> Then append "; did you mean `x`?" using a capped case-insensitive Levenshtein
> distance with a lexicographic tie-break. That logic already exists as
> `levenshtein` and `suggest_similar_name` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/suggest.rs, but that crate depends on config, so
> config can't call it. Either move the helper down into the config crate (or a
> small shared utility crate) and re-export it from checker/suggest.rs, or copy
> the 15-line function. Also apply it to `ConfigFile::set` (the `--set` path),
> where `resolve_key` accepts any dotted path. Nested structs with
> `deny_unknown_fields` already get serde's own "expected one of ..." message
> through `(section.check)`, so no change is needed there.
>
> (2) JSON Schema, cost M. Behind a `schema` cargo feature, add an optional
> `schemars` dependency and a `fn json_schema() -> schemars::Schema` hook on
> `config::Section`: either a supertrait bound gated by the feature, or a
> function pointer stored in RegisteredSection next to `check`. Derive
> JsonSchema on the 24 `*Settings` types and their nested types. The untagged
> enums (restricted_symbols.rs:64, baseline.rs:97, checker/settings.rs:34,
> ext/sidz.rs:47) map to anyOf automatically. Keep doc comments, which become
> the descriptions.
>
> `Schema::json_schema()` merges the section schemas into one root object. It
> places each at its PATH (the top-level sections merge their properties), sets
> `additionalProperties: false` to mirror check_table, and marks moved keys as
> `deprecated`. Expose it as `phpstan-rs config --schema`. Commit the generated
> file (for example `schema/phpstan-rs.schema.json`) with a unit test in
> crates/config/src/tests.rs or the app crate that fails when the committed file
> is stale. Document Taplo's `#:schema` directive instead of adding a `$schema`
> key, because a `$schema` key would itself need an owning section. Optionally,
> editors/vscode can add a tomlValidation contribution pointing at the committed
> schema. Leave LSP-side validation for later: the LSP already loads the file
> through lsp/workspace_config.rs, and it could report its existing errors as
> diagnostics without a schema.

#### K260. Instruction-count benchmarks

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: testing-strategy)
- **Benefit:** The perf signal becomes reproducible on every commit, including
  in CI and on a busy machine, so the nearest-ancestor gaps go away. Small
  regressions (1-2%) that wall-time noise hides become visible, and the
  regression can be tied to the exact commit.
- **Mago evidence:** `.github/workflows/codspeed.yml:36`, `Cargo.toml:207`
- **phpstan-rs:** `xtask/src/main.rs:1022`, `.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml:97`
- **Risks:** Instruction counts do not capture cache or allocator effects or
  parallel speedups, so they complement the wall-time gate rather than replace
  it. Callgrind is about 50x slower, so the benches it runs must be small.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out, with one clarification. In
  xtask/src/main.rs:1073 the wall-time limit is old_mean + max(2% of old_mean,
  3\*old_stddev), so it is the larger of 2% and 3σ, not both. The RSS limit is a
  flat 2% (xtask/src/main.rs:1084).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Build it offline rather than with CodSpeed. CodSpeed needs an external service
> and a GitHub app, and the facts it would add are already covered by the xtask
> gate-dir layout.
>
> 1. Add `perf-instr` to xtask/src/main.rs next to `perf()` (around line 1022).
>    It builds the bench binaries with `cargo bench --no-run`, runs each one
>    under `valgrind --tool=callgrind --dump-instr=no` with
>    `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` (or whatever serial switch the checker offers), reads
>    the `summary:` Ir total and writes `gate_dir()/perf/<hash>.instr`.
> 2. Compare that file with the parent commit's `.instr` using a 1% threshold.
>    The count is machine-independent, so every commit can record one.
>    `nearest_ancestor_with` then applies only to the hyperfine/RSS files.
> 3. Do not run the existing crates/phpstan-rs/benches/vendored_corpus.rs as-is.
>    It loads and checks all 2351 stub and phpstan-src files, so at about 50x it
>    would take many minutes per run. Add a small entry point for callgrind
>    instead, either a `harness = false` bench or `iai-callgrind`/`gungraun`
>    benches, covering:
>    - lex+parse of a fixed stub subset (the logic of
>      crates/syntax/benches/lex_parse.rs on about 100 files)
>    - load, finish_loading and check_all on a fixed slice of about 50
>      phpstan-src files
>    - stub registry initialisation (the `LazyLock` parse in
>      src/registry/stubs.rs, the 0.95s startup cost)
> 4. Optionally run `cargo xtask perf-instr` in .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml
>    after "Benches compile" (line 97), comparing against a count cached from
>    master.
>
> Keep the hyperfine+RSS gate as the end-to-end check for wall time and memory.

#### K300. Composer-distributed launcher package (vendor/bin/phpstan-rs) pinned by composer.lock

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** A PHP project can pin phpstan-rs per repo with
  `composer require --dev`, exactly as it pins phpstan/phpstan. CI caches it
  with vendor/, teammates get the same version, Renovate/Dependabot bump it, and
  editors can find it at a fixed path. This is the most direct fix for adoption
  among PHP users, who do not install Rust binaries by hand.
- **Mago evidence:** `composer.json:14`, `composer/bin/mago:36`,
  `composer/src/internal.php:109`, `composer/src/internal.php:159`,
  `composer/src/internal.php:538`, `composer/src/internal.php:368` (+1 more)
- **phpstan-rs:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:157`, `README.md:7`
- **Risks:** Packagist publishing needs a public repo with tags. If the package
  lives in the main repo, the whole Rust source ships in the Composer dist, so
  an archive-exclude list or a split repo is needed. The download happens at
  first run, not at install, so an offline CI run that did not warm the cache
  fails; document a `vendor/bin/phpstan-rs --version` warm-up step. The launcher
  adds roughly 20-50ms of PHP startup.
- **Verification:** The citations are essentially accurate, with two small
  offsets. composer/src/internal.php:109 is the docblock just above
  get_version(); the
  InstalledVersions::getPrettyVersion('carthage-software/mago') call is at about
  line 111.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Only worth doing once there is a first public tagged release. Until then the
> idea has no effect: `git tag` shows only `pre-merge-master2-6e192ca`, no `v*`
> tag, and the header comment of .github/workflows/release.yml (lines 3-9) says
> none of the matrix legs has been checked by a real CI run yet.
>
> When it is done: (1) Put the launcher in a separate small repo, e.g.
> darktorres/phpstan-rs-bin, which holds composer.json
> (`"bin": ["bin/phpstan-rs"]`, `require: php >=8.1, ext-zlib`), bin/phpstan-rs
> and src/Launcher.php. Don't put composer.json in the Rust monorepo root. The
> monorepo has vendor/phpstan-src and corpus submodules, crates/, editors/vscode
> (with a .vscode-test download tree) and many root plan .md files, and there is
> no .gitattributes to export-ignore them. Packagist would also see the `v*` tag
> at the same moment release.yml starts building, so the package would exist
> before its assets did. (2) Add a final job to release.yml, `needs: build`,
> that runs after all 5 `gh release upload` steps (release.yml:157). It pushes
> the same `v{version}` tag to the launcher repo, so the launcher can never
> point at an asset that isn't there. (3) The launcher reads its version from
> InstalledVersions::getPrettyVersion('darktorres/phpstan-rs-bin'). It maps
> PHP_OS_FAMILY and php_uname('m') to exactly the 5 triples release.yml builds.
> It downloads
> `https://github.com/{repo}/releases/download/v{ver}/phpstan-rs-{triple}[.exe].gz`,
> the same URL shape as editors/vscode/src/serverDownload.ts:220. It sends a
> GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN bearer if one is set, and checks the `.gz.sha256` with
> hash_equals before gzdecode. It writes to
> vendor/darktorres/phpstan-rs-bin/.cache/{ver}/{triple}/ through tmp-file +
> flock + rename (double-checked), then chmods 0755. (4) Detect musl (ldd
> --version, or /lib/ld-musl-\*) and fail with a clear message pointing to
> PHPSTAN_RS_BINARY. There is no musl asset, and Alpine-based PHP CI images are
> common, so a separate musl leg in release.yml (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) is a
> worthwhile follow-up. (5) Honour PHPSTAN_RS_BINARY as a full override. (6)
> Exec with pcntl_exec when it is available. Otherwise use proc_open with
> inherited STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR and pass on the exit code. (7) Add a README
> "Installing via Composer" section with a `vendor/bin/phpstan-rs --version`
> cache-warming step for offline CI. Leave out the schema-writing and
> Packagist-registration details until they are needed.

#### K266. SQL drivers behind cargo features

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: build-structure)
- **Benefit:** Clean builds, CI runs (where a clean or cold-cache build is
  common) and the `cargo hack` / `--no-default-features` gate steps no longer
  compile a C crypto library through cmake, a second TLS stack, tokio or bundled
  SQLite unless they are needed. That is most of the dependency graph by count.
  The ring switch alone drops the slowest C build (aws-lc-sys) and the need for
  cmake on contributor machines and CI images.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/prelude/Cargo.toml:17`,
  `crates/syntax/Cargo.toml:1`, `Cargo.toml:250`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/sql/Cargo.toml:13`, `crates/sql/src/reflector.rs:626`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:35`
- **Risks:** Default features must stay 'all drivers' so release behaviour is
  unchanged. Gate and test commands that exercise the reflector tests
  (crates/sql/src/reflector/tests.rs) need the features on, or those tests need
  cfg attributes. Feature unification in `cargo test --workspace` can re-enable
  the features and hide a missing cfg, so the standalone `cargo hack` gate
  should cover each feature. The ring backend has different FIPS and performance
  characteristics than aws-lc, which doesn't matter for a PREPARE-only metadata
  connection.
- **Verification:** One Mago line number is wrong. The workspace
  `zip = { version = "6", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }`
  entry is at /home/torres/projects/mago/Cargo.toml:223, not :250. Line 285 is
  the `zip = { workspace = true }` use. The other two Mago citations are
  correct.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Do it in two separate commits, with the ring switch first.
>
> (1) In crates/sql/Cargo.toml:12, change mysql's features from ["rustls-tls",
> "minimal-rust"] to ["rustls-tls-ring", "minimal-rust"]. mysql-28.0.3's
> Cargo.toml:77-84 defines `rustls-tls = [rustls, rustls/aws_lc_rs]` and
> `rustls-tls-ring = [rustls, rustls/ring]`. Check afterwards that
> `cargo tree -i aws-lc-sys` and `cargo tree -i cmake` return nothing. Postgres
> already uses postgres::NoTls (reflector.rs:316, 343), and mysql TLS matters
> only when a user configures SSL, so behaviour doesn't change.
>
> (2) Gate the drivers behind features.
>
> - In crates/sql/Cargo.toml, make these optional:
>   - `mysql`, behind a `live-mysql` feature
>   - `postgres` and `r2d2_postgres`, behind `live-postgres`
>   - `r2d2`, enabled by either of those
>   - rusqlite and r2d2_sqlite stay unconditional, per the recorded user choice
>     in crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:35-41. Gate SQLite only if the user
>     explicitly reverses that choice.
> - In crates/sql/src/reflector.rs, `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` the MysqlReflector
>   and PostgresReflector structs and impls (lines ~174-490) and the
>   build_reflector arms (lines 626-638).
> - A disabled driver's arm returns None, which degrades to the same fallback a
>   failed connect already produces. The config loader emits one startup warning
>   naming the missing feature.
> - In crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml, forward them with
>   `default = ["pcre-validate", "live-mysql", "live-postgres"]`.
> - Add a lean-deps check step to the xtask gates (xtask/src/main.rs:1464 area)
>   and to CI: `cargo check -p phpstan-rs-sql --no-default-features`, plus each
>   feature on its own. This catches missing cfgs that workspace feature
>   unification would hide.
> - Note the new meaning of the existing `--no-default-features` step
>   (rust-ci.yml:90-92, xtask 1464-1490): it now also drops the MySQL and
>   Postgres reflectors, not just PCRE. Cfg-gate any MySQL/Postgres cases in
>   crates/sql/src/reflector/tests.rs.
> - Update the CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN Appendix E sql row with the per-feature
>   dependency split.

#### K308. dump tokens subcommand: print the lexer stream with spans, raw keyword spelling, comments and lex warnings

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary
  commands)
- **Benefit:** The lexer can be debugged without writing a Rust test. You see
  exactly where a heredoc, a cast or `{$` interpolation was split, and the raw
  keyword spelling. This makes the queued lexer-divergence and short-open-tag
  work much faster to diagnose and to write up in bug reports.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/cst.rs:174`, `src/commands/cst.rs:181`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs:50`,
  `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:225`, `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs:37`
- **Risks:** Very little. It is a debug-only surface, and the Debug format of
  Token is not a stable contract (say so in the help text).
- **Verification:** Mago: in /home/torres/projects/mago/src/commands/cst.rs,
  `print_tokens` is at lines 174-231. It is reached through the `--tokens` flag
  on the cst/ast command (the flag is declared at line 114 and dispatched at
  line 140). It is a flag, not a separate subcommand.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a `DumpTokens { file: PathBuf }` variant to `Command` in
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main.rs, with its handler in a new
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/dump_tokens.rs, or fold the same code into
> main/demo.rs so that Demo does what its doc says. The handler calls
> `Lexer::from_bytes(&src).with_interner(&interner).tokenize_with_comments()`
> (crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs:225) and prints one line per token, in the form
> `L:C-L:C  {Token:?}` plus `raw=..` when keyword_raw is Some. It then prints
> the comments with their start positions and every LexWarning with is_error
> marked, and exits 1 if any warning is an error. Unlike parse(), it does not
> stop at the first error. The help text says the output is a debug format with
> no stability guarantee. Leave out --json: no consumer needs it, and it would
> mean adding serde to Token. Also fix or trim the Demo doc comment at
> main.rs:49-51, which says Demo dumps tokens when it does not.

#### K309. dump ast subcommand: compact tree with one line per node, spans and resolved names, that does not panic on parse errors

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary
  commands)
- **Benefit:** Checking how a construct was parsed and resolved becomes a single
  readable command. It also gives parser-recovery work and the differential
  syntax-acceptance tests a way to show _what_ was parsed, not just pass/fail.
  The --json form also lets you diff structurally against nikic/PHP-Parser.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/cst.rs:283`, `src/commands/cst.rs:140`,
  `src/commands/cst.rs:245`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:62`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:68`, `crates/syntax/src/visit.rs:19`
- **Risks:** A hand-written tree printer has to be updated when AST variants are
  added. Falling back to a Debug-derived kind name for anything unhandled keeps
  it complete. Adding serde to the AST would increase compile time for the
  syntax crate, so gate it behind a cargo feature.
- **Verification:** All the Mago citations check out. The CST command runs from
  src/commands/cst.rs:136. At :145-160 it builds an IssueCollection from
  program.errors and reports it through the reporting processor, which sets the
  exit code. At :162-168 it still prints the tree, JSON or names. print_cst_json
  is at :245;
- **Refined proposal:**

> Drop the new `dump ast` subcommand, the Visitor printer, `--at`, and
> `--json`/serde. Make two small changes instead: (1) In
> crates/syntax/src/token.rs, replace `derive(Debug)` on Position and Span with
> hand-written `impl fmt::Debug`. Position prints as `l:c` and Span as
> `[l:c-l:c]`, in the same style as the existing Name Debug impl at name.rs:142.
> This shrinks `{:#?}` AST output a lot everywhere: demo, dbg!, and assert
> failures in tests. (2) In crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs:62, replace
> `.unwrap()` with a match. On error, print `path:line:col: message` to stderr
> and exit with code 2. If a compact per-node tree still turns out to be needed
> later, it can go in as a Visitor-based printer then. It should fall back to
> the Debug kind name for any node it doesn't handle, so it stays complete.

#### K304. Multi-arch container image on ghcr.io

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** CI systems that are not PHP-centric (GitLab CI, Jenkins,
  pre-commit hooks) can pin an exact version by image tag without a PHP runtime
  or a download step.
- **Mago evidence:** `Dockerfile:1`, `.github/workflows/cd.yml:473`
- **phpstan-rs:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:16`
- **Risks:** Depends on the musl builds. Composer autoload resolution inside the
  container needs the project's vendor/ mounted.
- **Verification:** All citations are accurate. Mago's Dockerfile:1-4 is
  `FROM alpine:3`, then `apk add git`, then COPY mago, with the binary as the
  ENTRYPOINT. The `docker` job starts at .github/workflows/cd.yml:473 and is
  gated to tag pushes.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Only after .github/workflows/release.yml has musl legs
> (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl and aarch64-unknown-linux-musl) that a CI run has
> proven: add a Dockerfile at the repo root, `FROM alpine:3` with
> `apk add --no-cache git`, the binary copied to /usr/local/bin/phpstan-rs,
> `WORKDIR /app` and `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/phpstan-rs"]`. Then add a
> `docker` job to release.yml that runs only on tag pushes (not on
> workflow_dispatch), with `needs: build` and `permissions: packages: write`. It
> downloads the two musl artifacts, builds one image per arch (no QEMU
> emulation, since the binaries are prebuilt), and runs
> `docker buildx imagetools create` to tag
> ghcr.io/darktorres/phpstan-rs:{X.Y.Z,X.Y,X,latest}. Add a README snippet for
> `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app ghcr.io/darktorres/phpstan-rs check-project`,
> noting that vendor/ must already exist in the mounted tree (from
> `composer install` in an earlier CI step) or `--no-composer` must be passed.

#### K310. dump names subcommand: every name reference with its resolution, including type names in PHPDoc

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary
  commands)
- **Benefit:** Case-folding, the global fallback and wrong use-import resolution
  are a large share of the queued name-resolution ideas (use-site folding,
  class_alias, the case-variant fixture matrix). Seeing the resolution of every
  reference, in code and in docblocks, turns 'why is this class.notFound?' into
  a one-command answer. Mago can't show the docblock half.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/cst.rs:256`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:850`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:96`,
  `crates/syntax/src/name_resolution.rs:140`
- **Risks:** The docblock section has to reuse the same resolution call the
  registry and checker use. Otherwise it could show a resolution that differs
  from what the analysis actually does. Calling the same NameContext method
  avoids that.
- **Verification:** Mago: src/commands/cst.rs:255-274 `print_names` is reached
  through `mago cst --names` (flag at cst.rs:123-128, dispatch at :164-165). It
  prints `@start..end` byte offsets, the resolved name and an imported flag. It
  does NOT print the name as written.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't add a new top-level subcommand. Add a names section to the existing
> debug-only `demo` command (crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/demo.rs; declared in
> main.rs:46-50), or a `--names` flag on it. (1) Code names: a
> syntax::visit::Visitor walks the resolved stmts and prints each QualifiedName,
> one per line, as
> `line:col written -> Exact(X) | fallback(ns\f, f) | unresolved`. For
> class-kind names only (the only kind it covers), add `[imported]` from
> NameContext::is_use_imported (name_resolution.rs:140) and `[not found]` when
> registry.lookup_class misses. (2) Docblock names: do NOT re-resolve raw
> identifiers with context_at(..).resolve(..). The real pipeline first runs
> mark_template_params (registry/function_sig/generics.rs:133) and alias
> substitution (build_type_aliases/substitute_type_aliases), and only then
> resolve_names_in_type (registry/name_context.rs:13). A naive resolve would
> print `@template T` as `App\T` and a `@phpstan-type` alias as a class, which
> is exactly the misleading output the tool is meant to prevent. Instead, print
> the (written, resolved) pairs the registry already records through
> collect_class_name_case_refs: case_refs/set_case_refs/return_case_refs,
> type_alias_case_refs and mixin_case_refs in
> registry/class_info.rs:158,161,530,577. Label each pair with its owning symbol
> and tag, and mark the ones lookup_class can't find. Inline in-body @var types
> are resolved in the checker (checker/resolve.rs:99, oop.rs:421/491) and could
> be covered later through the same pairs. Having one source of truth means the
> dump can't drift from what the analysis does.

#### K312. CLI type-at/scope-at query that reuses the LSP span probe through a shared inspect module

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, M (aspect: developer inspection and CLI ancillary
  commands)
- **Benefit:** You can query read-only code (vendor, generated files, a
  colleague's branch) without inserting probes. It also makes a scriptable way
  to bisect type regressions across commits: diff one line of output instead of
  a whole check-project run. Moving the probe code out of the LSP also lets
  LSP-independent tests use it, and removes duplicated setup.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:529`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:988`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp/navigation.rs:152`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1350`
- **Risks:** Each query pays a full project load, which is fine for debugging.
  Capturing scope at a line needs care with multi-statement lines and loop
  passes: report the converged (final-pass) state and say so.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/mod.rs:529 is
  `fn inspect_arguments`, the helper. The actual `Mago\inspect()` type-report
  issue is built at mod.rs:558-571 ("Type information for arguments of
  `Mago\inspect()` call.").
- **Refined proposal:**

> Drop the `--scope` / Locals-capture half. `check-project --dump-types <out>`
> already covers it: crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs:56-59 writes
> every tracked variable's type after each statement, and the Checker holds it
> at checker.rs:811 keyed by (line, col, name), gathered in
> project/session.rs:711-737. If anything is built, keep it small. (1) Move
> `probe_receiver_type`, `probe_variable_provenance` and `run_probe_scope`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/lsp.rs:988-1055) into free functions that take
> `&Project`, for example `crate::inspect` or `lsp/navigation.rs` itself, and
> make `navigation` pub(crate) so non-LSP tests can call `resolve_at` plus the
> probe. (2) Optionally add a hidden
> `check-project --type-at <file>:<line>:<col>` flag that reuses the
> check-project load path. It would print the probed expression's type, its
> member owners and its reaching-definition lines. This is useful mainly for
> non-variable expressions such as receivers and property fetches, which
> `--dump-types` does not record. Don't create a new `dump` subcommand.

#### K305. Nix flake exposing packages.default and a devShell

- **Value/cost:** 2/10, M (aspect: distribution-packaging)
- **Benefit:** `nix run github:.../phpstan-rs -- check-project` and a
  reproducible per-project pin through flake.lock. Nix users are
  over-represented among people who adopt Rust dev tools.
- **Mago evidence:** `flake.nix:40`, `flake.nix:48`
- **phpstan-rs:** `rust-toolchain.toml:2`, `.github/workflows/release.yml:61`
- **Risks:** The build embeds a submodule, so the flake needs care or it breaks
  silently on a submodule bump. The nightly toolchain pin has to stay in sync.
- **Verification:** Mago flake.nix: naersk'.buildPackage { src = ./.; doCheck =
  true; } is at lines 40-44, and packages.default = built is at line 47, not 40.
  devShells.default starts at line 48. The devShell does not pin its toolchain
  through fenix.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Low priority, and only if a Nix user asks for it. Add
> /home/torres/projects/phpstan-rs/flake.nix and flake.lock with these parts:
> (1) fenix `fromToolchainFile { file = ./rust-toolchain.toml; sha256 = ...; }`,
> so the flake uses the same nightly-2026-09-22 pin as everything else. (2)
> crane `buildPackage` with `cargoExtraArgs = "-p phpstan-rs"`. The source must
> include vendor/phpstan-src. The simplest way is
> `inputs.self.submodules = true` (Nix 2.27 or later), because
> crates/stub-sources/build.rs:69-87 reads `../../vendor/phpstan-src/src` and
> `/stubs` from a fixed relative path and panics when the submodule is missing.
> Do not add a new env-var override to build.rs just for Nix. (3)
> `nativeBuildInputs = [ clang mold ]`. The x86_64-linux target in
> .cargo/config.toml hard-codes `linker = "clang"` and `-fuse-ld=mold`, and a
> Nix sandbox build fails without those two. `-Z threads=8` works because the
> toolchain is nightly. (4) `packages.default`, `apps.default` and a
> `devShells.default` containing the toolchain, php, composer, clang and mold.
> (5) One CI job, `nix flake check` or `nix build`, so a submodule bump or
> toolchain bump that breaks the flake shows up. Do not copy Mago's devShell. It
> installs unpinned `pkgs.rustup` (mago/flake.nix:48ff) and so gives up the
> reproducibility this proposal is meant to provide.

### 3.10 extensibility (9)

#### K181. Architecture rules generalized to symbol dependencies

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** The same probe gave Mago guard 6 breaches (use import, PDO
  parameter, 2 static calls, function call, constant) and phpstan-rs 1. Banning
  `PDO`, `curl_*` or `App\Infra\helper()` from a domain layer, and covering
  procedural code, is a common real use case that phpstan-rs cannot express
  today.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/guard/src/perimeter/mod.rs:279`,
  `crates/guard/src/perimeter/checker.rs:163`, `crates/guard/src/settings.rs:84`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:37`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:354`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs:332`
- **Risks:** Changes default output for existing rules only if the defaults
  change, so keep builtins opt-in. Functions need namespace fallback resolution
  (use_sites' candidates()) to avoid false positives on global functions.
- **Verification:** Mago citations are correct to within a line. The namespace
  source is walk_in_namespace at crates/guard/src/perimeter/mod.rs:66. The
  function-call breach is at ~279, the partial application at ~298, the
  class-constant access at ~317 and walk_in_constant_access at ~330-336.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Generalise crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/architecture.rs from class
> dependencies to symbol dependencies, keeping every current default.
>
> 1. Sources. Extend collect_declared to also collect:
>    - Declared::Function items (namespaced functions);
>    - one synthetic "top-level code of \<namespace block>" source per namespace
>      block/file, with span = the block and name = `<file>` or the namespace
>      name;
>    - conditional class-likes, instead of skipping them, carrying a
>      `conditional: bool`. Drop the `if classes.is_empty() { continue; }`
>      short-circuit (architecture.rs:~283). Sources are matched by the existing
>      `classes` selectors, which keep matching class-likes only, so current
>      behaviour is unchanged. Add new rule keys `functions: Vec<Selector>` and
>      `code_in: Vec<Selector>` (namespace/path pattern) in
>      crates/phpstan-rs/src/architecture.rs ArchitectureRule, plus
>      `is_conditional: Option<bool>` on Selector.
> 2. Targets.
>    - Consume RefTarget::Function in class_dependencies (renamed
>      symbol_dependencies). Resolve each name through the registry's function
>      lookup, trying the namespaced candidate first and then the global
>      fallback, since use_sites.rs:177 records only candidates().0.
>    - Add RefTarget::Constant(String) in use_sites.rs: a ConstFetch arm with
>      the same namespaced-then-global fallback. Keep the LSP consumers working,
>      since they match on RefTarget.
>    - Each Dependency gets a `kind: Class|Function|Constant`.
>    - Add `kind = "class"|"function"|"constant"` to Selector
>      (src/architecture.rs:36) so
>      `should_not_depend_on=[{kind="function", name="/^curl_/"}]` works. A
>      `name` alias for `classname` reads better for functions and constants.
> 3. Builtins.
>    - Replace the unconditional is_builtin drop (architecture.rs:332) with a
>      Dependency flag `builtin: bool`. Extend is_builtin to cover builtin
>      functions and constants from the stubs.
>    - Add an `is_builtin: Option<bool>` selector flag.
>    - Keep builtins implicitly allowed for `can_only_depend_on` and ignored by
>      `should_depend_on`, exactly as today.
>    - For `should_not_depend_on`, a builtin matches only when the selector
>      names it explicitly: a Text (non-regex) classname/name equal to it, or
>      `is_builtin=true`. So `{classname="PDO"}` and
>      `{kind="function", name="/^curl_/", is_builtin=true}` fire, while
>      existing namespace/regex rules keep their current output.
>    - `should_not_construct` gets the same builtin treatment.
> 4. Messages and identifiers. Generalise the report text to "\<source
>    description> depends on \<kind> \<name>". Keep the existing identifiers for
>    class→class so current baselines stay valid.
>
> 5. Tests. Add fixtures under tests/fixtures covering:
>    - a namespaced function using a banned helper;
>    - top-level code calling curl_init;
>    - a domain class taking a PDO parameter;
>    - global-constant use;
>    - an unqualified builtin inside a namespace (fallback resolution, no false
>      positive against NS\strlen);
>    - a conditional class declaration;
>    - `can_only_depend_on` not flagging builtin functions.

#### K231. Config extends/includes composition

- **Value/cost:** 6/10, M (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Organisations with many repos can share one strict ruleset (ext
  toggles, banned constructs, architecture rules), the way phpstan.neon
  `includes:` is widely used, while each repo keeps local paths.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/config/mod.rs:1332`, `src/config/mod.rs:1337`,
  `src/config/mod.rs:1458`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/config/src/lib.rs:197`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:286`
- **Risks:** Merge semantics are easy to get wrong, as Mago shows. Keep it
  minimal and documented, and have `phpstan-rs config` show the provenance of
  each value.
- **Verification:** Every cited location checks out. Mago: load_layer is in
  /home/torres/projects/mago/src/config/mod.rs, with its doc comment starting
  around line 1326 and the fn signature at about line 1332. It resolves each
  `extends` entry against path.parent() (resolve_extends_entry).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add layered loading in crates/config/src/lib.rs (369 lines). ConfigFile::load
> (line 197) currently reads a single TOML table, runs schema.apply_moves, and
> keeps one `path`. `dir()` at line 266 is the only base used for relative
> paths.
>
> 1. Load recursively. In ConfigFile::load, parse the file, remove a top-level
>    `extends` (a string or an array of strings) before apply_moves/validate,
>    and resolve each entry against the declaring file's parent directory.
>    Recurse depth-first with a Vec\<PathBuf> stack of canonical paths, popped
>    after each branch; hitting a path already on the stack is a cycle error.
>    Keep a HashMap\<canonical, Table> memo so diamonds load once and work. Run
>    apply_moves on each layer before merging, so deprecated keys in shared
>    files still migrate and warnings name the file.
> 2. Absolutise paths per layer. The set of path-typed keys is small and closed:
>    session `paths` and `baseline` (session.rs:285-297, check_project.rs:70),
>    reflection `scan_paths`/`stub_paths` (registry/settings.rs:15,19;
>    session.rs:359,370), and `ext.sql.reflection.schema_file` (session.rs:333).
>    Register them on Schema, e.g.
>    `Schema::path_keys(&["reflection","scan_paths"])`. Rewrite each relative
>    string to layer_dir.join(..) before merging. Then the final dir() base only
>    applies to --set values and the root file, which keeps current behaviour.
> 3. Merge in order parent[0] < parent[1] < ... < self. Tables merge deeply, and
>    scalars and arrays take the later value (arrays replace by default, unlike
>    Mago's concat, which can't remove an entry). An explicit `key_append`-style
>    or `+`-prefixed form can come later if needed; don't ship concat as the
>    default.
> 4. Keep provenance: record the source layer per dotted key in ConfigFile, so
>    `phpstan-rs config` (or its errors) can show where a value came from.
>    validate() error messages should name the layer the unknown key came from,
>    so validate each layer separately before merging.
> 5. LSP: lsp/workspace_config.rs:59-77 loads only root/phpstan-rs.toml. Expose
>    ConfigFile::sources() (all layer paths) so the LSP file watcher reloads
>    when any parent changes, not just the root file.
> 6. Tests go in crates/config/src/tests.rs: diamond, cycle, relative path in a
>    parent resolving against the parent's directory, array replace, a move
>    applied inside a parent, and an extends path into vendor/ (a shared package
>    ruleset).

#### K235. Virtual-content inputs (stdin, substitute)

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, S (aspect: config-cli-composer)
- **Benefit:** Editor integrations without LSP support (vim ALE, Emacs flycheck,
  pre-commit on unsaved buffers) and mutation-testing frameworks, which need
  'does the mutant still type-check?' without writing to the original file, both
  work without temp-dir copies of the project.
- **Mago evidence:** `src/commands/stdin_input.rs:14`,
  `crates/database/src/loader.rs:186`, `src/commands/args/substitution.rs:57`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:569`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:627`
- **Risks:** Whole-project passes such as dead code see the substituted content,
  which is correct. The only real work is keeping the logical-name mapping
  consistent.
- **Verification:** All cited locations check out. Mago:
  src/commands/stdin_input.rs:14 resolve_stdin_override requires exactly one
  path, reads stdin as raw bytes with read_to_end, strips the workspace prefix
  and leading './' to get the logical name, then calls set_source_paths.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Add a per-path content-override map to the `check-project` session, keyed by
> the analysed logical path as the session spells it (root-relative, the same as
> `collect_php_files` output). Fill it through `project::session::Overrides`
> (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project/session.rs:70), which already carries the other
> CLI-over-config values, as `content_overrides: FxHashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>`.
> In `Session::read_and_parse_file` (session.rs:569), look the path up in the
> map first and fall back to `std::fs::read(self.root.join(path))`. Loading,
> parsing, the registry, dead-code passes and the baseline then run unchanged,
> and reported paths stay the original names.
>
> CLI in crates/phpstan-rs/src/main/check_project.rs: (1) `--stdin-input <PATH>`
> (or `-` plus `--stdin-path`) reads raw bytes from stdin into the map for PATH.
> PATH must fall inside the analysed paths and must not be excluded. Printing is
> limited to PATH (filter the `results` keys at check_project.rs:218/258), and
> project-wide passes still see the buffer. (2) Repeatable
> `--substitute ORIG=TEMP`, which conflicts with stdin. It reads TEMP's bytes
> into the map for ORIG after normalising ORIG to the session's spelling, and
> errors if ORIG is not an analysed file. Also accept PHPStan's Infection-facing
> spellings `--tmp-file TEMP --instead-of ORIG` as aliases, because Infection's
> static-analysis integration already emits those flags. That makes phpstan-rs a
> drop-in static-analysis gate for Infection with no adapter.
>
> Normalise the path for both flags by canonicalising, then stripping the root,
> so absolute and relative spellings hit the same key. Add tests for: a parse
> error in the override, a class declared in an override being seen by other
> files, excluded ORIG, and non-UTF-8 bytes (these already go through
> `from_utf8_lossy` plus the `&bytes` parse path).

#### K183. restricted_symbols patterns and namespace scoping

- **Value/cost:** 5/10, M (aspect: semantics-guard)
- **Benefit:** Enables 'nothing outside App\\Legacy may touch App\\Legacy\\**',
  'no code may read PHP_EOL-style legacy constants', and namespace-based rather
  than path-based carve-outs, which survive directory moves and PSR-4 remaps.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/guard/src/settings.rs:59`,
  `crates/guard/src/perimeter/checker.rs:132`, `crates/guard/src/matcher.rs:27`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs:355`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs:45`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs:129`
- **Risks:** Pattern matching on every call site costs something. Bail out when
  the pattern bucket is empty, as the exact maps already do (is_empty,
  restricted_symbols.rs:374).
- **Verification:** Mago's citations are correct. DependencyRestriction is at
  crates/guard/src/settings.rs:59-72, with dependency: SymbolSelector,
  allow_from/deny_from: Vec\<String>, and kinds: Vec\<PermittedDependencyKind>
  (ClassLike/Function/Constant/Attribute, :83-89).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Extend crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs and
> checker/restricted_symbol_usage.rs in four parts. Do not port a second matcher
> wholesale. (1) Name patterns. At compile time (RestrictedSymbols::compile,
> restricted_symbols.rs:~384), any entry whose `name` or `class` contains `*` or
> `{` goes into a
> `patterns: Vec<(RestrictedSymbolKind, CompiledFqnPattern, RestrictedSymbolEntry)>`
> bucket. Exact names stay in the FxHashMaps. `is_empty()` (:374) also checks
> the bucket. Each lookup fn (`function`/`class`/`method`/… at :437+) tries the
> exact map first and then scans the bucket. Put a small segment-aware FQN
> matcher in a new `crates/phpstan-rs/src/fqn_pattern.rs`, modeled on mago
> crates/guard/src/matcher.rs:27: `*` = one segment or partial segment, `**` =
> any depth, `{a,b}`, a trailing `\` = namespace prefix, case-insensitive except
> the final segment of constants. It needs segment semantics because the
> existing ignore_errors::glob_matches (ignore_errors.rs:96) lets `*` cross `\`,
> and it has no braces. (2) Fix the function lookup to use FQNs.
> check_restricted_function_call (restricted_symbol_usage.rs:652) strips the
> namespace (`rsplit('\\')`) before looking up. So a ban on `dump` hits
> `App\X\dump()` too, and a namespaced function can't be banned exactly. Look up
> the resolved FQN first, keeping the bare-name lookup only for global
> functions. (3) Add a RestrictedSymbolKind::Constant (:45) for global
> constants, hooked at the ConstFetch handling in checker/expr.rs, with a
> case-sensitive final segment. (4) Add
> `allow_in_namespaces`/`allow_except_in_namespaces` using the same FQN matcher,
> checked against the checker's active namespace. It sits next to
> is_allowed_by_calling_context (:534) and is_allowed_by_instance_of_context
> (:597), and follows their has_params_in_allowed_directive guard. Update the
> module doc (:30-32), which says namespaces are out of scope. Add unit tests in
> restricted_symbols.rs's test module and one fixture per new kind or directive.

#### K166. restricted_symbols presets and extension bans

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: linter-catalog-other)
- **Benefit:** One-line configs for common policies. Extension bans are more
  complete than Mago's hand-maintained table, and the debug preset is
  type-precise about print_r(..., true).
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_debug_symbols.rs:92`,
  `crates/linter/src/rule/security/disallowed_functions.rs:191`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/banned.rs:137`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/stubs.rs:836`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs:46`
- **Risks:** The preset contents are opinionated, so presets stay opt-in. The
  extension kind must ignore user-defined functions shadowing built-in names in
  namespaces.
- **Verification:** No material corrections. In Mago,
  crates/linter/src/rule/security/no_debug_symbols.rs:92 is the start of
  `fn check`. The print_r/var_export exemption is at lines 100-104 and only
  tests `function_call.argument_list.arguments.len() > 1`, so
  `print_r($x, false)` really is exempt.
- **Refined proposal:**

> 1. In crates/phpstan-rs/src/banned.rs, extend `restricted_symbol_preset` with
>    `debug-functions`: Function entries for var_dump, debug_zval_refcount,
>    debug_print_backtrace, dump, dd, dumpe, xdebug_\* (use a glob if the
>    Function kind supports one, otherwise the explicit xdebug names from the
>    stubs' xdebug extension, found via
>    `builtin_function_extension(..) == Some("xdebug")`), plus print_r and
>    var_export with `allow_params_anywhere = [{position = 2, value = true}]` so
>    only the returning form is allowed. Add `unsafe-unserialize`: unserialize
>    with `allow_params_anywhere_any_value = [{position = 2}]`, worded as "pass
>    an options array with allowed_classes". Update the unknown-preset error
>    list and project/tests/banned.rs.
> 2. Leave out md5, sha1, rand and mt_rand, or put them in a separately named
>    `weak-hash-and-rng` preset whose message says it is a blanket ban, because
>    use can't be told apart from a symbol.
> 3. Add `RestrictedSymbolKind::Extension` in
>    crates/phpstan-rs/src/restricted_symbols.rs with an
>    `extensions: HashMap<lowercase ext, entry>` in the compiled
>    `RestrictedSymbols`. In checker/restricted_symbol_usage.rs
>    `check_restricted_function_call`, after the existing name lookup, resolve
>    the called function to its real global target (namespace fallback
>    included). Only when the resolved signature is a stub, look up
>    `stubs::builtin_function_extension` and match the extension entry. Do the
>    same in the Class-kind paths via `builtin_class_extension`, applied only
>    when the class name resolves to a built-in class and not a user class.
>    Report as `restrictedSymbol.extension` with message "Call to \<fn>() from
>    restricted extension \<ext>". Add fixtures for a namespaced user function
>    that shadows a curl_\* name (must not fire) and for `new CurlHandle`-style
>    class uses.
> 4. Separately (a small existing bug found along the way): the Function kind's
>    match on the bare last segment at restricted_symbol_usage.rs:652 also hits
>    same-named namespaced user functions. Consider matching the resolved FQN
>    instead.

#### K190. Richer declarative framework tables

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, S (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Covers the most common framework dynamic-typing needs (service
  locators, config accessors, magic model attributes) with zero Rust code. Users
  also get feedback when a table entry has no effect.
- **Mago evidence:**
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/psr_container/get.rs:72`,
  `docs/content/en/extensions/analyzer/return-types-and-callable-signatures.md:1`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:1476`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/external/protocol.rs:3125`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/assertion_tables.rs:76`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/assertion_table.rs:65`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/assertion_table.rs:77`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/assertion_tables.rs:25`
- **Risks:** Property type overrides can mask genuine undefined-property errors,
  so apply them only to the configured class hierarchy and document that they
  are authoritative. Keep literal maps exact-match.
- **Verification:** Mago:
  crates/analyzer/src/plugin/libraries/psr_container/get.rs has only about 62
  lines, so line 72 does not exist. TARGETS (MethodTarget::any_class(b"get")) is
  at line 22.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't add the new `[[method_returns]]`, `[[function_returns]]` or
> `[[property_types]]` table kinds. PHPDoc in a `stub_paths` stub already does
> all three, and it goes through the normal inheritance and generics machinery.
> Make two small fixes to the existing tables instead.
>
> (1) crates/phpstan-rs/src/registry/assertion_table.rs, lines 60-72: an
> `[[assertions]]` class+method entry only searches the named class's own
> `info.methods`. When the method is only inherited (the entry names a subclass
> of the declaring class), resolve it with `lookup_method_with_owner`
> (registry/hierarchy.rs:462) and tag the owner's signature. Tagging the owner
> is harmless because the assertion is about the parameter's semantics. Also
> decide whether an entry naming a parent should reach overrides in subclasses;
> `class_argument_return` in checker/expr/member_resolution.rs:415-419 already
> matches through `is_subclass_of`, so follow that.
>
> (2) An entry that doesn't resolve should produce a warning instead of a silent
> `continue` (lines 72 and 77-80: missing class, method, function or parameter).
> The same goes for a `type` that `parse_type_string` can't parse. Add these to
> the warnings built at project/session.rs:338-344, next to the SQL schema drift
> warnings. Only warn for user-configured entries, not the built-in
> Tester/Mockery defaults, which are expected to be missing in most projects.
>
> (3) Documentation: in the module doc at
> crates/phpstan-rs/src/assertion_tables.rs:25-27, point container and
> magic-property users to stub files. The stub for a literal service id uses
> `@return ($id is 'logger' ? Logger : mixed)`, and
> `@template T @param class-string<T> $id @return T` covers `get(Foo::class)`.
> Magic properties use `@property-read` in a stub.

#### K193. Out-of-process extension ABI as a later stage

- **Value/cost:** 4/10, XL (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Lets framework authors write Laravel, Symfony or container
  knowledge in PHP, and even run the app's real container, without rebuilding
  phpstan-rs. This is the only route to an ecosystem comparable to PHPStan's
  extensions.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/analyzer/src/external/protocol.rs:133`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/external/mod.rs:1397`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/external/mod.rs:806`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/external/protocol.rs:2365`,
  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:90`, `crates/extension/src/pool.rs:57`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/rule.rs:12`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/ext.rs:1`
- **Risks:** Mago's own implementation is about 10.7k lines of Rust (external/)
  plus 4k lines (crates/extension) plus a 17k-line PHP SDK. IPC per call site is
  expensive and needs matching in Rust and memoization to stay usable. LSP
  incrementality needs generation invalidation. Worker processes run arbitrary
  code (a trust model is needed), and the type wire format becomes a
  compatibility contract that constrains changes to the crates/types Repr. A
  WASM-component plugin model is an alternative with better sandboxing but no
  precedent in either codebase.
- **Verification:** None of the citations are materially wrong. Small precision
  notes: the MANA magic and major/minor constants are at mago
  crates/analyzer/src/external/protocol.rs:133-135.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep this as a deferred, gated item. Do not start it before an in-process
> provider layer exists and has been stable for a while. Stage 0, a prerequisite
> that is worth doing on its own merits: pull the hard-coded dynamic-return
> logic in crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, and the
> per-framework knowledge under src/ext/\*.rs, out behind a small set of traits:
> return type, property type, assertion, and issue filter. Add host-side target
> matching (by FQN or method name) and a capability flag per trait, so an
> unmatched call site costs only a hash lookup. Stage 1: give the request and
> response types a serializable form. Pass argument types as printed PHPDoc
> strings, which crates/types already prints and crates/phpdoc already parses.
> Add spans and literal text. Treat the format as versioned and lossy, so
> internal Repr variants do not become an ABI. Stage 2: add an opt-in
> `[[extension_hosts]] command = [...]` in crates/config. It would spawn a small
> worker pool that speaks length-prefixed frames, with a magic value and a
> major/minor version. Copy Mago's policies: a per-request timeout; a provider
> failure falls back to native analysis, as in the Mago analyzer's
> plugin/registry.rs:90 `optional_external_hint`, while lifecycle failures stay
> fatal; opt-in memoization keyed by an analysis generation that
> Project::update_file bumps for the LSP; and batched nested metadata queries.
> The PHP SDK would be a separate package. Workers run only when a project's own
> config names them, which is the trust model.

#### K189. Wire external Rule API into Project/Session/LSP

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, S (aspect: plugins-extensions)
- **Benefit:** Makes the already-built extension API actually usable. A company
  wrapping phpstan-rs can ship framework rules without forking, and the in-tree
  extension checks could later move onto the same trait.

  `crates/analyzer/src/plugin/registry.rs:688`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/src/checker.rs:1131`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1416`, `crates/phpstan-rs/src/rule.rs:99`,
  `crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs:1561`
- **Risks:** The API becomes a stability commitment, so mark it unstable and
  version it. `type_of` on arbitrary expressions re-infers them, which costs
  time; the infer_cache (expr.rs:320) mitigates this within one outermost
  check_expr.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/orchestrator/src/lib.rs:115-122 is
  `get_analyzer_plugin_registry`, a lazy `OnceLock` init that calls
  `create_registry_with_plugins` (a second call is at :132). wasm also calls it
  (crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:197, :316).
- **Refined proposal:**

> Keep this small, and treat it as finishing an API that is already half-built
> rather than as new work. (1) Add a
> `pub struct Extensions { rules: Vec<Box<dyn rule::Rule>>, reflection_rules:
> Vec<Box<dyn reflection_rule::ReflectionRule>> }`
> field on `Project` (crates/phpstan-rs/src/project.rs), empty by default, with
> a `Project::set_extensions` setter. It should not go in `ProjectSettings`,
> which is config-deserialized data and has no place for trait objects. (2) In
> `checker_for` (project.rs:1416), call
> `checker.set_external_rules(&self.extensions.rules)`. The `&'a` lifetime on
> `Checker::external_rules` (checker.rs:609) is already satisfied by borrowing
> from `Project`. `run_checker` (project.rs:1447) and the LSP paths (inlay
> hints, semantic tokens) go through `checker_for`, so they pick the rules up
> with no further change. (3) In project/session.rs, append
> `project.run_reflection_rules(&extensions.reflection_rules)` output to the

> ignores apply to them. Add a `Session::with_extensions` builder. (4) Add
> `Scope::type_of(&self, e: &Expr) -> Type`, delegating to
> `self.checker.infer_expr(e, self.locals)`. That function already takes `&self`
> (checker/expr.rs:4448), so this is a three-line change. Also add
> `Scope::registry() -> &Registry`. (5) Mark `rule`/`reflection_rule` as
> unstable in their module docs. Drop the "ProviderRegistry::register_\*" part:

#### K267. wasm32 target crate

- **Value/cost:** 3/10, L (aspect: build-structure)
- **Benefit:** An online playground for bug reports and docs, and a web-hosted
  VS Code extension (the repo already has editors/vscode). The wasm check also
  works as an architecture gate: it mechanically keeps the engine free of I/O
  and C dependencies, which the plan's 'no engine I/O' rule (gate 10) states but
  only enforces by path.
- **Mago evidence:** `crates/wasm/Cargo.toml:1`, `crates/wasm/build.rs:9`
- **phpstan-rs:** `crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml:10`,
  `crates/stub-sources/src/lib.rs:25`, `CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN.md:120`
- **Risks:** stacker (psm) and any other remaining native dependency must be
  verified for wasm32. This was not checked here and needs a
  `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` probe per crate. Wasm memory is
  limited: stubs plus a project AST may be large without idea 3's compact
  snapshot or C5's lazy layer. Also an extra target to keep compiling.
- **Verification:** Mago: crates/wasm/Cargo.toml has crate-type = ["cdylib"] at
  line 16. Dependencies at lines 25-39 are allocator, word, reporting, database,
  php-version, linter, analyzer, formatter, orchestrator, syntax, prelude
  (features = ["serde"]), wasm-bindgen, serde-wasm-bindgen and serde.
- **Refined proposal:**

> Don't build a wasm crate now. The cheap and useful part is the architecture
> gate, and it can start without a playground. Once the crate split has happened
> and the SQL drivers are behind a feature (the split already has `live-*` in
> mind), add a CI step that runs
> `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p phpstan-rs-syntax -p
> phpstan-rs-types -p phpstan-rs-phpdoc -p phpstan-rs-stub-sources`
> and, later, the engine crate with `--no-default-features`. That mechanically
> keeps the pure layers free of I/O and C dependencies.
>
> Three prerequisites come first:
>
> 1. Move `rusqlite`/`mysql`/`postgres`/`r2d2*` in `crates/sql/Cargo.toml`
>    behind a feature and keep sqlparser-only schema typing always on. The user
>    has previously and explicitly chosen to keep rusqlite ungated (see the
>    comment in `crates/phpstan-rs/Cargo.toml` under the features section), so
>    they need to decide this first.
> 2. Route the 34 non-test `rayon`/`par_iter` sites in `crates/phpstan-rs/src`

> Only after that, and only if a public playground or the web VS Code extension
> becomes a real goal, add `crates/wasm` with wasm-bindgen exports
> `analyse(files_json, config_json) -> diagnostics_json` and
> `hover(path, offset)`. It would sit on `project::Session` and pull in no
> pcre2, sql-live, clap, lsp-server or dhat.

## 4. Suggested sequencing

### 4.1 Hard dependencies

- **Parser:** K1 stage 1 (statement/member recovery) comes before K4 (lexer
  strictness), because stricter lexing without recovery drops more files. K2
  (located parse diagnostics) can ship first and on its own.
- **Exit codes and severity:** K194 exit codes come before K160 (severity model
  and fail threshold). K142 (central identifier catalog, CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN D6)
  feeds K160, K202 (identifier filters and stats) and K257 (identifier-coverage
  gate).
- **Narrowing:**
  - K90 (merge per-disjunct states for `||`-true and `&&`-false) comes first.
  - K92 (cross-variable implications from disjunct deltas) builds on K90's merge
    decomposition.
  - K91 (persistent CNF clause set) comes after K90, and only if K90 and K92
    leave real gaps.
  - K135 (possibly-undefined offsets) depends on K94 (container filtering).
  - K132 (generic impossible/redundant diagnostics) should follow K133 and the
    narrowing fixes.
- **Generics and calls:**
  - K77 (check arguments against template-resolved parameters) comes before K81
    (pin invariant slots).
  - K76 (whole-call inference) and K114 (contextual closure types) share one
    call pipeline, so build them together. K79 and K80 slot into the same
    binder.
  - K82 (callable values) feeds K76, K118 (pipe operator) and K273 (callable
    dead-code references).
  - K116 (named-argument-aware call view, "CallCx") comes before K126 (typed
    provider registry) and before reworking builtin extensions: K115, K117,
    K123, K188, K185.
- **Registry identity and incremental:**
  - K35 (case-folded symbol ids) underlies K26, K27, K30 and K29. The S-sized
    fixes K25, K27 and K28 can land first.
  - K219 (incremental-vs-full differential tests) comes before the incremental
    optimizations K53 (signature/body split) and K41 (dirty-set finishing
    passes), and before K212, K216 and K217.
  - K39 (own vs derived class state) comes before K237 (re-index descendants for
    stale inherited docblocks). K42 (retract-and-replay per-file contributions)
    comes before K43 (total priority order), which uses the same machinery.
- **CRATE_SPLIT_PLAN folding:**
  - C4 (lazy per-class memos): K40, K41, K55, K39.
  - C5 (lazy version-keyed stub layer): K50, K57, K56, K49, plus K58 as a free
    first step.
  - C6 (overlays): K44, K60.
  - D6 (identifier families): K142, then K160, K202 and K257.
- **Workspace:** K228 (one shared workspace resolver and membership matcher)
  underpins K224 (excludes), K225 (never analyze vendor or a file twice), K227
  (CLI config auto-discovery) and K221 (classifying runtime-created files). K214
  (symlink-safe discovery) and K198 (canonical file identity) belong in the same
  change.
- **Dead code:** K268 (type-resolved member references) comes first, then K269
  (transitive reachability), then K270 (whole-program reachability). K268 pairs
  with K272 (trait accesses to host private members). K187 (entry points)
  supports K270.
- **Property initialization:** K283 (definite init at constructor exit) comes
  before K284, K289 and K290. K285 and K291 build on the per-path state K283
  introduces. K286, K287 and K288 are independent.
- **Distribution:** K266 (SQL drivers behind features, which removes the ring
  and aws-lc build requirements) comes before K301 (musl and old-glibc targets).
  K304 (container image) and K300 (Composer launcher) follow, then K302, K306
  and K307.
- **Docblocks:** K239 (one pre-processor and tag path) comes before K238
  (TypeNode to Type), then K241 (precise in-docblock spans) and K242
  (docblock-aware navigation). K243 (inherit asserts/throws/param-out) goes with
  K237.
- **Inspection tooling:** K312 (type-at CLI) and K311 (dumpType/dumpScope) share
  an extracted inspect module from the LSP probe. K308-K310 and K313 replace
  `demo`.

1. **Quick correctness wins (S, independent, each with fixtures):**

### 4.3 Near-duplicate clusters (design together, keep separate entries)

- Parser diagnostics: K1 and K2; `php -l` oracle: K9 and K184.
- PHP-version modelling: K49, K56, K179, K180, K233 and K303.
- Stub overlays and loading: K44, K54, K60 and K124; K18, K50, K55, K57 and K58.
- Termination and flow: K103, K147 and K299; definedness: K100 and K104.
- String offsets: K120 and K134. Readonly compound writes: K286 and K291.
- Member usage and dead code: K161, K268, K272 and K273. Imports: K36 and K37.
- Workspace identity: K198, K224, K225 and K228.
- Identifier catalog: K142, K160, K202 and K257. Type inspection: K302, K311 and

## 5. Refuted ideas (do not re-propose)

1. **Per-file token/trivia table for comments, docblocks and highlighting:**
   none of the claimed benefits hold. phpstan-rs already attaches doc comments
   at every statement site, and its other consumers work without a retained
   token table.
2. **Compact flags variant for refined strings instead of accessory
   intersections:** the claimed allocation gains do not exist, because types are
   already hash-consed and interned. The rewrite would be XL with high
   regression risk, and phpstan-rs's separate refined strings are more precise
   than Mago's AND-ed flags.
3. **Parameter-variable types anywhere in a signature (`key-of<$map>`):** in
   phpstan-rs, `$param` is only a conditional-type subject, and the verifier
   judged the general form not worth adding.
4. **Paradox/redundant-condition diagnostics from persistent clauses:** these
   would only duplicate the existing type-based always-true/false diagnostics.
   Mago's own output shows the duplication.
5. **Tool-version pin in config:** fits Mago's frequent 1.x releases and
   self-update, but gives phpstan-rs no real value.
6. **Flatten concat chains and bound literal growth:** stack depth is already
   handled by `syntax::stack::guard` in Type::concat. Of the remaining claims,
   one is already handled and the other shows up only on unusual input.
7. **Max file-size guard:** Mago reads the whole file before checking its 256
   MiB cap, so its evidence is overstated. More work than it is worth.
8. **Workspace clippy denials:** CI already runs
   `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, which covers the
   proposed lints.
9. **Per-body syntactic effect summary in one walk:** the walks cost almost
   nothing next to type checking. The one worthwhile piece is an S-sized
   lazy-evaluation fix.
10. **Fold the property-initialization walker into the main checker's Locals:**
    the standalone walker's in-order helper absorption and read-before-init
    detection are strengths. Folding it in would lose them for no measured gain.
11. **Route inaccessible declared properties through `__get`/`__set` instead of
    reporting visibility errors:** the runtime rule is real, but the proposal as
    framed was refuted. The related, accepted piece is K292 (clamping memoized
    values to the magic read type).
12. **Resolve workspace-local `vendor/bin/phpstan-rs` in the editor extension:**
    it depends on a Composer launcher package that does not exist yet. It only
    becomes meaningful after K300.
